### Record: agents/frobenius/C3_smooth_cone_independent_REVIEW.md

# Independent audit of C.3u: ordinary Picard classes on a smooth cone

**Conclusion:** the complete typed proof in ../real_weil/C3_smooth_cone_draft.tex passes. We checked ordinary algebraic equivalence, integral coefficients, arbitrary characteristic, nonhomogeneous divisors, and each new external input. The result is restricted to the stated smooth cone source; it does not extend to a deformation or an arbitrary local germ by this argument.

## Exact statement checked

Let \(V/k\) be smooth projective integral of dimension at least three over an algebraically closed field, with \(L\) very ample and its full section ring generated in degree one. On the strict cone puncture \(X\), pullback identifies the **point group** of \(\operatorname{Pic}^0_{\mathrm{red}}(V)\) with line bundles ordinarily algebraically equivalent to zero. For any nonzero local element \(f\) with regular divisor puncture \(Y\), ordinary restriction is integrally surjective. The kernel is zero in characteristic zero and a finite \(p\)-primary point group in characteristic \(p\). Ordinary rational \(J^1\) therefore restricts isomorphically.

## Proof checks

1. **Resolution and boundary.** Degree-one generation identifies the vertex blow-up with the total space of \(L^{-1}\). Localization and ind-etale strict henselization preserve regularity. The resulting integral noetherian \(Z\) is proper over \(R\), its closed fibre is the single reduced prime divisor \(V\), and its normal bundle is \(L^{-1}\). The actual projection \(\pi:Z\to V\) survives. Closing a rational divisor extends each line bundle on \(X\), and the kernel of \(\operatorname{Pic}(Z)\to\operatorname{Pic}(X)\) consists of powers of \(\mathcal O_Z(V)\).

2. **Actual family and pointwise injectivity.** The normalized Poincare bundle on \(V\times A\), with \(A=\operatorname{Pic}^0_{\mathrm{red}}(V)\), pulls back to an actual bundle on \(X\times A\). If \(\pi^*Q=\mathcal O_Z(bV)\), restriction gives \(Q=L^{-b}\); algebraic triviality and ampleness force \(b=0\). The proof correctly asserts injectivity on points without assuming a trivial infinitesimal kernel. Restricting to chains of curves in \(A\) proves ordinary algebraic triviality.

3. **All torsion at one suitable prime.** Choose \(\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k\) avoiding torsion in \(\operatorname{NS}(V)/\mathbf Z[L]\). An \(\ell^n\)-torsion bundle \(M\) extends to \(\widetilde M\) with \(\widetilde M^{\ell^n}=\mathcal O_Z(bV)\). Its restriction \(Q\) has class in \(\mathbf Z[L]\). If \([Q]=a[L]\), twisting by \(\mathcal O_Z(aV)\) has the correct sign and makes the restriction algebraically trivial. Restriction of the remaining power identity and ampleness force its boundary coefficient to vanish. Both the new extension and \(Q\) are torsion. The quotient \(T=\widetilde M\otimes\pi^*Q^{-1}\) defines a finite etale Kummer torsor trivial on \(V\), because its defining unit lies in the divisible group \(k^\times\). Proper henselian finite-etale equivalence lifts its section to \(Z\). Thus \(M=\rho^*Q\), giving the claimed equality of all \(\ell^n\)-torsion groups.

4. **Density without arbitrary family algebraization.** C.3n places an ordinary class in a closed abelian image \(B\) of the local Picard scheme. Its dense prime-to-characteristic torsion lies in the closed proper image \(P\) of \(A\); therefore \(B\subset P\). For the target, the proof correctly uses the product of local Picard schemes of finite normalizations. C.3p lifts all target \(\ell^n\)-torsion to the source. Thus each target ordinary abelian image is contained in the closed proper image \(r(P)\). Every point of this image lifts to a point of \(P\) over the algebraically closed field, and that point already comes from the actual Poincare family. This gives integral surjectivity without inferring that arbitrary henselized-product families algebraize.

5. **Kernel.** The closed kernel in \(A\) has no nonzero prime-to-characteristic torsion by C.3p and pointwise injectivity. A positive-dimensional reduced connected subgroup would be an abelian variety with such torsion. The kernel scheme is therefore finite; its finite point group is zero in characteristic zero and \(p\)-primary in characteristic \(p\). This is precisely the claimed conclusion.

## Independently opened primary inputs

- **Stacks Project, Lemma 58.9.1, Tag 0A48:** https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A48 . Fresh full opening confirmed the exact proper-scheme hypothesis over a henselian local ring. It is not an arbitrary-family algebraization statement.
- **Cheng, Ji, Larson, and Olander, Theorem of the Base, author version dated July 1, 2021:** https://chngr.github.io/assets/theorem-of-the-base.pdf . Fresh full opening and local text check of **Theorem 7.3, p. 18**, confirm finite generation of the Neron–Severi group in the required all-characteristic smooth projective case. Local PDF: ../real_weil/sources/cheng_ji_larson_olander2021.pdf.
- **Kleiman, The Picard scheme, arXiv:math/0504020v1 (April 1, 2005):** https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0504020 . Fresh full opening and direct local PDF reading checked **Theorem 2.5(2), p. 18; Exercise 4.3, p. 27, with Answer 4.3, p. 65; Theorem 5.4, pp. 37–38; Proposition 5.10, pp. 41–42**. These supply the universal bundle with a section, properness of the identity component, and ordinary algebraic equivalence. The version-qualified web URL initially failed; the unqualified PDF successfully opened the same unique v1. Local PDF: ../real_weil/sources/kleiman_picard2005v1.pdf.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C3_surjectivity_independent_REVIEW.md

# Independent audit: the deformed-cone ordinary Picard surjectivity counterexample

## Scope and outcome

We independently read the entire draft `research/agents/real_weil/C3_surjectivity_draft.tex` on 19 November 2026. The construction and proof pass this audit. The result concerns ordinary algebraic equivalence defined by actual families on the fixed punctured scheme. It does not rely on identifying that relation with the connected component of a local Picard functor.

The claimed range is every complex local dimension N at least four. The source ordinary algebraically trivial Picard group is zero, whereas the target contains an injected copy of the Fermat quartic Jacobian, including a specified point of infinite order. Thus the ordinary J1 restriction map fails surjectivity integrally and rationally in this range.

## Geometry and first neighbourhood

1. In the total space of O(-1,-1) over P^m × P², the equation F+tℓH is globally typed as a section of O(0,4). The codimension-two locus F=ℓH=0 cannot contribute an additional irreducible component to its hypersurface. The Segre contraction is proper, is an isomorphism away from the zero section, and has the asserted radical equations on its reduced image.
2. Smoothness near the exceptional V=P^m × C follows from dF. Properness permits removal of the image of the nonsmooth complement. The map factors through the finite normalization, whose fibre above the vertex consists of one point: the proper surjection from the connected exceptional V cannot cover two points of a finite discrete fibre. Strict henselization preserves the relevant regularity and exceptional-divisor statements.
3. The principal function f=tℓ has smooth strict transform D equal to the total line bundle over the incidence projective bundle H0→C. This supplies a regular punctured target without a projective-normality assumption.
4. The first-neighbourhood deformation class is the boundary of ℓH in the normal sequence twisted by L. Its curve components δ(z_i H) are exactly the three surviving degree-five Fermat Jacobian-ring monomials. The dimensions used are consistent: h0(O_C(5))=18, the derivative image has dimension15, and its cokernel H1(O_C) has dimension3. The Euler-sequence computation gives H1(T_P²|C⊗K_C)=0.
5. Serre duality turns these three independent boundary classes into an injective contraction cκ:H0(K_C)→H1(V,L). The same argument has rank3 for every m≥2.

## The integral family argument

The key improvement over the earlier possible route is that the proof uses the obstruction for an actual Poincaré family. It does not infer a global vector-group extension from a tangent calculation.

The square-zero extension obstruction for a line bundle on V×P is κ contracted with its V-Atiyah class. Its mixed component is the image of the normalized Poincaré tensor under cκ. Since cκ is injective, an extension to V2×P forces ψ*:H1(J,O_J)→H1(P,O_P) to vanish. For a homomorphism of complex abelian varieties this forces ψ=0. Normalization by the Abel-map diagonal identifies the mixed tensor correctly; only an irrelevant overall sign depends on conventions.

The previously audited finite-descent and smooth-compactification argument supplies an actual line bundle on X×P with P an abelian variety and fibre0 trivial. Its divisor closure on the regular noetherian product Z×P is Cartier. The fibre0 correction is O(bV), since V is the sole boundary prime divisor. Restriction to V×P is therefore a family in Pic0(V), and the obstruction proves that all its fibres there are trivial after a harmless pullback twist from P.

The square-zero unit sequence then expresses its class on V2×P by H1(V×P,L). The Künneth decomposition shows that restriction to any point of the proper connected P is the same map on the first summand and zero on the second. Hence all fibre classes on V2 agree, and the normalized fibre0 makes them trivial. For r≥2, both H1(V,L^r) and H2(V,L^r) vanish. The resulting Picard isomorphisms and surjective unit maps provide compatible trivializations on every infinitesimal neighbourhood.

## Completion and target injection

The equality m_R O_Z=I_V is justified in both directions: the old Segre coordinates generate the local ideal (t), and every additional normalization function in the maximal ideal vanishes on the reduced divisor V. Thus the V-adic formal neighbourhood is exactly the one to which proper formal full faithfulness applies after completing R.

Proper formal full faithfulness gives a trivialization on the completed resolution and hence on the completed puncture. A rank-one reflexive extension Q=j_*M is finite. Its local cohomology in degrees0 and1 vanishes; flat base change and the fact that the completion has a one-point closed fibre identify Q⊗Rhat with the extension of the now trivial punctured line bundle. It is Rhat. Faithfully flat descent makes Q a finite projective rank-one module over the local ring R, hence free. This closes the passage from formal triviality to the original strict local puncture.

The target injection Pic0(C)→Pic(Y) is also integral. A trivial target restriction would differ on the regular D by O(bH0). Restriction to a line in a P^{m−1} fibre gives b=0, and the projective-bundle Picard formula then gives the trivial source line bundle. This is where m≥2 is used essentially. The Poincaré family gives ordinary algebraic equivalence of its image. The point involving a transcendental coordinate has infinite order because all torsion points of the Qbar-defined Jacobian are Qbar-rational and the Abel map is a Qbar-defined closed immersion.

## Independently opened sources

- Illusie, *Cotangent complex and deformations of torsors and group schemes* (1972), Theorem2.6, printed p.166, and formula(2.7.2), printed p.167. Primary reprint opened at https://bibliotheque.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/media/filer_public/ce/24/ce243c31-2953-498e-92cb-c8b2e70d207d/i_illusie-64.pdf . The torsor obstruction is exactly the extension class composed with the Atiyah class. For G_m the co-Lie term is the trivial line, giving the displayed H2 obstruction. The draft also provides a direct Čech proof.
- Illusie's author errata, opened at https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~luc.illusie/ErrHalifax.pdf . Its corrections concern printed pp.177,185,189 and do not change the used theorem or formula.
- Stacks Project, Lemma30.24.1, Tag0883, opened at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0883 . Its assumptions are precisely a noetherian complete base and a proper morphism; its conclusion is full faithfulness of formal completion for coherent sheaves. The proof uses it only after completing the base.

## Status limitation

This audit proves no assertion in dimension3 and makes no identification between ordinary Chow algebraic equivalence and all connected local Picard families. The construction establishes the stated failure of surjectivity for N≥4; previously proved injectivity results are compatible with a zero source.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C3ab_surface_cone_independent_REVIEW.md

# Independent audit of C.3ab: integral surface-cone top cycles

**Reviewer:** `/root/frobenius`. **Tool-clock date:** 2026-11-19 08:11:29 UTC.  
**Draft reviewed:** `research/agents/real_weil/C3_surface_cone_top_draft.tex`.  
**Outcome:** full typed proof and targeted primary-source applicability check pass, subject only to the harmless displayed-relation comma typo reported to the owner. This is a proof audit of the stated theorem and its use of the cited results, not an independent reproof of all cited K-theory theorems.

## Exact scope

The theorem concerns the strict henselization at the vertex of the normal, degree-one-generated full section ring of a smooth projective surface over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field. Its extra condition is the vanishing of H²(V, Ω¹ over Q tensor L^j) for every j≥1. It does not silently replace absolute differentials by relative differentials. Under that condition the conclusion is integral: CH² of the puncture is CH₀(V)/(L CH¹(V)), and the ordinary algebraic-equivalence quotient is Z/gZ, where g is the positive gcd of intersection degrees of L with integral curves. The stronger assertion for arbitrary three-dimensional local germs is not made.

## Proof checks

1. **Resolution and infinitesimal neighbourhoods.** The section-ring assumptions identify the blow-up with the total space of L inverse. Strict henselization preserves the Artinian quotients because the residue field is already algebraically closed. The closed-fibre thickenings are therefore the actual split truncated graded algebras O⊕L⊕…⊕L^(a−1), with their projections to V. This splitting is used, correctly, at both the relative K-group and determinant steps.

2. **Finite detection, not an unjustified formal limit.** Morrow's Theorem 3.7(i) applies to the noetherian quasi-excellent Q-schemes in this square. Its relative pro-isomorphism supplies the displayed pro Mayer–Vietoris exact sequence. Since K₀(R) and each K₀(R/m^a) are Z with identity transition maps, quotienting the graph n↦(n,n[O_Z]) identifies the cokernel with constant K₀(Z). Thus K₀(Z) maps monomorphically to the pro-system K₀(V_a). The kernel system consists of decreasing subgroups of one fixed group and inclusion transition maps. Pro-zero therefore forces one of these subgroups to be zero. The claim of injectivity at all sufficiently large finite thickenings is justified and stronger than pointwise separation by an inverse limit.

3. **Relative K₂ retains integral information.** Weibel's Consequence 1.4 explicitly says that the relative K-groups of a nilpotent ideal in a Q-algebra are Q-vector spaces. Consequently Goodwillie's rational comparison is an isomorphism of the underlying integral abelian groups here. For A[t]/(t^a), in positive degree j<a the quotient of t^jΩ¹_A plus A t^(j−1)dt by d(b t^j) has the unique horizontal representative t^j(ω−db/j). Horizontal inclusion is injective and surjective. Under t′=u t it transforms by u^j, so the global summand is Ω¹ over Q tensor L^j. The relation a t^(a−1)dt=0 removes degree a. No extra conormal summand remains. The displayed draft had a literal comma in `t^j,db`; the owner was asked to replace it by a space.

4. **Descent spectral sequence and determinant.** Thomason–Trobaugh's Zariski descent theorem applies to both K-theory spectra and hence their fibre. On a surface, only H¹ of relative K₁ and H² of relative K₂ can contribute to relative K₀, since relative K₀ sheaf is zero. The latter term vanishes by hypothesis, and the H¹ term has no incoming or outgoing differential. The determinant identifies the surviving piece with relative Picard. The split restriction then identifies SK₀(V_a) with SK₀(V), and finite detection plus the section p* identifies SK₀(Z) with SK₀(V).

5. **Integral vanishing of CH₀(Z).** At each closed point z of the proper regular resolution, a regular system of parameters with first parameter the equation of V produces a one-dimensional integral transverse germ. Its closure D has zero-dimensional closed fibre. The proper image of a non-quasi-finite locus would meet the closed point of the local base, so D is quasi-finite and proper, hence finite. Its normalization is finite by excellence and local because it is an integral finite algebra over a henselian local ring. It is a DVR with residue field k. A uniformizer has the unique closed point as divisor; proper pushforward kills [z] with coefficient one. This is an integral argument.

6. **Codimension-two Riemann–Roch.** Fulton's Example 15.3.6 gives the two composites with multiplier (−1)^(2−1)(2−1)!=−1, so CH² and F²K₀/F³K₀ are integrally isomorphic. The limiting argument through smooth pointed étale blow-up neighbourhoods carries vector bundles, support filtrations, cycles, and finite rational-equivalence witnesses to the strict-local Z. Its F³ group is generated by point classes and vanishes by the previous step. Thus the Chern-class comparison and pullback really give CH²(Z)≅CH₀(V).

7. **Localization and ordinary algebraic equivalence.** Self-intersection sends the boundary map to multiplication by −L. Actual flat pullback on the fixed products with parameter curves preserves ordinary algebraic equivalence. The already audited C.3e injection modulo that equivalence is the same map as the resulting surjection, so it is an isomorphism. Zero-cycles on V modulo ordinary algebraic equivalence are classified by degree, yielding Z/gZ. Positivity of g follows from ampleness.

8. **Vanishing examples.** Akizuki–Kodaira–Nakano gives H²(Ω¹ over k tensor L^j)=0 on every such characteristic-zero surface. For k=Qbar the absolute and relative sheaves agree. For arbitrary k, the exact differential sequence and H²(L^j)=0 give the absolute condition; the possibly infinite constant vector space Ω¹_(k/Q) causes no problem because coherent cohomology on this finite affine cover commutes with direct sums. Serre duality proves the additional H²(L^j) vanishing for K3 surfaces and for surfaces with p_g=0, exactly as claimed.

## Independently opened or read primary locators

- Morrow, *Pro cdh-descent for cyclic homology and K-theory*, Theorem 3.7(i), author pp.21–22. Opened full author PDF and read the theorem and characteristic-zero proof: https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~matthew.morrow/Morrow,%20M.,%20Pro%20cdh-descent%20for%20cyclic%20homology%20and%20K-theory.pdf . Tool references `turn151369822view0`, `turn295699166view0`.
- Weibel, *Mayer–Vietoris sequences and mod p K-theory*, Consequence 1.4, printed p.392. # Independent audit of C.3ac

We independently read the complete `cycles/finite_field_abelian.tex` fragment. Its unconditional conclusions are the vanishing of every nonzero Beauville grade, the vanishing of ordinary algebraically trivial Chow groups after tensoring with Q, and Chow hard Lefschetz for abelian varieties over the algebraic closure of a finite field. The rational–numerical comparison, strict positivity, and equivalence with the corresponding numerical category remain explicitly conditional on the source-qualified 2026 CM Hodge input already audited in D.4c–e. Nothing here independently verifies that preprint's analytical proof.

## Primary source inspection

1. Künnemann, *A Lefschetz decomposition for Chow motives of abelian schemes*, Inventiones Mathematicae 113 (1993): we independently viewed the primary scans of printed pp. 99–100. Theorem 7.1 is exactly `CH^p(h^i(A),Q)=0` for `i != 2p`, over a finite field. Its proof on p. 100 uses purity of `h^1` and tensor powers. Theorem 7.3 on p. 100 is exactly the ample-divisor Chow hard Lefschetz isomorphism. Item 7.2 is a definition, not this theorem. The independent primary URL opened in this audit chain was <https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/download/pdf/PPN356556735_0113/LOG_0011.pdf>; local decisive scans are `research/agents/cycles/output/Kunnemann1993-16.png` and `Kunnemann1993-17.png`.

Kahn, *Équivalences rationnelle et numérique sur certaines variétés de type abélien sur un corps fini*, Annales scientifiques de l'École Normale Supérieure 36 (2003): we opened the primary PDF <https://www.numdam.org/item/ASENS_2003_4_36_6_977_0.pdf>, read Definition 1, printed p. 978, and independently viewed Theorem 1.10 and its complete proof, printed p. 982. The theorem concerns the actual rational-equivalence Chow groups and requires the product to lie in `B_tate`, not merely that the Frobenius grading be pure. Its proof explicitly invokes Kimura finiteness, Frobenius semisimplicity, and Proposition 1.7. The category in Definition 1 includes Artin motives and abelian motives. The decisive scan is `research/agents/cycles/output/Kahn2003-06.png`.
3. Soulé, *Groupes de Chow et K-théorie de variétés sur un corps fini*, Mathematische Annalen 268 (1984): we independently viewed printed p. 343, §3.5.5, Corollary 3, in the local primary scan `research/agents/cycles/output/Soule1984_pages/page-28.png`. The hypothesis is explicitly `Y_j = X_j tensor K` with `X_j` defined over the finite field. It does not cover arbitrary nonconstant varieties over a function field. The direct web retrieval of <https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/download/pdf/PPN235181684_0268/LOG_0047.pdf> failed during this check; the local primary page was successfully inspected. No failed retrieval is represented as opened.

## Mathematical checks

* Cycles and rational-equivalence witnesses descend to finite extensions. This justifies taking the filtered union of finite-field Chow groups. The canonical multiplication projectors commute with base change; the grading convention `i = 2r-s` is correct.
* The argument works for every ample class. Over the algebraic closure of a finite field its antisymmetric Picard component is torsion, so the rational symmetric-class convention introduces no restriction.
* For the asserted Gysin surjectivity, the range `2r >= g-1` makes both exponents in the displayed factorization nonnegative. Hard Lefschetz supplies `z = h^(2r+2-g) a`; then `z = i_* i^*(h^(2r+1-g) a)`. The dimensions and Chow codimensions agree. Ordinary Chow localization, rather than a nonexistent homological-equivalence localization sequence, supplies the complement assertion.
* Under the qualified Tate input, Tate surjectivity passes through products, algebraic projectors, direct sums, Tate twists, and Artin factors. Kahn's `B_tate` hypothesis is therefore available for the claimed abelian-type Chow motives.
* A geometric numerically trivial cycle descends to a finite field and is numerically trivial there: every finite-field complementary test cycle is among the geometric test cycles. Kahn then makes the descended representative rationally zero. This proves the geometric injectivity without an unsupported descent of every geometric numerical test cycle.
* Applying the same argument to products proves full faithfulness on correspondences. Idempotent splitting gives the stated equivalence only onto the corresponding generated numerical category. The manuscript correctly excludes arbitrary source varieties outside this category.
* Strict positivity uses the separate qualified Hodge-standard-conjecture input. Chow hard Lefschetz alone is not used to infer positivity or injectivity of grade-zero cycle classes.

No correction to the typed fragment is required by this audit. The constant-variety warning and the qualification of the recent CM Hodge theorem are mathematically material and should remain.

# Independent complete audit of C.3ae

Reviewer: `/root/frobenius`. Tool clock at certification: **2026-11-19 08:53:01 UTC**. Result: **passed**.

We read the complete typed `cycles/higher_local_surjectivity.tex` after it appeared, including the integral cokernel statement, explicit equations, normalization, specialization invariant, conormal obstruction, Hodge projection, and actual-family argument. The conclusion is an integral surjection from the cokernel of **ordinary algebraically trivial codimension-two restriction** to `Pic^0(C)(C)`, for every local dimension at least seven. This is stronger than a single rational witness, but it is not a theorem about the image of arbitrary `CH^2(X)`.

## 1. The algebraic local scheme

The four displayed matrices agree entry for entry with the first tuple in the retained rank computation and with the tuple used in the basepoint computation. The coefficient of the linear fiber variable has no common divisor with the Fermat equation: `F=ell G=0` has codimension two in the smooth base. The graph description therefore gives an integral hypersurface with no extra vertical component. The differential of F makes it smooth near the entire exceptional divisor.

The Segre blowdown is proper and is an isomorphism away from its zero section. Removing the closed image of the singular locus is legitimate because that image misses the vertex. Normality of the resulting model supplies factorization through the finite normalization. Its connected exceptional divisor maps to one point of the finite fiber, and surjectivity shows there are no other points over the vertex. The dimension is `m+4=N`.

For complete explicitness, the scheme-theoretic fiber assertion can be justified in one sentence: every function in the normalized local maximal ideal vanishes on V, while the Segre coordinate functions `t x_i w_j z_k` generate `O(-V)` because their coefficient sections are basepoint free. Hence `m O_Z=O(-V)`. This is an immediate clarification of the written construction, not an additional existence hypothesis.

The strict transform of `f=t ell` is the split line bundle over H. The four-section surjection has kernel of rank m, so H is the smooth projective bundle of lines in that kernel. The normal line and the transversality of the two divisors are correct. Étale descent and nilpotent invariance of pointed étale neighborhoods preserve the specified first neighborhood.

## 2. Exact finite certificates

The earlier independent certificate audit was repeated with a distinct column-wise matrix construction and finite-field `DomainMatrix` operations. Rank is 57 for the 64 by 57 matrix, and the determinant of its first 57 rows is **47 modulo 101**. We also recomputed all twelve projective charts using lexicographic rather than grevlex Groebner bases; all are `[1]`. This is emptiness over the geometric fiber, not merely absence of F101-points. Properness of the common-zero scheme over Z promotes the empty fiber at 101 to an empty generic fiber.

The independently reproducible code is `code/audit_quartic_certificates.py`, with exact outputs in `output/audit_quartic_certificates.json` and `.out`. These computations certify only the linear algebra and basepoint freeness; the following steps are the separate mathematical audit.

## 3. The specialization invariant

Chow localization on the fixed proper model times a fixed proper parameter gives a lift of every class on the puncture. Two lifts differ by a boundary pushforward. Refined restriction changes that difference by multiplication by the normal Chern class `-(h+a)`, exactly the stated denominator. Thus sigma is well-defined on ordinary Chow groups, including all rational-equivalence witnesses.

The parameter-fiber embeddings and the exceptional-divisor embedding are independent regular embeddings. Their refined pullbacks commute. Hence sigma, projective-bundle evaluation, intersection with tau, and proper pushforward all commute with parameter fibers. There is no change of the parameter-dependent étale neighborhood in this argument.

For rank E equal to m at least three, the first projective-bundle relation has codimension at least three. Therefore in codimension two the quotient by `h+a` is exactly the base Chow group, with evaluation `b0+h b1+h^2 b2 -> b0-a b1+a^2 b2`. The source formula follows from the transverse refined restrictions to V and to the strict transform of the principal divisor. This argument remains integral.

## 4. The first-neighborhood obstruction

We independently opened the primary Stacks statements <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FEX> (Lemma 42.58.1) and <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FEZ> (especially Remark 42.59.9). They give the rational Chern-character realization on the regular scheme and its compatibility with refined pullback. The alternative argument through smooth finite-type pointed étale models is also valid, since the cycles, virtual bundles, and maps are finite data and the parameter is fixed and proper.

For a rank-one conormal kernel, the second exterior-power sequence has exactly the displayed kernel `L tensor Omega^1`. Its cohomological boundary is contraction with the first-neighborhood extension class. The local transition-matrix/Atiyah-class calculation in the draft supplies a lift of the degree-two Chern character through the middle term. Consequently every closure class satisfies the required necessary vanishing. No converse deformation criterion or unproved sufficiency of a Hodge condition is used.

The projection of the construction to `P^m × W` shows that the extension class has only a curve-tangent component. The three `delta(z_k G)` classes are the basis of the degree-five Fermat Jacobian quotient. Taking the source basis Serre-dual to them makes the obstruction coefficients precisely the displayed integers, without an unproved coordinate normalization.

## 5. The Hodge projection and boundary corrections

The Euler and normal sequences give the dual descriptions `H^1(Omega_W^1)/C H_W = R4^*` and `H^1(Omega_W^1(1))=R3^*`. Multiplication by a coordinate is dual to `R3 -> R4`. Thus the certificate matrix acts on exactly the claimed quotient; no unmentioned self-dual monomial basis is needed. The hyperplane class is killed by all these twisted multiplication maps.

In the selected target component, contraction can only act on the curve differential. Its source is exactly `H^1(W,Omega_W^1) tensor H^0(C,K_C) tensor H^1(P,O_P)`. Projective-space differential terms cannot enter that component. The injectivity of the 64 by 57 matrix makes the primitive W-component vanish. Pairing with tau then annihilates the remaining hyperplane component.

The correction terms are explicitly controlled. Since the K3 surface has no first cohomology of O and no global one-forms, a varying mixed divisor component on `W × C × P` comes from `C × P`. Multiplication by a adds `H_W`, which pairs to zero with tau. All other divisor terms, and the codimension-zero term, are constant in the parameter. Thus the boundary correction cannot restore a varying Picard component.

The intersection numbers `H_W^2=4`, `H_W D_W=1`, `D_W^2=-2`, `tau H_W=0`, and `tau D_W=-9` are correct.

## 6. Actual families and the conclusion

Every ordinary algebraic-equivalence generator can be compactified to a smooth proper parameter curve by closing its cycle in the fixed product; its specified open fibers do not change. The constructed line bundle on `C × P` has zero mixed Hodge component, so its classifying map to `Pic^0(C)` is constant. Indeed the induced homomorphism from the Jacobian of P has zero map on `H^1(O)`; over C it therefore has zero differential and is the zero homomorphism. This proves vanishing of rho on the source **ordinary** group.

The target classes obtained from `D_W` and a degree-zero divisor on C are actual ordinary algebraic families. Their rho image is exactly `-9` times the input. Divisibility of the complex points of `Pic^0(C)` gives the asserted integral cokernel surjection. The specified transcendental point yields a nontorsion Abel class because all torsion points of this Qbar-defined Jacobian are Qbar-defined and the Abel map is a closed immersion over Qbar. The resulting rational failure of surjectivity follows.

No remaining mathematical gap was found in this typed proof. The distinction between ordinary algebraically trivial cycles and arbitrary Chow classes is essential and is correctly retained.

# Complete independent proof audit: C.3ag

**Outcome: passed, 2026-11-19 at 09:08:47 UTC (tool clock).** File read in full: `research/agents/cycles/dimension_six.tex`. The auxiliary Hodge fragment is independently proved and source-audited in `C3_N6_Hodge_inputs.tex`, `C3_N6_Hodge_source_audit.md`, and `C3_N6_Hodge_references.bib`.

The conclusion is an integral surjection from the cokernel of ordinary CH2_alg restriction, for an excellent normal strictly henselian complex local ring of dimension six with regular source and divisor punctures, onto Pic0 of the Fermat plane quartic. It implies rational ordinary nonsurjectivity. The statement properly distinguishes its Hodge-generic quartic from the integer-coefficient Fermat construction of C.3ae. It asserts no vanishing for the image of every arbitrary Chow class.

## 1. Surface and section choices

The fixed-line quartic family has thirty coefficients (35 monomials of degree4 minus the5 supported on the line). A Hodge-generic complex point is part of the specified data. The separate Hodge lemma proves that its Picard lattice is generated by H,D and that End_Hdg(T)=Q. This is not inferred merely from Picard rank2, and it is not asserted for every complex embedding of generic rational coefficients.

The field K0 generated by the thirty selected coefficients over Qbar is countable, so thirty-six algebraically independent complex section coefficients exist. This guarantees every nonempty Zariski-open condition over K0. The Bertini condition on three sections of the very ample M is nonempty; their reduced transverse common zero scheme has length3·4·4=48.

The second rank condition is also nonempty and defined over K0. The common kernel of the four multiplication maps H1(Ω_W)→H1(Ω_W(1)) is precisely C·H. This follows for every smooth quartic from the Euler/normal sequences, not merely the Fermat monomial presentation: R3^4→R4 is surjective because the quotient is homogeneous. Since τ is primitive and has square−36, some linear form w gives μ_w(τ)≠0. The special triple wz_i makes the required three-column map injective. It is used solely to demonstrate the nonempty rank-open, so its nongeneric base locus is immaterial. The two opens intersect in irreducible affine section space, and the chosen independent tuple lies in both.

## 2. Incidence and local geometry

H⊂P2×S is a P1-bundle away from the48 basepoints and has P2 fibres above them. At each basepoint the ds_i form a cotangent basis, so Σx_i ds_i is nonzero for all projective x. This proves smoothness. The exceptional fibres have codimension2 and cannot supply extra irreducible components, so H is integral.

The previous C.3ae contraction construction applies: regularity near V follows from the smooth Fermat curve equation, not from basepoint freeness of the selected sections. The full Segre coordinate system, not the three selected sections, generates the zero-divisor ideal. Thus the scheme-theoretic exceptional fibre is still V and its first neighbourhood is preserved. The dimension is dim(P2×W×C)+1=6. The strict transform of f=t·ell is the line-bundle total space on smooth H; its intersection with V is transverse. No flatness of H→S is used.

## 3. Integral incidence invariant

Removing p^{-1}(B)×P, of codimension2 in smooth H×P, preserves its Picard group. Removing B×P from S×P also preserves Picard. On the remaining projective bundle the relative degree-one class h splits Pic, giving exactly p*Pic(S×P) plus h·CH0. This is sufficient to control every divisor in the localization ambiguity.

The hypersurface class h+a in P2×S gives p*1=0, p*h=1, p*h2=a, p*h3=0. Expanding (h−2a)(h+a)(γ0+hγ1) and pushing gives −3a2γ1. Its product with τ pushes to zero on C×P: the τH2 term is already zero by dimension on W and the 2τH·K_C term has coefficient degree(τH)=0. Hence the map Φ, and therefore ρ=Φσ, is integrally well defined on the localization quotient.

The weight-(d) relative sheaves vanish below degree (d), and the degree-(d) sheaf is the direct sum of (\Omega^{d-1}_{V/\mathbb Q}\otimes L^j) for (1\leq j<a). KST Theorem A applies to every abstract blow-up square of noetherian schemes. It does not require resolution of singularities or characteristic zero. Its equivalent long exact sequence (1.6) gives the exact three-term segment used in the proof.

Geisser–Hesselholt Theorem A, printed p. 29, explicitly concerns the nonconnective Bass-completed spectrum and every integer degree. ## 1. Statement and geometric scope

For \(V=\mathbf P^m\times C\), \(m\ge2\), and \(L=\mathcal O(1)\boxtimes K_C\), coherent Künneth gives
\[
H^1(V,L)=k^{m+1},\quad H^2(V,L)=0,\quad

On the incidence divisor, the sequence \(0\to\mathcal O_V\to L\to L_H\to0\) gives
\[
H^1(H_0,L_H)=H^1(V,L)/U,\qquad
U=\ell H^1(C,\mathcal O_C),\qquad \dim U=3.

The weight-two projector preserves component restrictions and endpoint classes. The component-map isomorphism identifies its endpoint difference with exactly the desired component point difference.

Moving points off the double boundary and passing a smooth proper curve through two such points generate each component CH0 degree-zero group. Conversely degree is constant for an actual perfect family, using the regular component's Chern character and pushforward to the connected parameter curve. This proves the exact relation-group statement and the Q^c quotient, without any assertion that component Albanese kernels vanish.

In the resolved consequence, the previously fully audited weighted energy identity proves surjectivity of the joint edge degree map even with triple points. For rational edges, Pic(C_e)_Q is exactly its degree coordinate, so this supplies the full ρ hypothesis. The negative weighted component intersection matrix then kills all remaining component degree vectors. ## 1. Parameter curve and interpolation

The zero cases are separated correctly. For a nonzero tuple of degree-zero bundles, a smooth proper curve through the two required points of the product Jacobian supplies one common parameter for all edges. The prescribed-point complete-intersection construction works over every algebraically closed field, including positive characteristic. The normalized Poincare bundles provide actual line bundles and specified trivializations at the zero endpoint.

For each of the finitely many marked evaluations, twisting by a sufficiently large effective divisor away from the two endpoints and using curve cohomology gives a rational section whose divisor avoids both endpoints. Its value at the zero endpoint can be normalized to exactly one in the specified fibre trivialization. This does not require the marked bundle to be trivial or torsion.

After these sections have been chosen, Riemann–Roch permits a rational function with only a pole at the zero endpoint, the prescribed nonzero value at the other endpoint, and zeros at every support point of every chosen divisor. A further prescribed simple zero can be imposed simultaneously. All conditions are finite evaluation or first-jet conditions in one sufficiently large linear system. They impose no characteristic bound.

## 2. The cover, including characteristic two and ramification

For the equation `(g-1)^2 = h g`, an additional simple zero of `h` gives an odd valuation of `h(h+4)` in odd characteristic. In characteristic two, the substitution in VE.4 gives the Artin–Schreier equation `y^2+y=1/h`; its simple pole cannot occur in an Artin–Schreier coboundary. Thus the function-field extension is a separable field extension of degree two in both cases. Normalization gives a smooth connected proper curve and a finite flat map between smooth curves.

The equation and its inverse show that zeros and poles of `g` occur only over the pole of `h`; conversely `g+g^{-1}=h+2` excludes a unit at a point above that pole. The endpoint with value `u` exists. At every point above one of the chosen divisor supports, the residue of `g` is exactly one.

Ramification is allowed and is actually expected at simple zeros of `h`. Pulling back a divisor introduces its ramification multiplicity. In the point pushforward description, this merely raises the residue unit to that multiplicity; the residue unit is one, so the contribution is zero. The argument does not incorrectly require the divisor to avoid the branch locus. The same reasoning handles wild characteristic-two ramification.

## 3. The normalized sheaf class

On each regular surface `C_e × P`, choose local frames extending the given trivialization on the boundary fibres. Near such a fibre the transition units have the form `1+z b'`, while `g=z^m v`. The symbol

`m <z,-b'> + {v,1+z b'}`

has the stated restriction away from the boundary. The minus sign matches Weibel's Dennis–Stein convention. Its pullback to the boundary fibre is zero term by term, including negative `m`.

Regular local Gersten injectivity applies to the sheaf of Quillen `K_2` on these smooth products. It identifies the local extensions on overlaps, proves their cocycle identity, and shows that changing normalized frames changes the resulting cocycle by a coboundary. No assertion about injectivity of a global affine `K_2` group is required. A Cech cocycle maps canonically to sheaf cohomology; no acyclic-cover claim is used.

At the nonzero endpoint the pulled-back cocycle is the ordinary cup of `u` with the line-bundle cocycle, and hence gives `u([L_e]-1)` in the first descent piece of the curve's actual `K_1`.

## 4. Exact marked restriction, rather than its norm

At a marked point, pull back the chosen rational section from the base curve. Its divisor is disjoint from the boundary and its value at every boundary point is one in the prescribed normalization. On the complement of that divisor it can therefore be used as a frame compatible with the boundary trivialization.

Comparison with the original normalized frames introduces symbols whose comparison units are also one at the boundary; the Dennis–Stein formula extends these symbols and gives no boundary point-unit contribution. The remaining local calculations occur where `g` is a unit. The ordinary Gersten divisor formula then gives exactly the finite sum in VE.8, with the pullback multiplicities retained.

Every term in that sum has coefficient the unit one. Consequently the marked restriction vanishes in `H^1(P,K_2)`, and then in `K_1(P)` under the descent bridge. No pushforward or norm is used to infer this vanishing. This is the substantive repair of the earlier variable-unit attempt.

## 5. Global `K_1` and the descent filtration

I freshly read Thomason–Trobaugh's exact spectral-sequence indexing and its complete proof. In their convention

`E_2^{a,b}=H^a(X,K_b) => K_{b-a}(X)`

and `d_r` has bidegree `(r,r-1)`. For a surface, every incoming differential to `(a,b)=(1,2)` has negative first index and every outgoing one has first index at least three. Thus this term survives unchanged and is `F^1_des K_1 / F^2_des K_1`.

Derived pullback of perfect complexes supplies the map of `K`-presheaves. The natural hypercohomology augmentation and Postnikov tower make the comparison with the indicated sheaf-cohomology pullbacks functorial. On a curve the second descent piece vanishes. Therefore any first-piece lift of the constructed sheaf class has precisely the horizontal and vertical restrictions already computed. Choosing the first piece excludes a determinant/unit term.

As an additional concrete verification for these particular Cartier inclusions, the second surface coniveau piece is generated by closed-point `K_1` pushforwards. Pullback to a disjoint curve is zero; when the point lies on the curve, the excess normal-line factor is `1-1=0`. This checks the necessary ambiguity statement without claiming that arbitrary pullback preserves codimension of supports.

The marked edge-family lemma is therefore an actual integral `K_1` construction on fixed proper products. Its proof does not rely on a formal family or an affine-only parameter.

## 6. Whole SNC descent and coherent ambiguity

UK.2 retains the canonical geometric nullhomotopy and the actual two-stage fibre, rather than replacing the diagram by homotopy groups. The characteristic-positive rational closed-union descent input is the one already audited in C.3bq. The two displayed long exact sequences are compatible with endpoint pullback.

The proof of component-surjectivity is valid without any semisimplicity assertion for `pi_0(T)`: an obstruction with Adams eigenvalue four maps to zero on the double curves and hence comes from triple-point `K_1(k)`, where the eigenvalue is two. It must vanish. The weight-two projector on projective `K_0` then produces a lift in `S(E)`.

For a component-kernel class, the stated operation removes the edge unit piece while retaining its boundary. Picard-times-unit generation and the already proved weighted restriction-degree identity reduce the edge data to a finite sum of degree-zero tuples, one constant unit at a time. Subtracting actual component `K_1` images changes no boundary; no full Picard restriction surjectivity is used.

The marked families make every required edge-to-vertex restriction literally zero in `K_1(P)`, so they lift to the actual fibre `T_P`. Their boundaries are actual perfect families, and the rational weight-two projector on `K_0(E × P)` puts their endpoint differences in the defined relation group. The argument can keep the unprojected fibre lifts while comparing edge images, and apply the projector to their boundaries afterwards. Any remaining difference has zero edge image and comes from triple-point `K_2(k)`. The previously audited proper-curve symbol construction and natural double boundary put this complete coherent ambiguity in `J_K(E)`. No unique fibre lift is assumed.

## 7. Exact conclusion and limits

The conclusion is the unconditional inclusion of the whole component-map kernel in `J_K(E)` under the stated negative SNC exceptional-surface hypotheses. Pointwise component-surjectivity is also proved.

The final denominator splitting is exact. ### Record: agents/frobenius/C4_Orlov_method_REVIEW.md

# A restricted Orlov-transform construction does not remove the even-surface denominator

## Status and scope

This note records a proved limitation of one attempted construction. It is not an obstruction to all algebraic cycles on A×Adual, and it does not resolve the remaining type(1,2) surface case. In particular we do not infer that the integral numerical class P²/2 is nonalgebraic.

The construction studied takes exterior products of algebraic K-classes on a fixed polarized abelian surface, applies the standard Orlov equivalence, and then forms integral sums, differences and tensor products before taking second Chern classes. The calculation below shows that when the polarization degree e is even, all resulting second Chern classes have an even coefficient in the P²/2 direction of the rational divisor-generated degree-four subspace.

## Primary source and exact normalization

We opened Markman's manuscript *Secant sheaves on abelian n-folds with real multiplication and Weil classes on abelian 2n-folds with complex multiplication*, arXiv:2509.23079v1, at https://arxiv.org/html/2509.23079v1 . Section10.1, equation(10.1.3) and the following sentence define the equivalence Φ as the inverse of μ_* composed with the Fourier–Mukai transform on the second factor, where μ(x,z)=(x+z,z). This is the normalization used here.

The same manuscript uses normalized characteristic classes κ(E)=ch(E)exp(−c1(E)/rank(E)) for deformation arguments. These are rational classes. The present fixed-surface integral calculation does not test all those deformed constructions, nor does a rational algebraicity conclusion by itself establish the needed integral class.

## Exact calculation

Let A have Néron–Severi group generated by a polarization θ of type(1,e). Its integral algebraic even Mukai lattice has basis 1,θ,pt, with θ²=2e·pt. Write

\[
 v=r+d\theta+s\,\mathrm{pt},\qquad
 w=r'+d'\theta+s'\,\mathrm{pt},
\]

with integral coefficients. All such basis classes are represented by virtual algebraic K-classes: θ=ch(L)−1−e·pt. Todd classes are trivial on abelian varieties.

With x the first A-coordinate, z the integrated A-coordinate and y the dual coordinate, Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch gives

\[
 \operatorname{ch}\Phi(v\boxtimes w)
   =\int_{z\in A}v(x+z)\,w(z)\,\exp(-P(z,y)).
\]

In dimension two the inverse Fourier transform has this sign; replacing y by −y only reverses the sign of P and leaves the parity conclusion unchanged.

Put D=pr_A^*θ and Dhat=pr_Adual^*θdual. We resolve degree-four classes in the linearly independent rational basis

\[
 D^2/2,\quad DP,\quad DDhat,\quad P^2/2,\quad PDhat,\quad Dhat^2/2.
\]

The symbolic exterior-algebra calculation gives

\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{rank}\Phi(v\boxtimes w)
   &=rs'+sr'+2edd',\\
 b:=\operatorname{coeff}_{P}(c_1\Phi(v\boxtimes w))
   &=sr'+edd',\\
 q:=\operatorname{coeff}_{P^2/2}
        (\operatorname{ch}_2\Phi(v\boxtimes w))
   &=sr'.
 \end{aligned}
\]

These identities follow by bilinearity from the nine basis calculations recorded in the output file. Since

\[
 c_2(E)=c_1(E)^2/2-\operatorname{ch}_2(E),
\]

the coefficient of P²/2 in c2 is b²−q. For even e we have q≡b modulo2, so b²−q is even.

This congruence persists under integral sums and differences of the K-classes, since both b and q are additive. It also persists under tensor products: if E and F have ranks r_E,r_F, then

\[
 \begin{aligned}
 b(EF)&=r_Eb(F)+r_Fb(E),\\
 q(EF)&=r_Eq(F)+r_Fq(E)+2b(E)b(F).
 \end{aligned}
\]

The other products of degree-two basis vectors do not contribute to the P²/2 coordinate. Thus q≡b modulo2 remains true throughout this ring of constructed classes. Products of two integral divisors likewise have even P²/2 coefficient.

Consequently the integral span of these particular second Chern classes and divisor products cannot contain a class with odd P²/2 coefficient, and in particular cannot produce P²/2 itself.

## What has not been shown

There is no claim that the full algebraic K-group of A×Adual is generated integrally by the transformed exterior products. A derived-category generation statement with idempotent completion would not establish the required generation of K-classes without further argument. Nor is there a claim about arbitrary surfaces, arbitrary sheaves on the product, cycles obtained after varying the surface, or all characteristic classes arising from Markman's deformation methods.

The exact residual question therefore remains the integral numerical algebraicity of P²/2 from C.4r. This calculation explains why this fixed-A method does not settle it.

## Reproduction

- Script: research/agents/frobenius/code/orlov_surface_parity.py.
- Complete symbolic output: research/agents/frobenius/code/orlov_surface_parity.out.
- The script implements the exterior product directly, integrates the four z generators, solves for the displayed basis coordinates, and checks the polynomial parity after substituting e=2d.
- No floating-point arithmetic or sampled value of e is used.

The full table, rather than only the parity assertions, is retained in the output for independent inspection.

to the current version.

If \(X_{2i-1}\) is a smooth Cartier divisor in a smooth Tate-motive
\(R_{2i}\), then \(X_{2i-1}\times\{0\}\) is the regular zero scheme of the
two-component section of
\(\operatorname{pr}_1^*O(X_{2i-1})\oplus\operatorname{pr}_2^*O(1)\) on
\(R_{2i}\times P^1\). The incidence equation in the projective bundle of
lines is exactly the Rees-algebra presentation of its blow-up. Thus the
new blow-up is a smooth Cartier divisor in a Tate-motive ambient variety
of one higher dimension. There is no unsupported small-codimension
embedding claim.

For the codimension-two centre, the blow-up formula and its displayed
forward/inverse maps are correctly typed. The exceptional self-intersection
has the required minus sign; its pushforward is the identity on the
centre. These algebraic correspondences preserve algebraic equivalence.
The unique Griffiths summand therefore moves from degree \(i\) to
\(i+1\), while the ambient part stays finite dimensional. Multiplication
by projective space gives the claimed string of Griffiths groups in
degrees \(i+1,\ldots,n-i\). The source in degree \(i\) remains finite
dimensional and the target in degree \(n-i\) infinite dimensional.
This validates all \(1\le i<n/2\).

## 2. New C.4 deliverables and proved results

C4_additions.tex contains C.4h–l and an unnumbered remaining-work paragraph.
C4_references.bib adds only the two
new keys; the other keys already occur in the cycles bibliography.

1. Scalar factorizations through finite products of Jacobians form
   an ideal \(I_J(A)=s_J(A)\mathbb Z\). Its generator is one exactly when
   \(A\) is an actual direct summand. Duality preserves it and products
   take the least common multiple.
2. In every characteristic, \(s_J(A)\mid(2g-1)!\). This follows from the
   explicit integer composite in Scavia–Suzuki Proposition 3.4,
   applied to the Poincaré line bundle on \(A\times\widehat A\).
   No unproved integral Hodge conjecture is used.
3. For \(g\le3\), \(s_J(A)\) also divides
   \(\delta(A)=\gcd_{L\in\mathrm{Pic}(A)}\chi(L)\). Mumford's group-scheme
   principalization has degree \(\chi(L)\), and Oort–Ueno identifies the
   principally polarized quotient with a product of Jacobians.
4. Consequently
   \(s_J(A)\mid\gcd((2g-1)!,\delta(A))\).
   Different polarizations may be used at different primes. A finite
   Bézout combination of the resulting maps gives one exact retraction.
5. Surface case: the sufficient local checks are at 2 and 3. Threefold
   case: 2, 3, and 5. The check at the characteristic is retained for
   characteristic 2 or 3. We use group-scheme kernels throughout.
6. A surface with NS rank one and primitive type \((1,d)\) is settled
   whenever \(\gcd(d,6)=1\). For a complex threefold with primitive type
   \((1,d_2,d_3)\), the sufficient test is

7. For NS-rank-one complex surfaces with End equal to \(\mathbb Z\),

The strongest isogeny formulation retains kernel exponents: if
\(A\to B\) has kernel killed by \(e\), then
\(eI_J(B)\subset I_J(A)\) and conversely. For a separable polarization
of type \((d_1,\ldots,d_g)\), one may use \(e=d_g\). Inseparable cases
use the actual kernel group scheme, or the always valid degree bound.

## 3. What remains unproved

### Priority and targeted-search record

No priority or novelty claim is made for the factorial bound, the
scalar-factorization ideal, or the polarization gcd criterion. These are
elementary quantitative deductions from the opened Matsusaka formula,
principalization, and the low-dimensional Jacobian theorem. Searches for
the exact direct-summand formulation and its nonprincipal surface and
threefold variants found Beckmann–de Gaay Fortman, Voisin, and
Scavia–Suzuki; their exact theorems are identified above. The search
neither established that these elementary deductions are new nor
established a published resolution of every residual small-prime case.
Accordingly we record them as proved deductions and reserve every
priority judgment.

We have not shown that every nonprincipally polarizable surface or
threefold has \(s_J=1\), nor produced one with \(s_J>1\). In particular,
the computations do not settle generic type \((1,2)\) or \((1,3)\)
surfaces.

The following proposed shortcuts were checked and do not close the gap:

- Integral Hodge for curves on \(A\) alone: the converse to the
  direct-summand condition in the opened theorems requires a unimodular
  line bundle. Without one, the criterion is on \(A\times\widehat A\).
- All rational Hodge classes are generated by divisors: rational
  generation does not imply integral generation; the explicit
  divisor-product lattice has the residual index above.
- Choosing many principalizations: if \(\ell\mid\delta(A)\), no
  prime-to-\(\ell\) isogeny from \(A\) to a principally polarized
  variety of the same dimension exists. Pulling back the principal
  polarization would contradict the definition of \(\delta(A)\).
  Thus merely varying these quotients cannot remove that prime.
- Zarhin's trick: the principalizable product has dimension \(8g\),
  so the dimension-three Jacobian theorem no longer applies.
- Engel–de Gaay Fortman–Schreieder 2026: the opened theorem concerns a
  very general ppav of dimension at least four. Its hypotheses do not
  automatically include the restricted family \(A\times\widehat A\).
  A separate degeneration argument is necessary.
- Rational Tate results for abelian varieties over finite fields do
  not themselves supply integral all-prime curve classes or eliminate
  the characteristic-prime condition in Scavia–Suzuki.

These statements distinguish a proof gap in this contribution from a
claim that the cases are known to be open in the literature. Further
non-divisorial degeneration or geometric constructions remain under
investigation at the parent's request.

# Independent proof audit: partial Fourier correspondence test

19 November 2026. GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), ChatGPT Pro mode; run /root/frobenius; effort setting not exposed.

Verdict: the complete typed mathematical proof in research/agents/cycles/partial_fourier_correspondence.tex passes. This is a reformulation and construction exclusion, not a solution of the residual type-(1,2) splitting problem. This audit reuses the previously checked Fourier–Mukai and Poincare normalizations. It does not claim a fresh opening of the owner’s Mukai, Yoshioka, BPS or Kahn sources or a rerun of the retained exterior-algebra certificate.

The scalar action of an integral correspondence on H1, T and NS is integral under the explicitly retained Hodge-endomorphism hypotheses. The integral unimodular H2 lattice and primitive polarization of square4 give 4|(n−s) by applying the operator to a class pairing1 with the polarization. The displayed decomposition of the (2,2) Kunneth component follows from the same orthogonal decomposition; there are no rational Hodge maps between the transcendental part and the polarization line.

The class obtained by pushing the structure sheaves of resolutions of cycle components lies in integral K0, has Chern characters zero in degrees0/1 and the prescribed cycle in degree2. Partial Fourier–Mukai pushforward preserves integral K0 even when the transform is virtual. Bidegrees show that c1 has the form a ell1+tP, with no ell2 term. The (2,2) part of c2 is exactly (t²−s)P²/2+(n−s)ell1ell2/4. Terms of other bidegrees cannot contribute to the (3,3) mixed homomorphism component after multiplication by P.

The normalization P³=−3 ell1ell2P and mixed action of P³/6 equal to the identity give the exact integer 3(t²−s)−(n−s)/2. Its parity is t−s. An odd such integer combines with the already proved factorization of2 to give a splitting through a product of Jacobians.

The converse uses actual integral Poincare divisors on A×C and their pushforwards. The cohomological H1 action is the desired sum of Jacobian composites; the H2 transcendental action vanishes because it factors through the curve’s Tate group. With the normalized mixed Poincare divisor, its entire H2 action in fact vanishes, though the weaker asserted conclusion suffices. No isogeny inverse or rational saturation is used.

For the residual fibre-product surface, the trace correspondence is gamma* gamma_*−id. The rational target has H1 zero and H2 algebraic; hence the residual action is −1 on both H1 and T, and the odd-parity test fails. This does not extend to arbitrary non-semihomogeneous Fourier transforms or to every integral codimension-two cycle on A². The limitation is stated correctly.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C4_prym_REVIEW.md

# Prym improvement and supplementary independent audits

## 1. Exact new result and limits

The new fragment `C4_prym_addition.tex` proves two numbered statements.

- **C.4m:** Every principally polarized abelian variety of positive
  dimension at most five over an algebraically closed field has
  multiplication by two factoring through a product of Jacobians.
  Characteristic two is included by polarized lifting and specialization
  of an actual integral curve cycle.
- **C.4n:** Every abelian surface satisfies
  `s_J(A) | gcd(2, delta(A))`. Thus an ample line bundle of odd Euler
  characteristic suffices for the exact direct-summand property.
  For Picard rank one and type `(1,d)`, every odd `d` is settled.

This improves the earlier surface bound six to two. In particular,
type `(1,3)` is positive despite the divisor-product index three
computed in C.4l. We have **not** proved the result for every surface
with even delta, and have not found a surface counterexample.
The general threefold bound remains `gcd(120, delta(A))` in this work.
Its possible residual primes are still 2, 3, and 5. We do not claim
that every unhandled case is known to be open in the literature.

## 2. Proof and exact coefficient checks

Beauville's generalized Prym includes a map into the generalized
Jacobian of a nodal curve. Composing with normalization gives a map
`j : B -> product J(C_i)` into an actual product of Jacobians of
smooth curves. Proposition 2.2 identifies the generalized theta as
the pullback of the product theta. Theorem 5.4 gives
`j^* theta_J = 2 Xi` in the Néron–Severi group. Since both
polarizations are principal, the polarized adjoint is an integral
homomorphism and `j^dagger j = [2]` exactly. No finite kernel is
inverted, and no principal polarization on a nonprincipal variety
is silently assumed.

The sum of the images of the normalization curves under `j^dagger`
has cohomology class twice the minimal class. This follows directly
from the associated alternating pairing, or equivalently from
`q lambda_J^-1 qhat = 2 lambda_B^-1`. The proof in the fragment
explains why that pairing determines the full curve cohomology class.

At characteristic two, Oort's valid lifting implication and
Corollary 2.4.2 provide a polarized lift over W(k). A finite base
extension defines the generic integral cycle. Its closures give
an integral special cycle. Fulton's Example 20.3.5 expressly supplies
the commutative diagram with the ell-adic cycle class map for
ell different from two. Numerical equality follows, and Matsusaka
then supplies actual homomorphisms whose composite is `[2]` over k.
No crystalline equivalence or rationally defined retraction is used.

For any fourfold or fivefold X, principalizing ample L and using
the preceding theorem gives `2 chi(L) in I_J(X)`. The ample gcd
lemma gives `s_J(X) | 2 delta(X)`. For the fourfold `A x Adual`,
the Poincaré bundle has Euler characteristic one, hence delta one.
Restriction and projection yield `[2]` on A. The earlier
same-dimensional principalization supplies `[delta(A)]`, and
Bézout gives the final odd-delta criterion.

The fragment includes a finite five-polarization interpolation
formula realizing the gcd construction. It also gives a concrete
alternative: `P tensor H^(72t)` has Euler characteristic congruent
to one modulo three, so a single such principalization and the
existing factorization of six yield a factorization of two.

## 3. Independent review

The cycles agent independently opened Beauville and Oort and checked
both the normalization map and the characteristic-two specialization
argument. Its conclusion was that the proof is sound, including the
finite-kernel issue and use of rational ell-adic equality only to
deduce numerical equality of an already integral cycle.

The script `code/verify_c4_prym_arithmetic.py` checks exact integers
in the finite interpolation formula on a polynomial basis and the
coefficient congruences for the one-polarization construction. This
is an arithmetic certificate only; the geometric existence theorem
comes from the proved construction and the cited primary results.

## 5. Other independent audits requested by the parent

### A.1h descent across the finite quadratic field

The parent's determinant descent argument is correct under its
nonemptiness hypothesis: the isomorphism sets before and after
base change to the algebraic closure are torsors under the same
group `Z_p^*`. An equivariant map between nonempty torsors for this
same group is bijective. Naturality under the two field embeddings
then makes the descended determinant rigidification independent of
the choice of embedding. This avoids a finite-field geometric-model
claim. The two `F^2=+p` and `F^2=-p` strata cannot be linked by a
nonzero F-intertwiner: its square relation gives `2p b=0` in a
torsion-free lattice, including at p=2. Thus without compatibility
with geometric base change the strata can carry independent
constants; imposing that compatibility identifies the constants.

### C.2 pencil induction

The lexicographic induction proposed by the parent is sound with
global A-prime available over all algebraically closed extensions,
including the algebraic closure of k(t). The smooth pencil centre
has codimension two. For the exceptional contribution, the fibre
class restricts to `O_{P^1}(1)` on `E=B x P^1`, so the coefficient
of `i_B* beta` is positive one. Weak Lefschetz gives the required
preimage `b0` since `2i-2 < n-2`. The lower-codimension induction
and hard Lefschetz prove its algebraicity from the algebraic class
`L^(k+2) b0`. Finite trace with rational coefficients handles the
generic-fibre descent. No nodal Lefschetz-pencil hypothesis is needed.

### C.2 reduction to critical dimension

The parent's incidence construction is also correct. For
`d=2r+1-n >= 0`, the variety `T=X x P^d` has the critical dimension
`2r+1`. The incidence divisor defined by `sum s_j t_j=0` is smooth
when the common zero locus is a smooth complete intersection:
outside it a fibre derivative is nonzero; on it independence of
the differentials `ds_j` gives a nonzero derivative for every
projective coordinate vector. For d=0 this is just the initial
critical case. On `U=X\Y`, the section s0 trivializes the line
bundle and a triangular projective coordinate change sends the
incidence divisor to the standard hyperplane. Its Gysin image in
the Chow projective-bundle decomposition is exactly divisible by h.
Thus the constant coefficient restricts to zero in CH(U), and
localization puts it in the image of CH(Y). The cohomological
projective-bundle decomposition identifies its class with the
original z. This requires the given hyperplane Y to come from the
very ample embedding in the statement; no extra singular-pencil
assumption enters.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C4_pt6_REVIEW.md

# Threefold improvement via Prym–Tyurin sixfolds

## Result

`C4_pt6_addition.tex` proves C.4o and C.4p. Every principally
polarized sixfold over any algebraically closed field has an integral
curve of class six times the minimal class, so `[6]` factors through
a product of Jacobians. It follows that every abelian threefold
satisfies

\[
 s_J(A)\mid\gcd(6,\delta(A)).
\]

Together with C.4n, the strongest current bounds are two for surfaces
and six for threefolds. The residual primes in this contribution
are respectively `{2}` and `{2,3}`. Thus rank-one surface type
`(1,3)` and threefold type `(1,1,5)` are affirmative. No general
resolution or counterexample is claimed for the residual cases.

## Primary theorem and field-transfer check

The published ADFIO2020 PDF contains **Theorem 1** and **Corollary 2**
on p.165. The latter explicitly states the effective curve assertion
for every complex principally polarized sixfold. The older preprint
numbers the main theorem 0.1, so that number must not be attached to
the published pagination. The exponent-six theta-restriction
identity is on p.164.

To pass from C to an arbitrary algebraically closed field of
characteristic zero, one must preserve more than an arbitrary
factorization of `[6]`: the curve class is needed for the next
specialization. We therefore spread the curves, their pointed maps,
and the exact identity

\[
\sum_a m_a f_a\lambda_{J(C_a)}^{-1}\widehat f_a\lambda_B=[6].
\]

These data spread to a nonempty finite-type scheme over the finitely
generated field of definition of `(B,Xi)`. A closed point has a
finite residue extension and can be embedded into the target
algebraically closed field. The same adjoint identity then holds.
The pairing calculation identifies the resulting curve class with
`6 gamma_Xi`; no argument based only on the existence of an
unpolarized retraction is used.

In characteristic p we use the polarized Witt lift already audited
in C.4m. Fulton's geometric specialization and compatibility with
cycle classes yield an actual integral special cycle. Rational
ell-adic equality for one ell different from p suffices for the
numerical equality used by Matsusaka. Neither p=2 nor p=3 is
excluded: the scalar six is never inverted.

For a sixfold X, principalizing every ample L gives
`6 chi(L) in I_J(X)`, hence `s_J(X)|6 delta(X)`. The Poincaré
bundle on `A x Adual` has Euler characteristic minus one, so delta
is one. Restriction to A and the earlier `delta(A)` factorization
complete the proof. The fragment gives a seven-polarization
integer interpolation formula, so the gcd construction is finite.

## Integration

Input the new fragment after `C4_prym_addition.tex`. Add
`C4_pt6_references.bib`, `C4_pt6_results.csv`, and
`C4_pt6_CHECK_EVENTS.tsv` to the corresponding master aggregations.

The final unnumbered scope paragraph in `C4_pt6_addition.tex`
supersedes the two older remaining-work paragraphs in
`C4_additions.tex` and `C4_prym_addition.tex`. For a clean narrative,
retain only the latest one. The earlier bounds 6/120 and their
tables are valid intermediate results, but they are no longer the
strongest bounds in the report.

the upper-bound proof is based on the opened ADFIO primary article.
The companion EGFS2025 paper is used only to explain the scope of
generic sharpness. No very-general ppav theorem is applied to the
special family `A x Adual`.

## Why the requested matroidal obstruction does not directly apply

This is a proved limitation of that direct approach, not a claimed
obstruction to solving the residual cases by other degenerations.

Suppose a complex family `X=A x Adual` has unipotent monodromy around
a loop, and let N be its logarithm on `H1(A,Q)`. On the dual family
the logarithm is minus the transpose. Consequently

\[
 N_X=N\oplus(-N^{\mathsf t}),\qquad
 \operatorname{rank}N_X=2\operatorname{rank}N.
\]

Thus every nonzero such monodromy operator has even rank. Passing
to an isogenous abelian scheme conjugates rational monodromy;
finite ramified base change replaces N by a positive integer
multiple, which also preserves its rank.

In EGFS2026, Definition4.1(3), the monodromy form for each coordinate
divisor is a positive multiple of `y_s^2`, of rank one for a nonloop
of the matroid. Definition2.12 identifies that form with N through
the principal polarization, so its rank is the rank of N.
Hence a nontrivial isotypic family obtained in this way cannot
directly satisfy the stated matroidal-family condition. This
explains a concrete missing hypothesis in the proposed application
to `A x Adual`; an adaptation to rank-two monodromies would need
new work.

Opened locators: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.15704v3,
Definition2.12 (`turn596713770view0`), Definition4.1 and Remark4.2
(`turn950968762view1`), and Theorem1.6
(`turn199065391view3`). This rank calculation does not exclude a
different family or a different geometric obstruction, and does
not by itself imply that the residual cases are known open.

## Remaining search status

The principalization method has reached its precise local limit:
if ell divides delta(A), every same-dimensional principalization
has degree divisible by ell. The new generalized-Prym and
Prym–Tyurin constructions overcome some of those denominators
using `A x Adual`, but leave the primes recorded above. Searches
and checks in this contribution have not found an exact all-case
theorem or counterexample for nonprincipal surfaces or threefolds.
No novelty or priority claim is attached to the new deductions.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C4_residual_REVIEW.md

# Residual-prime research: exact lower-dimensional subvariety gate

## Status and deliverables

`C4_residual_gate.tex` proves C.4q. It does not resolve the remaining all-case surface or threefold direct-summand question. The all-characteristic upper bounds remain

\[
s_J(A)\mid\gcd(2,\delta(A))\quad(g=2),\qquad
s_J(A)\mid\gcd(6,\delta(A))\quad(g=3).
\]

The new result identifies the entire lattice generated by a natural further source of curves, beyond divisor products. For a simple complex A with End(A)=Z and primitive rank-one NS type (1,d2,...,e), curves supported in translates of proper abelian subvarieties of X=A×Â have Fourier images exactly

\[
\mathbb ZD\oplus\kappa(e)\mathbb ZP\oplus\mathbb Z\widehat D,
\qquad \kappa(e)=\prod_{\ell\mid e}\ell^{\lceil v_\ell(e)/2\rceil}.
\]

Thus that construction cannot produce the primitive Poincare curve class whenever e>1. For type (1,3) surfaces, for instance, this subgroup retains a factor three even though the generalized-Prym argument already proves actual splitting. This is a concrete distinction between a limitation of this subgroup and a true obstruction to all algebraic curves.

The proof is valid for both g=2 and g=3 over C. We do not claim the identical integral Fourier/divisor lattice assertion in positive characteristic, especially at the characteristic prime. This restriction does not weaken the earlier all-characteristic upper bounds.

## Independent verification

On 2026-11-19 `/root/cycles` independently read the fragment and confirmed all steps: dimensions of proper abelian subvarieties, the scalar determinant eac−b², the resulting valuations, positive semidefiniteness of the constructed divisor, integral descent to a quotient at the NS-class level, and realization of its inverse Fourier class by integral curves in dimension at most three. The reviewer specifically confirmed that no Pic0 rigidification is required for the NS-class descent. No gap was found.

Grabowski's thesis is an image scan, so the primary theorem was visually inspected rather than trusting OCR alone.

## Nearby theorems and their exact limitations

Grabowski's Corollary3.1.9 proves IHC for curves on every complex abelian threefold, including nonprincipally polarized ones. Proposition3.1.8 explains the mechanism: express integral divisor classes by differences of ample classes, principalize each ample class, and push the Fourier images of principal theta classes from the dual principalized varieties. The output is a curve class on the dual threefold. It is not a theorem about all curve classes on the sixfold A×Â.

Totaro's Theorem7.1 proves the integral Tate theorem for abelian threefolds over the separable closure of a finitely generated field. Its Section1 formulation uses primes invertible in that field; no crystalline-at-p assertion follows merely from that theorem. Proposition7.2 is the Fourier-and-principalization analogue of Grabowski's reduction. It likewise does not address the needed class on A×Â.

The new proof uses the full strength of the dimension-three theorem for the proper abelian subvarieties of X. Even after allowing every integral curve class on all those subvarieties, the off-diagonal coefficient remains divisible by kappa(e). Thus the missing curves would have to include at least one component whose smallest containing translated abelian subvariety is all of X.
