\qquad m\ge0,
\]

where the $W_i$ are smooth cubic surfaces, the conormal is the external product of their hyperplane bundles with $\mathcal O(1)$ and $K_C$, and the actual projection to the projective/cubic factors survives on the resolution. A nil line bundle times one divisor from each cubic is nonzero on the puncture whenever its designated relative Milnor differential cup is nonzero. The proof removes **the entire exceptional image**, retaining all torsion in the curve Picard group and all Smith invariant factors.

The lemma alone does not construct an ordinary family or a principal cut with zero target endpoint. The separately audited combined C.3bl, owned by real_weil, supplies those geometric conditions. We do not infer a rational kernel from these exact-order-(p) constructions.

## Complete proof architecture

1. The relative ordinary Milnor sheaf has exponent (p), a canonical quotient to the rank-one conormal differential module, and the exact actual-line-product formula, including characteristic two. Rost localization proves the needed preceding Milnor cohomology groups divisible, so relative classes reducing to zero have unique lifts.
2. The integral cellular Chow decomposition retains the entire curve Picard group. An elementary positive-adjoint calculation proves (b^2) injective on the required rational free lattice for all (m\ge0), including its weight-zero endpoint. This removes every free/numerical part of the exceptional kernel. Smith form then writes its entirety as (\sum v_jQ_j), with (b v_j=d_jw_j) and (d_jQ_j=0) in (\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)).
3. The designated coherent cup factors through the **free integral** quotient

   \[
   \bigotimes_i\bigl(\operatorname{Pic}(W_i)/\mathbb Z A_i\bigr).
   \]

   Each (A_i) is primitive because it pairs to one with a line. The selected multidegree of a (b)-multiple inserts an (A_i), so this quotient kills the entire (b)-image and its saturation. Euler cohomology gives (\mu_{A_i}=0), proving the factorization in every characteristic. No Smith denominator or factorial is inverted.
4. The canonical actual extension (\widetilde K=\mathcal O(-V)\otimes q^*L_T^{-1}) replaces a nonexistent projection to the curve. Every curve line bundle lifts by the finite-obstruction/formal-existence/approximation argument. The unique relative degree-two class of (\widetilde K\widetilde Q) has a differential independent of the chosen lift: changing it gives a cup with two degree-one curve cohomology factors, hence zero. It is an additive map from the divisible group (\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)(k)) to a (p)-killed coherent group, hence vanishes.
5. The actual Chow projection formula expresses every possible boundary as the sum of the saturated terms from step 3 and the curve terms from step 4. Finite pointed-etale descent permits the integral Milnor–Bloch ring comparison on a smooth finite-type model. Its restriction to the fixed first jet, and uniqueness of relative lifts, give the contradiction. No Bloch formula on a nonreduced scheme is used.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C3_smooth_exceptional_REPORT.md

# C.3az: smooth exceptional divisor in positive characteristic

## Status and exact scope

The final complete proof is in `C3_smooth_exceptional_top.tex`. Root and real_weil independently read the complete proof and exact primary inputs and passed it; real_weil completed at 11:38:43.203963 UTC, and both receipts were present at the 11:39:52 UTC tool-clock reading. The canonical result row is now registered. The hypotheses are an algebraizable strictly henselian normal local ring of characteristic p, a regular projective modification that is an isomorphism on the puncture, a single smooth connected exceptional Cartier divisor E, and ample conormal L. The result applies in every positive characteristic and every dimension d+1 >= 2. No cone retraction is assumed.

The conclusion is stronger than the ordinary-quotient vanishing alone: refined restriction gives CH^d(Z)_Q ≅ CH_0(E)_Q; Chow localization then gives CH^d(X)_Q ≅ CH_0(E)_Q/(c1(L) CH_1(E)_Q). The ordinary quotient on Z is Q by restricted degree, and that on the puncture X vanishes.

## New step, with the uniform exponent made explicit

The previously audited KST/GH argument supplies injectivity, without any retraction. The new argument constructs actual families. Through any two points of E, successive ample sections cut a smooth projective curve C, and lifted sections cut a regular projective surface W. Properness over a local base forces global regularity once regularity is known along the closed fibre.

For every proper smooth parameter curve P and line bundle F on C×P, the obstruction at the nth infinitesimal step is H²(C×P,L_C^n⊠O_P) = H¹(C,L_C^n)⊗H¹(P,O_P). Choose n0 so that the first factor vanishes for every n>=n0. The finitely many earlier additive obstructions are killed by taking pth tensor powers; after at most n0−1 such operations, the same exponent p^e works over the entire parameter curve and for all later infinitesimal levels. This does not use an unbounded sequence of p-powers.

The ideals defining C and the closed fibre are cofinal. Projective formal existence algebraizes the compatible family over the completed base. Popescu descends that actual line bundle to a smooth algebra over R; henselian smooth lifting supplies a map back to R with the same residue point. Hence the result is a line bundle on the actual fixed product W×P, with precisely F^(p^e) on C×P.

Take P=C and the normalized diagonal line bundle. Proper pushforward of its two fibre Chern classes supplies an ordinary algebraic relation on Z restricting to p^e([x]−[o]). After rationalization every degree-zero class lifts. An exceptional curve has restriction −c1(L)[D] of nonzero degree, which supplies the remaining degree, proves the top Chow isomorphism, and kills the open ordinary quotient.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C3_surface_reduction_Fpbar_REPORT.md

# C.3be — arbitrary excellent local domains with residue Fpbar

## Certified conclusion and exact scope

**Proved.** Let R be an excellent local domain of dimension N at least two with residue field isomorphic to the algebraic closure of Fp. Then CH_1(Spec R) with rational coefficients is zero. The puncture, equipped with the inherited dimension function delta(p)=dim(R/p), consequently has CH^(N−1) with rational coefficients zero.

The ambient domain need not be normal or henselian. Its puncture need not be regular. No coefficient field, equal-characteristic hypothesis, algebraization over a field, or resolution in dimension greater than two is used. In particular the assertion includes mixed-characteristic domains. Ordinary B is a quotient and vanishes wherever that quotient has been defined; the text does not impose a product-family definition over a nonexistent coefficient field on a mixed-characteristic ring.

This is a residue-field-specific positive result. It does not close the unrestricted rational top-quotient question over arbitrary algebraically closed fields, and it is not counted as resetting the scheduled main-gate movement clock. No integral vanishing, finite torsion group, or common annihilating exponent is asserted.

Final proof: C3_surface_reduction_Fpbar.tex. The previous draft file is now a pointer to the final file.

## Complete proof structure

1. **Surface geometry with all required properties at once.** An excellent normal local surface is regular outside its closed point. Stacks/Lipman 54.14.5 and the normalized-point construction 54.6.5 resolve it by normalized closed-point blowups over that point. Excellence makes each normalization finite. A further sequence of point blowups from 54.15.6 makes the whole reduced closed fibre SNC. These constructions preserve the puncture. Starting with the closed-point blowup also covers an already regular surface.

   The exceptional divisor of an ordinary blowup is effective Cartier, with its negative tautological bundle relatively ample. Finite dominant normalization preserves effectivity, the Cartier property, and relative ampleness. A sufficiently weighted sum of the preceding total transform and the next exceptional divisor is negative ample for the composite. The first divisor's total transform retains the whole closed-fibre support. This simultaneously gives a projective regular model, preserved puncture, SNC fibre E, and D=sum a_i E_i with all a_i positive and −D relatively ample. It does not use the invalid conjunction of separate resolution and projectivization existence assertions identified in the earlier C.3bd audit.

2. **One finite K0 detecting level.** KST Theorem A and (1.6) give the exact pro sequence for the closed point and the resolution. Since K0 of the local ring and of all its Artinian quotients is Z, quotienting by the diagonal graph makes the restriction from the constant K0(Z) a monomorphism of pro-groups. Its level kernels form a descending system of subgroup inclusions. Pro-zero therefore forces an actual zero kernel at one finite level.

   At every infinitesimal closed fibre E_b, p^b=0, even in mixed characteristic. The reduction E inside E_b is nilpotent. GH Theorem A applies to rings in which p is nilpotent, not only to Fp-algebras. Finite affine-cover K-theory descent gives K0(E_b)_Q=K0(E)_Q. Hence K0(Z)_Q injects into K0(E)_Q. No nilpotence assumption on the ambient ring or on Z enters.

3. **Determinant, with the order of operations explicit.** A multidegree-zero line bundle on the SNC curve E is torsion: component Jacobian points descend to finite fields, and the remaining node-gluing scalars lie in the torsion group k*. For a line bundle L on Z, first choose M with L^M|E actually trivial. K0 injectivity makes [L^M]−[O_Z] a torsion K0 class. Projectivity over an affine base supplies the resolution property, so vector-bundle K0 equals perfect K0 and the vector-bundle determinant is available. Applying it to an integer annihilating this K0 class makes L torsion. Thus Pic(Z)_Q injects into the multidegree space Q^c.

4. **An explicit intersection argument.** The exceptional degree matrix M is symmetric with nonnegative off-diagonal entries, and Ma has strictly negative coordinates. For Q=diag(a)Mdiag(a) and b_i its row sums,
   x^tQx=sum b_i x_i^2−sum_(i<j) Q_ij(x_i−x_j)^2.
   This proves negative definiteness and invertibility. The exceptional line bundles span all multidegrees and therefore Pic(Z)_Q. Cartier-divisor closure on regular Z makes Pic(Z)→Pic(U) surjective, while those exceptional bundles restrict trivially. This proves Pic(U)_Q=CH_1(Spec B)_Q=0 for the normal local surface.

5. **Every curve comes from a surface, without henselianity.** Catenarity puts a curve prime p in a two-dimensional prime quotient B=R/q. Its finite normalization T is a normal integral semilocal ring; every maximal residue field is still Fpbar. Each maximal localization has dimension at most two. In dimension two, Steps 1–4 give torsion of its class group, with no henselian hypothesis; in lower dimensions it is a field or DVR. For any fixed Weil divisor on T, a common positive multiple is therefore Cartier at every maximal ideal, hence Cartier everywhere by the rank-one reflexive-sheaf description. Every invertible module over a semilocal ring is free. This common multiple is thus principal and Cl(T)_Q=0. The finite pullback of the dimension function has generic value two, so Cl(T)=CH_1(T). A prime above p/q is a height-one prime, and finite pushforward sends its class to a positive finite residue-degree multiple of [V(p)]. The surface result therefore kills every generator of CH_1(Spec R)_Q. Localization at the omitted closed point loses no dimension-one cycle. No assertion about equality of all maximal heights in T is needed.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C4_genus5_integral_lattice_REPORT.md

# Genus-five Prym construction: the complete integral Hom obstruction

**Status:** proved conditional construction exclusion, not a counterexample to Question2. This report is reconstructed after the 2026-11-19 10:14 UTC scratch reset. The original exact calculation ran at 09:37:18.986283 UTC (0.013099318s); the reconstructed program has a separate measured runtime. Cycles and parent independently checked the full lattice argument before recovery. Cycles' audit was conditional on the stated geometric premise, not a fresh source check.

## 1. Geometric premise and exact conclusion

Let A be a complex abelian surface with End(A)=Z and a primitive polarization of type (1,2). The genus-five construction considered here starts with a genus-three curve D and its elliptic quotient, with the complementary abelian surface of type (1,2), and an étale double cover F→D obtained from a degree-two principally polarized isogeny B→A. We assume the principally polarized Prym of F/D is the indicated B, with the compatible lattice markings described below. This is the precise Prym premise in the Clingher–Malmendier–Shaska construction, not an assumption that every conceivable genus-five map has this shape.

Under this premise, **every actual composite A→J(F)→A is even**. More precisely the ideal of all such integer scalars is either 4Z or 2Z, depending on the marking. All 720 possible symplectic mod-two markings give 4Z in 672 cases and 2Z in 48 cases. Thus this particular family of full-span genus-five curves does not remove the residual factor two, even if arbitrary integral homomorphisms through its Jacobian are allowed. This conclusion is stronger than computing only the class of the displayed curve, but does not constrain arbitrary Jacobians.

The primary source is Clingher, Malmendier, and Shaska, *Geometry of Prym varieties for certain bielliptic curves of genus three and five* (7 September 2021 author version), <https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.04839v2>. The complete PDF was opened; diagram(1.3) p3 and Theorem1.2 p5 were read. Its letters differ from ours. The ramified-Prym quotient convention must not be confused with the principally polarized étale Prym used below. The proof below is an independent integral lattice computation under that exact premise.

## 2. The genus-three lattice

Write Λ=H₁(A,Z)=Z(e₁,f₁,e₂,f₂), with alternating polarization form

`E_L=diag(J,2J)`, where `J=[[0,1],[-1,0]]`.

Its dual lattice is `Λ#=Z(e₁,f₁,e₂/2,f₂/2)`. Let u,v be a symplectic elliptic basis. On the rational decomposition `H₁(J(D),Q)=H₁(A,Q)⊕H₁(E,Q)`, the principal form is `2E_L⊕2J`. An integral symplectic basis is

`a₁=(e₁+u)/2, b₁=v, a₂=(f₁−v)/2, b₂=−e₁, a₃=e₂/2, b₃=f₂/2`.

Direct pairing gives one in each pair and zero between distinct pairs. The projection J(D)→A acts as multiplication by two on the A coordinate. The duality calculation uses this principal form; it does not treat the nonprincipal E_L as a unimodular form.

Choose the degree-two principally polarized cover B→A with lattice `Λ_B=Z(2e₁,f₁,e₂,f₂)`. The restricted form E_L/2 is principal on this lattice. All changes of its symplectic marking are represented by

`P=diag(2,1,1,1) G`, with `G∈Sp₄(Z)`.

Write P_j for its columns. The character of the cover detects the e₁ coordinate; on J(D), it is nontrivial on a₁ and trivial on the remaining displayed symplectic basis vectors.

## 3. The genus-five lattice

Use the rational decomposition `H₁(J(F),Q)=H₁(A,Q)⊕H₁(B,Q)⊕H₁(E,Q)`, identifying the B vector space with that of A via its isogeny. The principal polarization form is

`4E_L ⊕ E_L ⊕ 4J`.

An integral lattice is generated by

`A₁=(e₁/2,0,u/2), B₁=(0,0,v/2)`,

`a₂±=(f₁/4, ±P₁/2, −v/4), b₂±=(−e₁/2, ±P₂/2,0)`,

`a₃±=(e₂/4, ±P₃/2,0), b₃±=(f₂/4, ±P₄/2,0)`.

This is the standard integral transfer/difference lattice of the étale double cover with the chosen character, glued to its marked principally polarized Prym. In particular the factor two in the transfer and the factor four in the invariant form are retained. Omitting either factor changes the answer incorrectly.

Since A is simple and End(A)=Z, its rational homomorphisms to either A-vector-space factor are scalar and its homomorphisms to E vanish. Therefore every rational A→J(F) is `(a,b,0)` and every rational J(F)→A is `(c,d,0)`.

## 4. All incoming integral maps

Testing an incoming map against the dual lattice under the principal form amounts to testing `(4a,b)` against the E_L-dual conditions. The resulting necessary and sufficient form is

`(a,b)=(x/2,y)`, with x,y integers satisfying

`x+yG₂₁=0 (mod2)`, and `yG₂j=0 (mod2)` for j=2,3,4.

These conditions are not merely necessary for a convenient pair of maps: they describe the full integral Hom lattice. The use of the principal dual lattice is essential; testing only the visible A projection would miss the half-integral incoming coordinate.

## 5. All outgoing integral maps

Testing every displayed lattice generator shows that an outgoing integral map has the form `(c,d)=(2u,v)` for integers u,v with

`u f₁+vP₁=0`, `vP₂=0`, `u e₂+vP₃=0`, `u f₂+vP₄=0` modulo2.

The first factor two follows already from A₁. The remaining congruences arise from the four plus/minus pairs. Again this is the full integral Hom lattice. The composite of an incoming and an outgoing map is the scalar

`xu+yv`.

## 6. Parity and the exact ideals

If v is even, the outgoing equations force u even, so the composite is even. If v is odd, the equations force u odd and imply that the second row of G is `(1,0,0,0)` modulo2. The incoming equations then force x≡y, so `xu+yv≡x+y=0`.

If row₂(G) differs from `(1,0,0,0)`, the incoming conditions force both x and y even; the outgoing conditions force both u and v even. Each lattice is precisely 2Z², so the scalar ideal is 4Z.

If row₂(G) equals `(1,0,0,0)`, incoming `(x,y)=(1,1)` is allowed. Outgoing `(u,v)=(2,0)` is always allowed, giving the scalar two. The parity proof gives the reverse divisibility, so the ideal is exactly 2Z. We do **not** need to claim that the row condition guarantees an outgoing vector with v odd; that stronger assertion is unnecessary and was deliberately not used.

The full mod-two symplectic group has 720 elements. Exactly 48 have the indicated second row, giving the 48/672 split. The program enumerates all matrices by their four columns, tests every symplectic pairing, constructs both inverse-image lattices from their mod-two residues together with 2Z², and computes the gcd of all pairwise scalar products of generators. This is an exact finite certificate of the stated gluing calculation. The arbitrary-marking proof above is independent of the enumeration.

## 7. What remains

The remaining surface question is still whether the integral numerical cycle P²/2 exists on A×Â, equivalently whether A is an actual direct summand of some product of Jacobians. Excluding this one genus-five Prym construction does not exclude higher-genus Jacobians or other families of integral curves. It must not be counted as closing or narrowing that universal existence statement without an additional theorem that every candidate factors through this construction; no such theorem is asserted.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C4_lagrangian_divisor_obstruction_REPORT.md

# Exact obstruction for Lagrangian-surface divisor pushforwards

Status: **proved method exclusion; no main-gate movement and no priority claim**.

We prove that every divisor on each of two proposed full-span Lagrangian surfaces has an even mixed Matsusaka coefficient after mapping to `A × A^dual`, when `A` is a generic type-(1,2) surface with `End(A)=Z`. This checks all divisor classes, not merely the fundamental surface class or the restrictions of ambient divisors.

The decisive property is that the surface's Albanese variety admits an odd-degree isogeny from a power of `A`. On `A^n`, every integral curve homomorphism is `lambda_d S`, with `S` a symmetric integral matrix. A homomorphism to `A × A^dual` has rows `(r, lambda s)`, and its mixed curve coefficient is `2 r S s^t`. Finite-flat pullback along an odd-degree isogeny preserves the parity obstruction. Albanese factorization handles every divisor curve on the surface.

The full proof is `C4_lagrangian_divisor_obstruction.tex`. It is intentionally unnumbered and separate from the integrated main results. The parent may assign a label if it is useful in the final methods discussion; it should not be counted as a resolution of the remaining surface case.

## Opened primary sources

* Bastianelli, Pirola, and Stoppino, *Galois closure and Lagrangian varieties*, author version v2 (14 June 2010), <https://arxiv.org/pdf/0912.3377>. We opened the complete primary PDF and read Theorem 6.8, author pp. 25–26, including the Albanese-lattice proof. It identifies the Albanese variety of their LG surface with the square of the associated type-(1,2) surface. The publication is Advances in Mathematics 225(6), 3463–3501 (2010), DOI 10.1016/j.aim.2010.06.006. No assertion here relies on their Proposition 7.6 or on a claim that the surface's Neron–Severi group is generated by ambient divisors.
* Grossi and Moretti, *An explicit class of Lagrangian surfaces*, author version v1 (18 February 2025), <https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13087v1>. We opened the full primary HTML and read Proposition 4.2, Theorem 5.6, Proposition 6.2, and Corollary 6.3. Their associated type-(1,2) surface is `A_0/G`, with `|G|=3`, and the quotient surface has Albanese variety `(A_0 × A_0)/diag K`, with `K=(Z/3)^2`. The two are related by odd-degree isogenies. Publisher metadata gives International Journal of Mathematics 37(10), article 2650052 (2026), DOI 10.1142/S0129167X26500527; the mathematical locators used here refer to the opened author version, not to an independently read published PDF.

## Independent check

The cycles agent independently checked the full algebraic argument and its treatment of arbitrary surface divisors. In particular, that audit confirmed the direction of the isogeny, the factor of two in the mixed block, the odd-degree pullback argument, and the absence of any ambient-NS-generation hypothesis.

## Remaining gate

The argument controls only curves obtained from varieties whose Albanese is odd-isogenous to a power of the original surface. It does not control all curves spanning `A × A^dual`. The exact integral numerical Poincare-cycle criterion remains unchanged. Likewise no consequence for arbitrary supersingular threefolds in characteristics two or three is asserted.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C4_positive_characteristic_RM_REPORT.md

# C.4x — full real multiplication in positive characteristic

The original Yu 2003 paper gives a direct argument in positive characteristic. No canonical lift, supersingular realization, or ordinary hypothesis is needed.

## Exact proved scope

For a dimension-g abelian variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, with a full degree-g totally real integer-ring action and a compatible polarization, the polarization Euler-characteristic gcd is a p-power. Under the intrinsic equality of Lie-module and regular-module classes in the Grothendieck group, that gcd is one. Total ramification of p forces the equality because the coefficient algebra is local Artinian with a unique simple module and both modules have length g.

Combining with the previously proved actual-factorization bounds gives s_J dividing 2's p-part for surfaces and 6's p-part for threefolds. The Lie condition removes the remaining characteristic-prime factor. No failure statement is inferred if the condition fails.

# C.4v: full real multiplication

We prove a new affirmative family rather than merely a reformulation of the residual gate. For a characteristic-zero abelian variety of dimension g with the full ring of integers of a totally real degree-g field acting and fixed by the Rosati involution of a polarization, the gcd of Euler characteristics of line bundles is one. The proof is an integral trace-lattice argument. The homology is projective of rank two over the full integer ring. Its balanced integral alternating forms form an invertible codifferent-valued determinant module. A local generator supplies a perfect pairing at any chosen rational prime; its residue lifts globally, and a large positive multiple of that prime times an existing polarization supplies positivity without changing perfection. All balanced forms have Hodge type (1,1), as shown explicitly on the real two-plane decomposition. The prime may be two; no inversion of two is hidden.

The same result includes simple varieties whose full endomorphism ring is the maximal order of a CM field, using the unique positive involution. ## October2026 supersingular derived-isogeny theorem

An Jiang, Zhiyuan Li, and Ziwei Lu, *Derived equivalences and isogenies of supersingular abelian varieties*, arXiv2610.24666v1,17October2026. Complete primary PDF downloaded and read. Theorem1.2 and its proof in §3 pp5–6 show derived isogeny for all supersingular abelian varieties of the same dimension; the construction uses twisted Fourier–Mukai equivalences. It does not give an actual untwisted product decomposition or a prime-to-p factorization of the identity.

Theorem4.1 pp6–7 gives, in every characteristic and dimension g>2, supersingular examples A such that Aⁿ is never isomorphic to Âⁿ. The proof uses A=Eᵍ/H with an alpha_p subgroup defined by F_{p²}-linearly independent coefficients. An assumed isomorphism would produce an endomorphism of E^{gn} of degree p^{2n} whose kernel contains ker(F^{gn}), forcing p^{gn}|p^{2n}. This contradiction shows that principal polarizability of arbitrary supersingular threefolds is not a valid shortcut. It still does not obstruct being a direct summand of a larger product of Jacobians.

## EGFS monodromy scope

Engel–de Gaay Fortman–Schreieder, arXiv2507.15704v3, was reopened, including Theorem1.6. Its specified matroidal-family criterion uses independent boundary monodromy logarithms proportional to rank-one quadratic forms. In the family A×Â obtained by varying A, H¹ contains two isomorphic copies of the same variation, so every corresponding monodromy logarithm has even rank. Thus this precise criterion cannot simply be applied to that correlated subfamily. The very-general principally polarized fourfold theorem also does not specialize automatically to the three-dimensional type(1,2) product locus. No extension of the theorem was proved.

## New Chern-method exclusion after09:50

`C4_semihomogeneous_obstruction.tex` proves that all semihomogeneous Chern constructions miss P²/2 and have even mixed degree-three coefficients. The proof uses the full general semihomogeneous Chern identity, not just rank-two examples. It also covers Chern classes of the familiar odd-rank virtual Fourier transform of a universal one-point ideal sheaf, by its exact K₀ decomposition. Arbitrary moduli kernels and arbitrary algebraic cycles are outside its scope.

## Exact current Fourier/motive literature limitations

Li–Zou's author primary text, <https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~hzou/papers/derivedab/>, was opened completely. Corollary1.2.2 relates derived isogenies to motive isomorphisms; §3.1 explicitly uses Chow correspondences with Q coefficients, and equation(3.1.1) is ch(P) in CH*(X×Y)_Q. The integral twisted Mukai lattice in §3.2 is a different realization. Neither the rational-motive theorem nor integrality of that cohomological realization supplies an integral numerical P²/2 cycle.

Hasan–Hassan–Lin–Manivel–McBeath–Moonen (2025), *Integral aspects of Fourier duality for abelian varieties*, DOI10.1007/s00229-025-01662-7, was opened at the complete publisher HTML. Theorem4.5 and §1.2 construct integral transforms lifting (2g+d)! times the classical transform; Theorem5.5 works after inverting (2g+d+1)!. This is a precise integral denominator theorem, but it does not remove the prime two in the residual surface problem. The statements and coefficient rings were checked; no claim that their full proof was independently rederived is made.

Fresh acquisition records, URLs, SHA256 hashes and times are in `output/residual_and_K2_sources_manifest.json`. ## 4. Why the literal matroidal-family theorem is not immediately applicable

Opened the latest full Engel–de Gaay Fortman–Schreieder version, https://arxiv.org/html/2507.15704v3 . The relevant hypotheses are in Definition 4.1 and Theorem 4.10; the monodromy formalism is in Section 2.5, especially Definition 2.12 and Lemma 2.13.

Their matroidal family has nonzero rank-one monodromy logarithms around the distinguished independent boundary components. For a family of abelian varieties of the form A×Ahat, a relative polarization identifies H1(A,Q) and H1(Ahat,Q) as rational local systems. Thus every monodromy logarithm on the product is a direct sum of two conjugate operators and has rank twice the rank of the operator on A. This persists under isogeny and finite base change. Consequently a nonzero rank-one logarithm cannot occur in such an isotypic family.

This elementary rank observation shows that the literal matroidal-family hypothesis cannot simply be asserted for the residual surface family. It does **not** rule out adaptations to grouped rank-two degenerations, and does **not** imply algebraicity or nonalgebraicity of the desired cycle. The very-general ppav conclusion also does not specialize in either direction to this special locus.

# Relative Milnor quotient: exact scope and validation

The auxiliary proof is `K2_relative_Milnor_all_characteristics.tex`. It establishes, for a square-zero invertible-ideal thickening E of a smooth k-variety V, the canonical quotient

J_r = ker(K_r^M(E) → K_r^M(V)) → I ⊗ Ω^{r−1}_{V/k}.

It is normalized by {1+i,u₂,…,u_r} ↦ i dlog(u₂)…dlog(u_r), is independent of a splitting or frame, and exists in every characteristic. In characteristic p the relative sheaf J_r is killed by p. The proof uses tensor presentations, actual lifts of Steinberg relations, and the canonical rank-one conormal exterior kernel. It does not assert that the quotient is an isomorphism at p=2 or that Milnor and Quillen K-theory agree on E.

The proof also gives the actual transition-symbol cup formula for products of line bundles, first in degree two and then explicitly in every degree, and the resulting relative-to-absolute cohomology injection if H^{r−1}(V,K_r^M) is p-divisible. ### Record: notes/ROOT_ALL_CHARACTERISTIC_PICARD_RESEARCH.md

# Uniform ordinary-quartic construction after review 9

Research lead proposed after review 9; not a registered theorem at this writing. The certified C.3bf remains in its exact characteristic-five, N≥4 scope. Frobenius is preparing a separate complete extension, provisionally C.3bg; cycles independently checked the ordinary-quartic and canonical-cup calculations below. This note does not itself change a main status.

## An explicit ordinary open set in every characteristic

For any prime p, put F0=xyz(x+y+z). This is the union of four projective lines with six distinct transverse nodes in every characteristic. Its dual graph is K4. The normalization exact sequence identifies H¹(O_C0) with the three-dimensional graph cokernel k^6/(k^4/k); semilinear Frobenius is bijective because the incidence matrix has entries in Fp.

There is also a direct coefficient calculation. In the standard H²(P²,O(-4)) basis indexed by a1=(2,1,1), a2=(1,2,1), a3=(1,1,2), the plane-quartic Hasse–Witt entry is the coefficient of x^(p a−b) in F^(p−1). For F0, factor

    F0^(p−1)=(xyz)^(p−1)(x+y+z)^(p−1).

Each diagonal coefficient becomes the coefficient of one pure monomial of degree p−1, hence equals one. Every off-diagonal coefficient has one exponent −1 after the factor is removed, hence equals zero. Thus the Hasse–Witt matrix at this singular quartic is I3 for every prime. The formula itself follows from the plane-curve exact sequence and the Cech representatives, so it does not presuppose smoothness at this test point.

Let t_m run through fifteen algebraically independent coefficients, one for each degree-four monomial, and set F=F0+sum(t_m m). The Hasse–Witt determinant is a polynomial in these coefficients with value one at zero, and is therefore nonzero at the generic point. The nonempty smooth open in the full quartic linear system meets this ordinary open. Thus the specified geometric generic quartic is smooth and ordinary in every characteristic. Its coefficient of z^4 is nonzero, so z0,z1 restrict to a basepoint-free canonical pencil when that pencil is needed for N=3.

## Producing the nonsplit first neighborhood

For any smooth plane quartic C, its canonical system is O_C(1). The Euler sequence and Serre duality show H¹(T_P²|C)=0: the map H¹(O_C)→H¹(O_C(1))^3 is dual to the basis map k^3→H⁰(K_C), hence is an isomorphism. The normal sequence then makes

    H⁰(C,O_C(4)) → H¹(C,T_C)

surjective. The canonical multiplication Sym²H⁰(K_C)→H⁰(K_C²) is an isomorphism: both spaces are the six-dimensional quadrics on the canonical plane curve, which has no quadratic equation. Serre duality therefore lets the normal displacement H realize any symmetric cup form on H⁰(K_C). A nondegenerate form exists also in characteristic two. Choosing an independent generic quartic H gives a nondegenerate form.

Thus the source pairing is with f*eta, and Serre duality identifies the resulting cohomological map precisely as tr_(f,L). Contraction commutes with trace because the geometric map and the line bundles are defined over Qbar. Derivations separate coefficient-field forms. This proves the required first-jet pushforward identity, including the ramification locus, with the stated normalization.

The use of supports is legitimate: on a finite quasi-projective model, choose a rational section of A_a that is a unit at the relevant generic points of the fibre divisors and of their intersections with T. Semilocal triviality permits this finite set of conditions. The resulting product-cycle components are curves not contained in T, so they meet T at finitely many points. Normalization reduces their local traces to finite curve-branch traces. No attempt is made to restrict a residue fraction whose whole support lies inside the exceptional divisor.

The Cartier square is Tor-independent with multiplicity one, so exceptional refined pullback commutes with proper pushforward. Pushforward of the actual parameter family remains an actual family. The ordinary quotient on V is degree, and the exceptional image has nonzero degree by its normal self-intersection. Therefore B²(Z)_Q≃Q and B²(X)_Q=0, exactly as claimed.

## Scope retained

The base is the strict henselization at a closed k-point of a normal local ring essentially of finite type over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0. The dimension is d+1, with d>=1. A projective birational modification is regular and is an isomorphism away from the closed point. Its reduced exceptional fibre E is a single smooth connected Cartier divisor, and O_E(-E) is ample. These are genuine restrictions. There is no retraction from the modification Z to E. The theorem proves CH^d(Z)_Q ≅ CH_0(E)_Q, the exact quotient formula on the puncture, and B^d(Z)_Q ≅ Q with B^d(X)_Q=0 for actual ordinary algebraic equivalence.

## Independent derivation

1. Abstract blow-up pro-descent and K_0 of local rings give a monomorphism from the constant K_0(Z) pro-object to the infinitesimal exceptional fibres. Its kernel terms form a decreasing system of inclusions. A pro-zero such system has a zero term, so one finite stage detects K_0(Z). Nil-relative K-theory in characteristic p becomes zero after inverting p; finite affine Mayer–Vietoris descent gives injectivity into K_0(E)[1/p]. No uniform p-exponent over infinitely many infinitesimal stages is used.
2. The algebraizable strict-local hypothesis permits finite pointed-etale smooth models for Z. Regularity and properness over the local base allow removal of the image of any nonsmooth locus away from the marked point. The natural rational Chern-character ring isomorphism passes to the filtered limit and commutes with the Cartier pullback. This yields the required injective codimension-d Chow map.
3. A sufficiently ample complete-intersection curve C in E can be chosen smooth and connected through any prescribed points x,o. Relative Serre vanishing lifts its cutting sections to Z. Independence of the restricted differentials makes their common zero scheme W regular of dimension two along C. Any nonempty closed bad locus in the proper scheme W has image containing the closed point of the local base, which contradicts this regularity. The same properness argument excludes additional components. The induced conormal on C remains ample.
4. For an entire line bundle F on C×P, where P is a smooth connected projective parameter curve, the obstruction to the successive square-zero lift is H^1(C,L_C^n) tensor H^1(P,O_P). Serre vanishing kills every such group after one fixed index n_0. At the finitely many earlier indices, tensoring by p kills the additive obstruction. We can take the fixed total exponent p^(n_0−1) for the whole family. The preceding restrictions are raised together at each step; this gives a compatible formal system, rather than unrelated pointwise lifts or an unbounded sequence of powers.
5. The C-adic and closed-fibre-adic ideals have the same radical on the noetherian proper surface, hence cofinal powers. Projective Grothendieck existence over the completion algebraizes the line bundle. Algebraizing its inverse and their pairing verifies actual invertibility. Excellence makes completion a regular map. Popescu gives a smooth finite-stage algebra carrying the bundle. The residue-field point of that smooth algebra lifts to the henselian ring. Pullback gives an actual bundle on the fixed product W×P with the prescribed entire closed-fibre family. Preserving the residue-field map preserves that family, not merely its numerical class.
6. For P=C and the diagonal line bundle, the two fibre classes push from W to Z. Tor-independent Cartier base change sends their difference to p^e([x]−[o]) on E. Thus all degree-zero zero-cycles on E lift rationally to actual ordinary algebraically trivial classes on Z. Injectivity then identifies the exact ordinary kernel of the restricted degree map.
7. An exceptional curve D has restricted self-intersection −c_1(L)[D] of nonzero degree. It supplies the missing degree direction, proving surjectivity of the full Chow map. Localization gives the quotient by c_1(L)CH_1(E). The same boundary class spans B^d(Z)_Q and restricts to zero, proving B^d(X)_Q=0.

## 1. Actual proper parameter and finite interpolation

If the requested class is nonzero, the tuple of degree-zero line bundles is a nonzero point of a positive-dimensional product of Jacobians. A smooth connected proper curve through it and the origin exists by the previously audited prescribed-jet complete-intersection argument. The normalized Poincare bundles are rigidified at the origin and along the chosen edge base points. Every marked-point restriction is therefore a line bundle on this one proper parameter with a specified trivialization at the origin.

For each of the finitely many marked bundles, a rational section can be chosen nonvanishing at the origin and the desired second parameter point, and scaled to value1 in the prescribed origin trivialization. This follows by twisting by a sufficiently large divisor away from these two points and using the surjective two-point evaluation map. Its divisor has finite support away from both endpoints. Riemann–Roch then allows one function h with poles only at the origin, the prescribed nonzero value (u−1)^2/u at the second point, and zero at every support point of every marked divisor. First-jet conditions can make all those zeros simple and add another simple zero; increasing the pole order makes the evaluation map onto. A nonzero leading principal part can also be prescribed by the same vanishing after reducing the pole order by one.

The normalized quadratic cover (g−1)^2=hg is an actual finite connected proper curve. In odd characteristic a simple zero of h gives odd valuation of h(h+4), so the quadratic is irreducible and separable. In characteristic two, (g+1)/h satisfies the Artin–Schreier equation y²+y=1/h; its simple pole prevents the right side from being a coboundary. Normal proper curves over the algebraically closed base are smooth. The only zeros and poles of g lie above the origin, and every point above a pole of h is one of them, by g+g^−1=h+2. Above the desired second point there is a point with g=u even when that point is ramified (in particular u=−1 in odd characteristic). Above every chosen divisor support, g=1, including at wild branch points in characteristic two.

On each regular surface C_e times P, the pulled-back Poincare line bundle has a specified trivialization along all zero/pole fibres of g. The Dennis–Stein defining word specializes to zero when its first argument is zero; the second Steinberg symbol becomes {v,1}=0. Negative m causes no difficulty in the abelian group.

Regular-local Gersten injectivity proves the cocycle identity, compatibility of these local extensions, and independence under changes of frames compatible with the rigidification: all are identities in the function field, and the corresponding comparison symbols also extend. This proves an actual H1 of the Zariski K2 sheaf, not merely a tame-residue-zero rational expression. Its horizontal origin restriction is zero; its other endpoint is the usual u-times-line-bundle cup.

At a marked point the chosen rational section pulls back to a frame of the evaluation line bundle outside its divisor and has value1 at every boundary point. Every such point-unit is1, hence zero in the additive K1 group. Ramification multiplicities do not change this. The construction is integral on these smooth products; it does not rely on an assumed rational Adams decomposition of their K1 groups.

The pointwise component map is onto: a pure-weight-two component tuple restricts to zero in edge K0. Its canonical obstruction in pi0(T_k) consequently comes from vertex K1(k). The construction still does not generate all algebraic K0(A×Adual) integrally by a proved argument. In particular, generation of a derived category after taking direct summands would not itself supply the required integral generation of K0. We do not infer nonalgebraicity for arbitrary surfaces, product sheaves or deformation constructions. The main C.4 gate is unchanged.

### Record: notes/ROOT_CUBIC_SURFACE_LINE_CUP_RESEARCH.md

# A nonzero twisted divisor cup product on a smooth cubic surface

AI-produced by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode), RESEARCH_SA06, root. Written 19 November 2026 after checkpoint15. This auxiliary calculation does not by itself prove a local Chow-kernel theorem.

## 1. Exact claim and explicit smooth surfaces

Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic p, let W be the smooth cubic surface specified below, put A=O_W(1)=−K_W, and let D be its displayed line. We compute

μ_D:H⁰(W,A)→H¹(W,Ω¹_W⊗A), a↦a c₁(O_W(D)),

where the Chern class is the algebraic dlog class. The target has dimension four, and the map has rank two, including in characteristics two and three.

For p≠3 use the Fermat surface x₀³+x₁³+x₂³+x₃³=0. Its partial derivatives 3x_i² have no common projective zero. Make the invertible coordinate change u=x₀+x₁, v=x₂+x₃, s=x₁, t=x₃. Its equation is

F=u³−3u²s+3us²+v³−3v²t+3vt²=uQ₀+vQ₁.

The line D is u=v=0, with Q₀|D=3s² and Q₁|D=3t².

For p=3 use F=us²+vt²+u²t+v²s. Again D is u=v=0, with restricted quadratics s²,t². Its gradient is (s²−ut,t²−vs,−us+v²,−vt+u²). A zero coordinate at a common gradient zero forces all coordinates zero. Otherwise normalize u=1. The equations give s=v²,t=v⁻¹,v⁵=1; at these points F=4v⁴=v⁴≠0. Hence W is smooth over the algebraic closure, not just at its rational points.

## 2. The duality calculation

The cubic conormal sequence twisted by A is

0→O_W(−2A)→Ω¹_{P³}(1)|W→Ω¹_W(A)→0.

The restricted Euler sequence is

0→Ω¹_{P³}(1)|W→O_W⁴→O_W(A)→0.

Its map on H⁰ is the coordinate-basis isomorphism. The hypersurface sequence on P³ gives H¹(O_W(nA))=0 for every integer n and H²(O_W(nA))=0 for n≥0. Thus H¹ and H² of the middle conormal term vanish. The connecting map and Serre duality give

H¹(Ω¹_W(A))≅H²(O_W(−2A))≅H⁰(O_W(A))∨.

Twisting the tangent normal sequence by −2A gives

0→T_W(−2A)→T_{P³}|W(−2A)→O_W(A)→0.

Both H⁰ and H¹ of its middle term vanish. The Euler sequence reduces H¹-vanishing to the dual of the same coordinate-basis isomorphism. Hence its boundary δ₁:H⁰(A)→H¹(T_W(−2A)) is an isomorphism. Multiplication by a∈H⁰(A) takes δ₁(b) to δ₂(ab), where δ₂:H⁰(2A)→H¹(T_W(−A)) comes from the tangent normal sequence twisted by −A.

Up to the one fixed sign of the contraction convention, the Serre pairing of μ_D(a) with δ₁(b) is the trace of c₁(O_W(D)) contracted with δ₂(ab), in H²(O_W(−A))=k.

## 3. Direct calculation of the line-bundle obstruction

The normal sequence for D⊂W⊂P³, twisted by −A, is

0→O_D(−2)→O_D²→O_D(2)→0,

with last map (a₀,a₁)↦a₀Q₀|D+a₁Q₁|D. It is surjective because the two quadratics have no common zero. Consequently

H¹(O_D(−2))≅H⁰(O_D(2))/⟨s²,t²⟩.

The class of st is a basis. Let λ_D be the quotient functional normalized by λ_D(st)=1; it kills s² and t².

For q∈H⁰(W,2A), extend q to a quadratic on P³. In the total space of O_{P³}(1), the first neighborhood defined by F+τq=0 has conormal O_W(−A) and deformation class δ₂(q). Local lifts of the ideal of D have equations u+τa₀,v+τa₁. Substitution gives exactly q|D modulo the two Q_i|D. Thus the embedded-line obstruction is its class in H¹(O_D(−2)), with no factor of two or factorial.

The image under H¹(O_D(−2))→H²(O_W(−A)) is the line-bundle obstruction, namely contraction of δ₂(q) with c₁(O_W(D)). This equality follows directly by lifting the local defining equations: their differences on double overlaps are the normal cocycle; its divisor-sequence boundary is the failure of the lifted transition units on triple overlaps. This is the dlog/Atiyah contraction, with the same fixed sign. It introduces no characteristic-dependent factor.

This map is an isomorphism. It is the boundary of

0→O_W(−A)→O_W(D−A)→O_D(−2)→0.

Adjunction gives D²=−1 and A·D=1. Ampleness gives H⁰(O_W(D−A))=0 since A·(D−A)=−2. Serre duality gives H²(O_W(D−A))=H⁰(O_W(−D))∨=0. The cubic hypersurface sequence gives χ(O_W)=1. Surface Riemann–Roch then gives χ(O_W(D−A))=1+(D−A)·D/2=0, so H¹(O_W(D−A))=0 as well. The division by two here is in an integer Euler-characteristic formula, not in k.

The Serre-dual bilinear form of μ_D is therefore, up to a common nonzero scalar,

(a,b)↦λ_D((ab)|D).

In the basis (u,v,s,t), its only nonzero entries are (s,t) and (t,s). Its rank is exactly two in every characteristic. In particular μ_D(s) evaluated at t is nonzero.

## 4. Intended local application and outstanding checks

The proposed construction uses V=P^m×W×C, where C is the ordinary plane quartic of C.3bf/bg, with L=O(1)⊠A⊠K_C and m≥1. A deformation of C by τ ell H has a Picard extension whose vector image is the span of the canonical-section coefficients in ell. A coefficient with nonzero s or t restriction to D can have nonzero product with c₁(D) by the calculation above. The divisor D extends to the actual resolution because its projection to W is retained.

The first unresolved local case is m=1,r=2,N=5. Separate proof obligations remain: choose a smooth incidence divisor and verify the contracted regular punctures; show the relative K₂ class survives the nonsplit thickening and the K₁(V) boundary; realize the Picard kernel by actual proper-curve families; and show that nonzero relative K₀ detects the codimension-two Chow product. Integral Adams-weight separation in characteristic five is a proposed last step, not yet a proved replacement. This note establishes only the twisted line cup-product calculation.


## 5. Independent audit, finite certificate, and exact follow-up sources

The Frobenius collaborator independently read the complete proof and passed the embedded-divisor obstruction, semiregularity isomorphism, Serre duality and all-characteristic rank calculation; its full review is agents/frobenius/C3_cubic_line_cup_independent_REVIEW.md. Root ran code/check_cubic_surface_line_cup.py at14:21:08.341662UTC:17exact checks passed in0.20215913099673344seconds. Full stdout is code/check_cubic_surface_line_cup.out and the structured output is logs/cubic_surface_line_cup_certificate.json. A preliminary program incorrectly demanded every coordinate square belong to the specialized gradient ideal, stronger than the radical statement in the proof; that assertion was replaced by the valid fourth-power membership test. A subsequent serialization issue was fixed by converting the integer Gram matrix to native integers. Neither preliminary issue changes the mathematical claim.

For the proposed K-theory bridge, root freshly opened Geisser and Hesselholt (2011), TheoremA, printedp29, at https://math.mit.edu/~larsh/papers/025/bounded.pdf. It gives bounded p-primary relative groups for nilpotent ring extensions. We also opened Iwasa and Kai (2021), Isomorphisms up to bounded torsion between relative K0-groups and Chow groups with modulus, DOI10.1017/S1474748020000055, published22-page PDF, and read Definition3.9, Lemma3.10 and its entire proof (p1960), plus Theorem4.2 and its proof (pp1961–1962). The first gives the integral Adams eigenvalues on the coniveau graded pieces of a regular finite-dimensional scheme; the second supplies the ordinary cycle map to those graded pieces. We do not use the paper’s separate relative-modulus main theorem, whose affine-neighborhood hypothesis is not supplied here. ### Record: notes/ROOT_ENDPOINT_LIFTING_REVIEW.md

# Root audit: actual proper-curve endpoint lifting

Reviewer: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), ChatGPT Pro mode, `/root`.
Date: 19 November 2026. The complete original EL proof was read and independently reconstructed before16:49 UTC. The four requested geometric refinements were reread in full at16:52:22 UTC, and the final lifting, endpoint, and tetrahedral sections were reread in full immediately after review12. This is a mathematical proof audit, not a numerical certification or a claim of priority.

**Verdict: PASS in the exact stated scope.** Source: `agents/real_weil/C3_endpoint_family_lifting_draft.tex`, to be superseded by the owner's audited auxiliary. Both independent reviewers also passed the complete proof; their detailed receipts are retained in the two other agent directories. The hypotheses include positive characteristic, an excellent henselian algebraizable local k-algebra with residue k, a regular projective threefold modification, a reduced SNC exceptional divisor E, and an effective exceptional Cartier divisor D with ample negative restriction. The parameter is one fixed smooth connected projective curve P. The theorem produces an actual class on Z×P with the two prescribed endpoint restrictions. It does not lift the originally prescribed whole class on E×P.

## Complete proof checks

1. **Projective singular perfect K0.** A power of the maximal ideal annihilates O_D. The quotient of the local k-algebra by that power is finite-dimensional over its residue coefficient field k. Thus D and D×P are projective over k and have the resolution property. The gamma dimension theorem applies to their vector-bundle K0, including their singular and nonreduced structures. In particular gamma-three vanishes on E, a projective surface. No Cartan map to coherent G0 is used to discard classes.

2. **Generated-bundle reduction.** Dualizing a generating surjection for V-dual tensor L^m and then twisting by L^m gives an exact sequence from V to a sum of L^m with quotient Q tensor L^m, where Q is generated. Products of generating Q-sections and first-jet-generating line sections generate the required first jets. Hence a rank-zero virtual bundle is a difference of equally ranked sufficiently generated bundles; a common positive summand arranges rank at least two and positive determinants. Expanding gamma_t(A−B) gives the stated gamma-two identity, including both determinant cross terms. Products of rank-zero classes reduce modulo gamma-three to products of line differences, and then to differences of positive lines.

3. **Perfect lci curves.** For a generic map O^(n−1)→A, the deeper rank-drop locus has codimension six and misses the threefold. An invertible minor leaves a two-entry column. Its two entries are a regular sequence on the Cohen–Macaulay Cartier divisor D×P. The local Koszul verification yields the global Hilbert–Burch sequence and its exact perfect K0 identity. The flag splitting principle identifies its degree-two term with gamma-two of A−n. This represents every gamma-two class modulo gamma-three by a finite rational combination of perfect lci curve classes. First-jet incidence on the finitely many reduced SNC strata and two endpoint fibres gives transverse component curves, finite double-stratum intersections, avoidance of triple strata, and finite endpoint lci schemes. The bad incidence images need not be closed; their closures are proper by the dimension estimate. The revised proof states this correctly.

4. **Actual regular hypersurface family.** After a high twist, the conormal rank-two bundle on the curve has generated sections. A general section is nowhere zero on its one-dimensional reduction. Its hypersurface H contains C as a Cartier divisor. At C the selected combination has nonzero ambient differential because the two normal equations were transverse along the relevant SNC stratum; away from C the ordinary first-jet incidence argument supplies the same condition. The extra requirement excluding every entire surface E_i×{v} is legitimate: the restriction space has dimension at least two uniformly in v, using a generated twisted ideal and a further very ample factor, while v ranges in dimension one. C cannot contain a whole such surface. H is flat over P by the fibrewise Cartier criterion.

5. **Lifting the equation and regularity.** Relative Serre vanishing on the fixed actual Z×P lifts the equation defining H. The resulting Cartier hypersurface W is regular along the closed fibre. Its nonregular locus is closed by excellence; if nonempty, its proper image in the local base would contain the closed point, a contradiction. The equation is a nonzerodivisor on every Z-fibre over P: every regular component meets the exceptional fibre by properness, where the relevant surface is not identically annihilated. Thus W is also flat over P. No parameter-dependent henselian neighbourhood has replaced the fixed product.

6. **One finite p-power, not an unbounded sequence.** For J=O_W(−D) and L=J|H, relative ampleness over the curve P gives eventual higher-direct-image vanishing. Leray therefore gives H²(H,L^n)=0 for all sufficiently large n. H¹ need not vanish. At each of the finitely many earlier steps the square-zero Picard obstruction is killed by p. Raising the current partial line bundle, together with every previous restriction, to its pth power preserves compatibility and permits the next extension. After the vanishing threshold the exponent stays fixed. There is one compatible formal line bundle restricting to O_H(−C)^(p^e).

7. **Algebraization retaining the whole curve.** The exceptional and maximal-ideal filtrations have cofinal powers. Projective existence over the completion algebraizes the line bundle; algebraizing the inverse and using full faithfulness verifies invertibility. Regular completion and Popescu descend the finite presentation to one smooth R-algebra. Henselian smooth lifting is performed modulo a fixed power m^M contained in J, rather than merely modulo m. It therefore preserves the whole H, including its entire proper parameter curve, and gives an actual invertible sheaf on the fixed W.

8. **Exact endpoint identity.** The Cartier pushforward j_*(1−Q) is perfect. Flatness and the regular sequences give the required Tor-independent endpoint and divisor base changes. Each C_u is finite Artinian, so every line bundle on it is trivial. The geometric-series identity gives exactly p^e[O_Cu] in perfect K0(D). This does not require a singular gamma-filtered pushforward theorem. Division by p^e, summation of the finite generators, and gamma-three vanishing on E prove the endpoint assertion.

# Finite jets, fixed bundles, and the remaining actual-family problem

Root research, 19 November 2026, after checkpoint 14. This records an attempted route to the unrestricted characteristic-zero rational top quotient. It does not change a numbered theorem or the movement ledger.

Let E be a projective exceptional variety, L an ample conormal line bundle on E, and C a fixed smooth projective parameter curve over the coefficient field. If a vector bundle F0 on E×C is fixed, relative Serre vanishing for the projection to C gives

    H²(E×C, End(F0) ⊗ pr_E*L^n) = 0

for all sufficiently large n: all positive higher direct images vanish, and C has coherent cohomological dimension one. This removes the high-order deformation obstructions for that fixed restriction. The bound depends on F0. Moreover, pr_E*L is not ample on the entire product, so it would be incorrect to infer vanishing of every positive cohomology group on E×C; H¹ coming from C can remain.

The unresolved step is to represent the desired relative K0 classes by a compatible family with a fixed mod-E object and a controlled bound. An equality of vector-bundle classes in K0(E×C) does not imply a stable isomorphism of the bundles: exact-sequence relations need not split on a projective scheme. Finite detection of an endpoint class, or eventual constancy in a particular Adams weight, therefore does not by itself supply the compatible objects to which Grothendieck existence could be applied. We have not established that stronger representability statement. The already proved descent from an existing completed actual family remains available, but does not construct that family.

# Finite detection along a principal centre: exact remaining boundary issue

Root research, 19 November 2026, 12:58–13:01 UTC. This is a method analysis, not a new registered theorem for the remaining ordinary restriction gate.

Suppose a regular projective modification f:Z→Spec R is an isomorphism outside the closed point of a local domain R. For any nonzero h in its maximal ideal, the enlarged centre V(h) also makes an abstract blowup square: the modification is already an isomorphism away from this centre. KST Theorem A and exact sequence (1.6), freshly opened in the root C.3be audit, apply to its h-adic thickenings. K_0(R)=K_0(R/h^b)=Z, so the same diagonal-graph quotient and descending-kernel argument prove that K_0(Z) injects into K_0(Z×_R R/h^b) at some actual finite level b. In characteristic p, the finite thickening to the full divisor Z_h has p-primary nil-relative K-groups by GH Theorem A. Thus one obtains rational injectivity into K_0(Z_h). This is a full-divisor assertion, not an assertion about its punctured open part.

Let X be the puncture and Y=X∩V(h), and suppose an actual class alpha on X restricts to zero on Y. A K_0 lift z on Z need not vanish on Z_h. Its restriction lies in the kernel of restriction from the whole divisor to its punctured part, hence in perfect K-theory with support at the exceptional part. Finite detection cannot be applied to declare z zero. To deduce the desired punctured restriction injectivity one would have to prove that this supported class is the restriction of an exceptional-boundary class on Z, with a controlled nonzero integer multiplier. That is the additional step.

The whole divisor Z_h can be singular. Its supported perfect K_0 cannot silently be replaced by G_0 of the reduced exceptional fibre. Coherent exceptional sheaves have derived Tor contributions under restriction, and the Cartan map K_0→G_0 on a singular scheme can have a kernel. In the SNC calculation, even the degree-unit edge terms are subject to the weighted negative-ample intersection identity; a preserved dual-complex loop alone supplies no surviving obstruction. The source and target of the missing boundary lift must therefore remain explicit.

The real_weil agent independently confirmed this diagnosis on 19 November 2026 and is testing whether codimension and depth yield an actual range theorem. No such theorem or counterexample has been established here. Termwise rational nilinvariance also does not identify an inverse limit of integral K_0 groups, tensored afterward with Q, with the inverse limit of their rationalizations; it provides no uniform denominator across infinitely many thickenings.

The root additionally read the complete current owner note `agents/frobenius/C3_SNC_top_RESEARCH.md` and its entire weighted energy proof. The product E=(cycle of rational curves)×P^1 cannot simply be placed with ample conormal in a regular threefold while keeping its proposed top torus class: the self-intersection/Cartan relation contradicts that proposed survival. The explicitly opened Kollár2014 primary paper gives the relevant plumbing and isolated-contraction construction, but its subsequent small resolutions alter the component restriction map. One tempting route would represent every relative weight-two perfect class on S×P by one-cycles whose closures avoid D×P. ### Record: notes/ROOT_MULTIPLICATIVE_TOP_EXTENSION_RESEARCH.md

# Attempt to propagate the multiplicative surface quotient to higher top degree

AI-produced by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode), RESEARCH_SA06, /root, 19 November 2026, 15:04–15:10 UTC. This is an unsuccessful approach record, not a registered theorem or a progress-gate reduction.

## The tempting surface reduction is false over arbitrary coefficient fields

The residue-field-restricted theorem C.3be reduces rational top Chow vanishing to normal local surfaces and proves it over Fpbar. Replacing its torsion argument by ordinary algebraic equivalence over an arbitrary algebraically closed field does not work. The already proved C.3y has exceptional rational triangle and ordinary B1(X)=k* plus (Z/4)^2. Proper parameter curves cannot change the multiplicative gluing scalar. For fields of positive transcendence degree over Fpbar, k* tensor Q is nonzero. This is an actual counterexample to the proposed surface lemma, not merely a missing proof. The normal-surface pushforward to a higher-dimensional local scheme could annihilate its classes, so this observation does not settle the higher-dimensional top quotient.

## Why the direct projective-space product does not yield a regular puncture

C.3y starts from the triangle D(z)=z0 z1 z2 and quartic G, with G nonzero at its vertices. Its resolution is locally the hypersurface D−tau G=0 in the total space of O_P2(−1). The nonzero normal derivative at each triangle vertex makes the surface smooth.

A prospective dimension-N=m+2 Segre version uses the total space of O_{Pm×P2}(−1,−1) and equation D−tau ell(x)G=0, with ell a projective linear form. The exceptional divisor would initially be Pm times the triangle. Along a triangle vertex over ell=0 the equation is locally u v=tau w, with smooth extra coordinates. Thus the source is singular there; a simple product argument is invalid. For any positive projective twist the coefficient of tau has zeros at that vertex, so choosing a different single section cannot remove this defect.

Resolving the local model by blowing up (u,tau) gives charts u=a tau, w=a v and tau=b u, v=b w. The resulting source is smooth locally, but one exceptional component becomes the blow-up of Pm×P1 along the hyperplane H×{vertex}. The other component and their double locus Pm are unchanged locally. The new exceptional divisor on the blown-up component restricts to the hyperplane class on that double Pm and is supported away from its other attaching locus.

This creates a precise problem for the intended top-weight gluing detector. Before modification the formal product Pm×triangle has a k* contribution from its cyclic gluing, multiplied by h^m. After the local modification, the added exceptional divisor times h^(m−1) has intersection degree one on the affected double locus. Multiplying by a constant unit gives a class in the component's K1 of weight m+1 whose restriction hits that edge generator. Therefore the top-weight edge gluing that the naive product was intended to preserve is no longer protected. A global conclusion about the full resolved K-theory complex would require additional work; none is asserted. In particular we have not constructed a higher-dimensional nonzero rational Btop class.

A higher-rank vector-bundle variant instead keeps only the exceptional triangle as a curve and can make the source regular using several normal derivatives. It does not preserve the required top Adams weight: after inverting p, finite K0 detection restricts to that one-dimensional exceptional scheme, whose rational K0 has weights at most one. For N>=3 that is insufficient to detect a codimension-(N−1) class. This is another reason the surface witness alone does not propagate.

## Remaining exact gate

Construct an actual higher-dimensional regular puncture with a nonzero rational ordinary top quotient and a detector surviving the entire exceptional boundary and all fixed proper-curve families; or prove universal rational top vanishing beyond the current smooth-exceptional/cone/residue-Fpbar cases. The multiplicative surface example is a useful constraint on either approach, but it does not reduce this gate by itself.

### Record: notes/ROOT_PARAMETER_SURFACE_LIFTING_RESEARCH.md

# Constant proper parameter surfaces: an integral gamma bound and the boundary-node gate

Credit: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), ChatGPT Pro mode; /root; effort setting not separately exposed.19November2026,20:12–20:16UTC. No priority claim. **Auxiliary proof PS.1–PS.4 passed two complete independent mathematical reviews at20:18 and20:20UTC; registered as C.3bw. PS.5 remains unresolved; no main-gate movement.**

## PS.1. Exact setup and claim

Let k be algebraically closed, R a noetherian local coefficient-k algebra with residue field k, and S a smooth connected projective surface over k. Put B=SpecR×_kS. The claim is integral:

`F_gamma^3 K0(B)=0`.

Neither characteristic, regularity, normality nor henselianity of R is needed for this bound. K0 means perfect K-theory; B has the resolution property because it is projective with an ample line bundle over the affine base. Its vector-bundle and perfect K0 descriptions agree. The following proof uses finite semilocal supports, not a bound by the larger total dimension of B.

## PS.2. Relative sections and finite supports

Fix an ample line bundle H pulled back from S. For every vector bundle V on B, relative Serre vanishing gives surjectivity of global sections onto the closed-fibre sections after a sufficiently high twist: apply it to the coherent sheaf mV. On the smooth projective closed fibre, sufficiently high twists generate first jets. Thus the finite-dimensional first-jet incidence argument used in AE permits general sections with the following properties.

If rankV≥3, one such section of V⊗H^n has no zero on the closed surface: vanishing has codimension rankV>2 in the section incidence. Its zero scheme on B is proper over SpecR and misses the closed fibre, hence is empty. The section therefore splits off a line subbundle with locally free quotient. Iterating expresses [V] as a sum of line-bundle classes and one rank-two bundle class. Ranks zero and one are handled separately.

If V has rank two, a general section of V⊗H^n has finite transverse zero scheme on the closed surface. Its actual zero scheme F on B is etale over R near every point of that fibre: locally the two section equations have invertible relative Jacobian on the smooth relative surface B/R. The non-etale locus is a closed subset of the proper F and misses the closed fibre, so it is empty. Properness and quasi-finiteness make F finite etale over R. The same reasoning applied to two transverse high-twist Cartier sections gives finite etale complete intersections. Relative effective-Cartier flatness near the closed fibre is the exact Stacks062Y(3) criterion; properness extends it to all of B. Finite support is also directly covered by Stacks02UP and02LS, whose full displayed proofs were freshly read in the NK audit.

Every such finite R-scheme is semilocal. Every invertible module on it is trivial, by the Chinese-remainder/Nakayama proof already supplied in WP.4. More generally, every vector-bundle class of constant rank zero restricts to zero in K0(F), since finite projective modules over a semilocal ring are classified by their locally constant rank. The finite etale immersions used here are regular of codimension two, so their structure sheaves and pushforwards are perfect even when R is singular.

Let G be the subgroup of K0(B) generated by the classes [O_F] of the finite zero schemes just constructed, including the transverse intersections of two line-bundle sections. If I is the rank-zero subgroup, the perfect projection formula gives

`I G=0`,

because x·[O_F]=j_*(j^*x)=0 for every x∈I. Tensoring any such class by a line bundle leaves it unchanged.

## PS.3. Exact generation in gamma degree two

First, for any two line bundles M,N on B,

`([M]−1)([N]−1) ∈ G`.

Choose high twists M H^a,H^a,N H^b,H^b and four sections whose closed-fibre zero curves are smooth and pairwise transverse wherever a pair is used. Such simultaneous choices are a finite collection of open first-jet conditions. Write their relative Cartier divisors D_M+,D_M−,D_N+,D_N−. The Cartier exact sequences give the exact identity

`[M]−1 = [M][O_D_M+] − [O_D_M−]`,

and its N analogue. Multiplying expands the product into four perfect classes of the transverse intersections, with line-bundle twists. Each intersection is finite etale over R, and its twists are trivial. This proves the assertion integrally. It also applies to a square of a line difference by using two independently chosen divisor representations of the same line bundle.

For a rank-two bundle V, set

`c(V)=gamma^2([V]−2)=[det V]−[V]+1`, and `d=[det V]−1`.

Choose h=[H^n] as in PS.2 and W=V⊗H^n. The Koszul resolution of its transverse section gives

`[O_F]=1−[W^*]+[det W^*]`.

Multiplying by detW converts the right side to c(W), because W^*⊗detW≅W. The left side is unchanged since detW restricts trivially on finite semilocal F. Therefore c(W)=[O_F]. Direct expansion, with no discarded higher term, gives

`c(W)=h c(V)+h(h−1)d+(h−1)^2`.

Consequently

`c(V)=h^−1[O_F]−(h−1)d−h^−1(h−1)^2 ∈ G`,

using the line-product calculation and invariance of G under line twists.

Every rank-zero class is now a sum of line differences and elements of G: reduce bundles to rank two by PS.2 and use [V]−2=d−c(V). It follows that I²⊂G and I³=0. Conversely each generator of G is a rank-two Koszul gamma class, so G⊂F_gamma²K0(B).

For completeness this proves the gamma bound, not just the augmentation bound. For a line element, gamma_z([M]−1)=1+([M]−1)z. For a rank-two bundle, gamma_z([V]−2)=1+([V]−2)z+c(V)z². Gamma series of arbitrary virtual rank-zero classes are finite products and inverses of these expressions, because the preceding bundle reductions generate K0. Every coefficient of total degree at least three belongs to I³+IG and vanishes. Products of gamma operations of total degree at least three vanish for the same reason. This proves PS.1 integrally and also shows F_gamma²K0(B)=G.

## PS.4. Polynomial form and proper-surface lifting

On the rank quotient, psi² acts as1; on I/G it acts as2; on G it acts as4. The last equality can be checked on c(V) directly: psi²c(V)=4c(V)+c(V)(d+[V]−2)=4c(V), since IG=0. Thus

`A(psi²)=0 on K0(B)`, where `A(X)=(X−1)(X−2)(X−4)`.

The same polynomial annihilates K0(S), by taking R=k. This statement requires no Adams semisimplicity.

Now assume characteristic p>0 and retain the fixed-product KST/GH/TT blow-up hypotheses of FF: g:Z→SpecR is proper, Z regular, an isomorphism away from the closed point, and E is its reduced closed fibre. The every-degree FF exact sequence on the fixed proper parameter S gives

`K1(Z×S)_Q ⊕ K1(S)_Q → K1(E×S)_Q → K0(B)_Q → K0(Z×S)_Q ⊕ K0(S)_Q`.

For a class eta with psi²eta=8eta, its boundary is killed by A(psi²) on K0(B), while A(8)=168. Hence that boundary is zero rationally. The K1(S) summand can be absorbed by its actual pullback to Z×S. Every such weight-three class on E×S therefore lifts to an actual K1 class on the same Z×S. No localization or henselization of R tensor_k k(u) occurs.

Similarly, any class of weight three in the kernel of K0(Z×S)_Q→K0(E×S)_Q is zero: exactness puts the pair (x,0) in the image of K0(B)_Q, so A(psi²)x=0; weight three gives168x=0. This is injectivity on the indicated eigenspace, not on the entire K0 group. Polynomial corrections can be used throughout in place of a global singular-K1 splitting.

## PS.5. The still unresolved boundary step

Suppose a varying proper parameter curve over k(u) is spread over an open of a smooth projective surface S with SNC boundary D. Localization puts the obstruction to extending its exceptional K1 class in K0(E×S on E×D). Contributions coming from the smooth boundary components can be lifted by WP (for the top weight in exceptional dimension two); the proper-surface statements above can then remove the corresponding forget-support obstruction and correct an extendable remainder.

But the supported boundary need not decompose into those contributions. At intersections of boundary components, support-union exactness involves negative K-groups of E; in the relevant shifted weight it includes K_-1(E) of weight one. These groups can be nonzero. Replacing D by its normalization or using the full K0 lift over a nodal parameter curve does not supply supported devissage in the singular ambient product. No theorem in this note kills the node term for the actual HK/VE class. The compactification route therefore remains incomplete and UK.7 is unchanged.

## Source, execution and review scope

The section-generation and first-jet arguments reuse the completely audited AE geometric construction, with the actual local-base properness argument written above. Stacks062Y,02UP,02LS were freshly opened by root and their complete printed proofs read at20:08UTC;02M9's source gives only proof hints and the complete elementary proof is explicitly supplied in WP/NK. Perfect Koszul identities, lambda-ring identities and projection formula are independently expanded above; the existing TT/Weibel source audits are reused. The FF fixed-product exact sequence is the previously audited KST/GH/TT theorem in exactly its characteristic-p scope. No numerical or symbolic program was run for this exact general argument. This note claims no novelty and does not assert that its literature search establishes absence of a prior result. Independent proof review is requested before promotion.

At20:26UTC the complete proof was transferred into sections/C3_parameter_surface_lifting.tex as C.3bw. The two full independent receipts were read by root.
