# Intrinsic proper-family research after checkpoint 20

GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), ChatGPT Pro mode, `/root`. Research window beginning17:50UTC,19November2026; updated18:12UTC. This note retains attempts and their exact limits. It is not a new universal vanishing or nonvanishing theorem and does not by itself count as hourly main-gate movement.

## 1. Present certified position

C.3bm gives the intrinsic perfect-family presentation for every algebraizable normal strict-local threefold with regular puncture in positive characteristic. C.3bo removes component degrees and Albanese coordinates in that entire branch. C.3bn gives endpoint comparison under the stated regular projective modification hypotheses in every dimension, without requiring SNC support. C.3bp extends the mixed component-Albanese elimination when that higher-dimensional support is SNC. These last conditional scopes must not be confused with an arbitrary-dimensional resolution-existence theorem.

C.3bq now supplies a complete restricted edge/triple correction: the kernel of component restriction is a proper-family relation if every signed triple-point period on the double curves vanishes (in particular if rational dual H2 vanishes). Its ordinary-vanishing corollary separately assumes zero component rational Albanese kernels. C.3br supplies a different complete restricted theorem: no triples plus joint rational Picard restriction surjectivity kills all component degree-zero CH0, including their Albanese kernels. Negative rational double curves give the joint restriction right inverse explicitly. Neither restricted result makes all remaining intrinsic classes vanish.

## 2. Why component Albanese vanishing alone did not solve graph gluing

For E=S union_C T, a Poincare family on a curve A in S restricts along C times its proper parameter to a finite sum of point classes on C externally multiplied by evaluation-line classes on the parameter. A line twist from the parameter can remove a selected degree/Albanese coordinate after rational division, but does not thereby kill the Albanese kernel of the product C times the parameter. A zero component Albanese image does not imply that this perfect edge class vanishes.

The C.3br construction avoids that inference: use the graph of a smooth proper curve through the desired component points, then cancel each of its finitely many edge intersection coefficients by actual rational component divisor lifts at that fixed parameter value. Joint Picard surjectivity is exactly the hypothesis needed for this finite correction. In the triple-free setting the corrected tuple lifts through the actual two-column K-theory fibre sequence. No full Poincare family is required to lift on the other component.

The proposed extension to rational edges with triple points remains a question. One can choose the graph and divisor representatives away from the finitely many triple points. However equality of their edge K0 classes still need not give compatible trivializations in the three-column homotopy totalization. The missing check is the actual vertex K1 obstruction, including whether moving supports away from vertices supplies the required coherent nullhomotopies. This extension has been assigned for independent investigation; it is not asserted here.

## 3. Triple-point periods can lie in a component-Albanese kernel

For a rational dual-complex 2-cycle, the signed marked-point divisor on each edge has degree zero. Pushing the entire signed vector into the direct sum of component Albanese varieties gives zero: at each triple point its two incident contributions on a fixed component cancel with opposite signs. This only places the period vector in the kernel of the edge-to-component Albanese map. It does not force each individual edge period to vanish, and if all components are rational it imposes no additional condition.

A concrete candidate is the union of two smooth transverse quadrics and a plane in P3. Its quadric–quadric edge is a smooth elliptic quartic; the other edges are smooth conics, and the plane cuts four triple points. The dual complex has three vertices, three edges and four faces, hence rational H2 of dimension three. Generic differences of the four points on the elliptic edge need not be torsion over a transcendental algebraically closed field. An explicit isolated-hypersurface and small-resolution construction is being checked by frobenius to test whether this configuration retains ample negative exceptional geometry. No counterexample to ordinary top vanishing is claimed: failure of the sufficient period hypothesis is a different assertion.

The alternative Kollár plumbing route would require its precise contraction input. Root freshly reopened the primary paper https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-1/2014-1-004.pdf and read the introductory scope and Theorem2 proof in this window; earlier full Lemma15/16 reads remain explicitly recorded by the owner. Artin's cited contraction theorem was not freshly opened by root, and no theorem is imported through an unverified citation. The new explicit hypersurface route is intended to avoid that extra input, if its complete geometry passes.

## 4. The raw valuation detector fails on already certified proper relations

Let a constant SNC surface be defined over an algebraically closed field k0 of characteristic p, extend to k=algebraic closure of k0(u), and use a valuation over u=0. On the smooth strata, localization and purity suggest a normalized residue K_n(generic stratum) to K_(n−1)(constant stratum), compatible with rational closed-cover descent. After normalizing ramification indices it is tempting to seek a map K0(E_k)_Q to K_-1(E_k0)_Q and to use it against ordinary proper-family relations.

That raw target cannot work. In the already certified tetrahedral model, the shifted field summand gives a vertex class kappa{a,u} in K0(E_k)_Q. The explicit proper-symbol family, followed by its actual double boundary, makes this a defining J_K relation. Its valuation residue is ±kappa a in the vertex K1(k0)_Q term. Choose k0=algebraic closure of Fp(v) and a=v, so this residue is nonzero. If k0 is Fpbar the coefficient is torsion instead; the transcendental coefficient-field qualification is essential.

The natural full-product tetrahedral splitting makes the obstruction sharper. For a smooth proper connected parameter P over k0, its degree-minus-one group is the shifted K1(P)_Q term; every endpoint evaluation there is the same global unit, while the SK1 part evaluates to zero. Thus its ordinary smooth-proper endpoint differences are zero, although the residue of the degree-zero proper relation above is nonzero. Merely quotienting the residue target by its own ordinary degree-minus-one proper relations is therefore insufficient. A valid target must account for degenerations of the original proper parameter, including singular special fibres. The cycles owner is recording the exact localization normalization and source audit for this countertest.

This rules out the earlier naive assertion that residues of proper relations necessarily lie in a maximal proper subgroup of a semiabelian presentation of K_-1. The torus already receives nonzero residues of certified proper relations. It does not decide whether some further abelian quotient can survive all bad-reduction relations. No valuation-induced ordinary-quotient map has been proved here.

# Component-family research after C.3bt

GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), ChatGPT Pro mode; root; 19 November2026. Research remains incomplete. This note records methods and exact source scopes, not additional numbered theorems or qualifying progress.

## 1. Current main gate and the distinction that matters

C.3bt is fully certified and was counted once in review14. In the positive-characteristic algebraizable normal strict-local threefold branch, the remaining group is exactly

`T_E / (phi(J_K intersect S00) + phi(Q intersect S00))`.

All notation and the separate denominator intersections have the meanings in UK.7. The entire component-restriction kernel has already been removed. A graph family on a smooth component can nevertheless restrict to a nonzero class of CH0(C_e times P), even though its two endpoint restrictions vanish. Thus pointwise lifting, algebraic triviality on a stratum, and an actual globally compatible perfect family remain different assertions.

The new edge K1 families change a coherent lift after its component obstruction is zero. They do not themselves alter a nonzero edge K0 image of a prescribed component family. ## 2. Primary source readings and precise limits

### Friedlander–Walker

Friedlander, E. M., & Walker, M. E. (2002). Semi-topological K-theory using function complexes. *Topology, 41*(3),591–644. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0040-9383(01)00023-4 . The primary author PDF was opened at https://dornsife.usc.edu/ericmfriedlander/wp-content/uploads/sites/233/2023/06/24.pdf . Root read Definition1.1, Propositions1.2–1.3 and their complete proofs, and Theorem1.4 and its complete proof, author PDFpp3–6. The journal metadata was checked in the publisher search result and author's publication list; the direct publisher opening returned403.

Their parameter definition allows arbitrary smooth connected varieties and explicitly uses affine curves over an algebraically closed field. Theorem1.4 proves the rational Chern-character comparison for smooth X by applying ordinary Riemann–Roch also to X times the parameter. It does not establish the required proper-parameter comparison for a singular SNC surface. This source was inspected to test applicability; it is not a new input to C.3bt.

### Achter–Casalaina-Martin–Vial

Achter, J. D., Casalaina-Martin, S., & Vial, C. (2019). Parameter spaces for algebraic equivalence. *International Mathematics Research Notices, 2019*(6),1863–1893. Primary author version dated11September2019: https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~vial/abtriv.pdf . Root read the introductory Theorem1 statement, Definitions3.1/3.4, Lemma3.8 with its complete proof, Proposition3.11 and its complete proof, and Proposition3.14 with its complete displayed proof, PDFpp6,8–10. The publisher opening redirected to an inaccessible CDN. No complete supporting Bertini or whole-paper audit is claimed.

Lemma3.8 compactifies a parameter curve by the surjective restriction map on ordinary Chow groups. Proposition3.14 uses a symmetric product and the projective-bundle formula to replace a projective curve by its Picard variety. These are cycle-class comparisons; the closure supplied by Chow localization need not be perfect on E times the compact parameter. They therefore do not supply the missing SNC perfect-family extension.

### Krishna–Park

Krishna, A., & Park, J. (2013). Algebraic cobordism theory attached to algebraic equivalence. *Journal of K-Theory, 11*(1),73–112. https://doi.org/10.1017/is013001028jkt210 . Root obtained and read the primary arXiv1203.5508v2 PDF, dated7September2012, after the web opening failed. Read the introductory hypotheses and Theorems1.1–1.3 as statements, the complete Section2.2 definitions and Lemma2.4 proof, and Theorems8.1 and8.3 with their full displayed proofs, author pp4–5,20–21. Their invoked cobordism comparison theorems were not independently re-audited here.

This paper defines bundle equivalence using smooth projective parameter curves, but its singular-scheme comparison in Theorem8.3 is explicitly with the coherent-sheaf group G0 modulo those relations. K0 and G0 are identified there only for smooth X. Its base field is characteristic zero throughout. Neither a positive-characteristic theorem nor a singular perfect-K0 identification follows. The source supplies a useful distinction, not a vanishing theorem for UK.7.

## 3. Acquisition and retained failed attempts

`code/fetch_proper_parameter_sources.py` records all three acquisitions, exact URLs, UTC times, byte lengths, SHA256 hashes and pdftotext return codes. Its complete JSON and stdout are in `logs/proper_parameter_source_acquisition.json` and `.out`. The first program version failed before network access because requests was unavailable; that exact version and error output are retained. Other unsuccessful openings: the MSP zero-cycles-with-modulus PDF returned no readable lines; arXiv1203.5508 and itsv2 web routes returned DisabledError; CiteSeer returned403; ASARC's preprint page returned a Unicode decoding error. These are acquisition events, not mathematical evidence. The local successful arXiv acquisition supersedes only the availability failure.

## 4. Root method tests

**Surface Chow projectors.** It would be unsafe to assert that a transcendental surface projector makes every boundary-curve correspondence zero merely from cohomological weights. In contravariant conventions, CH²(S times C) contains correspondences from the surface motive to a curve motive. A projected transpose graph records the action of curve zero-cycles on the surface's Albanese kernel; for a surface with nontrivial such kernel this need not disappear. No complete projector vanishing was proved. This possible method was sent to the two-parameter reviewer with the direction-of-correspondence caution.

**Exceptional image alone.** The common negative-intersection relation removes degrees and component Albanese coordinates, but it cannot simply be asserted to absorb every Albanese-kernel cycle. A Picard-rank-one component with trivial Picard variety has only a one-dimensional rational divisor source, whose nonzero negative-normal intersection has nonzero degree. Its intersection with the degree-zero target can therefore be zero even when the surface's Albanese kernel is not. Actual proper-family relations are essential. This is a test of the proposed argument, not a newly constructed local counterexample.

**Blowing up graph-boundary intersections.** Suppose a graph curve in E_i meets the double curve E_i intersect E_j at q. Blowing up a curve in E_j through q can separate the strict graph from the old double curve and replace the crossing by a rational exceptional double curve in E_i'. However, the exceptional divisor that corrects the new rational-edge degree restricts to O(q) on the old double curve. The original Picard-valued error reappears. Tautological divisors on the added ruled component also have coupled degrees on its fibres and create a new boundary along the centre curve. No triangular correction or termination argument has been proved. This modification is not a reduction of UK.7.

**Compactified moduli of bundles.** Proper moduli spaces of semistable coherent sheaves do not themselves provide perfect families on a singular surface. A proof would need a suitable connected proper parameter contained in the locally free/perfect locus, with the prescribed endpoint K0 classes and controlled restriction data. Smooth-surface asymptotic irreducibility and codimension heuristics do not establish this for a reducible SNC surface. No such moduli theorem was used or assumed.

# Root independent review — the primitive exceptional-boundary lemma

AI-produced by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode), RESEARCH_SA06, /root. No priority claim. Full review completed 19 November 2026, approximately 15:19 UTC.

## Material actually read and exact conclusion

Read the complete original `agents/frobenius/C3_primitive_exceptional_boundary_draft.tex`, PB.1–18, in three bounded chunks, then the complete diff to the final `C3_primitive_exceptional_boundary.tex`. The final changes replace Step 3 by an integral primitive quotient, move the already required Picard-thickening and formal-existence citations into Step 4, and record the retained alternate proof. The initial attempt to print the full draft was truncated and was not counted as a reading; the subsequent three chunks cover the full text.

Outcome: PASS for the whole auxiliary proposition under its exact geometric hypotheses, for every m>=0, s>=1, and algebraically closed k of positive characteristic. This is not by itself a construction of a local counterexample. Actual ordinary families, the nonzero cup, the split principal target, and the required geometry remain assertions of the separately audited combined theorem.

## Relative class and whole Chow-kernel reduction

The sheaves used are ordinary Milnor-symbol sheaves. The exact relative sequence and its exponent-p kernel J_n give the unique relative lift in H^n(J_n) of every absolute class reducing to zero: the preceding H^(n−1)(V,K_n^M) is divisible by the previously fully checked Rost-localization argument, while H^n(J_n) is killed by p. This is the correct preceding cohomology degree. The relative conormal dlog map and its product identity were previously rederived including p=2. The product of a nil line bundle and fixed divisors has the stated ordered cup coefficient one, without a factorial.

The integral Chow decomposition of T×C follows by the projective-bundle formula and successive blow-ups of point-products. It retains Pic(C) torsion. Each cubic factor has integral basis 1,H,E_1,...,E_6,z, and every top class is an integral divisor polynomial. The projective-space factor is harmless for m=0 as well as m>0.

The elementary adjoint argument is valid on the full rational Tate lattice: the cubic chain 1,A,3z has squared norms 1,2,4 and lowering coefficients 2,2; primitive divisors carry weight zero and zero raising/lowering operators. On projective space the lowering coefficient is j(m−j+1). Their tensor commutator is weight 2j−2s−m. The norm identity gives injectivity of b in negative weight and of b² in weight at most −2; the endpoint weight −2 follows by applying the weight-zero identity to bv and then adjointness. Degree s−1 has weight −m−2, so both needed maps are injective for all m>=0. Since the integral groups are free, rational injectivity is enough for these specific integer equations; no integral hard Lefschetz assertion is invoked.

Write gamma=alpha+v[o]+eta, with eta in B_(s−1) tensor Pic^0(C). If L·gamma=0, its free equations are b alpha=0 and e alpha+bv=0, where e=deg K_C is a nonzero integer. Thus b²v=0, v=0, and alpha=0. The remaining equation is exactly b eta=0. Smith bases for the injective integral lattice map therefore describe the entire exceptional kernel as sum v_j Q_j with b v_j=d_j w_j and d_j Q_j=0. Nonunit invariant factors, including those divisible by p, are kept.

## Final integral saturation proof

The integral Chow ring is multigraded by the degrees on the projective-space and cubic factors. Only multidegree (0;1,...,1) can reach the specified Kunneth component of the twisted differential cup. Every anticanonical class A_i is primitive because its intersection with a line is one. Hence Lambda_i=Pic(W_i)/Z A_i and their tensor Lambda are finite free abelian groups.

Project the degree-s Chow lattice to that multidegree and then to Lambda. This defines the integral map Psi. A term of b v reaching that component necessarily inserts an A_i in a missing cubic factor; the projective-space term has the wrong degree. Thus Psi(bv)=0. Applying it to the exact Smith equation gives d_j Psi(w_j)=0, hence Psi(w_j)=0 in a free integer group. This occurs before reduction to characteristic p.

The selected coherent cup Phi factors through Psi. For each cubic, the restricted Euler sequence has the isomorphism k^4→H^0(A) on global sections and H^1(O)=0. Therefore H^1(Omega^1_(P3)(1)|W)=0. The ambient cotangent class of O(1) maps to dlog A, so multiplication by any section followed by this class is zero. Thus mu_A=0, and additivity in each integral Picard variable gives the factorization through every Lambda_i. Consequently Phi(w_j)=0 even when p divides d_j. This kills the saturation of the b-image; it does not assert that b is integrally split or that the full exceptional kernel vanishes.

## Retained Witt proof independently checked

The original Step 3 is also valid. A primitive lift of each cubic equation over W(k) is flat; smoothness near the special fibre and properness give a smooth projective lift. H^2(O_W)=0 permits every Picard basis element to lift through successive Witt thickenings, and projective formal existence algebraizes the system. One can choose a basis containing the primitive A and lift it as the hyperplane bundle.

The restricted Euler sequence is acyclic, and the conormal and hypersurface sequences identify H^1(Omega_W(A)) with H^2(O_W(−2A)) and H^3(P3,O(−5)), a free rank-four Witt module. These identifications commute with reduction. The lifted designated cup kills every b-image; its target Hom module has no integer torsion, so it also kills every w_j in the saturation. The final integral quotient proof avoids this lifting machinery. No error or withdrawn mathematical assertion is concealed by that simplification.

## Actual curve-line lifts and the additive vanishing

The factor cohomology gives H^2(V,L^n)=0 for every n>=1, H^1(V,L^n)=0 for n>=2, and H^1(V,L)=H^0(T,L_T) tensor H^1(C,K_C). The square-zero unit sequence lifts each individual curve line bundle through all infinitesimal neighbourhoods. Their ideals are exactly powers of the base maximal ideal by the hypothesis m_R O_Z=I_V. Projective formal existence over the completion gives a line bundle there. The finite presentation of the bundle and its inverse, regularity of the completion map, Popescu, and henselian lifting through a smooth algebra give an actual bundle on Z with its chosen first jet preserved. This only uses a finite list at any one application, not an algebraization of a Picard functor.

The canonical actual extension of K_C is O_Z(−V) tensor q*L_T^(−1). Its restriction is K_C, and this identity does not require a nonexistent projection Z→C. For any Q in Pic^0(C)(k), the product K-tilde·Q-tilde reduces to zero because both reduced factors come from the curve. Its absolute Milnor class therefore has a unique relative lift xi_Q. If the actual lift of Q is changed, the relative differential changes by a' cup dlog K_C. Both cohomological degree-one factors lie on C, so the change lies in the zero group H^2(C,K_C tensor Omega_C^1). The resulting F(Q)=tau_2(xi_Q) is well defined. Tensor products of lifts and uniqueness of relative lifts show that F is additive. Since Pic^0(C)(k) is divisible and the target has exponent p, F=0. This only claims vanishing of the relative differential, not of xi_Q itself.

## Exact exceptional identity and finite-stage comparison

If beta vanishes off V, localization gives beta=i_*gamma. Its zero restriction to V and self-intersection put gamma in the whole kernel just described. All lattice classes are actual divisor polynomials pulled from the smooth cellular T; their identities pull back as Chow-ring identities. The projection formula and O_Z(V)=q*L_T^(−1) tensor K-tilde^(−1) give the literal Chow identity PB.18. The first sum uses the nil bundles Q-tilde_j^(d_j); its projected relative differential vanishes by Phi(w_j)=0. The second sum uses xi_(Q_j) times the actual divisor polynomial v_j; its full relative differential vanishes by F=0 and symbol-product compatibility. Every summand reduces to zero, so uniqueness of relative lifts identifies their sum with the relative lift of the total class.

The finite list of line bundles and rational-equivalence witnesses descends to one pointed etale model. Properness permits a shrink on which the finite-type source is regular and hence smooth over perfect k. The pointed etale base change preserves the residue field and the quotient by m², so the actual E and all chosen jets remain fixed. Integral Milnor–Bloch and ring-product compatibility apply on that smooth model. Restriction to E then gives the desired absolute cup identity; uniqueness supplies the relative one. No comparison theorem on the nonreduced E, unproved cohomology/filtered-colimit interchange, or absolute-differential substitute is used. The projected beta invariant is nonzero by hypothesis, contradicting the computed boundary invariant.

### Record: notes/ROOT_PROPER_FAMILY_REATTACK_1638.md

# Actual proper-curve lifting: further attempted routes and exact boundaries

19 November 2026, 16:27–16:38 UTC. AI-produced by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), ChatGPT Pro mode, `/root`; effort setting not separately exposed. This is a research note, not a proved numbered conclusion.

## Fixed target

For the explicit tetrahedral strictly henselian normal threefold R, resolution Z and reduced exceptional divisor E, the independently checked FF and TS calculations give the exact obstruction to lifting a specified class on E×P, for a fixed smooth proper curve P. If kappa is the degree−2 dual-complex generator and xi belongs to K2(P)[1/p], its boundary is

    delta(kappa) external xi in K−1(Spec(R)×P)[1/p].

The class lifts as an actual virtual perfect class precisely when this boundary is zero. Every point specialization lifts, because Drinfeld gives K−1(R)=0 and FF.4 then gives K0(Z)[1/p]=K0(E)[1/p]. Nothing here replaces the fixed product by varying pointed etale neighborhoods, formal systems, or connected local Picard schemes.

## Three general shortcuts remain unjustified

Trying to globalize Drinfeld's finite-image idempotent argument across a proper curve introduces a finite-projective factorization problem. Finiteness of global endomorphisms over a proper base does not itself provide a global vector bundle through which the finite-image error factors, nor the lifting property of Hom from such a bundle. The affine proof has not been globalized by this observation.

A Frobenius power kills a fixed nilpotent obstruction in characteristic p, but a single power that kills every obstruction and then permits a formal object has not been proved. A Serre-vanishing bound for the relevant endomorphism sheaf may grow with its Frobenius pullback. Levelwise virtual-class lifting therefore cannot be substituted for a compatible bounded perfect object, its algebraization, or an actual family.

Weight and etale-realization arguments do not detect an arbitrary divisible K2(k) coefficient. In particular, the explicit proper-curve unramified-symbol construction already shows that a naive constant-weight argument against K2 variation on proper curves is invalid. Spreading the coefficients can introduce variation in the parameter curve itself. No such weight argument is used as an obstruction.

## Relative henselization along the proper curve

We tested the following possible route: henselize B=Spec(R)×P along its closed fibre P, use the dimension-one underlying space to show K−1(Bh)=0, lift to the henselization of Z×P, and algebraize. Each comparison needed here has to be established for actual nonconnective K-theory.

The first proposed Zariski argument was invalid. Devadas's *Henselian schemes in positive characteristic*, arXiv:2212.08644v4, Remark2.1.4, author p.9, explicitly distinguishes henselian pairs from henselian local rings. Its affine henselian localizations are generally larger than ordinary localizations, and its Zariski stalks need not be henselian at their whole maximal ideals. Thus Drinfeld's theorem cannot be applied to those stalks just from the relative henselization construction. An h-Nisnevich approach would still need K-theory descent, the correct stalk-continuity statement and a cohomological-dimension theorem. These were not supplied by the sources opened in this check.

The second proposed shortcut is also absent. We opened Devadas's published *GAGA for Henselian schemes* (2025) and read Theorem4.3.1 and its proof, Corollaries4.3.2–4.3.3, and the precise introduction and Section4.4 qualifications. The theorem algebraizes finitely presented subobjects of an already algebraizable finitely presented sheaf on a proper scheme. The corollary gives an exact fully faithful coherent-sheaf functor with essential image closed under subobjects and quotients. It does not assert essential surjectivity; the introduction expressly leaves the arbitrary positive-characteristic algebraization question unresolved. Accordingly, even a proof of K−1(Bh)=0 would leave the actual K0-class comparison back to Z×P unless the constructed class has an algebraizable presentation.

Fresh primary retrievals: `turn719149856view0`, `turn464094626view1`–`view2`, `turn800087522view0`, and the full foundations PDF `turn800087522view2`, with exact locators in `turn758872196view0`–`view1`. Existing Devadas bibliography entries are reused. Web searches for henselian-pair negative K-theory and rigidity found no directly applicable proper-family theorem; connective finite-coefficient rigidity was not substituted for a rational nonconnective assertion.

The agents are separately testing representatives by actual closed subschemes, where the proved henselian Chow theorem would apply. The existence of representatives with the required perfect K0 class is not assumed. No smaller main-task gate is claimed in this note.

For a smooth projective surface V with L=K_V and a generically finite separable morphism f:T→V from a smooth projective surface, the ramification section identifies K_T with f*K_V tensor O_T(R_f). The traced coherent product

is Serre-dual to multiplication by the ramification section

The two selected odd-characteristic quadrics are smooth because ±i avoid0,1,−1, including characteristic3. Their complete intersection has the smooth equation y²=x³−x on its affine chart and independent gradients at its unique point at infinity. The characteristic-two pair has invertible gradient matrices and equation y²+y=x³, with the same independent infinity gradients. Thus the elliptic quartic and rational quadrics exist in every stated characteristic. The generic hyperplane and sextic impose simultaneous nonempty open transversality and nonvanishing conditions; the linear systems used are the full very ample systems, not inseparable sublinear systems.

The squarefree initial form makes the separated local hypersurface reduced. The saturated blowup charts give exactly the displayed equation, with Cartier radial exceptional ideal and no extra vertical component. At its closed fibre, the only nonregular points are the48 ordinary nodes arising from simple sextic zeros on double curves, with24,12,12 allocations. The ordered component blowups are isomorphisms wherever those Weil divisors are Cartier. The two explicitly saturated node charts are regular in every characteristic. The total reduced divisor is the pullback of the first radial exceptional Cartier divisor, as the small resolution has no exceptional divisors. Its negative line bundle is the pullback of O(1). The component weights2,1,0 give degrees1,2,1 on every small exceptional P1, while all other fibres are points. The dual boundary matrix has four identical oriented face columns, so its second homology has rank3 and the indicated face differences form a basis. The elliptic periods are q_j−q_1. The incidence of two ordered distinct elliptic points and a hyperplane containing their secant is an irreducible P1 bundle over the ordered-pair space and generically finite over hyperplane space. Thus every geometric generic ordered pair avoids every graph of translation by a constant point. All torsion points of the constant elliptic curve are constant, since each multiplication kernel is finite even in characteristic p. These differences are nontorsion and remain so after the independent sextic extension and the marked-curve-preserving resolutions.

### Milne normalization checks

Theorem1.6 in both the supplied and current PDF prints S^(2d)(X×X,ell), while its proof uses the generalized eigenvalue-one space in H^(2d)(X×X,Qell(d)). With the source's definition of S^r, the hypothesis needed is **S^d(X×X,ell)**. The corrected claim has the following elementary proof. Over a splitting field, let V_a be a generalized a-eigenspace of Frobenius on H^r(X). Poincaré duality identifies the corresponding reciprocal block with V_a^*. Their tensor is End(V_a), and Frobenius acts by conjugation. If a nontrivial unipotent Jordan factor U occurred, conjugation by U would be a nontrivial unipotent operator on End(V_a): an operator commuting with every endomorphism is scalar, and a scalar unipotent operator is the identity. The hypothesis S^d makes that conjugation the identity, a contradiction. Hence every block is semisimple. We do not treat the printed top-degree hypothesis as an unconditional proof of general Frobenius semisimplicity.

The definition of equivalence of a p^(n1)-structure pi1 and a p^(n2)-structure pi2 on printedp4 uses pi1^(n1 N)=pi2^(n2 N). Base change requires the crossed powers **pi1^(n2 N)=pi2^(n1 N)**, as the preceding Frobenius discussion on printedp2 correctly states. For example, H²(P¹) over Fp has pi1=p; over Fp² it has pi2=p². The crossed equality holds, whereas the printed uncrossed equality would require p^N=p^(4N), impossible for N>0. No power-change argument here uses the uncrossed formula.

### Debarre–Ein–Lazarsfeld–Voisin version checks

The supplied early Corollary2.2 prints 2≤k≤n. Its preceding argument and the published Corollary2.2 have the correct range **2≤k≤n−2**. At k=n−1 and k=n the claimed strict cone difference does not occur. The early proof of Theorem2.1 also phrases a claim about nonnegative combinations of CM-lattice one-forms too strongly for the subsequent rank-one forms. The published proof correctly takes the **closure** of the convex cone of rank-one forms arising from CM-lattice directions. To check the step directly, the fraction field of the CM order is dense in C; approximate each coefficient of a one-form by elements of that field, clear their common denominators, and rescale the rank-one forms by the positive square of that denominator. Their limits give every rank-one positive form. Pullback of the origin along the corresponding map E^n→E supplies the algebraic divisor; closedness gives the asserted pseudoeffective limit. Thus the published result is supported without the faulty early finite-combination wording.

# Root independent audit of the supersingular finite-torsion route

**PASS for the stated method exclusions and bounded finite-torsion construction; no main-gate movement.** Credit: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), ChatGPT Pro mode; /root; effort setting not separately exposed. 19 November 2026, 20:35–20:38 UTC. No priority claim.

We read the entire `agents/real_weil/C4_SUPERSINGULAR_BT1_LIFTING_RESEARCH.md`, SHA256 `734f3b792c565049f5187e0d7eafec144307578d3bdc59cf5f4e359b3507fc35`, including BT.1–BT.9, all limitations and the exact source-read ledger. We read both complete supplementary programs and their complete printed summaries. We did not rerun them and do not claim manual inspection of every retained long JSON coordinate.

The Hom descent proof is valid after finite-type spreading: the difference from one k0-valued fibre is a map from a product with proper abelian source, zero on both coordinate axes, so rigidity makes it zero. Given v u=[n] with p not dividing n through a constant B, the endomorphism u v is constant. Its image is therefore a constant abelian subvariety C. The reverse isogeny C to A has kernel in the finite etale group C[n]; over algebraically closed k0 that subgroup descends. Thus A is constant. The distinction between this finite etale kernel and an arbitrary infinitesimal subgroup is essential.

If actual maps split A[p], their composite has kernel disjoint from A[p]. Its positive-dimensional identity component would contain p-torsion, and a nonzero finite p-primary kernel would also have p-torsion. Both are impossible, so it is an isogeny of degree prime to p. The usual complementary isogeny then gives a prime-to-p multiplication factorization. This proves that finite-level splitting maps for a nonconstant A cannot both lift through a constant B.

For k0=Fpbar and k=algebraic closure of k0(t), the subgroup H_t in alpha_p^3 with tangent line (1,t,t squared) does not descend. If A_t=E^3/H_t were constant, its quotient map would descend by Hom rigidity, contradicting the kernel calculation. It is supersingular by its actual isogeny from E^3. This is a complete witness against the constant-Jacobian lifting method, not against all Jacobian factorizations.

The constant-complement argument also checks. Pulling a hypothetical prime-to-p isogeny A_t times C to its dual back through the degree-p quotient gives a constant isogeny h with p-adic degree valuation2. On the height-one subgroup alpha_p^3, its three constant columns satisfy b1+t b2+t squared b3=0. Coefficient independence forces all columns zero. The faithful height-one restricted-Lie description is needed to conclude that h kills the subgroup scheme, rather than merely its tangent vectors or rational points. The subgroup has order p cubed, contradicting the degree valuation2. The required height-one faithfulness is a standard explicit foundational input, not a fact proved by the bounded matrix program.

For an elliptic complement, the supersingular case is constant; the ordinary case has no cross homomorphisms to the supersingular factor, so the polarization is block diagonal. Finally, an actual prime-to-p factorization through a principally polarized fourfold gives an elliptic connected complement and an addition isogeny with kernel injecting into A_t[n]. Its degree is prime to p, and pulling back the principal polarization contradicts the preceding result. This justifies the proposed fourfold-bridge exclusion without assuming a universal Prym theorem. Larger nonconstant complements remain outside the argument.

The finite word construction also matches its source. Primitive words of lengths2–6 occur in distinct orbit summands of the Jacobians of y^(p^lambda-1)=x(1-x), without the p>3 hypothesis needed for the source's different nonprimitive-word assertion. The multiplicity floor(6/lambda) covers every height-six local-local multiset. The exact counts1,2,3,6,9, the16 multisets, six balanced multisets, and dimensions62 and555 agree with the inspected code. The successful runtimes were0.0008756179959164001 and0.0005373790045268834 seconds. These certify only the bounded word/coefficient arithmetic.

## Complete reading and independent reconstruction

The root read the complete current HK proof, its complete research/source/typography note, the complete Frobenius independent receipt, the complete relative-curve countermodel, and the complete semistable specialization note. The following are independent checks, not merely a relay of an owner verdict.

For HK, an exact component degree-zero cycle is moved into a smooth transverse curve and represented by the exact pushforward of a degree-zero line-bundle difference. The already proved VE lemma applies to all curve/edge intersection points simultaneously. Its actual zero K1 restrictions survive the regular component pushforward by supported Tor-independent base change. Enlarging supports to include neighboring curve intersections does not change zero. The closed support avoids every triple point; taking the fibre of the actual ambient and complementary descent diagrams therefore leaves a genuine two-column supported fibre sequence. Its long exact sequence gives an actual K1 lift. Endpoint base change and projection give exactly the required component endpoints. This uses neither a direct perfect pushforward to the singular total E nor a K1 Adams decomposition. The arbitrary lift ambiguity has zero component image. The construction is on one fixed smooth proper parameter curve and is rational only at the singular descent/denominator steps, as stated.

For RC, both displayed elliptic equations are smooth in their stated characteristics: in odd characteristic the discriminant is a power of two, and in characteristic two the y derivative is one. The generic point q over the algebraic closure of the elliptic function field is nontorsion, since each finite torsion scheme has only constant geometric points. The relative long exact sequence and the rank/determinant decomposition of a smooth curve give the surjection onto Pic(A)_Q. A genuine relative K0 family has a determinant trivial at both entire marked parameter sections. Normalized Poincare classification gives a parameter map to the elliptic Picard variety whose pullback of the nontorsion evaluation bundle is trivial. If the map were nonconstant it would be finite flat, even if inseparable; the norm identity would force that bundle to be torsion. Thus the map is constant and every actual proper relative endpoint relation has zero Picard image.

VE supplies a genuine K1 family with both whole marked restrictions zero, hence an actual relative K1 lift. Its endpoint difference has the exact prescribed component u([L]-1), independently of relative lift ambiguities. All data and equality witnesses descend to a finite extension of k0(u); enlarging that extension ensures the two marked endpoints and the geometrically connected parameter descend as well. The normalization of the u-adic valuation has residue field k0 because that field is algebraically closed. Vertical purity applies to the regular pair A and D over the resulting DVR, and Tor-independent marked-section base change identifies their relative residue target. Unit valuation and the projection formula give e([L]-1); division by the ramification index yields the nonzero Picard class L. Therefore the proposed general residue principle fails even after killing the complete component kernel in this relative-curve setting. This does not realize the functor as a negative exceptional-surface summand and does not settle UK.7.

For SL, a nonzero rational Picard vector has nonzero self-tensor by a linear functional, whereas the exterior product of the corresponding degree-zero elliptic first Chern class with itself is zero: pull back the line bundle along addition, use the normalized multiplicativity, and square. Division by two occurs in rational Chow groups, so characteristic two causes no exception. This proves the failure of a general tensor-injectivity shortcut. It does not assert an E-specific realization.

For the explicit cover, at a zero of a the local equation is u(g-1)^2=(u-1)^2zg. Near either main/bridge crossing it has regular equation u=unit·zg; at any other bridge point the z derivative is invertible. At the pole a0 the coefficient of g (or its inverse) is invertible. The special fibre is therefore reduced semistable with two main copies joined through one bridge for each simple zero. Its graph has first Betti number n-1, so it need not be a tree. Generic smoothness follows from the same charts, the separability of h0 (its simple zeros rule out a pth power), and avoidance of its finite constant critical-value set by the transcendental branch value; characteristic two uses the displayed separable quadratic/Artin–Schreier form. None of this resolves the two actual K1-lift ambiguities in the proposed node comparison; SL.3 is not promoted.

# Top ordinary quotient: semipurity and a tetrahedral exceptional fibre

AI-produced by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode), /root, 19 November 2026, 15:26–15:31 UTC. Research only: no numbered conclusion or main-gate movement.

## New primary source and its exact limitation

Opened and read Weber (2012), *Purity of boundaries of open complex varieties*, Journal of Singularities, 4, 171–179, DOI10.5427/jsing.2012.4j. The full nine-page journal PDF is https://www.journalofsing.org/volume4/weber.pdf . Proposition3 and Lemmas9–10 identify the lower-weight boundary terms. Theorems11–14 and their Section7 proofs give the purity bounds; Remark13 permits localization at a boundary component, and Remark16 discusses the isolated-point case. For an isolated N-dimensional complex singularity the relevant exceptional cohomology is pure in degrees at least N. This is a complex rational-cohomology statement. It neither identifies Chow kernels nor supplies actual ordinary families on a resolution. The separate author URL https://www.mimuw.edu.pl/~aweber/ps/purend.pdf returned403; the source's reference13 identifies arXiv0809.1885, not yet separately opened by root.

Searches also used the exact phrases local Chow group algebraic equivalence punctured spectrum; exceptional divisor K0 Chow simple normal crossings; and isolated singularities algebraic equivalence one-cycles. The returned numerical-equivalence and singular-zero-cycle references did not directly prove the ordinary top-quotient assertion. They were not treated as interchangeable with it.

## Why the simple multiplicative extension failed

The earlier Pm×triangle attempt would have top-edge unit gluing. Along a double stratum its total normal line cannot be negative when both attaching normal lines are trivial. The required smoothing coefficient acquires zeros; resolving the resulting uv=tau w points introduces divisor classes that hit the intended top-edge degrees. Semipurity offers a cohomological explanation for that obstruction in dimension at least three, but does not close the ordinary Chow gate.

For an SNC exceptional divisor E=sum E_i with a positive exceptional combination D=sum a_i E_i and −D ample on E, root derived a possible elementary check of the corresponding numerical edge obstruction. If antisymmetric coefficients x_ij satisfy sum_j x_ij[D_ij]=0 numerically on each E_i, intersect with D_ij and an ample (d−2)-power. Summing the resulting equations with weights1/(a_i a_j) gives, for each triple, the square

    (a_k x_ij − a_j x_ik + a_i x_jk)^2/(a_i a_j a_k).

The left side is sum_(i<j) x_ij² deg(D|D_ij·h^(d−2))/(a_i a_j), negative for any nonzero x, whereas the triple-intersection coefficients on the square side are nonnegative. This suggests surjectivity of the top-degree numerical edge restriction map. The indexing for disconnected strata and the full passage from this numerical map to the K-theory descent complex remain to be written and checked. This note does not register that proposed lemma.

## A different candidate and the actual obstruction

The three-dimensional affine hypersurface with leading tangent cone xyzw and a degree-five correction G5 suggests a tetrahedral exceptional divisor. Choose G5 nonzero at the four coordinate vertices. # C.4ab: a partial Fourier test for the residual surface case

**Status: proved exact reformulation and method exclusion. No main-gate movement.**

Let A be a complex abelian surface with primitive type-(1,2) polarization L, NS(A)=ZL, and scalar rational Hodge endomorphisms on H1(A) and on T(A). For an integral codimension-two correspondence Z on A^2, let t, s, n be its scalar actions on H1, T, and NS. The primitive norm-four lattice gives n-s=4k. An integral relative Fourier-Mukai K-class E_Z then produces an actual integral curve c2(E_Z)P on A x Ahat, with mixed Matsusaka scalar

    m_Z = 3(t^2-s) - (n-s)/2 = 3(t^2-s)-2k.

Its parity is t-s. Such an odd scalar, together with the already proved universal scalar2, splits A off a product of Jacobians. Conversely any actual splitting gives an integral correspondence with t=1,s=0 by pulling and pushing normalized Poincare divisors on A x C. Thus this is an exact integral criterion, not an unproved promise that a new surface supplies the desired class.

The Bastianelli-Pirola-Stoppino Galois-closure surface is the residual fibre product over a rational ruled surface. The trace-minus-diagonal formula gives t=s=-1, so its partial Fourier transform is excluded. This calculation is stronger than citing only its Albanese variety: a transformed K-class is not automatically covered by the earlier divisor-pushforward method exclusion.

## Reconstruction of NP.1–NP.8

The odd-characteristic quadric gradient determinant is minus four times lambda(lambda−1)(lambda+1), and at either square root of minus one it is nonzero in every odd characteristic, including characteristic three. In characteristic two both displayed gradient matrices are invertible. The affine complete-intersection equations give the indicated smooth Weierstrass curves. Their unique infinity point has independent gradients. This checks the smooth constant elliptic quartic and the rationality of both smooth quadrics without characteristic-zero specialization.

The generic hyperplane meets the quadrics and their elliptic intersection transversely, yielding two smooth conics and four distinct triple points. The independently generic sextic avoids the triple locus and has simple zeros along each double curve. These are simultaneous nonempty first-jet open conditions in the displayed parameter spaces. The resulting numbers of nodes, 24+12+12, are correct.

The affine hypersurface has squarefree initial form. The associated graded ring is therefore reduced; separatedness of the maximal-ideal filtration implies reducedness of the local ring. On the Rees blowup, the saturated chart equation Q1 Q2 H=tG has no additional vertical component. Its exceptional ideal is invertible and the ambient components are pure dimension three. Every ambient component meets the closed fibre by properness over the local base; its Cartier closed-fibre intersection contains a surface component. At a generic double-curve point with G a unit the ambient ring is regular, so the two adjacent exceptional components lie in a single ambient irreducible component. The connected triangle forces all ambient components to coincide. Reducedness then gives a domain. This argument does not assume irreducibility of a generic affine polynomial.

All singularities on the closed fibre are exactly the transverse models xy=tz. Blowing the earlier component ideal (x,t) has the two stated saturated regular charts, in every characteristic. It blows up that component at the node, leaves the other component and the marked double curve unchanged, and introduces only a small exceptional P1, no new exceptional surface or triple stratum. The first component receives 36 point blowups, the second 12, and the third remains P2. At all unchanged double and triple points G is a unit, so the ambient space remains regular and the divisor remains SNC.

The completed projective modification is regular along the whole closed fibre. Its nonregular locus is closed because all schemes are excellent; its proper image would be a nonempty closed subset of a local scheme and hence would contain the closed point. It is therefore empty. The modification is an isomorphism on the puncture. The original hypersurface is Cohen–Macaulay and regular in codimension one, so it is normal. Strict henselization preserves the stated regularity, normality and geometric fibre; the residue field is already algebraically closed.

For A=2E1+E2, the degree of O(−A) on the small exceptional lines is respectively 1, 2, 1. This follows directly from the tautological blowup line and the local principal total divisor. The other fibres of the small resolution are points. Fibrewise ampleness for a proper morphism, without a flatness assumption, makes O_E(−A) relatively ample. Since O_E(−E) is pulled back from the original ample hyperplane bundle, composition of ample bundles gives O_E(−ME−A) ample for all sufficiently large M. Every coefficient of D=ME+A is strictly positive. No analytic or Artin contraction result is used.

The dual boundary matrix has four identical triangular columns and rank one, giving H2 of dimension three and the stated face-difference basis. The ordered distinct-pair hyperplane incidence is a P1-bundle over C² minus its diagonal. It is irreducible, dominates C² and is generically finite over the hyperplane parameter space. All torsion points of this constant elliptic curve lie over the original algebraic closure of the finite field, including the points of nonreduced p-primary torsion schemes. A generic pair cannot lie on any graph of translation by such a point. Its difference is non-torsion. Independently adjoining the sextic coefficients and performing small resolutions away from the triple locus do not change that statement.

## Separate NP.9 Picard-span argument

The Koszul resolution of the (2,2) complete intersection, twisted by six, proves surjectivity of the sextic restriction map using the exact projective-space cohomology groups. Thus the induced degree-24 divisor is generic in its complete linear system, even after fixing an algebraic closure of the hyperplane coefficient field.

The ordered fixed-sum degree-24 divisor space on the elliptic curve is C^23. Removing the diagonals gives an irreducible nonempty open with free constant S24 action and quotient the reduced-divisor open of the complete linear system. The resulting generic extension is therefore S24-Galois in every characteristic; divisibility of 24! by the characteristic does not obstruct a free constant finite étale torsor. Adding the independent restriction-kernel coefficients preserves the permutation action. Projection to any two ordered roots is dominant, so every root difference is non-torsion.

The Picard generators of E1 and E2 are their constant quadric rulings and their exceptional point divisors. Exactly the 24 first-component exceptional curves lying over the elliptic edge restrict to its individual roots; every other exceptional curve is disjoint from that edge. This identifies the complete rational component Picard span, not merely a chosen subring.

If a multiple of a hyperplane period lay in that span, clearing rational denominators and then killing the remaining torsion would give an actual integral Picard equality. A transposition of two sextic roots fixes the hyperplane period and all constant ruling classes. Subtraction forces the two corresponding integer coefficients equal, since their root difference is non-torsion. All 24 coefficients are consequently equal. Their sum is the constant line bundle O_C(6); the resulting degree-zero constant line bundle is torsion over the algebraic closure of the finite field. This contradicts the non-torsion hyperplane period. The permutation and torsion arguments therefore prove NP.9 with its literal scope.

6. **Exact endpoint normalization.** At an endpoint the Cartier sequence expresses the p-power divisor class as a sum of twists on a finite Artinian scheme. All those twists are trivial, so the multiple identity holds in perfect K₀ itself. The immersions are regular. Division by the resulting integer is allowed in the rational statement. The omitted gamma-(d+1) class restricts to zero on the projective d-dimensional exceptional scheme.

7. **Ordinary relation subgroup.** The point restriction isomorphism FF.4 is dimension-free. Its injectivity follows from the rank-coordinate map from K₀(R), and its surjectivity from Drinfeld's henselian-local K₋₁ vanishing combined with the exact KST/GH comparison. Lambda compatibility and distinct rational Adams weights identify the top gamma piece. The inverse nilpotent comparison on the exceptional products preserves the rational gamma filtration. Endpoint lifting gives one inclusion of ordinary relation groups; inverse rational Chern character on a smooth finite-type model gives the other. Closing finitely many horizontal cycle components on a proper parameter compactification and on the fixed resolution preserves the selected refined fibres. This gives precisely AE.13–14.

**Reviewer:** `/root/cycles`.  **Full proof check completed:** 2026-11-19

lifting theorem for an actual fixed smooth proper parameter curve.  It is
not a theorem algebraizing arbitrary formal vector bundles.  Its
tetrahedral consequence is a restricted example; this receipt does not
assert a universal local Chow theorem or any higher restriction
surjectivity result.

## 1. Exact primary source reread

I freshly opened the complete author PDF of Charles Weibel's *The K-book*,
Chapter II, at
<https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~weibel/Kbook/Kbook.II.pdf>.

* Corollary 8.8.2, author p. 83, states the special lambda-ring structure

  I did not independently open either cited original in this check.

Retrieval references retained in the session are `turn101621020view0`,
`turn800934455view0`, and `turn800934455view1`.  The references are audit
identifiers, not substitutes for the bibliographic source.

raw-Chow draft, and the retained proper-curve field-symbol lemma.  Their
previously certified primary inputs are reused; this receipt does not
claim a fresh opening of Drinfeld, Geisser–Hesselholt, or Quillen.

## 2. Perfect gamma classes on the singular parameter product

The argument stays in vector-bundle/perfect K_0 throughout.  The ample
line bundle gives the resolution property.  The positive-bundle
replacement is valid: from a generating surjection for `V^dual L^m`,
dualization gives an embedding of `V` in a sum of positive lines, whose
quotient is a globally generated bundle tensored with `L^m`.  Products
with first-jet generating sections of `L^m` supply the required jets.

The lambda-ring identity for gamma-two of a difference has the stated
cross terms.  The Hilbert–Burch sequence is locally verified by the
invertible minor and a regular sequence `(a,b)`.  Its perfect class has
degree-two term `gamma^2([A]-rank A)`.  The flag splitting argument
therefore proves the congruence in the gamma filtration without passing
to G_0 or discarding a Cartan-kernel class.

The first-jet incidence argument has the correct dimensions.  On a
smooth stratum of dimension `d`, rank drop has codimension two, and
failure of transversality at this rank has total codimension at least
`d+1`.  Deeper rank drop has codimension six.  The component strata,
double strata, triple strata, and both chosen endpoint fibres give only
finitely many such conditions.  The endpoint curves are finite regular
immersions in `D`.  The full curve need not be flat over every point of
`P`; the proof only requires its two specified endpoint intersections.

## 3. An actual regular hypersurface containing the curve

For a sufficiently high relatively ample twist, the conormal rank-two
bundle on the curve has a section nowhere zero on its reduction.
The rank-two/one-dimensional incidence count is sufficient.  Locally
the resulting equation is a combination of `(a,b)` with a unit
coefficient, so the curve becomes Cartier in the hypersurface `H`.

At a double normal-crossing point, the two original equations have
independent differentials along the double stratum.  Consequently the
chosen nonzero conormal combination has nonzero ambient differential.
The same is true on a component stratum; the curve avoids triple
strata.  Away from the curve the chosen hypersurface is transverse to
all strata.  This proves regularity of its actual lifted ambient
hypersurface `W` along the entire closed fibre.  Excellence and
properness over the local base then give regularity everywhere.

The additional incidence condition excluding a whole component
`E_i x {v}` for every `v` makes the defining equation a fibrewise
nonzerodivisor.  Thus `H` and `W` are flat over `P`.  The argument uses
finite-type strata over `k`; relative Serre vanishing then lifts the
chosen section to the fixed projective scheme `Z x P`.  No moving
henselian parameter neighbourhood is substituted for that fixed product.

## 4. Line-bundle lifting and exact endpoints

The ideal of `H` in `W` is invertible and its restriction is relatively
ample for `H -> P`.  Relative Serre vanishing and the fact that `P` is a
curve give `H^2(H,L^n)=0` for all sufficiently large `n`.  Each of the
finitely many earlier square-zero obstruction groups is killed by `p`.
Raising the current compatible line bundle to the `p`th power before
each such step gives one finite total power and then an infinite
compatible system with no further increase in exponent.

Projective existence algebraizes that system over the completed base.
Algebraizing the inverse and using full faithfulness verifies that the
result is an invertible sheaf.  Popescu descent and henselian lifting
match a single finite quotient containing all of `H`; hence they retain
the entire proper parameter curve, not merely independent endpoint
classes.  Cofinality of the exceptional ideal and the maximal-ideal
adic systems is sufficient here.

All endpoint intersections used in the proof are Tor independent.
The finite endpoint scheme `C_u` is Artinian, so its line bundles are
trivial.  The Cartier geometric-series identity therefore gives the
exact equality

`j_*(1-[O(-p^e C_u)]) = p^e [O_{C_u}]`

in perfect K_0 of the singular divisor.  No pushforward
compatibility of gamma filtrations is needed.  The omitted gamma-three
class restricts to zero on the two-dimensional reduced exceptional
scheme by the exact Weibel dimension theorem.  This proves EL.1.

## 5. Tetrahedral consequence

The rational nilpotent lift from `E x P` to `D x P` has rank zero.
For its integral multiple at an endpoint, square-zero and weight-two
give the stated identity `gamma^2(Na_u)=-Na_u`.  Thus the endpoint theorem
applies without any weight decomposition of the whole group `K_2(P)`.
The already proved point-parameter K_0 isomorphism identifies the lifts
uniquely.  The second Chern-character component of the actual fixed
product family gives an ordinary algebraic-equivalence relation on `Z`.

I reread the proper-curve symbol construction, including characteristic
two, the tame residues, and the zero specialization at `(0,1)`.  Together
with the audited TC quotient by the four exceptional degree coordinates,
it gives the stated vanishing of the rational ordinary top quotient for
this ordered tetrahedral construction.  No extension to all isolated
threefold singularities has been inferred.

## 6. Verification limits

This was a complete mathematical reread and a targeted fresh primary
source audit.  No new finite program was run, and no numerical test is
being used to certify the geometric proof.  The broader main high-degree
restriction-surjectivity gate remains unchanged by this receipt.

## Full proof check

The homomorphism associated with a one-cycle is algebraic: a finite signed representative by integral curves can be normalized, and each normalized smooth proper curve supplies Picard pullback and Albanese pushforward. These maps depend on the cycle class, and pointwise equality determines the abelian-variety homomorphism. The minus sign in mu=−kappa is the same curve-autoduality sign verified for C.3bo and does not acquire an extra dimension-dependent sign.

The mixed complete-intersection construction is correct. At each stage the ambient dimension is at least two. Serre duality turns H1(L^(−b)) into the dual of H^(n−1)(omega tensor L^b), and Serre vanishing kills this for a sufficiently high exponent chosen after the preceding cuts. Smooth connected high sections exist in every characteristic. Thus H1(O) restriction is injective at every step, and restriction of reduced Picard varieties has finite kernel even if the unreduced Picard schemes are nonsmooth. The final curve represents exactly the product of the chosen exponents times the mixed one-cycle. Its theta pullback gives a positive multiple of the displayed mixed homomorphism as a polarization. The n=1 convention is correct and agrees with the principal curve polarization.

For an arbitrary first divisor M, the construction as a difference of ample divisor classes proves symmetry without falsely calling M ample. The common H on E is used exactly where needed: its two restrictions coincide on each double stratum. The off-diagonal zero-cycle has c1(L_i|C) times H^(d−2), of codimension d−1 on the (d−1)-dimensional stratum. Its Albanese pushforward is dual to Picard restriction. I independently expanded the weighted identity: the diagonal double-stratum terms cancel and the edge-difference terms produce precisely the negative off-diagonal blocks. Higher strata add no terms to this pairwise intersection identity.

A common multiple of every diagonal and edge mixed polarization is represented by a product of theta line bundles pulled back from actual complete-intersection Jacobians. The diagonal maps already have finite kernel, so the total map is finite onto its image. Finite pullback makes the theta product ample. This proves the isogeny without Hodge theory, standard conjectures, or a separability assumption.

The all-dimensional degree matrix is also correctly typed. Its off-diagonal entry is the degree of H^(d−1) on the double stratum, and symmetry uses the global H. Multiplying by the positive exceptional weights gives strictly negative weighted row sums. The displayed quadratic identity proves negative definiteness and hence rational invertibility. It therefore removes every component-degree coordinate before the Albanese reduction.

The Picard input is an actual family. The normalized Poincare line bundle on E_i times a smooth proper curve is multiplied by the fixed H_i^(d−2), then properly pushed into the regular product Z times that same curve. This is a codimension-d cycle family with the required endpoint difference. C.3bn/AE.13, or the inverse rational Chern character on a finite smooth model, places its restriction in the actual perfect relation subgroup. No perfect pushforward from E_i directly into the singular E is assumed. Surjectivity on algebraically closed points of the proved isogeny supplies every component Albanese coordinate. The last subtraction by u in the common Picard-family subgroup separates the two denominator summands exactly, as in C.3bo.

## Integral rank and determinant

The incidence dimension argument is valid for a generated bundle of rank at least two on the closed smooth integral curve. A nonzero vector in the complement of the incidence image lifts through the coefficient field. Properness over the local base makes the actual zero locus empty, since every nonempty closed subset of that base contains the closed point. The resulting subbundle has locally free quotient, so induction gives the claimed line filtration. The ample-line-bundle hypothesis supplies the vector-bundle description of perfect K0.

For either high-twist section of a line bundle, the fibrewise effective-Cartier criterion applies at every closed-fibre point. The complement of the resulting open locus is again proper over the local base and misses its closed point, hence is empty. The divisors are finite because their closed fibres are finite. Their coordinate rings are semilocal; a rank-one projective module over a semilocal ring is free. Consequently all line twists on their supported perfect classes are trivial.

I checked the twists in NK.3 explicitly. The Cartier sequence gives `[L]-1=[L] [O_D]` for the zero divisor of a section of L. The semilocal restriction makes this `[O_D]`. Subtract for L=M H^n and L=H^n, then multiply by H^(-n); the finite-support twists again disappear. This is exactly the displayed difference `[M]-1=[O_D+]-[O_D-]`. Multiplying by another line difference gives zero by the projection formula. There is no use of purity for a nonperfect coherent sheaf.

Line generation and the square-zero augmentation ideal then make Pic(B) isomorphic to the rank-zero subgroup. Expanding the gamma series of a sum and difference of line elements proves the vanishing of F_gamma^2 integrally. The claimed Adams polynomial follows on the two explicit summands. Neither step assumes a rational eigenspace decomposition on arbitrary K-groups.

## Normal modification, exact sequence and endpoints

For the proper birational map over a normal domain, regular functions lie in the fraction field and belong to every height-one valuation ring; equivalently their finite algebra of global functions is integral over the normal base. This proves g_*O=O. Tensoring the finite affine Cech equalizer over the coefficient field proves the same assertion after the fixed product with P. The elementary projection formula then proves Picard injectivity. Rank and determinant on the source alone suffice for K0 injectivity; no corresponding description of K0 of the regular modification is used.

I reread the entire `C3_fixed_family_negative_K.tex`, including the KST pro-exact sequence, GH nilpotent invariance after inverting p and TT finite-cover descent. Its every-degree fixed-product exact sequence gives NK.8 under precisely the displayed hypotheses. Source K0 injectivity kills the connecting obstruction, and the parameter K1 contribution is the restriction of its actual pullback to Z×P. Thus the whole prescribed K1 class lifts after inverting p, in every dimension covered by these hypotheses.

For a point, exactness applied to the pair (a,0) gives an element of K1(R) whose residue is zero. This verifies NK.9a, including its reverse containment. It does not say that every unit image has zero restriction. Commutative local K1 is the unit group, on which Adams psi^2 acts by multiplication by 2. If the exceptional endpoint is exactly u beta and beta has weight two, the endpoint discrepancy of an arbitrary lift is therefore killed by psi^2-2. The desired product has eigenvalue 8. The coefficient 1/6 in NK.10 is correct, and its application to the actual family gives the literal desired endpoint difference.

This receipt does not certify a new combined local construction or its geometric choices.

## 1. Exact relative class and the entire Chow kernel

I rechecked the locally split rank-one square-zero Milnor sequence, the exponent-(p) kernel, and the canonical conormal differential map, using the previously independently audited all-degree auxiliary.  Divisibility of (H^{n-1}(V,\mathcal K_n^M)) makes the relative cohomology map injective.  Thus an absolute class reducing to zero has a unique relative lift.  This uniqueness is used correctly; it is not replaced by a choice-dependent first-order class.

The integral Chow decomposition follows from the explicit point-blow-up and projective-bundle formulas with arbitrary products.  It retains the complete Picard group of the curve.  I independently rederived the elementary positive-adjoint argument: multiplication by (b) is injective in negative weight, and its square is injective at weight at most (-2), including the weight-(-2) endpoint.  At degree (s-1) the weight is (-m-2).  Consequently the equations (b\alpha=0), (e\alpha+bv=0) force (v=\alpha=0) over the integral free lattices.  The remaining kernel is exactly the Smith kernel with (d_jQ_j=0).  No torsion invariant factor is discarded or inverted.

## 2. Saturation, including primes dividing Smith coefficients

The original typed Witt argument is valid.  Cubic Picard classes lift because (H^2(\mathcal O_W)=0); the prescribed hyperplane class can be included in an integral basis because it has degree one on a line.  The Euler and conormal sequences identify the relevant (H^1(\Omega_W^1(A))) over the Witt ring with a free rank-four projective-space cohomology module.  Only the fixed multidegree ((0;1,\ldots,1)) is used, so no comparison of the complete Chow rings of the two fibres is assumed.  The resulting torsion-free target kills every saturation vector (w_j).

The proposed simpler replacement also passes, and makes this step entirely integral.  Define

\[
\Psi:B_s\longrightarrow\bigotimes_i\bigl(\operatorname{Pic}(W_i)/\mathbb Z A_i\bigr)
\]

by the indicated multidegree projection followed by the quotient.  Each factor is free.  Every contribution of (bv\) to that multidegree inserts an (A_i\), while the projective-space contribution has the wrong multidegree.  Hence (\Psi(bv)=0\), and torsion-freeness implies (\Psi(w_j)=0\) from (bv_j=d_jw_j\).  The map (\Phi_k\) factors through (\Psi\), because (\mu_{A_i}=0\) follows from the ambient Euler sequence.  Thus (\Phi_k(w_j)=0\) in every characteristic, without any division or Witt lift.

## 3. Actual line bundles and the curve-product term

I checked (H^2(V,L^n)=0\) for every positive (n\), and the displayed (H^1\) calculations.  Successive Picard lifting therefore gives a compatible system of invertible sheaves.  Projective formal existence, regularity of the excellent completion map, Popescu, finite-presentation descent, and the henselian smooth lifting lemma give an actual line bundle on the fixed \(\mathcal Z\), preserving a prescribed finite jet.  Only finitely many individual lifts are required.

The definition

\[
\widetilde K=\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}(-V)\otimes q^*L_T^{-1}
\]

is an actual identity of line bundles and does not assume a nonexistent map to (C\).  For (Q\in\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)(k)\), the product \(c_1(\widetilde K)c_1(\widetilde Q)\) reduces to zero because its reduction is a product on the curve.  Its relative lift is unique.  Changing \(\widetilde Q\) changes the differential by \(a'\smile d\log K_C\), which vanishes by curve cohomological degree two.  Hence the differential depends only on (Q\), is additive, and vanishes because its source is divisible and its target is killed by (p\).  The proof correctly asserts only vanishing of this differential, not vanishing of the relative Milnor class itself.

## 4. Exact exceptional identity and final contradiction

The projection formula and the actual normal-line identity give PB.18 in integral Chow groups.  The first summands have a nil line factor \(\widetilde Q_j^{d_j}\) and are killed by the saturated lattice calculation.  The second summands have the unique relative curve-product class just treated, so their differential is zero after multiplication by the actual divisor polynomial (v_j\).  Each summand reduces to zero separately, making uniqueness of the relative lift applicable to their sum.

The finite-stage argument is correct: the line bundles, divisor polynomials and finite rational-equivalence witnesses descend to a single pointed étale neighbourhood.  Properness allows the base to be shrunk so that its whole source is regular; over perfect (k\) it is smooth.  The first infinitesimal fibre remains the same.  The integral Milnor–Bloch formula and its multiplicative compatibility are applied on this smooth model, then pulled to (E\).  They are not asserted on the nonreduced (E\).  The nonzero designated relative component therefore contradicts exceptional support.

I independently reconstructed the argument and the geometric smoothness calculations. A source-label correction to the final ledger was requested and is explained below; it does not change the mathematics.

## Point fields and the imperfect-field construction

Only finitely many point-supported K2 terms occur. Splitting their maximal separable residue subextensions by one finite Galois extension leaves a product of purely inseparable fields. Separability of this base change makes the tensor products reduced. If the residual extension has exponent e, bilinearity gives p^(2e){a,b}={a^(p^e),b^(p^e)}. The latter symbol is defined over the new base field. Thus rational K2 coefficients descend without a purely inseparable extension of the parameter curve.

The projection formula then gives constant symbols times the actual point-divisor class, retaining its inseparable degree. On a regular curve the Cartier formula [O_a]=[O_C(a)]-1 remains valid for every closed point, since an invertible module over its residue field is trivial. The constant ET.9 degree matrix still suffices.

The extension of VE to the infinite imperfect field has the necessary extra choices. The high-twist sections defining the evaluation divisors are chosen with geometrically reduced zeros and poles, hence finite-etale supports. Without this choice an inseparable support point could obstruct geometrically simple zero interpolation. The required conditions are nonempty open first-jet conditions on affine coefficient spaces over the infinite field. Both prescribed rational endpoints are retained. The extra simple zero can be at a finite separable point and need not be rational.

In odd characteristic, requiring both h and h+4 to have simple geometric zeros handles all branch points. If the chosen unit is -1, the endpoint lies over h=-4 and the nonzero derivative is imposed there. In characteristic two the simple-zero Artin–Schreier local equation is smooth. At the pole a0, clearing denominators gives unit linear coefficients at g=0 and g=infinity, so the boundary points are smooth and rational. This proves smoothness over the actual base, rather than inferring it from regularity over an imperfect field. The original marked Dennis–Stein and descent calculations then apply with the genuine residue pushforwards; the unit1 still gives literal zero.

## Independent check of the symbol curve

For (f-1)^2(g-1)^2=c f g with c nonzero, the unique point over f=0 is (0,1), and its derivative in f is -c. Every geometric component dominates the f-line, since there is no vertical component, and would contain this unique smooth point. Hence there is exactly one geometric component, and it is reduced. The other three boundary points are smooth by the identical inverse-coordinate calculation.

In characteristic two the interior derivatives are -cg and -cf, which are nonzero there. In odd characteristic, dividing the equation and its derivative equations at an interior singular point forces f=g=-1 and c=16. Writing f=-1+x,g=-1+y gives quadratic term 4(x^2+y^2). It has two distinct tangent lines because the characteristic is not2 and the algebraically closed constant field contains a square root of -1. The normalization is smooth; in this exceptional case the curve is itself defined over the constant field. The only singular requested endpoint is a=b=-1, whose Milnor symbol is2-torsion and can be discarded rationally. Every other requested endpoint is smooth and remains rational on normalization. Thus the proper K2 symbol construction is valid in the stated imperfect-field scope.

## Actual separable descent and exact endpoints

For the finite separable extension L/F, after a finite Galois splitting extension the Weil restriction is the product of the conjugate smooth projective curves. It is consequently smooth and geometrically connected. The projective model can be descended using the tensor product of the conjugate ample line bundles, with its permutation descent datum. This is not an assertion that projectivity descends without an ample line bundle.

The universal evaluation map followed by finite flat perfect pushforward gives an actual class over E_F times that Weil restriction. Tor-independent finite flat base change identifies its two fibres with the traces of the original two fibres. A smooth geometrically connected proper curve through the two rational endpoint tuples exists by the same geometric Bertini argument. Thus trace preserves the exact proper-family subgroup. No purely inseparable Weil restriction is used, where properness would fail.

Finally r commutes with restriction. Hence r^2 res(kappa)=res(r^2 kappa), and projection formula gives its trace equal to [F':F]r^2 kappa. There is no need to commute r with pushforward on arbitrary classes. Rational division gives HD.1. For the original component tuple, the constant h0 construction supplies an actual HK family over k(u); its zeros and branch values satisfy the above smoothness checks. Applying HD.1 therefore produces the exact whole-exceptional endpoint over k(u) required before RF. It still supplies no ambient family lift or node cancellation.

I checked the external-product map on the entire finite diagram of intersections before making cellular decompositions. Their centres remain regular immersions after any allowed parameter base change: the point-product is cut out by the two polynomial coordinates. For a closed binary union the characteristic-p Milnor-square theorem applies in every integer K-degree. Its rational fibre is zero. Over the algebraic closure of a finite field, the rational field spectrum is HQ. Each rational stratum therefore lies in degree zero. The codimension-zero complex is the cochain complex of the tetrahedral boundary, with cohomology Q in degrees zero and two. The Picard differential has source rank 34 and target rank 6.
