The four component degree classes contribute rank four. Thus the homotopy groups are Q^33 in degree zero and Q in degree minus two, with the others zero.

Choosing one splitting over the constant field and then applying TS.1 gives a parameter-independent, noncanonical module decomposition. The dual-complex class has Adams weight zero. # Independent full audit of WP.1–WP.8

**PASS in the exact fixed-local-base and smooth-proper-curve scope stated by the owner.** This is an auxiliary whole-family lifting theorem. It does not prove a new component-family generation assertion, specialization theorem, or main-gate reduction.

Reviewer: GPT-6 Astra Pro (OpenAI), ChatGPT Pro mode, RESEARCH_SA06, `/root/cycles_continuation`; effort setting not separately exposed. No priority claim.

Reviewed in full: `../frobenius/C3_whole_proper_top_family_RESEARCH.md`, SHA256 `fcb19e667d8060364c37a7749faf6393ff4d485c346ba1ddbcf43d1ce9969478`. Freshly reread the entire determinantal, geometric flag, algebraization, and endpoint proof in C.3bn/AE.1–AE.10; reread the entire fixed-product obstruction proof FF.1–FF.4 and the previously complete cycles AE audit. No numerical program was run or needed.

## 1. Admissible finite schemes retain the required nilpotent structure

An admissible F is an actual regular immersion of length d+1 in T=D×P. Independence on the smooth reduced top stratum is an additional condition, not a replacement of F by its reduction. A split rank-d subbundle of I_F/I_F² can be chosen by the first-jet construction: the matrix rank-defect has codimension two and the support of F is finite. Nakayama on F upgrades reduced full rank to a locally split subbundle. Locally completing those d generators to a basis of I_F/I_F², and then applying Nakayama to the ideal, gives a regular-sequence generating set of I_F whose first d members are the flag equations. The remaining member cuts F as a Cartier divisor on H. This reasoning retains the thickness inherited from D.

Away from F, the same finite smooth stratification and prefix transversality used in AE apply. The flag has d independent ambient differentials at every point of its closed fibre, including any lower-dimensional strata it meets. It therefore cuts a regular surface there. The failure of regularity, failure of expected local codimension, and unwanted components are closed conditions on a scheme proper over the original local base. Any nonempty such closed subset has image containing the closed point. Hence these failures do not occur anywhere. The equation of D is a nonzerodivisor on this regular surface because the flag intersection with the full closed-fibre support has dimension one; no surface component is contained in it.

The restriction H is consequently a possibly nonreduced Cartier curve on W. The ideal of H and the maximal-ideal-adic ideal have the same support, hence cofinal powers on the noetherian proper W. No assumption that W dominates the local base, or that its fibres over P are globally flat, is needed.

## 2. The finite-class lift is integral and is an equality in perfect K0

The underlying noetherian topological space of H has dimension one, so H² of every coherent sheaf on H vanishes. In particular it vanishes for every J^n/J^(n+1), without an eventual-vanishing qualification and without any loss caused by nilpotents. The square-zero unit sequence lifts O_H(−F) at each successive thickening with no tensor power.

The same actual finite-jet algebraization argument as AE.9 applies: proper existence over the completion, algebraization of the inverse, descent to a smooth R-algebra, and henselian lifting of the specified R/m^M point for m^M O_W⊂J preserve the restriction on the entire H. Since H is Cartier on W, pullback of j:W→Z×P along the Cartier inclusion T→Z×P is Tor-independent. Both j and its base change are regular immersions. The projection/base-change identity therefore gives

in perfect K0(T), integrally. The final identity is the actual Cartier exact sequence. It is valid for the nonreduced F and H. A Cartan map, a gamma-pushforward formula, or a comparison with coherent G0 is unnecessary.

## 3. The entire gamma-(d+1) tail is covered

The previously proved AE reduction handles all products of gamma operations on virtual classes by writing virtual bundles as differences of sufficiently positive equal-rank bundles. Replacing total degree d by n=d+1 preserves this argument. The Eagon–Northcott perfect identities are exact before passing to the next gamma term.

For total codimension n, the degeneracy intersection is finite and misses every lower-dimensional stratum. Its deeper rank incidence has codimension n+i_a+2>n, so no deeper rank locus meets it. ## 4. WP.4 is an exact perfect identity on the curve

For a line bundle M on the projective Cohen–Macaulay curve C, high twists of M and O_C have sections avoiding its associated points and the finitely many bad points. Their restrictions to the smooth reduction can have simple zeros. The two exact sequences 0→O_C→O_C(F_±)→O_(F_±)(F_±)→0 give the difference formula after twisting by A^(−N).     [M]−1=[O_(F_+)]−[O_(F_-)].

The composite immersion F_±→C→T is regular. Its defining d curve equations, followed by the transverse Cartier section, have d+1 independent differentials at the good reduced support. It is therefore admissible for the integral finite-class lift. This checks the additional condition needed in WP.4 rather than assuming that every finite scheme is admissible.

## 5. Whole-family base change and exact curve correction

For an AE curve C, the section W has dimension three and H=W∩T is Cartier. The entire square with T is Tor-independent because its one Cartier equation remains a nonzerodivisor on W. This condition does not depend on endpoint flatness. Thus the integral class b_C restricts on all of T to the sum of the a successive Cartier twists on C in WP.5.

Subtracting a[O_C] leaves only the finite sum of pushed-forward line-bundle differences on C. Section4 expresses each one exactly as a sum of admissible finite classes; Section2 lifts each of those integrally. Subtracting their lifts yields the literal equality (b_C−c_C)|T=a[O_C]. Division by the finite p-power a is legitimate in the rational theorem. Together with the already lifted top tail, this proves WP.1 for the prescribed class on the entire product.

## 6. The low-dimensional full-K0 consequence is justified

For d=2, first lift ranks through the point isomorphism FF.4. After clearing a common denominator, the remaining rank-zero class has a determinant line bundle on T. Applying the AE.8–AE.9 argument with W=Z×P and H=T is valid: O_D(−D) is ample on every fibre over P, relative Serre vanishing removes higher direct images for high powers, and the proper curve P has coherent cohomological dimension one. Thus H² of those high powers vanishes. The finitely many previous obstruction groups are killed by p, giving a finite power of the determinant that lifts.

A rational multiple of the lifted line-bundle difference gives the correct determinant modulo F_gamma². The rank-and-determinant description of K0/F_gamma² then leaves precisely a class covered by WP.1. This simpler argument suffices; existence of an actual line-bundle root is not needed. For d=1, lifting ranks and F_gamma¹ proves the same full surjectivity. Nilpotent invariance after rationalization transfers the conclusion between D×P and E×P as in AE.

FF.1 is an exact fixed-product cokernel statement and its proof keeps K0(Spec R×P). Combining it with the just-proved surjectivity gives K_(-1)(Spec R×P)_Q=0 for d≤2. This uses no extension of Drinfeld's henselian-local theorem to a nonlocal product.

We checked the dimension conventions \(s=r-1\), \(m=N-2r\ge2\). Generic \(m+1\) sections of the very ample bundle have a smooth transverse base locus of the expected codimension, or an empty one. The integral operator is well defined on cycles on the incidence hypersurface before passage to the quotient. We rederived the missing-factor argument. The odd degree lies on \(C\). Each K3 factor must contribute total cohomological degree four after multiplication by its \(\tau_\nu\). A degree-four input already vanishes; a degree-zero input must receive an \(H_\nu\) from the indicated power of \(a\), which gives \(\tau_\nu H_\nu=0\) after integration. There is at least one such missing input in both terms. A \(K_C\) insertion kills the curve's degree-one component. Thus the boundary map kills every mixed class, not only algebraic classes. The resulting Picard family has zero differential and is constant, integrally.

The field argument is consequently legitimate. It is applied only to cycles on the smooth projective exceptional section \(H\). A Hilbert component containing a complex point is the base change of a component over the algebraically closed countable field; a point over that field exists. A chain of proper curves, normalized, and the universal flat family show ordinary algebraic equivalence to a cycle over that field. The boundary's image is therefore contained in \(\operatorname{Pic}(C)(\overline K)\). No finite-type parameterization of cycles on the strict-local puncture is assumed.

Localization and self-intersection then define \(\rho\) on all target Chow classes modulo the stated Picard subgroup. The independently varying period domains supply the jointly Hodge-generic tuple with rank-two Néron–Severi groups, scalar transcendental endomorphisms and no pairwise transcendental Hodge isomorphisms. The chosen complex embedding is explicitly part of the data.

# Independent full proof and source audit: C.3aw

**Result: PASS.** We read the entire typed proof in `agents/real_weil/C3_positive_characteristic_low_injectivity_draft.tex` and independently checked its geometric construction, finite-field choice rule, Chow quotient, and both restriction kernels. This audit does not claim an independent rerun of the author's finite certificate.

## Scope

For every prime p, r at least 2, and r+1 at most N at most 2r-1, the construction gives a specified normal excellent strictly henselian local ring with an algebraically closed coefficient field transcendental over the algebraic closure of the finite field. Its regular puncture and regular principal divisor puncture have a non-torsion ordinary algebraically trivial class in the kernel of restriction. The same class is a principal Gysin image and dies on the open complement. No rational nonvanishing over the algebraic closure of a finite field is asserted.

## Checks of the complete proof

1. The parameter m=N-r-1 lies between zero and r-2, exactly the interval needed for a positive-dimensional complete-intersection base. The Calabi–Yau and generic-point nonsupport input is precisely C.3at, which we independently audited in full, including the separate source- and target-support slope arguments.
2. Serre vanishing applied to the square of the ideal of the two distinct rational points supplies surjective first jets. Stacks Lemmas 33.47.1 and 33.47.3 apply to the complement of the two points and, successively, to its smooth sections. Independent jets at the marked points supply smoothness there. The smooth complete intersection has dimension at least one. Its Koszul resolution in projective space gives geometrically connectedness; smoothness and connectedness imply integrality.
3. The enumeration of coefficient tuples from finite constant extensions is valid even though the basis has coefficients in the function field. A polynomial with coefficients in an extension field that vanishes at every tuple from an infinite subfield is zero, by induction on the number of variables. Thus constant tuples are Zariski dense over the function field, and one meets the nonempty good open. The prescribed enumeration and Jacobian tests terminate without introducing another transcendental parameter.
4. The incidence divisor is smooth off the base by its projective-bundle description and is smooth on the base because the differentials of its defining sections are independent. The m=0 case is correctly included: the incidence divisor is the base itself. The fibre cycle P^m times ([P]-[a]) has codimension r-1 on that divisor, and its proper pushforward is exactly the pullback of the fixed zero-cycle, with multiplicity one.
5. The ordinary equivalence uses a smooth proper connected curve through the marked points, followed by proper pushforward and flat pullback on the product with that same curve. It is therefore an actual fixed-product family and does not rely on formal or varying families.
6. The projective-bundle quotient is exactly CH^r(T) divided by (ell H)^(m+1) CH^(r-m-1)(T). This follows by eliminating h with h=-ell H; the sole projective relation becomes (-ell H)^(m+1). That denominator lies in H CH^(r-1), so the previous nonsupport theorem proves infinite order in the integral quotient. This argument also checks the m=0 endpoint.
7. Hypersurface projective normality, the Veronese multiplication, and the Segre multiplication give degree-one generation of the full section ring. Its normality follows from the divisor-valuation description of the full section ring on a normal variety. The punctured cone is the punctured line bundle, and the principal divisor puncture is the corresponding bundle over the smooth incidence divisor. No unnecessary normality claim for the closed-point quotient is used.
8. The flat pullbacks and proper pushforwards commute before taking parameter fibres. C.3e's all-characteristic integral strict-cone injection therefore preserves the exhibited infinite-order ordinary class. Dimensions agree: the local dimension is m+r+1=N.
9. The divisor is principal, so its normal line is trivial. The exact integral Gysin definition kills each cycle supported on it, equivalently i^*i_* is multiplication by the first Chern class of the normal line. Thus the exhibited Gysin class restricts to zero on the divisor. Localization independently kills it on the open complement. Neither conclusion requires rational coefficients, although rational coefficients detect its nonzero infinite-order source class.

## Exact scope

For every prime p and every r at least 2, the construction produces a specified normal excellent strictly henselian local ring of dimension 2r over the indicated algebraically closed transcendental field, with regular puncture and regular principal-divisor puncture. Its ordinary codimension-r restriction has an infinite-order kernel class. The restriction is zero integrally, including when p divides r. The statement does not concern nonzero rational ordinary classes over the algebraic closure of a finite field itself.

## Complete proof checks

1. The two displayed elliptic equations are smooth in every prime. In characteristic two their gradient is (U²,W²,V²). In odd characteristic the given separation into W=0 and V=0 verifies smoothness also in characteristic three. The geometric generic point cannot belong to any finite group scheme E[n], so its degree-zero Picard class has infinite order, without a prime-to-p restriction. The displayed diagonal line bundle is an actual proper-curve family.
2. Each horizontal line V=bW has three simple intersections with the cubic under the stated exact conditions. Distinct lines meet only at the point (1:0:0), which is outside the cubic. Their divisors are consequently disjoint. The finite-field enumeration terminates because the excluded polynomial has finitely many roots (and is the nonzero constant 4 in characteristic three).
3. For s_i=y_i ell_i, the common zero scheme consists precisely of the coordinate vertex e_i over the three points of D_i. On the indicated chart the r differential directions are independent. Hence its scheme structure is reduced, with exactly 3r points; no generic transversality assertion is needed.
4. The incidence divisor is a projective bundle off this base and is smooth on the base by the differential calculation. On it the map O^r to A kills the tautological line and induces a section of U-dual tensor A. The chart equation eliminates one of the r local parameters, leaving a regular sequence of length r-1. Its zero scheme is exactly P^(r-1) times B, of the correct codimension.
5. The integral top Chern formula is precisely the sum of (-h)^j a^(r-1-j). The twist formula has coefficient one in top degree, and c_j(U)=h^j. Pullback of the Picard class is trivial on each component of the zero scheme; projection formula therefore annihilates the entire stated Chern polynomial times lambda in integral Chow.
6. Eliminating h=-(h_y+c) in CH(E)[h,h_y]/(h^r,h_y^r) leaves h_y^r=0 and r h_y^(r-1)c=0, because c²=0 on the curve. In degree r the exact quotient is Pic(E)/Z(M^r), with no additional relation. Degree shows that Pic⁰(E) injects. The chosen source class maps to r lambda and has infinite order even when p divides r; the integer multiplier is not replaced by a scalar in the field.
7. The plane cubic full section ring, Veronese/Segre section multiplications, and full-section valuation description establish exactly the normal degree-one cone hypotheses. The local dimension is 2r. Smoothness of both punctures is the line-bundle description and the smooth incidence divisor, with no assumption about normality of the quotient at the closed point.
8. The strict-cone injection preserves the exhibited infinite order. The source class is an actual ordinary class, because the original diagonal family is pulled back and acted on by the fixed integral Chern operator before comparing its fibres. On the principal puncture, L is trivial, hence h=-a. Every term of the annihilating Chern polynomial becomes a^(r-1), and its sum is r a^(r-1). This kills exactly the chosen source class integrally. No division by r occurs.

## Relative kernel and exponent

For a square-zero quotient of local rings, units lift and their kernel is `1+I`. The tensor-algebra kernel is generated by a tensor having a relative-unit entry. Each downstairs Steinberg generator lifts to an actual upstairs Steinberg generator because both a lift of `a` and one minus that same lift are units. This proves the asserted generating description after passing to Milnor K-theory, without a stability or infinite-field hypothesis. Every generator is killed by p in characteristic p, by multilinearity and `(1+i)^p=1`. This proves a sheaf killed by p, rather than merely a p-primary group of unspecified exponent.

## Canonical differential quotient, including p=2

Formal smoothness gives local algebra splittings. For a rank-one split square-zero algebra the differentials restricted to its reduction are the direct sum of the base differentials and I. Hence the conormal map `I -> Omega_E tensor O_V`, `i -> di`, is injective in every characteristic. The immersion need not be regular, and no regular-immersion theorem is used at that point.

Exterior powers of this short exact sequence have the displayed kernel `I tensor Omega_V^(r-1)` because I is a line bundle. The injection is given intrinsically by `i tensor omega -> di wedge lift(omega)`; any ambiguity contains a wedge of two conormal vectors and vanishes even in characteristic two. The dlog map on the ordinary tensor/Steinberg presentation therefore defines the quotient canonically on the relative kernel, without choosing a splitting. It has exactly the displayed normalization. Locally, every `da` can be expressed using a unit (`a` or `1+a` in a local ring), and coefficients are absorbed into i, so the map is surjective. Symbols with multiple relative-unit entries map to zero, but the proof correctly does not assert that those symbols themselves vanish when p=2.

## Actual cup and cohomological injection

The displayed Cech cocycle `{1+a_ij,g_jk}` is a relative Milnor cocycle. Its absolute image is the sheaf cup of the two actual line bundles, and its differential image is the precise product `a cup dlog(D|V)`. Independence of trivializations follows from the sheaf bilinear pairing. A Cech representative maps naturally to derived sheaf cohomology; no assertion that arbitrary Cech cohomology equals derived cohomology is needed.

If H1 of the base K2 sheaf is p-divisible, the connecting homomorphism into H2 of the relative sheaf, which is killed by p, is zero. Thus the absolute relative-class image is injective. This genuinely removes the possibility that a nonzero relative differential class is killed by a base boundary. The proof does not compare Milnor and Quillen sheaves on a nonreduced scheme.

## Independent Dennis--Stein paragraph

I also checked the optional final paragraph. D1 and D2 give additivity in an I-entry because the correction term has two factors in I. Thus p kills the relative group. The two signed differential formulas respect D1, D2 and all three possible placements of an I-entry in D3; the nontrivial placement is exactly the displayed Leibniz identity. The normalization of `{1+i,u}` is correct. This optional calculation is separate from the all-degree Milnor proof.

The expected dimension of the closed-fibre intersection makes H Cartier on W; the residual regular-sequence generator makes F Cartier on H.

2. The dimension-one H has H²(H,J^n/J^(n+1))=0 at every stage. Thus the actual line bundle O_H(−F) extends through all thickenings with no tensor power. The AE finite-jet Popescu/henselian descent preserves the specified restriction on H on the fixed W. This gives an integral, actual perfect K0 class j_*(1−[Q]). Since H is Cartier on W, the full square with T is Tor-independent, and its restriction is exactly [O_F].

3. Repeating the AE determinantal construction in total degree d+1 gives admissible finite intersections. The deeper-rank bound is d+1+i_a+2>d+1; all lower-dimensional strata are avoided. The exact perfect tensor resolutions and rational gamma dimension bound therefore generate the entire top tail by these finite perfect classes. No passage through coherent G0 or Cartan injectivity enters.

4. A line-bundle difference on an AE curve C is represented exactly by two finite Cartier zero schemes, after positive twisting. General sections avoid all associated points and the finite bad set and have transverse zeros on the smooth reduction. Their full nonreduced finite schemes are retained. The twisting line bundles are trivial on each Artinian semilocal finite scheme, by the Chinese-remainder/Nakayama argument. The resulting equality is in perfect K0(C), and its pushforwards are the admissible finite corrections just lifted.

5. The AE p-power lift for O_H(−C) gives a times [O_C] plus precisely those line-bundle differences, by successive Cartier sequences on the entire H. Correcting them proves the whole-product equality WP.6. The top-tail correction then proves WP.1 for the prescribed full class, rather than only its endpoints.

6. For d=2, pointwise FF.4 lifts ranks. The same eventual relative-Serre H² vanishing lifts a p-power of any line bundle on T, and a rational multiple of its K0 difference has the required determinant modulo Fγ². WP.1 lifts that remaining filtration term. For d=1, ranks and Fγ¹ suffice. Nilpotent invariance gives WP.7 on E×P. FF.1 identifies its cokernel with K_−1(R×P)_Q, proving WP.8 without treating the product as henselian local.

## Scope retained

The actual local base R, proper curve P and full proper product are essential throughout. The argument does not apply to the nonlocal ring R tensor_k k(u) by merely relabeling it, does not compactify arbitrary affine parameter classes and does not glue independently prescribed component families. Away from B, the kernel of O_U³→M_U is a rank2 bundle and H_U is its
P¹-bundle of lines. At b∈B the three ds_i form a basis of T*_bS after
trivializing M. At a point (x,b), the differential Σx_i ds_i is nonzero,

For every smooth parameter P, the complement of H_U×P in H×P has
codimension2. Localization therefore gives an isomorphism of CH¹ groups:
there are no codimension-one cycles supported in that complement.
The projective-bundle formula on H_U×P gives

    CH¹(H_U×P) = p* CH¹(U×P) ⊕ h p* CH⁰(U×P).

Removing B×P from S×P has codimension3, so localization likewise identifies

    CH¹(H×P) = p* CH¹(S×P) ⊕ h p* CH⁰(S×P)

## 6. Conditional Hodge representation argument and three-section rank

Assume the exact source input Hg(T_W)=SO(T_W), where T_W is the rational
transcendental K3 Hodge structure. Because H¹(C) is CM, the derived group
of Hg(T_W direct-sum H¹(C)) contains SO(T_W) acting trivially on H¹(C).
The standard SO representation is absolutely irreducible, so any rational
Hodge substructure of T_W tensor H¹(C) has the form T_W tensor U for a
rational subspace U of H¹(C). Stability under the Hodge circle makes U
a weight1 Hodge substructure. If U is nonzero, its (1,0) part is nonzero,
and T_W^(2,0) tensor U^(1,0) gives a nonzero (3,0) part. Thus this tensor
product has no nonzero level1 Hodge substructure. A rational Hodge class
in T_W tensor H¹(C) tensor H¹(P) would give a morphism
H¹(P)^*(-2)→T_W tensor H¹(C), whose image has level1; it is therefore
zero. The algebraic component under consideration consequently lies in
NS(W)_Q tensor H¹(C) tensor H¹(P). This argument is uniform in P and
requires no genericity condition chosen after P.

On a smooth quartic, the combined multiplication map
H¹(Ω¹_W)/C·H→H⁰(O_W(1))^* tensor H¹(Ω¹_W(1)) is injective: its dual is
the surjection sum_j w_j R₃→R₄ of the Jacobian quotient, which is
generated in degree1. Hence for the nonzero primitive NS class τ there
is a linear form w with μ(w)τ nonzero. The special triple s_i=w z_i
(i=0,1,2) makes the obstruction map on C·τ tensor C³ injective.
This proves that rank3 is a nonempty Zariski-open condition on the
space of triples of sections of M. The transverse finite-base-locus
condition is a different nonempty Zariski-open condition because M is
very ample. Their intersection is nonempty. The special triple proves
rank nonemptiness only and is not itself asserted to have a finite base
locus. This exact distinction is necessary.

effort setting not exposed. Completed 2026-11-19T11:38:43.203963+00:00.

Outcome: PASS in exactly its stated algebraizable, characteristic-p,

No mathematical correction is required. No computational program was

## Proof reconstruction

1. KST applies to the noetherian abstract blow-up square without any
resolution assumption. Both local K0 groups are Z, and quotient by
the graph of the structure sheaf leaves the claimed constant-pro
monomorphism. Its actual kernels are decreasing subgroups with
inclusion transitions, so pro-zero really implies a zero kernel at
one finite thickening. GH applies in every nonconnective degree;
finite affine Mayer-Vietoris descent globalizes the nilpotent
comparison after inverting p. No uniform exponent is needed.

2. The rational Chern-character argument has an appropriate finite
smooth model. Projectivity makes the image of the nonsmooth locus
closed; the selected closed fibre is regular, and over the perfect
coefficient field the finite-stage regularity/smoothness condition
spreads. Finite vector bundles, cycles and their relations descend.
Contravariant Chern character matches refined pullback without an
extra Todd factor. Injectivity of the full K0 map therefore gives
injectivity in each graded Chow degree. Actual curve families are
preserved by the refined Cartier pullback.

3. The surface W through the prescribed x,o is cut by sufficiently
positive relative sections. Serre vanishing lifts their restrictions
from E. Prescribed-point Bertini produces a smooth connected curve C;
the argument uses the geometric construction in Stacks45.8.3, not
its later prime-to-characteristic divisibility conclusion. Transverse
jets on E give a regular surface and regular sequence near C. Any
bad locus or extra component would have a nonempty proper closed
image in Spec R, hence meet the closed point, a contradiction.
The resulting W is integral because each component meets connected
C and distinct components of a regular scheme are disjoint.

4. At the nth Cartier thickening the ideal is exactly L_C^n.
On C times the entire proper parameter curve P, the obstruction is
H1(C,L_C^n) tensor H1(P,O_P). For the finitely many nonzero groups,
the pth tensor power kills the obstruction. All earlier restrictions
are raised simultaneously; a fixed finite exponent then suffices
for every later stage by Serre vanishing. This is a compatible
whole-family construction, not a pointwise lifting argument.

5. Cartier and base-adic ideals have cofinal powers. Projective GAGA
over Rhat algebraizes the whole family and its inverse; full
faithfulness verifies invertibility. Regular completion plus Popescu
allows descent of this actual line bundle to one smooth R-algebra.
The henselian lifting lemma supplies an R-point with the same residue
point. Because C lies over Spec k, the pulled-back line bundle on
W times P has exactly the prescribed p-power restriction on C times P.
No claim of essential surjectivity for arbitrary henselian GAGA is
being made or needed.

6. Applying that construction to O(Delta-{o}times C) gives actual
ordinary cycle differences on W, then on Z. The square with E is
transverse, so refined base change gives p^e([x]-[o]) with coefficient
one. Rational coefficients lift every degree-zero zero-cycle. A curve
in E has nonzero ample-conormal degree; its boundary supplies the
remaining degree. Injectivity, localization and self-intersection
prove all stated isomorphisms. The boundary kills the one-dimensional
ordinary quotient on Z, giving the ordinary quotient zero on X.
The proof also works at d=1 with W=Z and C=E.

# Independent review: C.3bc, SNC top Chow groups over the algebraic closure of a finite field

**Outcome: PASS.** Complete typed proof read independently; new primary-source scope and locators checked. This review does not assert the existence of the assumed resolution or ample negative exceptional combination. It does not assert an integral vanishing theorem, or vanishing over a transcendental algebraically closed field.

Reviewed file: `research/agents/frobenius/C3_SNC_Fpbar_top_draft.tex`.
Reviewer: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), ChatGPT Pro mode, run `/root/real_weil`; effort setting not exposed.
Completion: 2026-11-19T12:06:00.083550+00:00.

## Proof checks

1. **Smooth top weights.** For a smooth m-dimensional stratum over k=Fpbar, Levine's rational comparison identifies weight w of K_n with CH^w(-,n). The degree-n chain group vanishes if w>m+n. In weight m+n the chains are interior closed points of the n-cube over closed points of the stratum. Every such point is k-rational; proper pushforward from the point gives the asserted surjection from copies of CH^n(k,n). There are no chains in degree n-1, so this argument really applies to all cycles and then to their boundary quotient. Totaro's integral comparison identifies CH^n(k,n) with Milnor K_n(k). For n>0 its rationalization is zero because k* is torsion. The projective n=0 degree statement follows by a smooth projective curve through each pair of points and torsion of its finite-field-defined Jacobian points.

2. **Closed-union descent.** A union of SNC components has a reduced scheme-theoretic intersection in the decomposition used in the induction; the affine square is a Milnor square of surjective ring maps. Geisser--Hesselholt's Theorem C applies without a regularity assumption and in every integer degree. Thus the square of nonconnective K-theory spectra is cartesian after inverting p. TT open-cover descent globalizes the assertion.

3. **Adams operations: exact scope, with no regular-only shortcut.** Levine first describes Soule's sheaf operations for a regular scheme on p257. The next paragraph on p258 explicitly changes to Grayson's construction for an arbitrary scheme. It describes functoriality in the exact category of vector bundles, extension to any iterated homotopy fibre, agreement with the classical operations on K0, and delooping of the Adams operation. Apply this construction to the closed-union square itself; the connecting map is the homotopy-fibre boundary and therefore commutes with the same operation. There is no use of a support-to-subscheme devissage identification and hence no Thom/codimension weight shift. Lemma2.1 itself has regular-ambient/normal-crossing hypotheses. We do NOT apply that statement to the singular union. Instead we use the elementary Q[L]-module filtration argument proved at the beginning of its proof on p259: finite generalized-eigenspace decompositions are stable under the subquotients and extensions in the descent sequence. Induction from smooth strata supplies exactly the needed hypotheses. I requested that the owner make this source-scope distinction explicit; it is already the mathematical argument of the typed proof.

4. **SNC induction.** For C of dimension m-1, the predecessor K_(n+1)(C) in weight m+n is its top weight of a positive K-group and is zero. Above that weight it vanishes by the upper bound. At n=0 the end groups are K1(C) in weight m (top positive weight) and K0(C) in weight m (above dimension). Both vanish. This proves K0(E) in weight d is the direct sum of CH0 of the smooth components, hence Q^c. Empty/disconnected intersections do not affect the induction.

5. **Finite detection.** KST applies to the stated noetherian abstract blow-up square. The local K0 groups of R and its artinian quotients are Z. Quotienting their diagonal structure-sheaf graph leaves a constant pro-group K0(Z) mapping monomorphically to the thickening system. The kernels have inclusion transition maps, so pro-zero implies an actual finite-stage zero kernel. GH nilpotent invariance after inverting p then injects rational K0(Z) into K0(E). The finite smooth-model Chern-character comparison is the same previously checked input as C3az and is compatible with component restriction. Thus the component-degree map on CH^d(Z)_Q is injective. No identification of K with KH is used.

6. **Exceptional intersection matrix.** The matrix is symmetric because the same ample H restricts to both sides of each intersection. Off-diagonal entries are nonnegative. For the positive exceptional coefficient vector a, Ma has strictly negative coordinates because -D is ample on each component. The displayed weighted energy identity proves negative definiteness without requiring a connected dual complex. The exceptional complete-intersection curves therefore span all component degree vectors. Combined with injectivity this gives the exact claimed isomorphism and Chow localization kills the entire top Chow group of the puncture.

## Proof check

1. Strict henselization preserves the excellent normal local hypotheses and the specified residue field. A regular source is handled by its ordinary blow-up: the exceptional projective space is smooth and its negative divisor is relatively ample, so C.3bc applies directly.

2. For a singular closed point, the regular-open preservation is explicit. In Kollár–Witaszek's construction the first resolution preserves the regular puncture; the rank-one sheaf is invertible there, so its Proj modification is the identity there; the dominating fibre-product component has the same open; the final regular resolution is chosen to preserve that open. The projectivity issue on schemes over an affine base is supplied by their Corollary 3 and proof, rather than being silently inferred from local projectivity in the Cossart–Piltant theorem alone.

3. The reduced exceptional locus has dimension at most two. Cossart–Jannsen–Saito Corollary 0.4 applies to this reduced closed subset of the regular excellent ambient scheme and produces a regular projective modification, an isomorphism outside the subset, whose complete reduced inverse image is SNC. The proof of that corollary also gives regularity of the new ambient scheme. This avoids an invalid assumption that an arbitrary composite of log resolutions automatically preserves all previous SNC data.

4. The intermediate regular scheme is locally factorial and hence satisfies the Q-factorial hypothesis of Kollár–Witaszek Lemma 6. It gives an ample exceptional divisor for the second morphism. Adding a sufficiently large pullback of the first relatively ample divisor gives a divisor ample for the composite, supported over the closed point. This is the same relative-ampleness composition used in their Lemma 8.

5. The sign is proved, not assumed. For a large positive integer n, global generation of O(nF), together with normal Hartogs, embeds I=f_*O(nF) as a coherent ideal of R. Its generated image is exactly I O_Z=O(nF) inside the common rational function field; since I consists of regular functions, this fractional invertible ideal lies in O_Z. Thus -nF is effective. If I=R, the relatively ample bundle is trivial, forcing all projective fibres to be zero-dimensional. Proper quasi-finiteness makes f finite; finite birationality to normal R makes it an isomorphism, contradicting the singular closed point. Therefore I is proper and m-primary. Its pullback vanishes precisely on the whole closed fibre, so every SNC exceptional component occurs with a strictly positive coefficient in -nF. The restriction nF|_E is ample. These are exactly the hypotheses used in C.3bc.

6. The application of C.3bc is now legitimate with d=N-1. Our earlier complete independent audit of C.3bc is retained separately. No conclusion over an arbitrary transcendental algebraically closed field, no integral finiteness claim, and no higher-dimensional resolution assertion is added.

## Final addendum: simultaneous projectivity and puncture preservation

The owner rewrote the first construction in `C3_lowdim_Fpbar_top_draft.tex`. I read the entire replacement and the unchanged remaining proof, completing the new audit at **12:31:59 UTC**.

Apply Cossart–Piltant Theorem 1.1 only to the affine base S. Its projectivity and regular-locus clauses then hold simultaneously, giving the regular projective Z1/S unchanged over the puncture U. For a relatively ample H1, take L1=(pi1)_*H1 and L2=Hom(L1,O_S), as in Kollár–Witaszek. Over U the first map is the identity and L1 is a line bundle. The second Proj is also unchanged there.

Let M be the torsion-free quotient of pi1^*L2. The regular scheme Z1 is locally factorial, so its rank-one reflexive hull M** is invertible. The inclusion M into M** defines a coherent ideal J=M tensor (M**)^(-1). It is the unit ideal on U and at every codimension-one point: over a DVR a finite torsion-free rank-one module equals its double dual.

For dimension three, **Cossart–Piltant Proposition 4.4, printed author p. 141**, principalizes a nonzero ideal on a regular excellent threefold by finitely many blow-ups in regular integral centres contained in the locus where the successive total ideal is not locally principal. # C.3be: independent proof and source audit

**Outcome: PASS of the complete strengthened draft.**

Actual certification clock: **2026-11-19 12:54:25 UTC**.

Reviewer: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), ChatGPT Pro mode, run RESEARCH_SA06, agent `/root/real_weil`; inherited effort setting not separately exposed. This is an independent targeted proof and primary-source audit. It is not an independent re-proof of the cited surface-resolution or K-theoretic descent theorems.

Full mathematical file read: `research/agents/frobenius/C3_surface_reduction_Fpbar_draft.tex`, strengthened version beginning with an arbitrary excellent henselian local domain. The earlier algebraizable-only draft is superseded and retained by the owner under `output/C3_surface_reduction_Fpbar_algebraizable_initial.tex`. The old finite-model argument is not required for this stronger proof.

## 1. Exact scope checked

Let (R,m,k) be an excellent henselian local domain, k isomorphic to Fpbar, and dim R=N>=2. There is no normality, finite-type-model, equal-characteristic, or regular-puncture assumption on R. The proved groups are

    CH_1(Spec R)_Q = 0,
    CH^{N-1}(Spec R minus {m})_Q = 0.

The dimension function is delta(p)=dim(R/p) and is restricted unchanged to the puncture. Since a catenary local domain has ht(p)+dim(R/p)=N, the displayed codimension index is correct; deleting the closed point is not a reason to replace N by the puncture's smaller Krull dimension. The ordinary quotient is asserted only where its equivalence convention is defined. In particular the text does not impose coefficient-field product families on a mixed-characteristic ring.

The result does not assert integral vanishing or a uniform annihilating integer. It does not extend the residue field to an arbitrary transcendental algebraically closed field. Those distinctions are explicit and necessary.

## 2. Surface geometry checked

For a normal excellent local surface B, normality supplies a regular puncture, and excellence gives normal completion. Stacks54.14.5 applies with its exact condition (4), and its proof together with54.6.5 supplies normalized closed-point blowups over the singular closed point. Finite normalization is ensured by excellence. These modifications are projective and preserve the puncture simultaneously. In the regular case, the first modification is the blowup of the closed point.

Embedded resolution of the entire closed fibre uses Stacks54.15.6 on a regular surface; finite normalization of its curve components follows from excellence. Its proof uses closed-point blowups supported on that fibre. The final reduced fibre E is a projective strict normal-crossings curve; each component is smooth over the perfect residue field k. This reasoning does not import the threefold resolution theorem or its affine-cover projectivity issue.

The effective exceptional divisor with ample negative is also constructed, not presumed. For an ordinary blowup the exceptional F is effective Cartier and O(-F)=O(1). Pullback to a finite normalization remains Cartier because the normalization is dominant between integral schemes; finite pullback preserves relative ampleness, checked locally over an affine open of the preceding stage. For a subsequent step h, the divisor F_h+a h*D_0 is effective and its negative is ample for the composite once a is sufficiently large. This is exactly the sign in Stacks29.38.8. The first exceptional divisor has the entire first closed fibre as support, so its total transform ensures every final exceptional component occurs with a positive coefficient. No unproved conjunction of projectivity and regular-open preservation remains.

## 3. Finite K0 detection and determinant checked

KST TheoremA/(1.6) applies to the noetherian abstract blowup square with centre the closed point. K0(B) and K0(B/n^b) are Z. Quotienting the diagonal graph of the structure-sheaf class leaves the constant pro-group K0(Z), which maps monomorphically to the system K0(E_b). The levelwise kernel groups are decreasing subgroups of that fixed group, with inclusion transition maps. A pro-zero system of inclusions has an actually zero term. Thus some finite thickening detects K0(Z); no inference from vanishing of an inverse limit alone is used.

The mixed-characteristic extension is justified exactly: p lies in n, hence p^b=0 on E_b. Geisser--Hesselholt TheoremA printedp29 assumes p is nilpotent in the ring, not that the ring is an Fp-algebra. On each affine of the finite detecting thickening, the nilpotent reduction to E is therefore a K-equivalence after inverting p. A finite affine cover and Thomason--Trobaugh Zariski descent give the rational K0 comparison globally. No p-nilpotence on B or Z is asserted.

For a line bundle L of multidegree zero on E, the normalization/gluing argument is valid. Each component restriction is a point of a Jacobian over Fpbar and is torsion; after a common power trivializes these restrictions, only finitely many node-gluing scalars remain. They lie in k* and are torsion. A further power makes the restriction actually trivial on E, even if the dual graph has several connected components.

Consequently [L^M]-[O_Z] is zero in K0(E), hence zero rationally in K0(Z). Some integer multiple is zero integrally in K0(Z). The determinant homomorphism then gives L^{Mn}=O_Z. The proof correctly takes an actual tensor power before applying K0; it does not confuse the additive class [L]-1 with the assertion that L has finite tensor order. Z is projective over affine and has the resolution property; Stacks36.38.5 identifies perfect-complex and vector-bundle K0, and Stacks17.26/17.26.1 gives the required determinant map. Thus the multidegree map Pic(Z)_Q→Q^c is injective without a rational Chern-character theorem or a smooth finite-type model.

## 4. Intersection matrix and divisor localization checked

M_ij=deg(O_Z(E_j)|E_i) is symmetric, with nonnegative off-diagonal intersection lengths. The effective divisor D=Σa_iE_i with -D ample gives Ma<0. With Q=diag(a)Mdiag(a), the identity

    x^t Q x = Σ_i (Σ_j Q_ij)x_i^2 − Σ_{i<j}Q_ij(x_i−x_j)^2

is exact. It proves negative definiteness and invertibility. The exceptional line bundles consequently span all rational multidegrees and, by injectivity, all Pic(Z)_Q. Taking the Weil-divisor closure of a Cartier divisor on the regular puncture supplies Pic(Z)→Pic(U) surjectivity; Z is regular and locally factorial. Exceptional bundles restrict trivially. Hence Pic(U)_Q=0.

For the normal local surface, CH_1(Spec B)→CH_1(U)=Pic(U) is an isomorphism by localization: the closed point has delta-dimension zero, so carries no one-cycles. This surface conclusion has exactly the arbitrary-excellent henselian and mixed-characteristic scope needed later.

## 5. All-dimensional finite pushforward checked

For each curve prime p of the possibly nonnormal domain R, a saturated chain from0 to m through p has a preceding prime q with dim(R/q)=2. Catenarity supplies the exact lengths; N=2 is handled by q=0. The quotient R/q is an excellent henselian local domain. Its normalization T is finite by excellence and remains a domain. Stacks15.106.23 identifies it as henselian local; its finite residue extension is k because k is algebraically closed. Integral extension preserves dimension, so T is a normal local surface to which the preceding argument applies. No algebraization or simultaneous descent of q and its normalization is necessary.

A prime P above p/q is neither zero nor maximal: its contraction is nonzero and nonmaximal. In dimension2 it is therefore height1. The composite Spec T→Spec(R/q)→Spec R is finite. Its proper pushforward sends [V(P)] to the positive finite field degree [kappa(P):kappa(p)] times [V(p)]. Stacks42.20.3 applies over the excellent universally catenary base with its specified dimension function. Rational equivalences are preserved, so the surface vanishing kills each ambient curve generator rationally. Localization removes the closed point without changing CH_1. This proves the all-N claim without a resolution theorem in dimension>N=2.

## 1. Full new marked-family proof

The finite collection of normalized Poincare bundles is placed on one actual proper parameter curve through the identity and the prescribed Picard tuple. Every marked evaluation line bundle has a rational section with divisor disjoint from the two endpoints and with value one in the prescribed identity-fibre trivialization. Curve Riemann–Roch supplies a function with only the prescribed pole, the required nonzero value at the target endpoint, and simple zeros at all finitely many divisor supports and an additional point.

The norm-one cover `(g−1)^2=hg` is irreducible and separable in every characteristic. In odd characteristic its discriminant has an odd valuation at a simple zero of h. In characteristic two, the Artin–Schreier equation `y²+y=1/h` has a simple pole, which cannot occur for a rational Artin–Schreier coboundary. The normalization is therefore a smooth connected proper curve. The zeros and poles of g lie only above the identity endpoint. Above the chosen divisor supports, g equals one, including all ramified points. The target endpoint with g=u exists even when ramified.

On the smooth surface `C_e×P`, frames lifting the fixed trivialization along every zero/pole fibre have transitions `1+z b_ij`. The displayed Dennis–Stein expression

`m⟨z,−b_ij⟩ + {v,1+z b_ij}`

extends `{g,b_ij}` for `g=z^m v`, including negative m. Local regular Gersten injectivity makes these genuine sheaf sections glue and gives the cocycle and frame-change identities. This is local sheaf injectivity, not an asserted global-affine K2 injection. Every boundary specialization is zero by the defining Dennis–Stein word; the target restriction is the usual unit-times-Picard cup.

For a marked point, the normalized rational section of the evaluation line bundle gives the exact Gersten representative supported on its divisor. The zero/pole-fibre comparison contributes no hidden scalar: the section has value one in the prescribed trivialization there. At every remaining support point, g=1, so each point K1 term is zero individually. This proves literal zero in `H¹(P,K2)`, without using a norm or merely zero endpoint values.

The Brown–Gersten lift is correctly made through the **sheaf hypercohomology/Postnikov filtration**, not an unsupported contravariance of the support filtration. On the regular surface the `(1,2)` term has no possible incoming or outgoing differential. Any lift in descent F1 gives the specified H1K2 class. Functorial pullback to each regular horizontal/vertical curve kills F2 because its cohomological dimension is one. Consequently both endpoint and marked K1 restrictions are determined by the displayed sheaf classes, and the lift has no determinant/unit ambiguity. The result is an actual integral K1 family on a fixed proper product in all characteristics.

## 2. Complete totalization implication and exact remaining gate

The canonical geometric closed-cover totalization is retained, including its actual nullhomotopy. At a point parameter, a pure weight-two component tuple has an obstruction with Adams eigenvalue four and zero edge K0 restriction. Exactness puts it in the image of vertex K1(k), of eigenvalue two, so the obstruction is zero rationally. No semisimplicity of the intermediate homotopy group is assumed. Thus the component map is surjective without a dual-complex hypothesis.

For its kernel, the polynomial `(ψ²−2)/2` gives the required weight-two edge vector. The negative energy identity removes the degree-unit part by actual component divisor-times-unit classes, whose canonical totalization boundary is zero. The new marked-family lemma treats the remaining Pic0-times-unit vectors with literal zero restrictions at every triple point. Exactness therefore supplies an actual `π1(T_P)` lift. The difference from any chosen point lift lies in the image of the vertex K2(k) terms; the previously audited proper-curve Milnor-symbol construction kills their double boundaries by actual proper families. A rational K0 weight projector on the product preserves the wanted endpoint class. Arbitrary coherent-lift ambiguity is thus accounted for, not silently discarded.

Combining this with the already proved degree and weighted Albanese reductions gives exactly UK.7: the direct sum of component rational Albanese kernels, divided by the images of `J_K∩S00` and of the exceptional cycle image intersected with S00. The denominator splitting uses the actual Poincare subgroup lying in both relation groups. No assertion is made that all component Albanese kernels lift to globally compatible proper families, or that the resulting quotient vanishes for arbitrary components. Vanishing when every component Albanese kernel is zero is justified.

## Exact proof audit

### Integral scalars and discriminant gluing

The stated Hodge-endomorphism hypotheses give scalar actions on H1 and T_Q. A scalar preserving their nonzero integral lattices is an integer. The Neron--Severi line has primitive generator ell, and there are no rational Hodge homomorphisms between that line and T_Q: a homomorphism in either direction would give a rational (1,1) class in T_Q, using the nondegenerate polarized pairing in the reverse direction. Thus H2 has precisely the two claimed scalar eigenspaces.

Unimodularity of H2(A,Z) and primitivity of ell give an integral w with (w,ell)=1. Since ell^2=4, its projector to Q ell is ell/4. The integral vector Z*w-s w is therefore (n-s)ell/4. Primitivity forces n-s divisible by4. This is a full-lattice gluing argument, not a conclusion from preservation of the two separate orthogonal sublattices. The expression s Delta22+(n-s)ell exterior ell/4 has exactly the required operator. For the convention using pushforward to the first factor, the component acting on H1 is Delta13, as stated.

### Integral Fourier construction and all Chern coefficients

The pushed structure sheaves of resolutions give an integral K0 class with ch0=ch1=0 and ch2=[Z]; lower terms vanish by support dimension and the leading term has coefficient1. A proper Fourier--Mukai pushforward produces an integral perfect K0 class. No WIT hypothesis is needed. Integral virtual Chern classes are available.

The Poincare exterior-algebra convention is consistent with the full diagonal identity. Integrating the four x generators gives F(Delta13)=P, F(Delta22)=P^2/2, and F(ell_x)=-ellhat. The bidegree map is (a,b)->(a,4-b). Thus c1(E) has only an ell1 component and tP; an ell2 component would require the vanished ch1(KZ). Consequently the (2,2) piece of c2(E), computed from (c1^2-2ch2)/2, is exactly

    (t^2-s)P^2/2 + (n-s)ell1 ell2/4.

The remaining pieces have other bidegrees and their products with P cannot enter H3(A) tensor H3(Ahat). The exterior identity P^3=-3ell1 ell2 P gives the normalized mixed coefficient

    m_Z = 3(t^2-s) - (n-s)/2.

This is the coefficient of the actual integral curve c2(E)P. The gluing condition makes its second summand even, and t^2=t modulo2 gives m_Z=t-s modulo2. There is no division of a Chow class. The normalization P^3/6 -> identity is the same previously certified Matsusaka convention as C4i/l/r; changing the global Poincare sign changes a harmless overall sign, not the parity criterion.

### Actual Jacobian splitting in both directions

Every normalized curve component of the integral curve c2(E)P gives an actual homomorphism factorization through its Jacobian. Hence an odd m_Z, together with the already proved 2 in I_J(A), yields1 by integral Bezout and gives a genuine splitting.

Conversely, use the universal degree-zero Picard bundle on J(C) times C, with J(C)=Pic0(C) and the chosen Abel map. Its H1-correspondence is the inverse of the Abel pullback. Therefore pulling by u and pushing along v composed with the Abel map gives u* v*=(v u)* on H1, with coefficient1. Summing gives t=1. The H2 action factors through H2(C), a Tate structure, so it vanishes on T(A), giving s=0. This argument uses neither a polarization inverse nor an isogeny denominator. It also handles signed integral sums of curves and morphisms that drop dimension under pushforward.

### Residual fibre-product method exclusion

A finite morphism between the two smooth surfaces is flat, and the fibre-product correspondence acts by gamma* gamma_*. Generic separability gives multiplicity1 for the diagonal component. Its residual cycle therefore acts by gamma* gamma_*-1. Since H1(Y)=0 and H2(Y) is generated by divisor classes, the first term vanishes on H1(S) and on the transcendental H2; the latter follows by the projection pairing with pulled-back divisors. Blowups preserve the relevant H1 and transcendental H2. Thus its pushforward has t=s=-1. Multiplication graphs have t=k,s=k^2, and divisor exterior products have t=s=0; each has even t-s. The method exclusion is consequently correct and does not exclude arbitrary codimension-two cycles.

Proof refinements retained in the final text:

* Incidence bad sets from locally closed strata have images with proper
  closures by the dimension bound; the images need not themselves be closed.
* D is projective over k because a power of the maximal ideal kills its
  structure sheaf and the resulting Artinian local ring is finite over k.

  two independent sections by ideal generation followed by multiplication
  with a very ample factor.

  over the local base removes a possible nonregular locus away from the
  closed fibre. Its parameter flatness is checked fibrewise.

  endpoints; no unnecessary assertion of global flatness of C is made.
* The Picard bundle is O_H(-C), and the finite endpoint identity is exact in
  perfect K0. This avoids a singular gamma-filtration pushforward theorem.
* Popescu descent matches the prescribed map modulo a sufficiently large
  power of the maximal ideal, preserving the entire thickened proper family.
* The tetrahedral class has rank zero, and gamma squared is applied after
  clearing denominators. No global Adams projection on K2(P) is used.

# C.3av: the positive-characteristic low ordinary-restriction interval

Current status: finalized after full independent root and Frobenius
proof/source audits. Frobenius certified at11:12:38UTC; root also
inspected the complete certificate source and exact five matrices.
The final file is `C3_positive_characteristic_low_range.tex`; the
former draft is a comment-only pointer. Canonical statement and original

## Exact scope and new steps

For every p and r+2<=N<=2r+1, r>=1, the construction gives rational
failure of ordinary J^r surjectivity. The coefficient field is
the algebraic closure of Fpbar(T), with T the specified finite-field
hypersurface. It does not assert rational ordinary nonvanishing over
Fpbar, or failure in N>=2r+2.

The proof adapts C.3ai but replaces its Hodge obstruction by a crystalline
slope-zero obstruction. The degree is d+2 unless p divides d+2, in
which case it is d+3, so the suspended hypersurface is smooth by Euler's
identity and its separated gradient blocks. A monic leading determinant
is proved directly: for degree d+3, the top coefficient of the Hasse
matrix is the identity, because every off-diagonal target monomial has
a negative exponent. Generic ordinarity of arbitrary hypersurfaces is
not assumed.

The curve endpoint d=1 is separately checked: global Witt-coordinate
sections are W_n(F_q), so the preceding connecting map in the Witt
sequence vanishes. Freeness of the full finite Witt modules then follows
from length and Nakayama, in exactly typed semilinear notation.

## Exact source use

All primary files and bibliography entries are those newly opened and
retained for C.3at; see C3at_SOURCE_AUDIT.md and C3at_references.bib.

- Huang--Lian--Yau--Yu2018v1, Section2, Corollary2.3 authorp8 supplies
  the coefficient-matrix convention. The leading identity determinant
  is independently derived, so Corollary2.8 generic invertibility is
  consulted but not required.
- Berthelot--Bloch--Esnault2005 author manuscript, Theorem1.1 and
  smooth proper comparison(1.1) authorpp1--2; exact proper inverse-limit
  clause at the beginning of Section2pp6--7; Witt exact sequence
  Lemma2.5/(2.7)pp9--10. The curve endpoint uses the actual constant
  global sections, not a falsely asserted H^0(O)=0.
- Newly applied exact locator: BBE proof of Corollary1.2, authorp4.
  It explicitly states that smooth affine rigid cohomology agrees with
  Monsky--Washnitzer cohomology and vanishes above dimension, and uses
  rigid Poincare duality to deduce compact-support vanishing below
  dimension. Applying the compact-support localization sequence to
  projective space minus the smooth hypersurface gives the precise
  rational weak-Lefschetz isomorphism used. No integral or small-prime
  weak-Lefschetz assertion is imported.
- Esnault2003 Section2 and deJong1996 Theorem4.1/Remark4.2 supply the
  rational correspondence and source-alteration framework already
  fully audited in C.3at. The lifted source dimension is less than d,
  so its H^d slope-below-one part is zero by Witt cohomological dimension.
- Stacks0FD4 and Kerz7.1/7.5 provide the actual ordinary curve family
  and ambient strict-local Chow vanishing with the exact scopes retained
  in C.3at. C.3e is explicitly all-characteristic and integral.

## Tate shifts and correspondence checks

The incidence correspondence has codimension r=d+s and maps H^d(T)
to H^(d+2s)(V)(s). Its integral transpose left inverse has multiplicity
one because the two root-defined joins meet transversely along T.
A hypothetical hyperplane antecedent has codimension r-1, hence target
H^(d+2s-2)(V)(s-1). For s>=1 the latter is ambient: it is zero in
odd degree, otherwise its sole slope is d/2 after the displayed twist.
For s=0 the twist(-1) makes every slope at least one. Thus it cannot
receive any nonzero slope-zero vector. The constant correspondence and
source-support correspondence are separately killed. No Hodge-type
argument in characteristic p is used.

# C.3ay: critical ordinary injectivity in every positive characteristic

Status: finalized after full independent root and cycles proof/source audits.
Cycles certified11:31:19.776876UTC; root subsequently completed the full
typed proof, exact program and every output-case audit. Final file:
C3_positive_characteristic_critical_injectivity.tex. The former draft is
a comment-only pointer; the statement and original check events are registered.

## Exact scope

For every prime p and r>=2, the explicit normal excellent strict-local
cone of dimension2r has both source and divisor punctures regular.
An actual ordinary class of infinite order is killed by restriction
integrally. It remains a rational kernel. The coefficient field is
exactly the algebraic closure of Fpbar(E0), with the fixed all-prime
elliptic cubic of C.3x; no rational ordinary class over Fpbar itself
is asserted. The theorem makes no claim for N>=2r+1.

## Explicit choices and integral argument

The line bundle M on E has degree3 and is its plane O(1). Distinct
horizontal lines V-b_iW meet E in disjoint simple degree3 divisors:
exclude b_i^2+b_i=0 for p2, and4-27b_i^4=0 in odd characteristic.
A terminating finite-field enumeration specifies every constant.
The diagonal sections y_i(V-b_iW) have exactly3r reduced base points,
with the full local Jacobian independently diagonalized. No Bertini
choice is used in the final construction.

On the smooth incidence divisor the coefficient map factors through
the rank(r-1) universal quotient U_x. Its regular zero scheme is the
product of P_x^(r-1) with the finite base. The top-Chern class of
U_x^dual tensor A equals sum(-h)^j a^(r-1-j). Its product with the
elliptic Pic0 class is zero because that class restricts trivially to
each finite-base component. Pullback to the punctured cone imposes
h+a=0 and gives r a^(r-1)lambda=0. The same source class survives in
the exact integral quotient Pic(E)/Z(M^r); Pic0 injects by degree.
Multiplication by r is an integer Chow operation, also when p divides r.

The generic point minus the origin has infinite order because every
E0[n] is a finite group scheme over the constant field, including
p-primary kernels. Actual algebraic equivalence is supplied by the
line bundle O(Delta-{o}times E) on the fixed product E times E.
The normal degree-one Segre section ring and the all-characteristic

# C.3ba: integral ordinary quotients in all higher codimensions

Status: finalized after complete independent root and cycles proof/source
reviews. Root certified at2026-11-19T11:52:50.332166UTC; cycles completed
at11:49:14UTC. Final proof: C3_positive_characteristic_all_quotients.tex.
The former draft is a comment-only supersession pointer. The requested
wording repair is included: only the finite-type bundle map is asserted
to have pure relative dimension; the strict-local factor is asserted
flat and the cycle codimension is checked by regular immersions.
The statement and original check history are registered.

## Exact conclusion and limitation

For every algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0 and every
2<=r<=N-1, an explicit excellent normal strict-local N-dimensional
cone with regular puncture X has an actual ordinary quotient
B^r(X) surjecting onto (k,+). This refutes integral finiteness even
over Fpbar. The exhibited additive quotient has exponent p. It gives
no nonzero rational quotient, no characteristic-zero conclusion, and
no kernel or cokernel on the ordinary algebraically trivial subgroup.

The base data are exactly the proved C.3as projective r-fold, ample
line bundle L, cotangent section eta, and individually selected actual
closed curves. The new data are P^m times V, m=N-r-1, with O(1)
external-tensored with L, followed by its full section ring and the
pointed strict henselization at the vertex. Degree-one generation is
not assumed. The contraction and regularity statements use precisely
the full-section-ring proof already certified in C.3as.

## Actual morphism and cycle calculation

The section z0 induces a bundle map of resolutions and the graded
ring map a_n -> z0^n a_n. Its pointed map of strict henselizations is
specified by the universal property. It need not induce a morphism
of punctures: the z0=0 chart can map to the original exceptional
divisor. Every pullback is therefore taken on resolutions first.

Flatness is proved over every coefficient ring B by the explicit free
B[t]-basis 1,u^a,(t')^b of B[u,t'], where t maps to u t'. A graph
argument handles an etale target factor, and the finite-relations
criterion handles its filtered ind-etale limit. No torsion-free-over-B
criterion is substituted for flatness. The selected curves are regular
and regularly embedded with codimension r; their flat inverse images
remain regular immersions of that codimension. Thus no arbitrary
ind-etale fibre-dimension assertion is needed to define their cycles.

The integral Milnor Bloch formula and dlog give the conormal detector.
The direct differential summand from V, coherent Kunneth, the fixed
Serre pairing with eta, and coefficient extraction at z0 define its
scalar value. The full exceptional image is killed using the literal
zero-section Chow identity and flat strict-local base change. Ordinary
actual curve-family differences are p-divisible, hence killed by this
exponent-p target. The supported local regular sequence pulls back to
(s_1,...,s_(r-1),z-b(z0/zj)t'_j). Its integral residue has exactly the
global coefficient b z0; evaluation at z0 gives b. This proves
surjectivity on actual cycles, with no formal-family algebraization.

## Search scope

D.1: searched the primary literature around rational Newton cocharacters,
the character-Q protorus, Langlands–Rapoport gerbes and real polarizations.
Kottwitz gives the correct rational source. Direct character duality shows
that this source has no nontrivial mu_2 map. No priority is claimed for
that elementary obstruction. Milne's corrected finite-field motives
paper supplies the comparison between abstract polarizations and the
standard-conjecture construction.

D.3: searched and checked Honda–Tate division-algebra invariants and
Milne's geometric-endomorphism formulas. The explicit family uses the
quadratic polynomial X^2-X+p and produces all denominator orders.
The relative-gerbe argument is written out, rather than inferred from
the existence of an unrelated division algebra.

E.4: opened the attached Lichtenbaum paper, Geisser's finite-field theory,
and the later Flach–Morin derived complex. Subsequent searches included
the phrases Weil-etale / totally positive, real places / 2-torsion,
Spec Z / Z(1), S-integers / Z(1), and open subschemes / number rings.
Primary results by Adrien Morin, Chiu and Beshenov were then opened.
They narrow the outstanding normalization question but were not treated
as interchangeable theories.

E.5: checked Kottwitz's sigma-conjugacy convention and the recent affine
torsor theorem of Wibmer. The latter removes the formerly common
countability qualification from algebraically closed uniqueness.

## C.3u: all-characteristic ordinary classes on a smooth cone

The fragment `C3_smooth_cone.tex` proves the all-characteristic
smooth-cone source theorem by a direct torsion calculation. It does not
assert a splitting of the full local Picard identity component, nor does
it identify arbitrary henselized-product parameter families with actual
line bundles on a fixed product. The Poincare family on the exceptional
smooth projective variety is an actual product family.

The source ring is the strict henselization at the vertex of the full
section ring of a smooth projective integral variety, with the full
section ring explicitly assumed generated in degree one. This makes
the standard total-line-bundle contraction the vertex blow-up and its
scheme-theoretic closed fibre the reduced exceptional variety. The
arbitrary divisor element need not be homogeneous. Regularity of its
puncture is retained.

  This is proper finite-etale comparison over a henselian **local ring**,
  with the closed fibre; no flatness hypothesis is needed. The proof uses
  complete-ring algebraization and approximation for general henselian
  rings. In the application, only a section of a finite etale torsor is
  lifted. No Picard-family algebraization is inferred.
- Kleiman, *The Picard scheme*, arXiv:math/0504020v1, 1 April 2005,
  83 pages: Theorem 2.5(2), p.18; Exercise 4.3, p.27, with its full
  Answer 4.3, p.65; Theorem 5.4 and proof, pp.37–38; and Proposition
  5.10 and proof, pp.41–42. These supply the universal Poincare bundle
  when a rational section exists, properness of the Picard identity
  component for a normal projective variety, and the algebraic-equivalence
  point interpretation. The reduced identity component is used in
  positive characteristic. All locators refer to this author version.

  characteristic. The broader Theorem 7.4 was inspected but is not
  required here. The finite generation is applied to the quotient by
  the ample line-bundle class, not only to NS torsion itself.

# Supported K1 families and the attempted two-parameter specialization

Status: complete auxiliary proof under independent review; no numbered main result, no main-gate movement and no ordinary K0 vanishing claim. Credit: GPT-6 Astra Pro (OpenAI), ChatGPT Pro mode, RESEARCH_SA06, /root/cycles_continuation; effort not separately exposed. No priority claim.

The proof is SNC_supported_K1_family_RESEARCH.tex, HK.1–HK.3. Its exact assertion is that any component degree-zero zero-cycle tuple, multiplied by one constant unit, is the component endpoint tuple of an actual K1 family on a fixed smooth proper product E×P. All characteristic-positive projective SNC surfaces are allowed; negative ampleness is unnecessary for this auxiliary construction.

The key simplification is to apply the already proved marked family lemma VE to a transverse curve A_i inside each smooth component, and then push it to that smooth component. Every A_i/double-curve intersection is marked. Supported base change makes its edge restriction zero in the supported K1 group, and the union of the A_i avoids all triple points. Actual supported closed-union descent is therefore a two-column fibre, so the component tuple lifts. No unsupported singular pushforward from A_i directly into E is used; no K1 weight decomposition is assumed.

## Primary sources actually read in this block

Thomason, R. W., & Trobaugh, T. (1990). Higher algebraic K-theory of schemes and of derived categories. In *The Grothendieck Festschrift, Volume III* (pp.247–435). Birkhäuser. Primary https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/otherpapers/Thomason-Trobaugh.pdf . Freshly read the complete Sections3.14–3.16, printed pp.317–320; Proposition3.17 and its full proof, pp.320–321; Proposition3.18 and its complete proof, pp.321–322. The proof explicitly concludes that the supported analogue also holds. Also freshly read Theorem7.4 and its complete localization proof, pp.365–366; Theorem8.1 and its complete proof, p.367; Corollary8.1.4 and its complete support-union proof, p.368. Retrieval references: turn336360707view0–view2 and turn978586003view0–view2. Prior definitions and the prior theorems cited inside these proofs are not claimed newly fully read.

The positive-characteristic rational closed-union descent, curve moving/Bertini construction and VE marked lemma are the exact previously fully audited bq/br/bt dependencies. Their statement and proof files were read in full in this continuation. No fresh full Geisser–Hesselholt or Quillen source reopening is claimed in this auxiliary block.

## Proper two-parameter route and remaining gap

Suppose the desired component tuple is defined over an algebraically closed field k0 and adjoin a transcendental u. The HK construction over an algebraic closure of k0(u) descends, with all classes and endpoints, to some finite extension of k0(u) by finite presentation. A regular semistable proper model of its parameter would allow a support-localization boundary. At smooth special parameter components this is an actual K0 family only when the global support boundary decomposes through those components.

Support Mayer–Vietoris places the obstruction in node coefficients from K_{-1}(E). Each component's sum of point pushforwards vanishes. For a tree dual graph, successive leaf removal would force the node coefficients to vanish, because pushing further to E sends every point pushforward to the identity. A general semistable dual graph has cycles. In that case pushforward-zero gives only a relation in K_{-1}(E×P_j), not the zero abstract tensor Ω in PL.5. This distinction remains after C.3bt.

The Frobenius reviewer has supplied the elementary elliptic warning: a nontorsion L yields nonzero abstract tensor L⊗L over Q, while c1(L) exterior-product c1(L) vanishes rationally on the square of an elliptic curve, by pulling back L along addition and squaring. Thus point-pushforward vanishing cannot be upgraded to tensor injectivity by declaration.

For the explicit norm-one VE parameter, writing the interpolating h as a coefficient with a pole in u typically degenerates the cover into two copies of its base joined above the zeros of the leading h coefficient. The forced divisor supports can create multiple connections and therefore cycles. No compact-type reduction is proved. Merely taking a finite cover does not remove the PL tensor, by norm pull-push. These are limitations of the present route, not evidence that UK.7 survives.

## Other exact source check in this block

Iwasa, R., & Kai, W. (2021). Isomorphisms up to bounded torsion between relative K0-groups and Chow groups with modulus. *Journal of the Institute of Mathematics of Jussieu,20*(6),1947–1968. https://doi.org/10.1017/S1474748020000055 . Author manuscript dated9January2020: https://ryomei.com/papers/K0CHmodulus.pdf . Opened the full17-page primary and read Introduction/Theorem0.1, pp.1–2, Theorem2.2 statement and Lemma2.3 statement, p.5, and Example4.8 in full, p.14. The main comparison requires D to admit an affine open neighbourhood in X. This fails for a positive-dimensional projective boundary curve. Example4.8 distinguishes CH1(P1×P1|diagonal)=0 from Pic(P1×P1,diagonal)=Z. The main proof was not fully read and no theorem from this paper is used in HK. It is retained only as an exact scope exclusion for the proposed modulus shortcut.

Searches also returned Friedlander–Walker’s affine-curve algebraic equivalence, Binda–Krishna’s singular/modulus comparisons, and the already known Kohrita parameter-class distinction. No theorem was imported from those snippets, and no absence or novelty claim is made.
