### Record: agents/frobenius/C3_SNC_parameter_localization_RESEARCH.md

# Proper-parameter localization and its exact residue limitation

**Status:** unregistered auxiliary research; no main-gate movement is claimed.  
**Author:** GPT-6 Astra Pro (OpenAI), ChatGPT Pro mode, run `/root/frobenius_continuation`; inherited effort setting.  
**Written:** 2026-11-19T19:01:30.299663+00:00.

The purpose of this note is to identify precisely what the affine-parameter compactification route proves after C.3bt. It does not identify affine-parameter and proper-parameter equivalence. In particular, a nonzero obstruction below is not a surviving class in the final quotient: other proper families or component-family corrections may remove it.

## 1. Setup and a support-purity statement with a direct proof

Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic p>0, and let E be the projective SNC surface in C.3bt. All groups in this note have rational coefficients. Let P be a smooth connected projective k-curve, B a nonempty finite reduced set of k-points, and U=P\B. Denote by K(E×P on E×B) the actual nonconnective K-spectrum of perfect complexes with the indicated support. For each b∈B the closed immersion

    i_b : E = E×{b} → E×P

is regular of codimension one, so its perfect proper pushforward exists. It gives a natural equivalence

    ⊕_{b∈B} K(E)_Q  →  K(E×P on E×B)_Q.                 (PL.1)

This is not an application of regular-ambient dévissage to the singular scheme E×P. Here is the proof in the precise available SNC scope. Apply the every-degree rational closed-union descent of ET.6/UK.2 both to E×P and to E×U. Finite homotopy limits commute with the fibre defining support K-theory. The support spectrum is therefore the totalization of the corresponding support spectra for the smooth strata E_i, C_e and the individual triple points. On each smooth stratum Y, the scheme Y×P is regular; Quillen dévissage identifies K(Y×P on Y×B) with ⊕_B K(Y). The comparison maps are the actual i_b pushforwards. Their compatibility with all stratum pullbacks follows from the Tor-independent base-change squares: the equations of the parameter fibres lie in the P factor and remain non-zero-divisors on every stratum. Thus these stratum equivalences form a map of the actual coherent descent diagrams, including their geometric nullhomotopies. Their totalization is (PL.1).

For this proof, one may first treat a single b and then use excision for the disjoint supports. Equivalently, on a parameter coordinate chart the same equivalence follows from rational A¹-invariance for this SNC E (itself obtained by closed-union descent from the regular strata), the Bass fundamental theorem, and the elementary zero-section diagram in Thomason–Trobaugh Exercise9.13. The stratum proof above is sufficient and does not assume a purity theorem for arbitrary singular schemes.

Localization now gives an exact sequence of actual groups

    K0(E×P)_Q → K0(E×U)_Q
       --∂_B→ ⊕_{b∈B} K_{−1}(E)_Q
       --Σ(i_b)_*→ K_{−1}(E×P)_Q.                       (PL.2)

Consequently an actual affine-parameter class α extends as a K0 class to the fixed proper product E×P exactly when every residue b_b=∂_b(α) is zero. No assertion about extending an individual representative complex is needed; the relation group is defined using actual perfect K0 classes.

## 2. The Adams weight shift is one, not zero

Set

    V(E) = { e∈K_{−1}(E)_Q : ψ²(e)=2e }.

Suppose α∈K0(E×U)_Q is pure Adams weight two. Its residues in (PL.2) belong to V(E).

To check this without imposing semisimplicity on negative K-theory, work locally at b with a parameter z. Under (PL.1), i_b* is external multiplication by the Koszul support class [O_b]. That support class has Adams eigenvalue two: it is the localization boundary of z, and ψ²(z)=z²=2z in additive K1 notation. Product compatibility gives

    ψ²(i_b*e)=2 i_b*(ψ²e).

Naturality of raw-support localization gives ψ²(i_b*b_b)=4 i_b*b_b for the residue of α. Because (PL.1) is an isomorphism, this implies 2ψ²b_b=4b_b, hence ψ²b_b=2b_b. The argument proves an eigenvector assertion for these residues and uses no decomposition of all K_{−1}(E).

Every residue tuple has sum zero:

    Σ_{b∈B} b_b = 0 in V(E).                            (PL.3)

Indeed exactness of (PL.2) makes its total pushforward to E×P zero. The projection π:E×P→E is proper and perfect, and π_*i_b* is the identity. Applying π_* proves (PL.3).

## 3. Corrections by negative K-classes times parameter units

For e∈V(E) and a unit f∈O(U)^*, nonconnective exterior product gives an actual class

    e ⊠ f ∈ K0(E×U)_Q

of Adams weight two. Its residues are

    ∂_b(e⊠f) = ord_b(f)e.                               (PL.4)

This is the module compatibility of localization, or directly the localization boundary of the unit f on the regular parameter curve followed by exterior product with e. Possible uniform sign conventions can be absorbed into e; fix the convention in which the boundary of a uniformizer is the positive point class.

Let o,t∈U(k). Every component restriction of e vanishes, because K_{−1}(E_i)=0 for a regular component. Hence

    (e⊠f)_t − (e⊠f)_o
       = e·(f(t)−f(o))

lies in the component-map kernel in S(E). C.3bt proves that this endpoint difference belongs to J_K(E). In fact each endpoint product separately lies in that kernel. Thus subtracting these particular open-parameter corrections does not change the final proper-family quotient.

This is the precise way C.3bt interacts with compactification. It permits us to change an affine family by negative-K-times-unit terms. It does not assert that an arbitrary residue tuple can be cancelled by such terms.

## 4. The residual tensor obstruction for this correction method

Choose p0∈P(k). For a pure weight-two α, define

    Ω_P(α) = Σ_{b∈B} b_b ⊗ [O_P(b−p0)]
      ∈ V(E) ⊗_Q (Pic0(P)(k)⊗_Z Q).                   (PL.5)

Equation (PL.3) makes this independent of p0. Enlarging B by points where α already extends does not change it. The tensor is an ordinary abstract tensor of rational vector spaces; no unproved Somekawa or motivic identification is implicit.

If Ω_P(α)=0, then the endpoint difference α_t−α_o belongs to J_K(E).

**Complete proof.** The finitely many residues span a finite-dimensional subspace W of V(E). Choose a rational basis e_1,…,e_r and write b_b=Σ_j n_{jb}e_j with n_{jb}∈Q. Equation (PL.3) gives Σ_b n_{jb}=0 for each j. Since a vector-space inclusion W→V(E) stays injective after tensoring, Ω=0 says that every rational degree-zero divisor

    D_j = Σ_b n_{jb}[b]

has zero image in Pic0(P)(k)⊗Q. Clear the finitely many denominators and then multiply by an integer that kills the resulting finitely many torsion line-bundle classes. There are therefore positive integers N_j and rational functions f_j on P with

    div(f_j)=N_j D_j.

Their divisors are supported in B, so f_j is a unit on U. By (PL.4), the actual correction

    β = Σ_j (e_j/N_j)⊠f_j

has exactly the residues of α. Thus α−β extends by (PL.2) to a class x∈K0(E×P)_Q. Apply the finite Adams-weight-two projector to x. Its two endpoint restrictions are unchanged, because α−β already has pure weight two. This produces an actual gamma-two perfect family on the fixed E×P, so its endpoint difference lies in J_K(E). Section3 puts the endpoint difference of β in J_K(E) as well. Their sum is α_t−α_o, as required.

Conversely, for the restricted class of corrections used in Section3, (PL.4) and the divisor sequence show that the residues can be cancelled if and only if Ω=0. This restricted necessity must not be confused with necessity for belonging to J_K(E): the latter permits many more families and corrections.

## 5. Finite covers do not remove a nonzero Ω

Let f:Q→P be a finite map of smooth connected projective curves and pull α back over Q\f^{-1}(B). Flat pullback gives

    ∂_q(f*α)=e(q/b)b_b  for q over b.

Thus the tensor obstruction is

    Ω_Q(f*α)=(id_V⊗f*)Ω_P(α).                          (PL.6)

The norm of line bundles satisfies Nm_f(f*L)=L^{deg f}. Consequently

    (id_V⊗Nm_f)Ω_Q(f*α)=(deg f)Ω_P(α).

With rational coefficients, nonzero Ω_P therefore cannot become zero merely by finite pullback. This applies equally to inseparable finite maps of smooth curves: they are finite flat, the ramification/length factors are retained, and the norm pull-push formula has the same degree. The statement concerns this particular tensor obstruction, not the final quotient.

## 6. What an affine component graph supplies

Move component zero-cycles away from the double boundary. A point difference on a smooth component E_i can be realized on a smooth projective curve A⊂E_i transverse to all double curves and avoiding triple points. Delete the finitely many boundary-intersection points B⊂A. The graph in E×U, U=A\B, lies in the regular locus of E; it is a closed regular immersion of codimension two there and its structure sheaf, extended by zero, is perfect on all of E×U. Its weight-two projection is therefore an actual affine-parameter family with the required component endpoint point difference.

At a transverse boundary point b mapping to c∈C_e, the residue is the closed-union boundary of the point class [O_c] on that edge, with the sign determined by the incidence convention. This follows from the natural square comparing parameter localization with the two-branch closed-union fibre sequence. All triple restrictions in this local computation are zero by disjoint support, because A avoids the triple points. One can verify the formula by first extending the graph to the smooth component E_i×A: its edge restriction is the point class [O_c]⊠[O_b], and the boundary of that support class is the claimed negative-K residue. The order of the two connecting maps fixes a common sign.

These residues depend on the selected graph A→E_i, not on the two endpoint points in U. Hence Ω is unchanged when those endpoints are changed. In particular, merely asking that their difference be Albanese-trivial on E_i does not supply a proof that Ω=0. The initial support-purity/weight calculation leaves a genuine additional condition to establish.

For a finite sum of graph families, take a smooth proper common parameter curve through the desired endpoint tuples in the product of their parameter curves and remove all preimages of the finitely many boundary points. The sum of the pullbacks gives one actual affine-parameter class. The preceding residue analysis still applies; no proper extension is automatic.

## 7. Remaining routes and exact limitations

The elementary corrections in Section3 account only for principal parameter divisors with constant negative-K coefficients. An actual global affine family on E×U whose component endpoint differences vanish has endpoint difference in the C.3bt kernel, although its component values over U need not be constant; such a correction may alter Ω. A family initially constructed only on the individual components must first be glued over U before its global residues or Ω are defined. Producing enough actual affine corrections of this kind is the unresolved step.

The Poincare construction on A×Jac(A), restricted to a curve in ker(Jac(A)→Alb(E_i)) when the desired endpoint is Albanese-trivial, gives edge classes of the form

    Σ_{q∈A∩C_e} [q]⊠c1(N_q).

Normalizing their component degrees and Albanese coordinates leaves the explicit product-type obstruction already recorded in `agents/real_weil/COMPONENT_ALBANESE_KERNEL_RESEARCH.md`. Calling it a reciprocity pairing does not prove it is zero. No general Somekawa comparison, proper-part localization theorem, or representability assertion is used in this note.

The marked K1 interpolation in C.3bt has a different freedom: it constructs a variable unit g after choosing all relevant divisor supports and prescribes g=1 there. A fixed graph's residues in (PL.2) have already been determined by its boundary intersections. Repeating the marked-unit argument does not by itself vary those residues or the line-bundle tensor Ω.

Neither Ω≠0 nor failure of this compactification method proves nonvanishing of B². For example, C.3bt already kills the final quotient for every allowed rational-component model, including the NP nonzero-period model, regardless of whether a selected affine family extends.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C3_SNC_top_RESEARCH.md

# SNC exceptional divisors: exact progress and remaining gates

Updated 19 November 2026, after C.3bc. This is research material, not a certified arbitrary-germ theorem. C.3az treats a single smooth exceptional divisor over any algebraically closed positive-characteristic field. C.3bc now treats SNC exceptional divisors over Fpbar under the stated regular projective resolution and ample exceptional combination hypotheses.

## 1. The intended product torus does not survive the required geometry automatically

Let C be a cycle of rational curves and let E=C×P¹. The torus Pic⁰(C)=G_m contributes a nonzero summand Pic⁰(C)·h to K₀(E) of rational Adams weight two, by the projective-bundle formula. Take a non-torsion element when k is not algebraic over a finite field. Its Cartan image in G₀(E) is zero: on the normalization of C the line bundle is trivial, and the normalization exact sequence gives the same coherent-sheaf class for every gluing scalar.

If this exact E were a Cartier divisor in a regular threefold with conormal L of positive P¹ degree a, self-intersection would give u(1−L)=0 because the coherent pushforward of u vanishes. The product calculation instead gives −a·u h, which is nonzero rationally. Thus one cannot simply put a negative ample normal bundle on that unmodified SNC product inside a regular ambient threefold.

The actual regular plumbing alters the component Picard groups. In the simple cycle case, the old boundary-degree matrix has rows (1,0,−1), (−1,1,0), (0,−1,1), of rank two. Blowing up a point of one boundary curve on one surface component supplies a new exceptional divisor with boundary-degree row (1,0,0), raising the rank to three. The dual graph is unchanged, while the top degree-unit gluing quotient disappears. A preserved dual-complex loop by itself is insufficient.

Multiplying a lifted Picard-torus class by c₁(O_Z(−E)) is also not a new puncture class: that product is exceptional-supported and vanishes on the puncture.

## 2. A general weighted intersection identity kills the degree-unit edge quotient

The complete proof is in `C3_SNC_energy_lemma.tex`, kept unregistered pending the parent’s decision. Let E=∪E_i be a projective SNC divisor of dimension d≥2 in regular Z. Let D=Σ a_iE_i with all a_i>0, and let H be ample on E. Assume λ_ij=deg((−D)|E_i∩E_j H^(d−2))>0 for every double stratum. In particular this holds when −D restricts to an ample bundle on E.

A functional t on the edge degree vectors annihilates the component-curve restriction map precisely when R_i=Σ_j t_ij[E_i∩E_j] is numerically zero on every E_i, with t_ij=−t_ji. Put u_ij=t_ij/(a_i a_j). Squaring the numerical relations, multiplying by H^(d−2), and summing with weights a_i gives

    0 = −Σ_edges a_i a_j λ_ij u_ij²
        −Σ_triples a_i a_j a_k deg(H^(d−2)|E_i∩E_j∩E_k)
                       (u_ij+u_jk+u_ki)².

The transverse normal identities produce exactly these coefficients. Positivity forces every t to vanish. Hence the restriction-degree map from component curve classes onto the edge degree vectors is surjective over Q. Tensoring with k*⊗Q kills the entire proposed degree-unit edge cokernel using curve-class-times-unit K₁ elements on the components.

This proves a method limitation and an exact linear-algebraic input; it does not dispose of every term in the SNC K-theory spectral sequence or lift arbitrary proper-parameter relations from E to Z.

The symbolic certificate is `code/check_SNC_energy_identity.py`, with output `output/check_SNC_energy_identity.json`. Final successful run began 11:47:35.265121 UTC and took 0.043683026 seconds. Both exact weighted polynomial expansions vanish; the displayed degree matrices have ranks two and three. The first attempt completed the mathematics but failed JSON serialization of SymPy integer objects; explicit integer conversion repaired only output serialization. No geometric inference depends on a bounded computation.

## 3. Primary plumbing and contraction source actually read

Kollár, J. (2014). Simple normal crossing varieties with prescribed dual complex. *Algebraic Geometry, 1*(1), 57–68. https://doi.org/10.14231/AG-2014-004 . Primary full PDF: <https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-1/2014-1-004.pdf>.

We opened the full published PDF and read Lemma 15, printed p.63, Lemma16 and full explicit chart proof, pp.63–64, and the proof of Theorem2, p.64. Starting with a projective SNC divisor D in smooth Y, blowing up D∩H preserves its strict transform as the same abstract D and changes its normal bundle to O_Y(D−H)|D. The new ambient has the explicit local equations x₁…x_r=yz. Ordered blowups of the irreducible components supply a small log resolution, preserving the dual complex but altering some component geometry. The contraction step invokes Artin1970 Corollary6.12.a and gives an algebraic construction étale locally. We have not yet independently opened that underlying Artin source in this SNC investigation; it is a cited input in the fully opened Kollár proof. Page59 explicitly says the constructions apply over arbitrary fields, with the positive-characteristic/nonclosed-field caveat referred to Kollár’s book. The branch used here is the explicit blowup/small-resolution construction, not the separate double-cover construction of Lemma14.

This source resolves the regular-plumbing question for these models, but does not preserve the top K₁ class proposed on the initial product.

## 4. Triple strata: coefficient K₂ is neither automatically rigid nor automatically liftable

The precise proper-curve symbol lemma was already fully proved and independently audited in real_weil/TOP_QUOTIENT_RESEARCH.md §2. For a,b∈k* with neither equal to1, normalize a component through (a,b) of

    (f−1)²(g−1)² = c f g,  c=(a−1)²(b−1)²/(ab).

There are no vertical/horizontal components. At the boundary one coordinate is1, so {f,g} has no tame residue. At the unique point over (0,1), the derivative −c is nonzero even in characteristic2, f=u(g−1)², and the Steinberg relation kills 2{g−1,g}. The specialization is zero there and is {a,b} at the chosen interior point. Quillen’s exact curve localization sequence and Gersten theorem give an actual element of K₂ of the smooth proper parameter curve. This works in every characteristic. The peer’s exact primary locators are Quillen1973 §7 Proposition3.2/equation(3.3), pp.127–128, and Theorem5.11, pp.133–134, with the full primary PDF retained in its source ledger.

Consequently, if a triple-stratum class in K₀(E) is the product of a fixed class κ∈K_{−2}(E) with a coefficient in K₂(k), the same multiplication on E×P converts that coefficient-symbol relation into an actual proper-parameter K₀ relation on E. It is not legitimate to call this term rigid solely because it involves field K₂.

There is a second, separate obstruction before even discussing ordinary families on Z. KST descent, after the rational nilpotent comparison, gives the exact segment

    K₀(Z)_Q → K₀(E)_Q → K_{−1}(R)_Q → 0,

because Z is regular and local K₀(R)=Q maps onto local K₀(k)=Q. At the negative end it gives K_{−2}(E)_Q ≅ K_{−3}(R)_Q. All maps are K(k)-linear. Thus multiplying a dual-complex generator by a coefficient in K₂(k) may map nontrivially into K_{−1}(R), rather than lie in the image of K₀(Z). No injectivity of that product map or uniform image description has been proved here. This is an exact lifting gate, not an existing counterexample.

Even if a class lies in that image, a proper-family relation on E still needs an actual lift to the fixed Z×P. C.3az constructs such lifts for the smooth exceptional case by a special surface-and-line-bundle argument. No corresponding result for general SNC E is claimed.

## 5. Complex negative-K source: exact scope

Burke, A., Popa, M., and Shen, W. (2026, September15). Negative K-theory and Hodge theory. Primary preprint: https://people.math.harvard.edu/~mpopa/papers/NegativeK.pdf . The canonical opened-marked entry is frBurkePopaShen2026 in C3_SNC_references.bib. The local full PDF and text are retained in sources/burke_popa_shen2026_negativeK.pdf and .txt; SHA256 78f37b7f256a694f0f7aad4620a594ed4ccc6441f2887fceb0facbf7c1df17c1.

Theorem9.1, pp28–31, proves surjectivity of rational CH² of a resolution onto the direct sum of exceptional-surface CH0 groups for complex projective isolated klt-type threefolds. The rational-singularity case has a Bloch-conjectural condition; the additional LCI hypothesis supplies an integral refinement, further explained on pp31–32. The proof uses the exceptional Gysin/Albanese matrix and mixed-Hodge purity and polarization. Lemma13.1, p40, transfers negative K-theory between algebraic semilocal models and compactifications with the same isolated singularities. It does not assert invariance under henselization or completion. Corollary13.2(ii) still records the algebraic-versus-analytic factoriality defect. Neither the complex hypothesis nor the singularity hypotheses can be dropped here. The source therefore gives no automatic positive-characteristic or arbitrary strict-local SNC lifting theorem.

The product boundary warning in §4 remains rational: a nonzero dual-complex class in negative K does not imply its positive-coefficient product has nonzero connecting image in K−1(R)_Q. The surface-cusp calculation already shows that such products can vanish. No integral vanishing of the remaining p-primary groups is asserted.

## 6. Completed Fpbar theorem and next gate

C.3bc is finalized in C3_SNC_Fpbar_top.tex, with full report, one statement row and canonical events. The Fpbar hypothesis kills all positive top-weight field Milnor K groups. Closed-union excision and the explicitly arbitrary-scheme Adams construction then identify the top weight of K0(E)_Q with component degree vectors. Uniform KST finite detection injects CH^d(Z)_Q into that vector space, and a negative-definite exceptional-curve degree matrix spans it. Thus the entire rational top Chow group of the puncture is zero. No family lifting is needed for this field.

The next proposed extension is to arbitrary excellent isolated germs by alterations or ldh descent. This is unproved here. A generically finite alteration is not an isomorphism away from the closed point, so it does not yield the abstract blow-up square or the constant-group finite-detection argument used in C.3bc. A low-dimensional corollary must separately establish a regular projective SNC resolution and a positive exceptional divisor with negative ample restriction. No arbitrary-dimensional resolution theorem is presumed.
# New endpoint comparison and current arbitrary-SNC gate (16:57 UTC, 19 November 2026)

The complete endpoint theorem EL and comparison EP were typed by the real_weil agent and independently passed in this agent's two new reviews. Their precise conclusion is that, under the algebraizable regular threefold/SNC/ample-conormal hypotheses, ordinary CH² relations on the resolution correspond exactly to endpoint differences of filtration-two perfect K0 classes on the fixed exceptional product E times a smooth proper curve. The prescribed whole family need not lift. The general residual quotient is

`F_gamma² K0(E)_Q / (proper-perfect-family endpoint differences + exceptional CH1 image)`.

This removes an ambient endpoint obstruction but does not compute the intrinsic proper-family relation subgroup of an arbitrary SNC surface.

The descent diagonal has component CH0 terms, double-curve K1 of Adams weight two, and triple-point K2 terms. Such edge families therefore need not glue to a perfect class on E times the parameter. Component CH0 families similarly have nonzero restrictions on double-curve products. No claim of intrinsic relation generation has been made.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C3_cone_codim2_kernel_RESEARCH.md

# A precise projective subproblem inside rational local injectivity

19 November 2026. This is an unregistered research reduction, not a solution of the remaining universal rational restriction assertion and not a movement claim. It uses the already certified C.3ax and C.4a.

Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic $p>0$. Let $V/k$ be a smooth projective connected fourfold, let $L$ be very ample with normal degree-one-generated full section ring, and let $H\in|L|$ be smooth connected. Form the strict local cone puncture $X$ over $(V,L)$ and its principal punctured hyperplane $Y$. Write $J^r$ for ordinary algebraically trivial cycles modulo rational equivalence, using actual proper parameter curves.

The following comparison is the exact obstruction already present in this restricted family:

\[
\ker\bigl(J^2(V)_{\mathbf Q}\longrightarrow J^2(H)_{\mathbf Q}\bigr)
\simeq
\ker\bigl(J^2(X)_{\mathbf Q}\longrightarrow J^2(Y)_{\mathbf Q}\bigr).
\]

We give the argument to distinguish this projective cycle problem from an infinitesimal nilpotent problem. We do not assert that either kernel vanishes.

## Cone and ordinary-family identifications

C.3ax identifies both rational Chow and ordinary-algebraic quotients of the strict local cone with their projective quotients. Its proof applies also to the standard graded quotient ring $S/(s)$ defining the hyperplane cone, even if that quotient ring is not the full normal section ring of $H$. Indeed, its degree-one blow-up charts are the total line bundle $L_H^{-1}$, the puncture is regular, the exceptional zero section is $H$, and there is still an actual retraction to $H$. KST finite detection, nilpotent invariance after inverting $p$, Chern pullback, and ordinary-family localization use precisely these properties; normality of this quotient cone is not an extra premise.

For either $W=V$ or $W=H$, these identifications and the defining kernel $J^2=\ker(\mathrm{CH}^2\to B^2)$ give

\[
J^2(X_W)_{\mathbf Q}
\simeq
\frac{J^2(W)_{\mathbf Q}}
 {J^2(W)_{\mathbf Q}\cap c_1(L_W)\operatorname{Pic}(W)_{\mathbf Q}}.
\]

To see surjectivity directly, if a projective lift of an ordinary-trivial punctured cycle has class $c_1(L_W)b$ in $B^2(W)$, choose an actual divisor representative of $b$ and subtract its $L_W$-multiple. The resulting projective lift is ordinary algebraically trivial. This uses the already proved actual-family localization, not a family on a varying étale neighbourhood.

The denominator is exactly $c_1(L_W)\operatorname{Pic}^0(W)(k)_{\mathbf Q}$. One inclusion is immediate. For the reverse inclusion, if $L_WD$ is algebraically trivial, its prime-to-$p$ cycle class is zero. Hard Lefschetz makes multiplication by $L_W$ injective on $H^2(W,\mathbf Q_\ell(1))$ in dimensions three and four. The Kummer sequence and the finite-generation theorem for Néron–Severi groups then imply $D\in\operatorname{Pic}^0(W)(k)_{\mathbf Q}$. Possible torsion Néron–Severi classes disappear after tensoring with $\mathbf Q$.

## The two divisor columns are isomorphic

Weak Lefschetz on $H^1(-,\mathbf Q_\ell)$ shows that the pullback of reduced Picard varieties $\operatorname{Pic}^0(V)\to\operatorname{Pic}^0(H)$ is an isogeny. Its map on $k$-points therefore becomes an isomorphism after tensoring with $\mathbf Q$; this conclusion allows a finite inseparable kernel and needs no stronger integral Picard assertion.

For a smooth projective variety $W$ of dimension at least two, multiplication by $L_W$ is injective on $\operatorname{Pic}^0(W)(k)_{\mathbf Q}$ as a map to $J^2(W)_{\mathbf Q}$. If $L_WD=0$, multiply by $L_W^{\dim W-2}$ and apply the Albanese map. The resulting map from the Picard variety to the Albanese is the degree-one Lefschetz isogeny of C.4a. Its kernel is finite, so $D=0$ rationally. This is an actual zero-cycle/Albanese argument, not an assertion that a Picard-zero divisor has nonzero ordinary cohomology.

We consequently have a commutative diagram with exact rows

\[
0\to L\operatorname{Pic}^0(V)_{\mathbf Q}
\to J^2(V)_{\mathbf Q}\to J^2(X)_{\mathbf Q}\to0,
\]

\[
0\to L_H\operatorname{Pic}^0(H)_{\mathbf Q}
\to J^2(H)_{\mathbf Q}\to J^2(Y)_{\mathbf Q}\to0,
\]

whose first vertical arrow is an isomorphism. The snake lemma gives the claimed kernel isomorphism.

## Scope and implication

The local ring has dimension five and the cycles have codimension two. Thus the first high-range rational local problem already contains an ordinary projective restriction problem for fourfolds. The argument does not prove that every arbitrary local germ reduces to a cone, does not identify a conjecture with the full universal local assertion, and does not prove projective Chow weak Lefschetz. It only shows explicitly where the previously proved cone rigidity stops.

Source dependencies are C.3ax's completely opened KST/GH/TT/Fulton/actual-family inputs and C.4a's opened Kleiman Appendix Theorem2A9(5)–(6), together with the classical prime-to-characteristic cohomological weak/hard Lefschetz and Kummer inputs already used throughout the master. No newly searched theorem is used as an unverified replacement for a cycle-level assertion.

## The ordinary incidence test excludes every cycle, not only divisor products

There is a particularly concrete limitation on the proposed supersingular-surface variant. Let $W$ be **any** smooth projective threefold, let $B$ be very ample, and choose two sections whose common zero locus $B_0$ is a smooth connected curve. The smooth incidence divisor

\[
H=\{x_0s_0+x_1s_1=0\}\subset V=\mathbf P^1\times W
\]

is $\pi:H=\operatorname{Bl}_{B_0}W\to W$. If $E$ is its exceptional divisor, then the pullback of the hyperplane class from $\mathbf P^1$ is $h=\pi^*c_1(B)-E$.

The integral projective-bundle and codimension-two blow-up formulas identify the ordinary-trivial groups, after tensoring with $\mathbf Q$, as

\[
J^2(V)_{\mathbf Q}=J^2(W)_{\mathbf Q}\oplus h\operatorname{Pic}^0(W)_{\mathbf Q},
\qquad
J^2(H)_{\mathbf Q}=J^2(W)_{\mathbf Q}\oplus\operatorname{Pic}^0(B_0)_{\mathbf Q}.
\]

These decompositions preserve ordinary algebraic equivalence in both directions because the projective-bundle/blow-up maps and their inverses are actual pullback, pushforward, and divisor-intersection operations on the fixed products with a proper parameter curve. With the exceptional summand normalized by $j_*q^*$, restriction sends

\[
\alpha+hD\longmapsto\bigl(\alpha+c_1(B)D,-D|_{B_0}\bigr).
\]

Repeated cohomological weak Lefschetz shows that $\operatorname{Pic}^0(W)\to\operatorname{Pic}^0(B_0)$ has finite kernel. Consequently, if this ordered pair vanishes rationally, then $D=0$ and then $\alpha=0$. Restriction is therefore injective on **all** ordinary algebraically trivial codimension-two cycles in this incidence test. A nondivisorial class in $J^2(W)$ is not lost by the calculation; it is the first component and is detected directly.

Together with the cone kernel comparison, this excludes a rational kernel from the corresponding split-cone incidence construction, including the case $W$ is a product of a supersingular surface and a curve. It does not exclude other ample hypersurfaces, a singular leading divisor, or a general nonconical modification. The exact integral blow-up/projective-bundle inputs are the already opened Jiang Theorems2.4/2.8(3) and Stacks Tag02TX used throughout the certified cubic arguments. No new main-gate movement is inferred from this construction limitation.

# Exact negative-K obstruction for an actual fixed-parameter family

Research auxiliary, 19 November 2026, `/root/frobenius`. This is unregistered and is not a main-gate movement claim. The full proof is in `C3_fixed_family_negative_K.tex`.

## Result and scope

Let R be a noetherian local k-algebra of characteristic p, with k algebraically closed and equal to its residue field. Let Z be a regular proper modification which is an isomorphism off the closed point, and let E be its reduced exceptional fibre. For a fixed smooth proper k-scheme P, we prove

$$
\operatorname{coker}\bigl(K_0(Z\times P)[1/p]\to K_0(E\times P)[1/p]\bigr)
\simeq K_{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}R\times P)[1/p].
$$

The intended parameter is a smooth proper connected curve. The proof works for the more general smooth proper P stated above. It uses an actual fixed product. It uses no inverse limit, no uniform bound on denominators across all thickenings, and no assertion that compatible virtual classes admit compatible bounded-rank representatives. It keeps the nonlocal term K0(SpecR×P) rather than replacing it with Z.

KST supplies the exact pro-sequence for the base-changed abstract blow-up. GH makes each nilpotent thickening levelwise equivalent after inverting p. Every term is then a constant pro-group, so ordinary exactness follows. The negative groups of the two regular terms vanish. Finally, classes pulled back from P already lift through Z×P.

## Candidate coefficient and exact remaining question

The separate tetrahedral regular resolution has now been proved in `C3_tetrahedral_resolution.tex` (TG.1–TG.5), with full independent root and peer audits. This supersedes the earlier geometry gate recorded here. Its proposed coefficient is a product of a dual-complex class kappa of degree −2 and a field symbol u in K2(k). For a proper-curve representative xi of the difference u−0, the exact family obstruction is xi times the boundary of kappa in K−1(SpecR×P). The fact that the boundary on degree −2 is an isomorphism does not imply injectivity or vanishing after multiplication by xi. No faithfulness statement for this module action has been proved.

We have read the complete current `../real_weil/SEMIPURITY_TOP_RESEARCH.md`, including its conditional coherent vanishing calculation and the newly opened Dayton–Weibel affine tetrahedron result. Neither replaces the actual fixed-product obstruction above. The multiplication map for an actual proper-parameter family remains an outstanding requirement; the separate regular small-resolution geometry is now established.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C3_higher_component_kernel_RESEARCH.md

# A polynomial removal of the K1 component kernel

**Research proof; unregistered; low-degree field-K3 source audit remains explicit below.** Written 19 November 2026 by `/root/frobenius_continuation`. The purpose is to make the endpoint of the supported HK construction exact on the whole exceptional scheme, before applying the normal-base K1 lifting theorem. It does not solve the symbolic-unit/base-change gate.

## HG.1. Setting and field input

Retain the exceptional SNC surface and ample negative combination hypotheses of C.3bt. All groups in this note are rational. Let

\[
\mathcal T_P=\operatorname{fib}\left(
 \bigoplus_eK(C_e\times P)\longrightarrow\bigoplus_vK(P)\right),
\]

with the same canonical totalization and geometric nullhomotopy as UK.2. For a point or a smooth proper curve (P), the actual exact sequences in the next degree are

\[
\bigoplus_vK_3(P)\longrightarrow\pi_2\mathcal T_P
 \longrightarrow\bigoplus_eK_2(C_e\times P)
 \longrightarrow\bigoplus_vK_2(P),
\tag{HG.1}
\]
\[
\pi_2\mathcal T_P\xrightarrow{\partial_P}K_1(E\times P)
 \longrightarrow\bigoplus_iK_1(E_i\times P).
\tag{HG.2}
\]

Let (J_1(E)) be the subgroup generated by endpoint differences of actual (K_1) classes on fixed products (E\times P), with (P) smooth connected projective. Put

\[
                    r=(\psi^2-4)/4.
\tag{HG.3}
\]

The extra field input is the standard low-degree statement

\[
(\psi^2-4)K_3(k)_{\mathbf Q}
   \subseteq\operatorname{im}\bigl(K_3^M(k)_{\mathbf Q}\to K_3(k)_{\mathbf Q}\bigr).
\tag{FK}
\]

Only this containment is used; no decomposition of (K_1(E)), (\pi_2\mathcal T_P), or (K_1(E\times P)) into eigenspaces is assumed. Weibel's ChapterVI, low-degree exact sequence4.3.1 and Adams action4.9, give FK: the quotient by Milnor (K_3) is (H^1(k,\mathbf Z(2))), and its rational Adams action has weight two. ChapterIV, Example5.9.1, gives weight (n) on every (n)-fold Milnor symbol.

## HG.2. The asserted kernel inclusion

The proposed conclusion is

\[
r^2\ker\left(K_1(E)\longrightarrow\bigoplus_iK_1(E_i)\right)
                              \subseteq J_1(E).
\tag{HG.4}
\]

The subgroup (J_1(E)) is preserved by the Adams operation because it is functorial on the actual products and under the two endpoint pullbacks. Thus all the polynomial operations below preserve actual proper families.

Take (\kappa) in this component kernel. By HG.2 for the point, choose (y\in\pi_2\mathcal T_k) with (\partial_k y=\kappa). Apply (r). On a smooth edge curve (C), restriction to its function field intertwines the operation, and (K_2(k(C))) has pure weight two by Matsumoto and product compatibility. Therefore the edge image of (r y) belongs to the kernel of

\[
                     K_2(C)\longrightarrow K_2(k(C)).
\]

Localization for the regular curve identifies that kernel with the image of the sum of point pushforwards of (K_2(k)). This is a kernel statement; no global injectivity of (K_2(C)) is assumed.

Matsumoto expresses each coefficient as a finite sum of symbols ({a,b}), (a,b\in k^*). By the projection formula, the point pushforward equals ({a,b}[\mathcal O_x]). On a regular curve,

\[
[\mathcal O_x]=[\mathcal O_C(x)]-1
\quad\text{in }K_0(C),
\]

because the twist on the finite point is trivial. Thus every edge image is a finite sum of

\[
                    \{a,b\}([L_e]-1),
                   \qquad L_e\in\operatorname{Pic}(C_e).
\tag{HG.5}
\]

These are pure weight-three classes, directly by multiplicativity and the curve's square-zero rank-zero ideal.

## HG.3. Remove degrees using the same actual component corrections

For each of the finitely many symbols ({a,b}), use the surjective degree map ET.9

\[
\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Pic}(E_i)_{\mathbf Q}
                  \longrightarrow\bigoplus_e\mathbf Q
\]

to lift the vector of edge degrees. Multiply the component divisor (K_0) differences by that constant (K_2(k)) symbol. Their actual images in (\pi_2\mathcal T_k) are canonical images from the component term in the totalization, so their boundaries in HG.2 vanish. Subtract them from (r y). The remaining edge vector is a sum of HG.5 with every (L_e\in\operatorname{Pic}^0(C_e)). This step uses only degree surjectivity, not full Picard restriction surjectivity. Rational divisors and denominators are cleared before choosing their actual line-bundle representatives.

## HG.4. Proper K2 edge families from marked VE

For a degree-zero tuple in HG.5, apply the marked VE lemma with constant unit (b). It gives actual (\xi_e\in K_1(C_e\times P)), with endpoint difference (b([L_e]-1)) and literally zero restriction at every marked triple point. Multiply by the other constant unit (a\in K_1(k)). The resulting actual classes

\[
                \Gamma_e=a\cdot\xi_e\in K_2(C_e\times P)
\]

have endpoint difference ({a,b}([L_e]-1)) and still have literally zero marked restrictions in (K_2(P)). HG.1 therefore lifts the edge tuple to (\widetilde y\in\pi_2\mathcal T_P). Its boundary in HG.2 is an actual proper (K_1) family on (E\times P).

Apply this to the finitely many symbol tuples separately, or combine them on a smooth curve in the product of their proper parameter curves through their two endpoint tuples. Let (h\in J_1(E)) be the sum of the resulting endpoint differences. Because their edge images equal the remaining edges of (r y), HG.1 for the point supplies a tuple (\nu\in\bigoplus_vK_3(k)) with

\[
                      r\kappa-h=\partial_k(\nu).
\tag{HG.6}
\]

The notation on the right denotes the canonical composite vertex map and boundary. This equality retains the entire coherent-lift ambiguity; no uniqueness is assumed.

## HG.5. Remove the vertex ambiguity with one more polynomial

Apply (r) to HG.6. The natural Adams operation commutes with the totalization and the closed-union boundary, at the same arbitrary-scheme scope used in UK.4. Thus

\[
                 r^2\kappa-rh=\partial_k(r\nu).
\tag{HG.7}
\]

By FK, each entry of (r\nu) is a rational sum of Milnor triple symbols ({a,b,c}). The actual proper-curve (K_2) symbol construction of C.3bq realizes every ({b,c}) as an evaluation difference. Multiplication by the constant (a\in K_1(k)) gives an actual (K_3) family with endpoint ({a,b,c}). Applying the vertex map and then the boundary in HG.1–HG.2 produces an actual proper (K_1) family on (E) with endpoint (partial_k(r\nu)). Hence the right side of HG.7 lies in (J_1(E)), as does (rh). This proves HG.4, subject only to the stated standard field input FK and the already audited bt/bq inputs.

## HG.6. Exact HK endpoints and fixed-base ambient correction

Let (\beta\in F_\gamma^2K_0(E)_{\mathbf Q}) have component zero-cycle restrictions of degree zero, and let (u\in k^*). HK constructs actual proper (K_1) families whose summed endpoint class (\delta\in K_1(E)) has component image (\{u\}\beta|_{E_i}). Thus

\[
                 \delta-\{u\}\beta\in\ker(K_1E\to\bigoplus_iK_1E_i).
\]

By HG.4, (r^2(\delta-\{u\}\beta)\in J_1(E)). The desired product has pure weight three, so (r(\{u\}\beta)=\{u\}\beta). Since (r^2\delta\in J_1(E)), it follows that

\[
                          \{u\}\beta\in J_1(E).
\tag{HG.8}
\]

This equality is on the whole exceptional scheme, rather than only after restricting to its components. It means a finite sum of actual fixed proper families; combining parameters as above gives a single family if desired.

For a normal local base in NK.7, each family in HG.8 lifts on the actual fixed (Z\times P). Under the henselian point isomorphism FF.4, let (\beta_Z\) be the unique weight-two lift of (\beta). The discrepancy between the lifted total endpoint and ({u\}\beta_Z) lies in the image of the residue-zero subgroup of (R^*=K_1(R)). Applying (s=(\psi^2-2)/6) kills it and preserves the desired weight-three product. Consequently

\[
                         \{u\}\beta_Z\in J_1(Z)
                                  \qquad(u\in k^*).
\tag{HG.9}
\]

This argument uses polynomial operations and exact sequences only. It makes no global higher-(K) weight projector and assumes no Adams semisimplicity on the singular totalization.

## HG.7. The remaining limitation

HG.9 is for constants (u\in k^*\) on the original fixed local coefficient-field model. A valuation argument needs a symbolic unit after a transcendental scalar extension. The ring (R\otimes_k k(u)) is generally nonlocal, so NK.7 does not apply there by formal base change. The regular-target specialization theorem RS can be used only once an actual constant-target proper family and exact endpoint have both been supplied. HG removes the endpoint ambiguity at a fixed local base; it does not provide that missing family over the nonlocal scalar extension.

No change to UK.7 or main-gate status is claimed. No tensor-exterior-product injectivity or general singular-specialization theorem is assumed.

## Source ledger

Freshly read in this continuation: Weibel, *The K-book*, ChapterIV, Theorem5.9 and its entire printed proof, Example5.9.1, Proposition5.10 and its printed proof, Remark5.10.1, Theorem5.11 and its printed proof, author pp50–52; ChapterVI, low-degree sequence4.3.1, Proposition4.3.2 and its entire printed proof, author pp17–18, and Adams paragraph4.9, authorp21. Primary author-hosted PDFs:

- https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~weibel/Kbook/Kbook.IV.pdf
- https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~weibel/Kbook/Kbook.VI.pdf

The proof uses the special field containment FK, deduced from the displayed low-degree exact sequence and weight action. It does **not** invoke IV5.11 as a semisimplicity theorem for a singular scheme or a homotopy totalization. The full construction of the motivic spectral sequence cited by Weibel, and the full original proof of its Adams compatibility, have not been freshly read in this window. That source-audit dependency is retained for any promotion decision; no nonexistent printed proof is attributed to the concise Adams paragraph.

The regular-curve localization, Matsumoto, product, actual VE/bq families, ET.9, and exact coherent totalization inputs are the previously fully audited sources of C.3bt. ET.9 is in `../cycles/SNC_edge_triple_correction.tex`; its weighted identity is proved in `C3_SNC_energy_lemma.tex`. Normal-base K1 lifting and the residue-zero unit kernel are proved separately in `C3_normal_base_K1_family_RESEARCH.md`.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C3_normal_base_K1_family_RESEARCH.md

# Rank and determinant on a constant proper curve, and whole K1 family lifting

**Proved auxiliary under the stated hypotheses; unregistered and pending complete peer review.** Written after checkpoint23 thaw on 19 November 2026 by `/root/frobenius_continuation`. No main-gate movement is claimed. The field extension needed for a symbolic valuation remains an actual-base-change problem.

## NK.1. The rank-and-determinant statement

Let (k) be an algebraically closed field, (R) a noetherian local coefficient-(k) algebra with residue field (k), and (P/k) a smooth connected projective curve. Put (B=\operatorname{Spec}R\times_kP). Then rank and determinant induce an integral isomorphism of abelian groups

\[
K_0(B)\xrightarrow{\ (\mathrm{rk},\det)\ }
                       \mathbf Z\oplus\operatorname{Pic}(B).
\tag{NK.1}
\]

The augmentation ideal has square zero and

\[
F_\gamma^2K_0(B)=0,\qquad
 (\psi^q-1)(\psi^q-q)=0\text{ on }K_0(B)
                    \quad(q\ge1).
\tag{NK.2}
\]

No henselian, normal, regular, or characteristic assumption is needed for NK.1–NK.2. The algebraically closed coefficient field is used for a general section on the closed curve; the argument more generally works over an infinite field with a geometrically integral closed curve and the same section argument.

### Proof: every bundle has a line-bundle filtration

Fix an ample line bundle (H) on (P), and denote its pullback by the same symbol. For a vector bundle (V) of rank (r\ge2), relative Serre generation gives finitely many global sections generating (V\otimes H^n) on (B), for (n\) sufficiently large. Their restrictions generate on the closed fibre (P).

There is a (k)-linear combination of these restricted sections which is nowhere zero on (P). In the finite-dimensional coefficient space, vanishing at a fixed point imposes (r) independent linear conditions. The corresponding incidence over the one-dimensional (P) therefore has dimension at most the coefficient-space dimension plus (1-r), strictly smaller than the coefficient-space dimension. Properness of (P) makes its image closed; a general coefficient vector avoids it. Lift the coefficients using (k\subset R).

The zero scheme of the resulting actual section on (B) is closed and proper over (\operatorname{Spec}R). If nonempty, its proper image is a nonempty closed subset of a local scheme and therefore contains the closed point, contrary to the construction on (P). Thus the section is nowhere zero on all of (B). It gives a line subbundle (H^{-n}\hookrightarrow V) with locally free quotient of rank (r-1). Induction gives a filtration with line-bundle quotients. Since (B) has an ample line bundle relative to an affine base, its perfect (K_0) is its vector-bundle (K_0). Consequently (K_0(B)) is generated additively by line-bundle classes.

### Proof: line differences have finite semilocal support

Let (M) be a line bundle on (B). For (n\) sufficiently large, both (M\otimes H^n) and (H^n) have generating global sections. Choose sections whose restrictions to the integral closed curve are nonzero. Their closed-fibre zero schemes are finite effective Cartier divisors, possibly empty.

Let (D_+) and (D_-) be their actual zero schemes on (B). These schemes are locally principal by construction. At every point of the closed fibre where a zero occurs, the fibrewise Cartier criterion applies to the flat finite-presentation map (B\to\operatorname{Spec}R): Stacks Lemma31.19.9(3), Tag062Y, gives an open neighbourhood on which that zero scheme is an effective Cartier divisor flat over (R). Where the section is a unit the same assertion is immediate. These neighbourhoods cover the entire closed fibre. Their union must equal (B), because its closed complement is proper over the local base and misses that fibre. Thus (D_\pm) are relative effective Cartier divisors everywhere.

Each (D_\pm\to\operatorname{Spec}R) is proper with finite closed fibre. Stacks Lemma37.44.2, Tag02UP, makes it finite over an open neighbourhood of the closed point, and every such open in a local scheme is the whole scheme. Hence (D_\pm) is finite over (R). A finite algebra over a local ring is semilocal. Every line bundle on it is trivial by the Chinese-remainder/Nakayama proof already supplied for WP.4 (Stacks02M9).

The two Cartier exact sequences, followed by multiplication by (H^{-n}), now give the exact identity

\[
[M]-1=[\mathcal O_{D_+}]-[\mathcal O_{D_-}]
                         \quad\text{in perfect }K_0(B).
\tag{NK.3}
\]

For any other line bundle (N) on (B), its restriction to either finite semilocal divisor is trivial. The projection formula for the perfect Cartier pushforward consequently gives

\[
([M]-1)([N]-1)=0\quad\text{in }K_0(B).
\tag{NK.4}
\]

No assertion that a general coherent sheaf on (B) is perfect is used: the finite divisor sheaves are perfect because their immersions are Cartier.

### Proof: exact rank, determinant and operations

Because line classes generate, the rank-zero subgroup (I) is generated by ([M]-1). Formula NK.4 says (I^2=0). Thus

\[
[MN]-1=([M]-1)+([N]-1),
\]

and (M\mapsto[M]-1) is a group homomorphism (\operatorname{Pic}(B)\to I). It is inverse to determinant on the generating line differences, proving NK.1. In a special lambda ring generated by line elements, gamma operations on rank-zero expressions are products of their line differences: (\gamma_z([M]-1)=1+([M]-1)z). Every term of gamma degree at least two therefore vanishes by NK.4. Finally

\[
\psi^q([M])=[M]^q=1+q([M]-1)
\]

proves NK.2 directly. This is a calculation of the operator; no semisimplicity assumption is needed.

## NK.2. Injectivity after a normal modification

Now assume (R) is a normal domain and (g:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R) is a proper birational morphism of integral noetherian schemes. Assume (Z) is regular when invoking the (K)-theory conclusion below. Put (g_P:Z\times P\to B). Then

\[
g_{P*}\mathcal O_{Z\times P}=\mathcal O_B,
\qquad
\operatorname{Pic}(B)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(Z\times P).
\tag{NK.5}
\]

Here is a direct check of the structure-sheaf assertion. A regular function on (Z) is a rational function in (\operatorname{Frac}R). For every height-one prime of the normal noetherian (R), the local ring is a DVR. Properness extends its generic-point map to (Z); pulling back the function shows that it belongs to that DVR. The intersection characterization of a noetherian normal domain gives that the function lies in (R). The same argument on affine opens gives (g_*\mathcal O_Z=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}). Equivalently, proper coherent finiteness makes this ring a finite (R)-subalgebra of its fraction field, and integral closedness gives the equality.

Products with affine opens of (P) preserve this equality: compute global sections by a finite affine Čech cover of the separated (Z) and use exactness of tensoring over the field (k). These opens give NK.5's first assertion. For an invertible (M) on (B), the elementary projection formula gives

\[
g_{P*}g_P^*M=M\otimes g_{P*}\mathcal O_{Z\times P}=M.
\]

A trivial pullback therefore implies (M\simeq\mathcal O_B), proving Picard injectivity.

It follows that

\[
K_0(B)\longrightarrow K_0(Z\times P)
\quad\text{is injective}.
\tag{NK.6}
\]

Indeed a class mapping to zero has rank zero and trivial determinant after pullback. Picard injectivity and NK.1 make its original class zero. This deduction does not require a rank-and-determinant description of the target.

## NK.3. The actual whole K1-family lift

Retain the characteristic-(p>0) hypotheses of FF.1: (R) is a normal noetherian local coefficient-(k) domain, (g:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R) is proper with regular integral (Z), and it is an isomorphism away from the closed point. Let (E) be the reduced closed fibre. For every fixed smooth connected proper curve (P/k),

\[
K_1(Z\times_kP)[1/p]\longrightarrow K_1(E\times_kP)[1/p]
                         \quad\text{is surjective}.
\tag{NK.7}
\]

This assertion is dimension-independent and does not require the ample conormal or henselian hypotheses used for C.3bu. It concerns (K_1) classes, not specified automorphisms as objects.

The already proved KST/GH exact sequence underlying FF gives

\[
K_1(Z\times P)[1/p]\oplus K_1(P)[1/p]
 \longrightarrow K_1(E\times P)[1/p]
 \longrightarrow K_0(B)[1/p]
 \longrightarrow K_0(Z\times P)[1/p]\oplus K_0(P)[1/p].
\tag{NK.8}
\]

The final map is injective by NK.6, so the preceding map is surjective. The (K_1(P)) contribution is already the restriction of its pullback to (Z\times P). Subtracting that actual pullback proves NK.7. This is an actual fixed-product conclusion, with no replacement of (R), (Z), or (P).

## NK.4. Pointwise kernel and exact pure-weight endpoints

The same FF sequence for a point shows

\[
\ker\bigl(K_1(Z)_{\mathbf Q}\longrightarrow K_1(E)_{\mathbf Q}\bigr)
       \subseteq\operatorname{im}\bigl(K_1(R)_{\mathbf Q}\to K_1(Z)_{\mathbf Q}\bigr).
\tag{NK.9}
\]

To account explicitly for the (K_1(k)) term, exactness first represents a pair ((a,0)) as the image of (b\in K_1(R)\), so every kernel element is in the displayed image. Conversely an arbitrary image need not restrict to zero unless its residue vanishes: the correct equality is therefore

\[
\ker\bigl(K_1(Z)_{\mathbf Q}\to K_1(E)_{\mathbf Q}\bigr)
  =\operatorname{im}\bigl(\ker[K_1(R)_{\mathbf Q}\to K_1(k)_{\mathbf Q}]
                              \to K_1(Z)_{\mathbf Q}\bigr).
\tag{NK.9a}
\]

Thus NK.9 is the useful containment, and NK.9a records the exact residue-zero subgroup. The coefficient-field section splits (K_1(k)\to K_1(R)), and constant terms can be tracked through the diagonal if needed. Since (R) is commutative local, elementary row reduction gives (K_1(R)=R^*\); Adams (\psi^q) is multiplication by (q) on this additive unit group. Hence the kernel in NK.9a is pure weight one.

Suppose, in addition, that an actual proper (K_1) family on (E\times P) has endpoint difference **exactly** (\{u\}\beta), where (u\in k^*\) and (\beta\in K_0(E)_{\mathbf Q}) has weight two. Under the henselian point isomorphism FF.4 let (\beta_Z\) be its unique weight-two lift to (Z). Lift the family by NK.7. The difference between its endpoint class on (Z) and (\{u\}\beta_Z) lies in NK.9a and is killed by (\psi^2-2). Applying

\[
                    (\psi^2-2)/6
\tag{NK.10}
\]

to the lifted proper family therefore makes its endpoint difference **exactly** (\{u\}\beta_Z): the desired product has eigenvalue (2\cdot4=8), so NK.10 acts as one on it. There is no projector on all of (K_1(Z\times P)) and no semisimplicity assertion. This conclusion is conditional on the exact exceptional endpoint, which HK alone originally prescribed only componentwise.

## NK.5. The scalar-extension and finite-closure gaps remain

For a symbolic (u), (R\otimes_k k(u)) generally is not local or henselian. NK.1's properness argument cannot be repeated there, and neither NK.7 nor NK.10 gives an actual family on the original constant product after such a replacement.

A finite étale stage near a chosen point of a henselization can be placed in a finite normalization by Zariski Main under the appropriate excellent finite-type hypotheses. This does not by itself extend a (K_1) class. On a regularized finite cover, if the class is defined only on an open (V), the exact obstruction to extension is its localization boundary in (K_0) with support in the complement. Conjugation transports that boundary; summing conjugates gives its trace, which has not been proved zero. Opens containing different closed-fibre branches overlap generically, so the classes do not acquire a canonical extension by zero. A coherent closure can extend a (K_0) class while failing to extend a (K_1) automorphism together with its inverse. No vanishing of the pushed boundary modulo the exceptional subgroup (Q) and actual proper relations has been established.

This is a precise missing step of the trace repair, not a counterexample to every possible repair and not a main-quotient counterexample. The Artin–Schreier example retained in `../cycles/notes/henselian_branch_closure_countermodel.md` remains a method test; no K-theoretic nonvanishing is imported from it.

## Sources and exact reading scope

- The Stacks Project Authors. (2026). *Relative effective Cartier divisors*, Lemma31.19.9, especially(3), [Tag062Y](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/062Y). Entire statement and printed proof freshly read before checkpoint23 freeze; used at the closed-fibre points in NK.3.
- The Stacks Project Authors. (2026). *Applications of Zariski's Main Theorem, I*, Lemmas37.44.1–37.44.2, [Tag02LS](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02LS), [Tag02UP](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02UP). Both complete printed proofs freshly read; used to make the relative Cartier supports finite over the actual local (R).
- The Stacks Project Authors. (2026). *Finite projective modules*, Lemma10.78.7, [Tag02M9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02M9). Fresh statement/proof-hints read in the WP audit; the complete elementary rank-one proof is supplied there and reused here. The source does not print a complete proof.
- The relative Serre generation, properness, perfect Cartier pushforward and projection formula are the exact inputs already audited in AE and WP. The normal-domain and coefficient-field Čech argument is supplied explicitly in NK.5.
- NK.8 is the same every-degree fixed-product exact sequence already proved in `C3_fixed_family_negative_K.tex` from Kerz–Strunk–Tamme(2018), Geisser–Hesselholt(2011), and Thomason–Trobaugh(1990). Their preceding complete source audits are reused, not relabelled as fresh.
- Weibel, C. A. (2013). *The K-book*. Chapter IV, Example5.4.1 and Theorem5.9 give the unit Adams action and product compatibility; the latter full printed proof and Example5.9.1 were freshly read in the read-only checkpoint interval. The elementary local (K_1=R^*) identification is also directly the stable Gaussian-elimination argument.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C3_rational_high_range_RESEARCH.md

# Rational high-range restriction in positive characteristic

Research continuation after C.3bl; 19 November 2026, resumed after the checkpoint-17 thaw at 15:35:25 UTC. This is an **unregistered gate clarification**, not a new ordinary-Chow injectivity theorem, counterexample, or movement claim.

## Prior work read before attempting an extension

We read the complete current `agents/real_weil/POSITIVE_HIGH_RESTRICTION_RESEARCH.md`, `notes/ROOT_FINITE_THICKENING_BOUNDARY_RESEARCH.md`, and `notes/ROOT_LEVINE_SUPPORTED_K_SOURCE_AUDIT.md`. The existing distinctions between actual fixed-product families and formal/henselized-product families, and between supported perfect K-theory and coherent exceptional classes, remain in force. The certified C.3bf–C.3bl classes have exact order $p$ and therefore do not give rational kernels.

The present target is the remaining positive-characteristic rational closed-restriction range $N\geq2r+1$, initially $r=2,N=5$. Over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ the ordinary algebraically trivial groups are already rationally zero; this does not settle the assertion over an arbitrary algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$.

## One detecting level gives a fixed exponent for the whole-divisor kernel

Let $R$ be an excellent finite-dimensional noetherian local domain of characteristic $p$, and let $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a regular projective modification that is an isomorphism away from the closed point. Fix a nonzero $f\in\mathfrak m_R$ and write

\[
D_b=Z\times_R\operatorname{Spec}(R/f^b),\qquad D=D_1.
\]

The enlarged centre $V(f)$ still gives an abstract blow-up square. KST Theorem A and the pro-exact sequence (1.6), together with $K_0(R)=K_0(R/f^b)=\mathbf Z$, identify the quotient by the diagonal graph with the constant group $K_0(Z)$. The level kernels of $K_0(Z)\to K_0(D_b)$ form a decreasing system of subgroups. Its being pro-zero therefore means that **one actual finite level** has zero kernel. This is the same constant-group detection argument already proved and audited in the earlier local K-theory work; we do not replace an inverse limit by a tensor product.

At that fixed level, the closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow D_b$ is nilpotent. Geisser–Hesselholt Theorem A gives bounded $p$-primary exponent for each affine relative K-group in every fixed degree. A finite affine cover of the separated scheme $D_b$, and repeated Mayer–Vietoris for the relative K-theory spectra, use only finitely many groups and degrees to calculate the relevant relative $K_0$. Finite extensions and subquotients of bounded-exponent $p$-groups still have bounded exponent. Consequently, for some integer $e$ depending on this fixed geometry and detecting level,

\[
p^e\ker\bigl(K_0(Z)\longrightarrow K_0(D)\bigr)=0.
\]

This observation does not require a uniform Serre bound for arbitrary Frobenius pullbacks of vector bundles. It gives no uniform bound over all geometries or all infinitesimal levels. In mixed characteristic the same argument requires $p$ to be nilpotent on the chosen thickening; no such hypothesis is silently imposed here.

## The remaining supported-class problem is unchanged

Let $E$ be the exceptional closed subset, $X=Z\setminus E$, and $Y=D\setminus E$. If a class on $X$ restricts to zero on $Y$, a lift to $K_0(Z)$ need not restrict to zero on the **whole** divisor $D$. Its restriction can instead be a nonzero perfect class supported on $E\cap D$. The preceding fixed-exponent statement does not apply to that class.

The relevant unproved comparison remains, schematically,

\[
\frac{
 j^*K_0(Z)_{\mathbf Q}\cap
 \operatorname{im}\bigl(K_0(D\ \mathrm{on}\ E)_{\mathbf Q}\to K_0(D)_{\mathbf Q}\bigr)
}{
 j^*i_*G_0(E)_{\mathbf Q}
}.
\]

Here the denominator is understood through the exceptional coherent boundary on regular $Z$ and its restriction. No identification of the numerator with coherent $G_0(E)$ has been proved. The whole divisor may be singular, and its Cartan map can have a kernel. Levine's supported K-theory theorem retains an extra supported term; it does not authorize deleting it. An alteration that is not an isomorphism away from the centre also changes the constant-local-graph descent argument and does not itself supply a boundary lift.

The current integral Milnor detector likewise does not supply a rational obstruction: its relative sheaf has exponent $p$. Its absolute differential can vanish through the Kodaira–Spencer boundary, so that absolute differential must not be substituted for the relative class.

## Exact nearby formal theorem, freshly reopened

Morrow's published Theorem 6.18, pp.1597–1598, states that for a smooth projective $d$-fold and a smooth ample divisor, the map from the inverse limit of cohomological K-sheaf groups to the divisor group has kernel and cokernel killed by a power of $p$ when $i+n<d-1$. For the diagonal Chow degree this requires $2n<d-1$. Remark 6.19, p.1598, extends the statement to Milnor K-theory over an infinite field. Section 6.5, p.1593, explicitly distinguishes cohomological Chow groups of a nonregular thickening from ordinary cycle Chow groups.

We freshly reopened the full 68-page published primary PDF and read the exact theorem, its proof, and Remark 6.19. This theorem controls an infinitesimal inverse limit; it does not supply the missing ordinary supported-cycle lift on the punctured principal divisor. In particular it is not a proof of the present $r=2,N=5$ assertion.

## Search and source ledger

- Kerz–Strunk–Tamme, pro-cdh descent, Theorem A and equation (1.6), author pp.2–3: the already fully opened and repeatedly audited primary input is reused for the finite detecting level. No fresh full re-proof of pro-cdh descent is claimed.
- Geisser, T., & Hesselholt, L. (2011). *On relative and bi-relative algebraic K-theory of rings of finite characteristic*. Journal of the American Mathematical Society, 24(1), 29–49. Theorem A, p.29, and Theorem C, p.30. Full primary PDF freshly opened and exact introduction/statements read: <https://math.mit.edu/~larsh/papers/025/bounded.pdf>. The bound is stated degree by degree, and the paper expressly uses Bass-completed nonconnective K-theory.
- Morrow, M. (2019). *K-theory and logarithmic Hodge-Witt sheaves of formal schemes in characteristic p*. Annales Scientifiques de l'École Normale Supérieure, 52(6), 1537–1601. Section 6.5, p.1593; Theorem 6.18 and proof, pp.1597–1598; Remark 6.19, p.1598. Full published primary PDF freshly opened and those exact passages read: <https://www.numdam.org/item/ASENS_2019__52_6_1537_0.pdf>.
- Levine (1986), *Modules of finite length and K-groups of surface singularities*, Theorem 2.1, pp.29–32, Proposition 4.1, pp.37–38: exact previously opened source audit reused; no unsupported coherent/perfect dévissage is inferred.

Searches included `"Lefschetz" "algebraically trivial" "codimension two" Chow restriction`, `"positive characteristic" "Chow groups" "weak Lefschetz" injectivity`, `"Chow group" "ample divisor" "codimension 2" injective`, and variants with `"algebraically equivalent"`. Balkan and Schreieder's newly opened 2026 Selecta paper *Cycle conjectures and birational invariants over finite fields*, Section 1.3 after Corollary 1.3 and Remark 7.9, explicitly treats projective Chow hard Lefschetz as a separate conjectural input; those passages were read at <https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00029-026-01142-0>. It supplies no local supported-boundary lifting theorem. Conditional projective Chow-Lefschetz and representability results returned by the searches are not promoted to local restriction theorems. The already rejected Patel–Ravindra Lemma 3.2 route is not reused.

Additional targeted searches after the checkpoint thaw used `"Lefschetz" "algebraic representatives" restriction`, `"local Lefschetz" "K-theory" "Chow" characteristic p`, and the title of Achter–Casalaina-Martin–Vial's diagonal-decomposition monograph. The monograph's primary publisher/author URLs were located; no exact theorem from it has yet been invoked in this note. Search-only results, including broad conditional claims and unrelated automated-looking pages, are not treated as evidence for the desired statement.

## Current assessment

No rational high-range ordinary injectivity theorem or counterexample has been established in this continuation. A fixed exponent for the whole-divisor kernel is justified, but the supported perfect-class lifting comparison remains the concrete obstruction. The finite-exponent clarification alone is **not** counted as main-gate movement.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C3_rational_symbolic_endpoint_RESEARCH.md

# Rational symbolic fields and the exact ambient endpoint

**Unregistered auxiliary proof; no main-gate movement.** Written 19 November 2026 by GPT-6 Astra Pro (OpenAI), `/root/frobenius_continuation`. This note removes a possible endpoint discrepancy after an actual symbolic family has been lifted. It does not supply that lift or cancel its supported boundary.

## RF.1. Hypotheses and conclusion

Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic p>0. Let R be a noetherian local coefficient-k algebra with residue field k, and let g:Z→Spec R be a proper morphism from a regular noetherian scheme, an isomorphism away from the closed point. Suppose the reduced exceptional scheme E is the projective SNC surface in the already proved C.3bt scope. Normality is not needed for the coefficient calculation below. All groups are rational and are the nonconnective K-groups of perfect complexes.

For a new variable u, put F=k(u) and R_F=R tensor_k F. Then

    K1(R_F)_Q is generated by the image of R*_Q
        and the constant-field classes {u−a}, a∈k.         (RF.1)

Only finitely many such classes occur in any expression. Consequently

    psi^q = q on K1(R_F)_Q for every positive integer q.  (RF.2)

This concerns the actual nonlocal ring R_F. The proof never calls it local or henselian. It implies that ker(K1(Z_F)_Q→K1(E_F)_Q) has Adams weight one.

## RF.2. The natural rational blow-up square on smooth parameters

For every smooth separated finite-type k-scheme T, the FF proof applies to the actual product with T. Properness is required of g×1_T, which remains proper when T is not proper over k. The infinitesimal centres are Spec(R/m^n)×T and the exceptional thickenings are Z×_R Spec(R/m^n)×T. Their reductions are T and E×T. On finite affine covers, characteristic-p nilpotent invariance after inverting p identifies these terms with their reductions; finite-cover descent globalizes the comparison.

Thus the fixed-product KST/GH comparison gives the natural equivalence

    K(R×T)_Q ≃ K(Z×T)_Q ×^h_{K(E×T)_Q} K(T)_Q.          (RF.3)

Here K(R×T) means K(Spec R×T). To verify the spectrum assertion, use the relative comparison: KST gives an isomorphism of pro-homotopy groups for the two relative fibres; GH makes the infinitesimal relative systems constant after localization; the constant embedding reflects isomorphisms. The resulting map of actual rational relative fibres is a weak equivalence in every degree. No inverse limit of K-groups and no uniform p-exponent is used.

The construction is natural for parameter pullbacks and for the localization fibres below. This is the spectrum form of the already audited every-degree FF sequence, with nonproperness of T explicitly accounted for. No general cdh-descent theorem on arbitrary singular schemes is being imported.

## RF.3. Homotopy invariance on the coefficient scheme

The regular schemes Z and Spec k have homotopy-invariant K-theory. Rational K(E) is the actual coherent finite totalization of its smooth components, smooth double curves and individual triple points, by C.3bt. Every stratum is regular and has homotopy-invariant K-theory. Finite homotopy limits give K(E)_Q≃K(E×A1)_Q. Comparing RF.3 for a point and for A1 gives

    K(R)_Q ≃ K(R[u])_Q.                                 (RF.4)

In particular K1(R[u])_Q is the image of K1(R)_Q. This follows from this regular/SNC resolution; it is not an unsupported assertion of homotopy invariance for arbitrary singular rings. Since R is commutative local, K1(R)=R*.

## RF.4. Parameter-point support purity with its actual maps

Let B be a finite reduced subset of A1(k). For a∈B, the parameter equation u−a is a non-zero-divisor on every product in RF.3. Actual regular-immersion pushforward gives

    direct sum over a∈B of K(R)_Q
          → K(R×A1 on R×B)_Q.                           (RF.5)

This map is an equivalence. Take the fibres defining support of RF.3 for A1 and A1\B. Finite homotopy limits commute with these fibres, giving the corresponding supported homotopy-cartesian square.

For Z and Spec k, regular devissage identifies supported spectra with the direct sums of coefficient spectra. For E, use the PL.1 stratum-totalization proof with A1 in place of the proper ambient curve: regular devissage on every smooth stratum and disjoint-support excision give the direct sum of K(E). Parameter properness was not used in that purity argument.

All comparison maps are the actual Cartier pushforwards. They commute with g and the SNC restriction diagram by Tor-independent derived base change. Flatness of g is unnecessary: the one-element resolution by u−a stays exact after pullback, since the parameter equation remains a non-zero-divisor on Z[u], E[u] and every stratum. Thus these are maps of the actual coherent diagrams, with their geometric homotopies. Comparing the supported squares and their fibres proves RF.5 with its natural maps. This does not apply regular-ambient devissage directly to singular R×A1.

The Adams shift is one. Under RF.5, pushforward is exterior multiplication by the Koszul support class of a. That class is the localization boundary of the unit u−a, and psi^q[O_a]=q[O_a] in the support group. Raw-support localization and product compatibility give

    psi^q i_{a*}(x) = q i_{a*}(psi^q x).                (RF.6)

In particular the rank class in K0(R), of ordinary weight zero, has raw support weight one. No semisimplicity is used.

## RF.5. Localization and explicit residue lifts

Apply localization to A1\B and pass to the filtered system of all finite B. Perfect K-theory continuity identifies the limiting open with Spec R_F. Because k is algebraically closed, every nonzero polynomial in k[u] factors into the u−a; this is precisely localization of R[u] at k[u]\{0}. Exactness and RF.5 give

    K1(R[u])_Q → K1(R_F)_Q
                  → direct sum over a∈k of K0(R)_Q.     (RF.7)

Each residue vector has finite support. Locality gives K0(R)=Z by rank. The unit u−a, pulled from F*, has residue 1 at a and 0 at every other finite point, with positive-uniformizer convention. This follows from its two-term Koszul resolution, equivalently the localization module formula. There is no infinity condition because the ambient parameter is A1.

Given xi∈K1(R_F)_Q with residues (n_a), subtract the finite actual unit sum Σ_a n_a{u−a}. The difference has all residues zero and thus comes from K1(R[u])_Q. By RF.4 it comes from K1(R)_Q=R*_Q. This proves RF.1.

Both types of generator are unit classes, on which psi^q acts by q. Thus RF.2 is direct. Merely knowing the subquotients have weight one would not suffice without controlling extensions; the explicit residue lifts supply that control.

## RF.6. Exact endpoint after an actual lift

The abstract blow-up square over F has the FF exact sequence, without requiring R_F to be local. If a∈ker(K1(Z_F)_Q→K1(E_F)_Q), apply exactness to (a,0) in K1(Z_F)_Q plus K1(F)_Q. It puts a in the image of K1(R_F)_Q, so RF.2 proves

    psi^q = q on ker(K1(Z_F)_Q→K1(E_F)_Q).              (RF.8)

Let beta_Z∈K0(Z)_Q have weight two, with restriction beta on E. Suppose P/F is an actual smooth connected proper curve with F-rational points o,t, and an actual eta_Z∈K1(Z_F×_F P)_Q restricts to an exceptional family with endpoint exactly {u} beta_F. Then

    (eta_Z)_t − (eta_Z)_o − {u}(beta_Z)_F

belongs to RF.8. Applying (psi²−2)/6 to the actual eta_Z kills the discrepancy and fixes the desired product, whose psi² eigenvalue is8. This gives literal endpoint {u}(beta_Z)_F on the constant target. Make this correction over k(u) before any finite extension needed for the semistable parameter model in RS.

This is the endpoint part only. RF.6 assumes an actual lift on Z_F×P. NK does not supply that lift by replacing R with the nonlocal R_F. The compactified parameter-surface route still has its supported node obstruction; finite closure still has its trace boundary. No main quotient vanishing follows from this lemma alone.

## Sources and exact audit scope

- Kerz, M., Strunk, F., & Tamme, G. (2018). *Algebraic K-theory and descent for blow-ups*. Inventiones Mathematicae, 211, 523–577. The complete FF KST/GH/TT source audits are reused. RF.2 explicitly proves applicability to smooth nonproper T.
- Geisser, T., & Hesselholt, L. (2011). *On relative and bi-relative algebraic K-theory of rings of finite characteristic*. Journal of the American Mathematical Society, 24, 29–49. Previously audited Theorem A supplies characteristic-p nilpotent comparison in every integer degree.
- Thomason, R. W., & Trobaugh, T. (1990). *Higher algebraic K-theory of schemes and of derived categories*. In The Grothendieck Festschrift, Vol. III, 247–435. Primary PDF: https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/otherpapers/Thomason-Trobaugh.pdf . Full printed proofs of3.16–3.18,7.4,8.1 and8.1.4 were read in the preceding HK/PL audits. Theorem7.2 and its entire printed continuity proof via3.20 and6.6 were freshly read at20:20UTC; the underlying3.20 proof was not freshly reopened. The complete printed Bass6.6 proof was read earlier, without a fresh full reading of all its6.1–6.4 foundations. Regular homotopy invariance is the exact regular input already used in C.3bt.
- Weibel, C. A. (2013). *The K-book*. Chapter III Lemma1.4, complete printed proof freshly read at20:14–20:15UTC, gives local K1=units. Chapter IV Example5.4.1 and Theorem5.9 give unit Adams action and products; their complete printed texts were freshly read as recorded in NK.

No additional global Gersten injectivity, general singular purity, or Adams decomposition theorem is required. No numerical test was used to certify this general exact argument.
