# The generalized Kummer fourfold incidence route: an exact integral exclusion

**Status: complete auxiliary proof with independent mathematical passes conditional on the geometric input; that input's normalization is explicitly reconstructed in Section3.1 and the primary-source read scope is finalized in Section8. No main-gate movement, no algebraicity counterexample, and no priority claim.**

Credit: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), ChatGPT Pro mode, RESEARCH_SA06, run `/root/component_families`; effort setting not separately exposed. Research date: 19 November 2026, after checkpoint22.

## 1. Why this is a different construction

The current C.4ab gate asks for an integral codimension-two correspondence on a type-(1,2) abelian surface whose actions t on H1 and s on the transcendental H2 satisfy t−s odd. The preceding semihomogeneous, fixed-surface Orlov, graph, Prym, and Lagrangian-divisor methods do not exhaust positive-square sheaf moduli. A natural next construction is the Albanese fibre of the Hilbert scheme of three points: the generalized Kummer fourfold K=K2(A). Its universal length-three subscheme is an actual integral incidence correspondence and induces an isometry on second cohomology from A into K.

One may cut this moduli space by a surface cycle and compose its incidence correspondence with its transpose. This is not a semihomogeneous bundle construction and is not the fixed-A exterior-product Orlov ring previously excluded. The result below controls **every integral Hodge surface class used for that cut**, rather than only complete intersections or the familiar canonical K3 surfaces.

## 2. Precise theorem

Let A be a complex abelian surface with a primitive polarization ell of type (1,2), with

    NS(A)=Z ell,       End_HS(T(A)_Q)=Q,

where T(A)_Q=ell-perp in H2(A,Q). For the deduction via C.4ab also retain its hypothesis End_HS H1(A,Q)=Q. Put K=K2(A), and let U in CH2(A×K) be the universal length-three subscheme restricted from A×A^[3]. For any integral surface cycle z in CH2(K), form the integral correspondence

    Z_z = (p13)_*(p12^*U · p2^*z · p23^*(transpose U)) in CH2(A×A),

where the ambient product is A×K×A. Its action on H1(A,Q) is zero and its action on T(A)_Q is multiplication by an **even integer**.

The same statement about the two actions holds if z is any integral Hodge class in H4(K,Z); no algebraicity assertion for that arbitrary class is needed. Conversely an actual integral surface Y_p in K realizes transcendental scalar two. Thus the subgroup of transcendental scalars produced by this construction is exactly 2Z. In particular t−s is always even, and this entire incidence construction fails the C.4ab test.

This is a construction exclusion. It makes no claim that every correspondence on A×A factors through this construction, and no claim that P²/2 is nonalgebraic.

## 3. The geometric cohomology input and its normalization

Write R=Z_(2). The normalized incidence map is

    mu = U_* : H2(A,Z) → H2(K,Z).

The standard integral second-cohomology decomposition and Beauville form are

    H2(K,Z)=mu H2(A,Z) perpendicular-sum Z e,
    q(e,e)=−6,

where 2e is the exceptional divisor of the Hilbert–Chow map, up to a harmless simultaneous sign convention for e. The restriction of q to H2(A,Z) is the ordinary intersection form. The map mu is the divisor incidence map: the locus of length-three subschemes meeting a divisor on A. Its Nakajima normalization is explicitly 1/2 times theta^*(q1(a)q1(1)^2|0>), not the unnormalized Nakajima expression. K has H1(K,Q)=0.

Choose the integral hyperbolic basis

    u1,u2,v1,v2,w1,w2

of H2(A,Z), with q(u1,u2)=q(v1,v2)=q(w1,w2)=1 and all other pairings zero. Since ell has type (1,2), a symplectic basis of H1(A,Z) gives

    ell = u1+2u2.

We identify these six classes with their images in H2(K,Z), and put

    Q = u1u2+v1v2+w1w2 in Sym² H2(K,Q).

The Fujiki relation, polarized in four variables, is

    integral_K abcd = 3(q(a,b)q(c,d)+q(a,c)q(b,d)+q(a,d)q(b,c)).     (KI.1)

The integral classes from Kapfer–Menet, Proposition6.30, needed below are

    B_y = (y² − e y/3)/2,  for y in {u1,u2,v1,v2,w1,w2},
    Q/6 = [Y_p].                                                   (KI.2)

Here Y_p is the actual surface of length-three subschemes with fixed support point p and sum zero, for p outside A[3]. The equalities of cohomology classes are all that we use. Multiplication by three makes Q/2 integral. We do not assert that the B_y are algebraic for a general A: most y are not Hodge classes. Their **topological integrality** supplies the required lattice bound on all integral Hodge classes.

### 3.1. Explicit repair of the printed incidence normalization

There is a normalization inconsistency in the displayed derivation of Kapfer and Menet (2018, Proposition6.30, p.545): it writes y=theta^*(q1(a)q1(1)^2|0>) although their Notation5.13 gives the correct expression with the factor 1/2. We do not infer that the conclusion is correct merely from its appearance in the proposition. Here is a derivation with the correct normalization.

Use the Nakajima creation operators q_n, and the multiplication operators G0(gamma) and d from their Section3. Commutators below are graded. Their equations(3.2)–(3.4) give

    [G0(gamma),q1(eta)] = q1(gamma eta),
    [d,q1(eta)] = L1(eta),
    [L1(gamma),q1(eta)] = −q2(gamma eta).

Since G0(gamma) and the even multiplication operator d commute, the graded Jacobi identity applied to

    q2(eta)=−[[d,q1(1)],q1(eta)]

gives

    [G0(gamma),q2(eta)]=2q2(gamma eta).                    (KI.N1)

This verifies precisely the weight-two commutator used below from the printed relations, without appealing to an additional unverified general-weight formula. Proposition5.3 identifies G0(alpha)1 with the summation pullback of alpha for every alpha in H1(A). Its restriction to the zero-sum fibre K therefore vanishes.

Each of the six hyperbolic basis classes a on A is alpha beta for integral degree-one classes alpha,beta; in particular a²=0. For this paragraph only, write rho=theta^* and suppress the vacuum. Apply G0(beta) to q2(alpha)q1(1), then restrict to K. The graded sign and beta alpha=−a give

    0=rho(−2q2(a)q1(1)−q2(alpha)q1(beta)).

Applying G0(alpha) to q2(1)q1(beta) gives

    0=rho(2q2(alpha)q1(beta)+q2(1)q1(a)).

Consequently

    rho(q2(1)q1(a))=4rho(q2(a)q1(1)).                     (KI.N2)

The normalizations in Proposition4.4 and Notation5.13 are

    e=(1/2)rho(q2(1)q1(1)),
    y=(1/2)rho(q1(a)q1(1)^2)=rho(G0(a)1).

Multiplication by G0(a), using (KI.N1)–(KI.N2), now yields

    ey=(1/2)rho(2q2(a)q1(1)+q2(1)q1(a))
      =3rho(q2(a)q1(1)).

Likewise, [G0(a),q1(a)]=q1(a²)=0, so

    y²=rho(q1(a)^2 q1(1)).

Thus the printed subsequent identities are correct with the corrected normalization, and

    B_y=rho(((q1(a)^2−q2(a))/2) q1(1)|0>).               (KI.N3)

For a divisor class a, the operator in parentheses is Qin and Wang's m_(1,1),a, because the symmetric-function identity is m_(1,1)=(p1²−p2)/2. It is integral by their Theorem4.5; their Sections4.1–4.2 construct the integral geometric class for a smooth curve, prove the sign and addition rules, and treat a general divisor as a difference of very ample divisors. The conversion of an integral creation class to an integral operator is Proposition3.5, whose proof and prerequisite Lemmas3.2–3.4 were also freshly read. Kapfer and Menet's Corollary4.3 extends this operator to every integral a on a torus by deformation and monodromy. Applying it to the integral class q1(1)|0> and pulling back proves (KI.N3) integral. This is the exact integrality input needed in (KI.2), including the non-Hodge basis vectors.

The independent source chain for Q/6 is Kapfer and Menet's Corollary6.28, obtained from their preceding explicit Chern-class and surface computations, together with the actual Y_p construction and pairings in Hassett and Tschinkel (2013, Section4). No divisibility assertion from the full integral-basis theorem in Section6.6 is used.

## 4. A complete localization-at-two calculation

Let S=Sym² H2(K,Q) inside H4(K,Q). The pairing on S is nondegenerate by (KI.1). In the 28 ordinary quadratic monomials in the seven displayed basis vectors, its Gram determinant is

    det(Sym² lattice) = 2^14 · 3^38.                              (KI.3)

For completeness, this determinant does not require accepting a numerical program. If a rank-n symmetric form has determinant d and the induced pairing on its symmetric-square monomials is

    c(qij qkl+qik qjl+qil qjk),

diagonalize over an extension of Q. The off-diagonal monomials contribute c^(n(n−1)/2) times d^(n−1). The diagonal block is c D(2I+J)D, and contributes c^n 2^(n−1)(n+2)d². The determinant is therefore

    c^(n(n+1)/2) 2^(n−1)(n+2)d^(n+1).

The identity is invariant under change of basis and hence holds before diagonalizing. With n=7, c=3 and d=det(U³ perpendicular-sum <-6>)=6, it gives (KI.3).

Replace the six monomials y² by B_y from (KI.2), and replace u1u2 by Q/2, retaining the other 21 monomials. These are 28 independent integral cohomology classes. The change-of-basis determinant has absolute value 2^(-7): each square replacement contributes 1/2, and the Q/2 replacement contributes another 1/2. The extra e y/6 terms and the other two terms of Q/2 do not change that triangular determinant. Consequently the new integral lattice L has

    det(L)=3^38,

which is a unit in R. Thus L_R is self-dual for the intersection pairing in S_Q.

Let h be any integral class in H4(K,Z), and let h_S be its rational orthogonal projection to S. It pairs integrally with every element of L, because h does and its orthogonal complement pairs trivially with S. Self-duality therefore gives

    h_S belongs to L_R.                                         (KI.4)

This argument uses neither a computation of the complementary 80-dimensional lattice nor the full 3-primary gluing of H4(K,Z). It also works modulo torsion and hence does not rely on the torsion-freeness statement corrected in the later Kapfer–Menet erratum. The source's full integral-basis theorem is compatible with (KI.4), but its finite F3 orbit computations are not dependencies of this proof.

## 5. Hodge classes and the even scalar

S is a rational sub-Hodge structure, and the intersection pairing makes its orthogonal projection a Hodge morphism. Hence if h has Hodge type (2,2), h_S does too. The assumptions on NS(A) and End_HS(T(A)_Q) imply that all rational Hodge classes in S have the form

    h_S = a ell² + b ell e + c e² + d Q,       a,b,c,d in Q.       (KI.5)

Indeed H2(K,Q)=Q ell + Q e + T(A)_Q orthogonally. There are no Hodge classes in the T cross terms, and the Hodge classes in Sym²T form the one-dimensional line of the inverse intersection form, because End_HS(T_Q)=Q. The class Q differs from that inverse-form line by a multiple of ell². This proves (KI.5) without a claim about algebraic generation.

Expand (KI.5) in the 28-element basis of L. The only nonzero coordinates are

| Basis element | Coordinate |
|---|---:|
| B_u1 | 2a |
| B_u2 | 8a |
| u1 e | a/3+b |
| u2 e | 4a/3+2b |
| v1v2 | −4a |
| w1w2 | −4a |
| e² | c |
| Q/2 | 8a+2d |

By (KI.4), all these coordinates belong to R. In particular

    2a in R,      c in R,      2d in R.                         (KI.6)

The last assertion follows from the Q/2 coordinate and 8a=4(2a). No integral decomposition of all of H4 into Hodge summands has been assumed.

For alpha,beta in T(A)_Q, the four-variable formula (KI.1) gives

    integral_K mu(alpha)mu(beta)ell² = 12 q(alpha,beta),
    integral_K mu(alpha)mu(beta)ell e = 0,
    integral_K mu(alpha)mu(beta)e² = −18 q(alpha,beta),
    integral_K mu(alpha)mu(beta)Q = 12 q(alpha,beta).

For the final identity, the three hyperbolic products contribute 3q(alpha,beta) from their internal contractions, and their two cross-contractions sum to q(alpha,beta); multiply by the Fujiki factor three. The component h−h_S is orthogonal to every product of two degree-two classes and contributes zero. Therefore the scalar induced by the incidence composition is

    s_h = 12a−18c+12d
        = 6(2a)−18c+6(2d) in 2R.                              (KI.7)

The composition is an integral cohomological correspondence, so it preserves H2(A,Z). Its restriction to the nonzero transcendental lattice is scalar, making s_h an integer. Thus s_h belongs to 2R intersect Z = 2Z. Its H1 action factors through H1(K,Q)=0 and is zero. This proves the claimed parity for every integral Hodge class, and in particular every integral algebraic surface cycle.

For h=[Y_p]=Q/6, (KI.7) gives s_h=2. Its transpose-incidence composition is an actual integral Chow correspondence, so two is attained. Taking integral sums and differences gives exactly 2Z. This completes the theorem.

## 6. Failed extensions and what the result does not do

The preliminary divisor-only calculation gives s=3q(h1,h2). Since NS(K)=Z ell+Z e has Gram matrix diag(4,−6), all such values are even. Canonical K3 surfaces also give scalar two. Those preliminary observations alone would leave possible half-integral combinations of divisor and canonical classes untreated. Sections4–5 close that exact gap by using an odd-discriminant lattice in Sym²H2 and its orthogonal projection. They exclude arbitrary integral Hodge cuts, so invoking the rational Hodge conjecture on K does not improve this construction.

A possible expansion to all Albanese fibres of positive-square sheaf moduli was considered but is **not proved here**. One must control the actual universal or quasi-universal class, its integral multiplier, and the embedding of T(A) in the second-cohomology lattice of each fibre. No statement about arbitrary twisted universal kernels follows from the K2(A) calculation. Likewise no conclusion is asserted for different-dimensional Kummer varieties, non-tautological correspondences that do not have the displayed incidence factorization, or arbitrary cycles on A×Ahat.

The desired ordinary integral numerical P²/2 class remains unresolved by this work. The theorem is a genuinely different and stronger method exclusion than the prior fixed-A Orlov or semihomogeneous exclusions, but it is not a strictly smaller main existence gate and is not counted as qualifying movement.

### Record: agents/real_weil/C4_SUPERSINGULAR_BT1_LIFTING_RESEARCH.md

# Supersingular threefolds: finite torsion realization and the actual Hom gap

Owner: `/root/component_families`, 2026-11-19. Status: **proved method limitation and explicit bounded finite-torsion certificate; no main-gate movement**. Neither characteristic-two nor characteristic-three arbitrary supersingular threefolds are settled here. All constructions and arguments concern abelian varieties in the usual category and actual homomorphisms unless a finite group scheme is explicitly named.

## BT.1. Why this was a different route

C.4u and the universal threefold construction leave only the characteristic prime: (s_J(A)\mid2) in characteristic two and (s_J(A)\mid3) in characteristic three. Thus an actual factorization of some multiplication ([n]_A), with (p\nmid n), through a product of Jacobians would finish either case. The new lead was Pries and Ulmer's published theorem that every (BT_1) group scheme occurs as a direct factor of a Jacobian's (p)-torsion, with the curve defined over the prime field (Pries & Ulmer, 2022, Theorem 1.1). The full published thirteen-page article and every displayed proof have now been read.

That theorem has exactly the required finite group scheme direction, including the small characteristics. Its conclusion does not assert that the two splitting maps are restrictions of homomorphisms of abelian varieties. The following argument proves that a uniform lift of its constant-curve construction would be false, even for explicit supersingular threefolds. This is stronger than merely leaving the lifting step unproved, but it is only a limitation on this construction.

## BT.2. An elementary descent lemma for an actual prime-to-characteristic factorization

Let (k_0\subset k) be algebraically closed fields of characteristic (p>0). Call an abelian variety over (k) **constant** here if it is isomorphic, as an abelian variety, to a base change from (k_0).

**Lemma.** Suppose (B=B_0\times_{k_0}k) and there are homomorphisms

\[
 A\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{v}A,
 \qquad vu=[n]_A,
 \qquad p\nmid n.
\]

Then (A) is constant. No principal polarization or supersingularity assumption is required.

**Proof.** First, homomorphisms between constant abelian varieties do not enlarge under extension of algebraically closed fields. Here is a proof at the exact scope needed, rather than an appeal to a general trace construction. Spread a homomorphism (f:(B_0)_k\to(D_0)_k) and its group identities over an integral finite type (k_0)-scheme (T), after shrinking. Choose (t_0\in T(k_0)). The difference (f-f_{t_0}), viewed as a map (B_0\times T\to D_0), is zero on (B_0\times\{t_0\}) and on (\{0\}\times T). The proper-source rigidity theorem makes it identically zero. Thus (f) descends. The rigidity theorem and its complete proof were freshly reread in Milne (2008, I, Theorem 1.1, pp. 8–9); the equivalent Hom conclusion and complete displayed proof also appear in I, Corollary 16.4, p. 68. Spreading handles arbitrary algebraically closed extensions, not only a finitely generated one.

The endomorphism (uv\in\operatorname{End}(B)) therefore descends to an endomorphism (w_0) of (B_0). Since (vu=[n]), the map (v) is surjective and (u) has finite kernel. Consequently

\[
 C:=u(A)=\operatorname{im}(uv)
      =(\operatorname{im}w_0)_k.
\]

Write (C=C_0\times k). The restriction (v_C:C\to A) is an isogeny, and

\[
 v_Cu=[n]_A,
 \qquad uv_C=[n]_C.
\]

The second equality follows after precomposing with the surjection (u:A\to C). It implies (\ker v_C\subset C[n]). Since (p\nmid n), (C_0[n]) is a finite étale constant group scheme over the algebraically closed field (k_0). Every closed subgroup scheme of its base change descends: it is the union of a subset of its constant reduced points, and the subgroup condition is preserved. Let (H_0\subset C_0[n]) be this descended subgroup. Then

\[
 A\simeq C/\ker v_C\simeq(C_0/H_0)_k.
\]

This proves the lemma. The finite-subgroup quotient and the complementary isogeny use the usual scheme kernels, not merely rational points; compare Milne (2008, I, Remark 8.6 and the discussion following the construction of the quotient in §8). In the final step the subgroup is étale, so descent by reduced points is valid. \(\square\)

The argument allows any finite product of constant Jacobians, any choices of curves, and any signed sum of composites: a finite sum can be combined into a single factorization through their product. It does not require a fixed genus or a fixed Fermat degree.

## BT.3. Even a lifted retraction only on (A[p]) would suffice—and is excluded for nonconstant (A)

Suppose actual homomorphisms (u:A\to B) and (v:B\to A) restrict to a retraction on finite group schemes:

\[
 (vu)|_{A[p]}=1_{A[p]}.
\]

Then (e=vu) is an isogeny of degree prime to (p). Indeed its kernel has trivial intersection with (A[p]). If its reduced identity component had positive dimension, it would be a positive-dimensional abelian subvariety and would have nonzero (p)-torsion, a contradiction. Thus the kernel is finite. A nonzero finite commutative (p)-primary group scheme has nonzero kernel under multiplication by (p), so the kernel's (p)-primary part is zero. This proves the degree assertion. This reasoning does not confuse étaleness alone with prime-to-(p) degree.

Put (m=\deg e). The finite kernel is killed by (m), so the quotient property gives an actual homomorphism (h:A\to A) satisfying (he=[m]_A). Consequently

\[
 A\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{hv}A
 \quad\text{has composite }[m]_A,
 \qquad p\nmid m.
\]

If (B) is constant, BT.2 forces (A) to be constant. Thus for a nonconstant (A), **no retraction of (A[p]) inside the (p)-torsion of a constant abelian variety can be induced by a pair of actual homomorphisms**. The statement excludes all such pairs, rather than just one chosen finite-level splitting.

For the C.4u residual threefold problem, a lifted (p)-torsion retraction through a product of arbitrary Jacobians would prove (s_J(A)=1) by combining (m) with the existing (p)-power bound. This is an exact observation about what a lift would accomplish; it is not counted as a smaller existence gate or as progress on the missing lift.

## BT.4. Explicit supersingular threefolds witnessing the lifting failure

Fix (p=2) or (p=3), put (k_0=\overline{\mathbf F}_p), and let (k=\overline{k_0(t)}), where (t) is transcendental. Choose a supersingular elliptic curve (E/k_0) and a fixed (k_0)-isomorphism (\ker(F_{E/k_0})\simeq\alpha_p). Inside 

\[
 \ker(F_{E^3/k_0})_k\simeq\alpha_p^3
\]

take the closed subgroup

\[
 H_t=\{(z,tz,t^2z):z\in\alpha_p\}.
\]

The first coordinate makes this a closed immersion. Define the abelian threefold

\[
 A_t=E_k^3/H_t.
\]

It is supersingular because the quotient map is an isogeny from (E^3). It is not constant: if (A_t\simeq(A_0)_k), composing this isomorphism with the quotient map gives a homomorphism between constant abelian varieties, hence one defined over (k_0) by the rigidity argument in BT.2. Its scheme kernel would then descend to (k_0). But the tangent line of (H_t\subset\alpha_p^3) is 

\[
 k(1,t,t^2)\subset k^3.
\]

A line of this form defined over (k_0) would have (t\in k_0), by normalizing its first coordinate to one. This contradicts transcendence. Equivalently, in the coordinate Hopf algebra of (\alpha_p^3), the subgroup has ideal generated by (x_2-tx_1) and (x_3-t^2x_1); its degree-one relations do not descend.

It follows from BT.2–BT.3 that (A_t) admits neither a prime-to-(p) multiplication factorization nor an actual Hom lift of a (p)-torsion retraction through any product of constant Jacobians. Nevertheless Pries–Ulmer applies to (A_t[p]). The example therefore identifies the exact missing geometric information in this route. **It does not prove that (A_t) fails to be a direct summand of a product of Jacobians over (k)**, since such Jacobians may themselves be nonconstant.

The general (E^g/\alpha_p) construction is standard and also occurs in the already examined Jiang–Li–Lu argument in the other strand; no new claim about nonselfduality is made here. The descent proof above is independent of their nonselfduality theorem and does not require any a-number calculation.

## BT.5. A bounded, checked constant product already contains every possible threefold (p)-torsion type

There is no need to infer the finite-level existence from an unbounded search. For (d) prime to (p), let (C_d/\mathbf F_p) denote the smooth projective curve with affine equation

\[
 y^d=x(1-x).
\]

Using the word construction in Pries–Ulmer (2022, §§3–5 and Proposition 6.1(1)), form

\[
 B_p=\prod_{\lambda=2}^{6}
       J(C_{p^\lambda-1})^{\lfloor6/\lambda\rfloor}.
\]

Then (A[p]) is a direct factor of (B_p[p]) for every supersingular abelian threefold (A/k), for both (p=2,3). To see this, supersingularity implies that (A[p]) has neither an étale nor a multiplicative direct factor. In the Kraft classification every indecomposable factor therefore corresponds to a primitive cyclic word in (f,v) of length at least two, and the sum of all lengths is six. A factor of length (\lambda) occurs in (J(C_{p^\lambda-1})[p]), and its multiplicity in (A[p]) is at most (\lfloor6/\lambda\rfloor). Distinct words occur as distinct orbit summands, so those copies suffice simultaneously. This uses only the primitive-word statement, which has no (p>3) restriction. It does not incorrectly apply the nonprimitive-word part of Proposition 6.1 in characteristics two and three.

The genus is (\lfloor(d-1)/2\rfloor). Thus

\[
 \dim B_2=3\cdot1+2\cdot3+7+15+31=62,
 \qquad
 \dim B_3=3\cdot3+2\cdot12+39+120+363=555.
\]

The independent bounded program `code/check_bt1_height6_fermat.py` enumerates all primitive cyclic binary words of lengths two through six and verifies the complete integer base-(p) digit/orbit construction for (p=2,3). The counts are (1,2,3,6,9). It enumerates all sixteen local-local multisets of total height six and checks their required multiplicities. Exactly six have dimension and codimension three:

\[
 (fv)^3,\quad fv\oplus ffvv,\quad ffv\oplus fvv,
 \quad fffvvv,\quad ffvfvv,\quad ffvvfv.
\]

Here a word is a cyclic word, and the superscript in ((fv)^3) means three factors. These six are a covering list of balanced local-local (BT_1) types; **no assertion that every one is realized by a supersingular threefold is needed or made**.

Full words, all sixteen multisets, base-(p) representatives, and every orbit are retained in `output/bt1_height6_fermat.json`; the concise output is `output/bt1_height6_fermat.out`. **Word-order convention, independently flagged by the Frobenius peer.** The program's `actual_word` follows the orbit in the order $u_0u_1\cdots u_{\lambda-1}$. Pries–Ulmer §4.2 instead labels its associated word $w_a=u_{\lambda-1}\cdots u_1u_0$. These conventions differ by reversal, not necessarily by a cyclic rotation; in length six the asymmetric necklaces can therefore exchange labels. Reversal is a bijection on the entire set of primitive cyclic words of each length. Since this certificate includes every such word with the uniform capacity $\lfloor6/\lambda\rfloor$, the covering assertion, multiplicities, product dimensions, and proof remain unchanged. ## BT.9. The proposed principally polarized fourfold bridge is also obstructed for this explicit family

During this continuation root proposed testing whether a supersingular threefold in characteristic three could be a factor of a principally polarized fourfold up to an integer prime to three; a subsequent Prym construction with only powers of two as denominators could then be useful. The following complete argument excludes that bridge for the same (A_t). It does not assume or audit any universal Prym theorem.

**Constant-complement lemma.** For every constant abelian variety (C=(C_0)_k), the product (X=A_t\times C) has no polarization of degree prime to (p). In fact (X\to X^\vee) has no isogeny of degree prime to (p).

**Proof.** Let (D=E^3\times C_0), and let

\[
 q:D_k\longrightarrow X
\]

be the quotient by (H_t\times0). Its degree is (p). If (\lambda:X\to X^\vee) were an isogeny of degree prime to (p), then

\[
 h=q^\vee\lambda q:D_k\longrightarrow D_k^\vee
\]

would be an isogeny with (v_p(\deg h)=2). Both its source and target are constant, so BT.2's Hom rigidity argument makes (h) a homomorphism defined over (k_0).

Take the differential of $h$ on the three elliptic factors. Its three columns $b_1,b_2,b_3$ lie in the $k_0$-vector space $\operatorname{Lie}(D^\vee)$. Since $h$ kills $H_t\times0$,

\[
 b_1+t b_2+t^2b_3=0\quad\text{in }\operatorname{Lie}(D^\vee)\otimes_{k_0}k.
\]

The elements $1,t,t^2$ are linearly independent over $k_0$, hence all three derivative columns vanish. We now justify the required group-scheme conclusion by an elementary formal-coordinate argument, so a full height-one classification theorem is unnecessary.

Let $f:\alpha_p\to G$ be a homomorphism to a smooth algebraic group with $df=0$. Choose formal coordinates at its identity. Each coordinate of $f$ is a polynomial in $z$ modulo $z^p$ with zero constant and linear coefficient. If $f$ is nonzero, let $m$ be the least degree with a nonzero coefficient in some coordinate, and write that coefficient as $c\ne0$. Then $2\le m<p$. The identity $f(z+w)=F_G(f(z),f(w))$ holds in $k[z,w]/(z^p,w^p)$. On the left, the coefficient of $z w^{m-1}$ of total degree $m$ is $mc\ne0$. On the right, the linear part of the formal group law contributes only pure powers in $z$ or $w$, and every nonlinear term has total degree at least $2m$. This is a contradiction. For $p=2$, zero constant and linear coefficients already make every coordinate zero. Thus $df=0$ forces $f=0$ in every characteristic under consideration.

Apply this to the restriction of $h$ to each of the three coordinate copies of $\alpha_p$. Each restriction is zero. Since $h$ is a group homomorphism, it is zero on their product. Consequently $\alpha_p^3\times0\subset\ker h$ as a subgroup scheme. Its order is $p^3$. Factoring the isogeny by this finite subgroup shows $p^3\mid\deg h$, contrary to $v_p(\deg h)=2$. $\square$

This argument concerns the scheme maps throughout; checking only the geometric points of $\alpha_p^3$, which all equal the identity, would prove nothing. An earlier version of this paragraph cited standard height-one Lie faithfulness; the explicit formal-coordinate proof above supplies precisely the needed special case without leaving that step as an external assumption.

**Elliptic-complement corollary.** The product (A_t\times L) has no polarization of degree prime to (p) for any elliptic curve (L/k).

If (L) is supersingular, it is defined over (\overline{\mathbf F}_p) up to isomorphism, so the lemma applies. If (L) is ordinary, there are no nonzero homomorphisms between (L) or (L^\vee) and (A_t) or (A_t^\vee): the latter are isogenous to powers of a supersingular elliptic curve, whereas ordinary and supersingular elliptic curves cannot be isogenous. Every homomorphism

\[
 A_t\times L\longrightarrow A_t^\vee\times L^\vee
\]

is consequently block diagonal. A polarization of degree prime to (p) would restrict to a polarization on (A_t) of degree prime to (p), contradicting the lemma with zero-dimensional complement.

**Actual fourfold-factor corollary.** There do not exist a principally polarized abelian fourfold (B/k), actual homomorphisms (u:A_t\to B), (v:B\to A_t), and an integer (n) prime to (p) such that (vu=[n]_{A_t}).

Indeed (u) has finite kernel and (v) is surjective. Put (L=(\ker v)^0_{\mathrm{red}}), an elliptic abelian subvariety of (B). The addition map

\[
 a:A_t\times L\longrightarrow B,
 \qquad (x,y)\longmapsto u(x)+y
\]

is an isogeny. Its kernel projects injectively to (A_t[n]): if (u(x)+y=0), applying (v) gives (nx=0), and (y) is determined by (x). Hence the kernel is a finite étale group of order prime to (p), and (\deg a) is prime to (p). Pulling a principal polarization back along (a) gives a polarization of (A_t\times L) of degree ((\deg a)^2), contradicting the preceding corollary. This rules out the precise prime-to-three fourfold bridge, without confusing an isogeny decomposition with an actual product decomposition.

**Scope.** The lemma is an additional construction exclusion, not a counterexample to Question2. Larger **nonconstant** complements, and products of nonconstant Jacobians of arbitrary dimensions, are not covered. The p-adic degree obstruction is the same elementary mechanism as the already known nonselfduality examples, now applied to the particular fourfold bridge; it is not counted as a fresh main theorem or a strict reduction of the main gate.

Their ranks are respectively9,12,9,12. It lists the monomial bases of the truncated coordinate Hopf algebras of (\alpha_p^3), with dimensions (p^3), and checks the conflicting degree valuations2 and at least3. This verifies the bounded symbolic arithmetic only. In particular it does not replace the height-one group-scheme faithfulness, Hom rigidity, or isogeny arguments above. No failed run occurred.

## BT.11. Surface-complement extension considered at the checkpoint: not promoted

A different possible extension would use an explicit degree-$p$ presentation of a nonconstant supersingular abelian surface $C$ as $E^2/H_s$, with $H_s$ the line $(1,s)$ in $\alpha_p^2$ and $s\notin k_0$. Conditional on that presentation, the degree obstruction is immediate: the quotient $E^5\to A_t\times C$ has degree $p^2$. A prime-to-$p$ isogeny to the dual would pull back to a constant isogeny of degree valuation four. The independent coefficient comparisons $b_1+t b_2+t^2b_3=0$ and $c_1+s c_2=0$, followed by BT.9's elementary formal-coordinate lemma, would force its kernel to contain $\alpha_p^5$, whose order has valuation five. Constant surface complements are already covered by BT.9.

For a nonsupersingular surface complement, a further argument was only sketched: if it has no supersingular elliptic factor, Hom orthogonality should make the relevant homomorphism block diagonal. If it has such a factor, Poincare reducibility gives an elliptic complement, which must be ordinary; the intersection has no nontrivial $p$-primary subgroup because supersingular elliptic $p$-power torsion is local-local while ordinary elliptic $p$-power torsion is a product of multiplicative and etale groups. This should give a prime-to-$p$ product isogeny and reduce to BT.9. The exact presentation, classification dependencies, and full subgroup comparison were not audited to the required primary-proof standard before the source freeze. **No theorem excluding all surface complements or principally polarized fivefold factors is claimed here.** This remains a conditional proof attempt and supplies no main-gate movement.

# Component Albanese kernels and actual perfect families

Current record: 19 November 2026, after checkpoint20. C.3br and the restricted C.3bs extension are finalized, registered and fully root/two-peer audited. No general SNC or higher-dimensional conclusion is claimed here.

## 1. Exact two-component compatibility gate

For a projective SNC surface E=S∪_C T in characteristic p, rational closed-union K-descent gives the homotopy fibre of K(S×P)⊕K(T×P)→K(C×P) for every fixed smooth proper parameter curve P. A component family must have equal actual restrictions in perfect K0(C×P). Equality of its two endpoint restrictions alone is insufficient.

For a smooth curve A⊂S meeting C transversely, and a Poincare-type line bundle M on A×P, the restriction of the associated component zero-cycle family has the concrete form

    ζ = Σ_{x∈A∩C} m_x [x] ⊠ c1(M_x) ∈ CH0(C×P)_Q.

Each M_x has degree zero on P. Thus the Albanese coordinate on C vanishes. Tensoring M by the pullback of N∈Pic0(P) leaves the endpoint line-bundle classes on A unchanged and changes ζ by [A∩C]⊠c1(N). If n=A·C>0, divisibility of Pic0(P)(k) permits a choice N^n=(⊗ M_x^{m_x})^−1, killing the P Albanese coordinate as well. The remaining obstruction is an explicit element of the Albanese kernel of C×P, represented by

    Σ m_x ([x]−[c0]) ⊠ c1(M_x).

This is only an exact residual expression. It does not assert nonvanishing, injectivity of an exterior-product map, or survival in the puncture quotient. If a component cycle is Albanese-trivial, one may arrange its parameter in a connected reduced kernel of a curve Jacobian map after a rational multiplier, but that alone does not kill this residual product class.

## 2. A complete proper-family correction in C.3br

The final C3_triple_free_component_lifting.tex proves the following stronger positive case. Suppose E has no triple points and the joint alternating restriction

    ρ: ⊕ Pic(E_i)_Q → ⊕ Pic(C_e)_Q

is onto. Move a component point difference on a smooth proper curve P in that component, transverse to all double curves and with endpoints off them. Its edge restrictions are finite sums [c]⊠[p], with every parameter point p different from the two endpoints. For each such p, use ρ to lift the finite edge Picard tuple to component divisor classes. Their exterior products with [p] correct every edge restriction simultaneously and have zero endpoint values. Actual K-descent then produces a perfect family on the fixed E×P. No family-level Picard-surjectivity theorem is required.

The same ρ hypothesis kills the point-parameter K1 edge kernel through Picard-times-units generation. Thus the full top gamma group is the direct sum of component CH0 groups, and its proper-perfect-family quotient is just the component degrees. For a negative exceptional divisor with rational double curves and no triple strata, the normal self-intersection identity supplies an explicit diagonal right inverse to ρ. The exceptional degree matrix then kills all degrees. This proves B²_Q=0 in the exact C.3bm resolved scope, without restrictions on component Albanese kernels. It does not cover general positive-genus edges or any triple strata.

## 4. Remaining triple-stratum question

The initially proposed extension by support avoidance alone is insufficient: rational equivalences of edge point divisors can have different evaluations at the marked triple points. Equality of K0 restrictions by itself does not specify the coherent vertex nullhomotopies in closed-union descent. The canonical totalization and those homotopies must be controlled.

The final C3_component_lifting_no_top_dual_cohomology.tex (C.3bs) supplies one precise sufficient condition: H²(Δ,Q)=0. A rational right inverse to the edge-to-vertex incidence matrix, followed by constant K_j(P) pullback, is onto in every homotopy degree for every actual fixed parameter P. Thus both π0(T_P) and π1(T_P) inject into the edge groups. # Remaining higher ordinary restriction in positive characteristic

Research note, 2026-11-19. Owner: `/root/real_weil`.
**Status: no new proved restriction theorem or counterexample in the remaining high ranges.** This note records the precise source input, unsuccessful reductions, and the missing step. It is not a statement-register entry and does not count as main-gate movement.

## 1. Exact remaining range

For codimension r>=2, the paper has explicit rational ordinary restriction kernels for r+1<=N<=2r (C3aw/ay), and rational ordinary restriction-surjectivity failures for r+2<=N<=2r+1 (C3at/av), over specified transcendental algebraically closed extensions of Fpbar. The unresolved universal high ranges are therefore injectivity for N>=2r+1 and surjectivity for N>=2r+2. The ordinary subgroup is defined by actual fixed-product curve families. Over Fpbar itself all ordinary algebraically trivial classes are torsion; their rationalization is zero. An example over a transcendental algebraically closed extension is needed for a rational failure.

C3as/ba/bb give additive exponent-p quotients of the quotient by ordinary algebraic equivalence. They kill the ordinary subgroup by its p-divisibility. They therefore cannot supply any of the remaining rational ordinary kernels or cokernels.

## 2. The exact formal weak Lefschetz input

**Opened primary source:** Morrow (2019), *K-theory and logarithmic Hodge-Witt sheaves of formal schemes in characteristic p*, Annales scientifiques de l'ENS 52(6),1537--1601, DOI10.24033/asens.2415. Full published PDF:
https://www.numdam.org/item/ASENS_2019__52_6_1537_0.pdf

Freshly read: §6.5 p1593, Theorem6.18 and its complete proof pp1597--1598, Remark6.19 p1598; also Theorem0.7 and the hypotheses of Theorem0.1.

For X smooth projective of dimension d over a perfect field of characteristic p and Y a smooth ample divisor, Theorem6.18 proves that

    lim_s H^i_Zar(Y_s,K_n) -> H^i_Zar(Y,K_n)

has kernel and cokernel annihilated by a power of p if i+n<d-1. In particular its cohomological Chow version is an isomorphism after inverting p for 2n<d-1. Section6.5 explicitly defines CH^n(Y_s)=H^n_Zar(Y_s,K_n); on the nonregular thickenings these are not the usual groups of cycles. The proof uses continuous cohomology and controls the relevant lim^1 term. It supplies neither actual cycles on X nor an actual family on X times a proper parameter curve.

**Inference for the present problem.** Even in a smooth projective ample-divisor reduction, the remaining map from actual Chow classes to the formal cohomological system must be analyzed separately. Moreover, the arbitrary strictly local pair in the question does not automatically come from the ample-divisor setup of this theorem. Neither hypothesis should be suppressed.

## 3. Compatible K0 classes versus an algebraized object

**Opened primary source:** Morrow, *A Variational Tate Conjecture in crystalline cohomology*, author PDF,30pages:
https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~matthew.morrow/Morrow,%20M.,%20Variational%20Tate.pdf
Published metadata independently checked at https://ems.press/journals/jems/articles/16358 : JEMS21(11)(2019),3467--3511, DOI10.4171/JEMS/907. The theorem numbers and page locators below refer to the opened author version, not an uninspected published PDF.

Read Theorem0.6/3.3 and Corollary3.4 with proof, author pp3,18--20. Over a smooth proper scheme over k[[t1,...,tm]], the all-codimension theorem characterizes lifting a special-fibre K0 class to (lim K0(Y_s))[1/p] by a crystalline Chern-character condition. Corollary3.4 gives an actual Picard-group lift, using the separate algebraization isomorphism Pic(X)=lim Pic(Y_s). The author explicitly identifies this as the extra step for line bundles. The higher-codimension theorem does not assert K0(X) surjects onto lim K0(Y_s), or that arbitrary compatible classes admit compatible bounded-rank bundle representatives.

**Inference.** Proper formal GAGA is an equivalence for compatible coherent objects; a compatible sequence of their Grothendieck-group classes is different data. One cannot invoke that equivalence before constructing the required compatible objects. Even after producing a K0 class, preserving ordinary equivalence requires an actual family over the fixed proper parameter curve, rather than separate pointwise lifts.

## 4. Why the existing successful constructions do not immediately extend

### 4.1 Absolute differential detector

The complex C3ao construction uses absolute differential forms from the coefficient field. For an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, every element is a pth power and therefore Omega^1_(k/Fp)=0. Its absolute differential detector vanishes after perfection. A characteristic-p square-zero conormal invariant can instead be additive p-torsion, as in C3as, but then divisibility annihilates every ordinary class and rationalization removes the detector. This is a coefficient obstruction, not an omitted sign or normalization.

**Stronger exact obstruction to the literal product construction (checked 2026-11-19).** Suppose an actual divisor class a on the regular puncture satisfies p^e a=0, and let lambda be an ordinary algebraically trivial class for which the intersection product is defined. Ordinary algebraic equivalence through actual proper-curve families is p^e-divisible: represent lambda as a finite sum of correspondence images of degree-zero divisors on smooth proper curves, use surjectivity of multiplication by p^e on their Jacobians over the algebraically closed field, and push the resulting preimages forward through the same actual families. Thus lambda=p^e mu for another ordinary class mu, and

    a · lambda = a · (p^e mu) = (p^e a) · mu = 0

**integrally**. In particular, if the nil-Pic class in a characteristic-p analogue of C3ao is p-primary torsion, its product with the first Pic0 factor already vanishes; multiplying further factors cannot repair this. The cone rigidity theorem C3ax implies exactly this p-primary property for a divisor class restricting trivially to the exceptional divisor. This argument does not merely say that the differential detector or rationalization loses the class: it says that the proposed ordinary product class itself is zero. It does not assert that every possible characteristic-p ordinary restriction kernel is zero.

### 4.2 Frobenius and coherent deformation bounds

At each fixed nilpotent order, a Frobenius power can annihilate suitable deformation obstructions. This does not provide one power valid at all orders for an arbitrary vector-bundle family. Replacing a bundle V by Frob^{e*}V changes End(V), and the Serre-vanishing threshold for End(Frob^{e*}V) can depend on e. No uniform estimate was obtained here. The successful line-bundle family argument in C3az uses End(L)=O, which is independent of L and permits a fixed finite obstruction range. That step has not been established for higher Chow-family representatives.

### 4.3 Critical incidence example times a projective space

The C3ay relation comes from a regular zero scheme of rank r-1 on its incidence divisor; the zero scheme maps to finitely many points of the elliptic curve, so the chosen Pic0 class restricts trivially there. Increasing the ambient projective factor while retaining codimension r generally makes that base/zero scheme positive-dimensional over the elliptic curve. The Pic0 class no longer restricts trivially, so the crucial annihilator relation is lost. Taking a section independent of the new factor either fails ampleness/isolated-cone requirements or fails to retain the required regular puncture. No high-dimensional kernel follows from that product operation.

There is a precise dimension obstruction for the same elementary annihilator method. Let T have dimension t, let A be ample, and use m+1 sections to form an incidence divisor in P^m times T. A class obtained from the regular rank-m zero locus has the form A^m lambda in codimension r, so lambda has positive codimension c=r-m and m<=r-1. If the sections have no common zero, they define a finite morphism T to P^m: any positive-dimensional fibre would contain a curve on which A has degree zero. Therefore t<=m and the local cone dimension N=m+t+1 is at most 2r-1. If their regular base locus B has codimension m+1, the sufficient condition that lambda restricts to zero on B simply by dimension is

    dim B = t-m-1 < c = r-m,

equivalently t<=r. This gives N<=2r. Thus extending this construction into N>=2r+1 requires a genuine new restriction-vanishing assertion for lambda on the positive-dimensional base locus; dimension and the top-Chern identity alone cannot supply it. This is a limitation of this method, not a universal positive Lefschetz theorem.

### 4.4 Prime-to-p torsion and algebraic representatives

The local étale Lefschetz theorem controls finite covers and certain prime-to-p torsion. It does not, on its own, show that the kernel of a homomorphism from Jacobian points to an arbitrary higher Chow group is the point group of a closed subgroup scheme. Higher ordinary cycle groups need not have the degree-one local Picard representability used in C3n/w/z. Consequently density of prime-to-p torsion is not by itself a proof of the high-codimension rational restriction assertion.

### 4.5 Families on henselized products

Finite-presentation descent gives a cycle or bundle on an étale neighborhood of a henselized product. It does not automatically give a cycle on the fixed ordinary product. Compactifying a parameter curve and applying Zariski Main can introduce extra finite branches; a trace/norm argument has to control their cycle contributions at both parameter values. No such general higher-cycle transfer was proved here. The local Picard construction and the actual-family proof in C3w must not be promoted to an unproved higher Chow statement.

## 5. A higher-rank restriction theorem and its exact limit

The published Bhatt--de Jong paper was freshly reopened through
https://www.numdam.org/item/10.24033/asens.2228.pdf
(The older Numdam filename URL returned an access error.) Theorem0.2, printed p834, states: a vector bundle on a normal projective variety of dimension at least three in characteristic p that is trivial on an ample divisor becomes trivial after sufficiently high Frobenius pullback.

This controls an actual bundle with an actual trivialization after restriction. A zero element in a higher Chow group, or in K0 of the divisor, is not such a trivialized bundle. Converting arbitrary K0 relations into that input would require an additional argument; the theorem is not used here as a blanket injectivity statement for K0 or Chow groups. Existing bibliography key: D_BhattDeJong2014.

## 6. Actual divisor-family lifting on a smooth exceptional divisor

The following is a direct extension of the already audited line-bundle argument in C3az, useful for excluding another proposed counterexample method. It is not a claim about arbitrary higher cycles and is not counted as a separate main-gate advance.

Let R be an excellent henselian local k-algebra in characteristic p, with residue field k, and let Z be projective over R. Suppose the entire reduced closed fibre is a smooth effective Cartier divisor E with ample conormal L=O_Z(-E)|_E. For a **smooth proper curve** P/k and an actual line bundle F on E×P, some finite p-power F^{p^e} is the restriction of an actual line bundle on Z×P. The exponent can be bounded in terms of E,L alone. The curve-parameter hypothesis is essential to the proof.

Indeed, put E_n=V(O_Z(-nE)). The square-zero ideal of E_n×P in E_{n+1}×P is L^n boxtimes O_P. The Picard obstruction is in

    H²(E×P, L^n boxtimes O_P)
      = H²(E,L^n) tensor H⁰(P,O_P)
        ⊕ H¹(E,L^n) tensor H¹(P,O_P).

Serre vanishing makes both summands zero for all n>=n0, for one n0 depending only on E,L. Before n0 each obstruction group has exponent p; the obstruction homomorphism sends the pth tensor power of a partial lift to zero. Successively taking pth powers at these finitely many stages produces a compatible system restricting to F^{p^e}, e<=n0-1. Beyond n0 every step lifts without a further power. There is no unbounded exponent hidden in this construction.

The E-adic and closed-fibre-adic topologies are cofinal. Proper formal existence over the complete ring Rhat algebraizes the resulting compatible line bundle, together with its inverse, on Z_Rhat×P. The regular completion map R→Rhat is a filtered colimit of smooth R-algebras by Popescu. Finite-presentation descent puts the algebraized line bundle on one Z_A×P. The residue map A→k lifts to A→R because R is henselian and A is smooth. Pullback along this lift gives an actual line bundle on Z×P with the prescribed F^{p^e} restriction. Every parameter in this argument remains the fixed actual curve P.

The exact source inputs and their hypotheses are those freshly checked in C3az Step3: Stacks Lemma37.4.1 (Picard obstruction), Lemma30.24.3 (proper formal existence), Lemma15.51.14 (regular completion), Theorem16.12.1 (Popescu), Lemma32.10.3(2) (limit descent of line bundles), and Lemma15.13.3 (smooth henselian lifting), together with coherent Künneth and Serre vanishing. Frobenius independently checked this extension and explicitly confirmed the curve-parameter restriction.

In the algebraizable regular-resolution setting where the C3az K-theory argument gives K0(Z)[1/p]→K0(E)[1/p] injective, determinant consequently makes Pic(Z)[1/p]→Pic(E)[1/p] an isomorphism. The actual family lifting also identifies their ordinary Picard subgroups after inverting p. Using the rational Chern character in that same stated setting, the divisor-generated rational Chow subrings are identified, and products having an ordinary Pic0 factor lift as actual ordinary cycle families. Thus replacing a complex obstruction by an exceptional K3-divisor class times a Pic0 class cannot produce a rational obstruction here merely from failure of that divisor or Pic0 family to extend.

For a higher-dimensional parameter P there is an additional summand H⁰(E,L^n) tensor H²(P,O_P), which need not vanish. No uniform arbitrary-parameter lifting is asserted. More importantly, a general ordinary higher cycle is not necessarily a product of divisor classes on E. Lifting its supporting correspondence, rather than just these line-bundle factors, remains the substantive gap.

## 8. What surface reduction does and does not prove for the ordinary top quotient

Let R be an excellent henselian local domain of dimension N>=2 with an algebraically closed coefficient field k mapping isomorphically to the residue field. Set X=Spec(R) minus its closed point. For each prime q with dim(R/q)=2, let T_q be the finite normalization of R/q and let U_q be its puncture. The normalization is a henselian local domain, with residue field k; it is a normal surface and U_q is regular. Every prime p with dim(R/p)=1 contains such a q, by catenarity. A prime P of T_q over p/q has height one, and the finite map U_q→X pushes [P] to the positive finite multiple [kappa(P):kappa(p)] [p]. Hence the direct sum of these proper pushforwards is surjective:

    direct_sum_q CH¹(U_q)_Q -> CH^{N-1}(X)_Q.

This assertion also descends to the quotients by ordinary algebraic equivalence. Indeed a finite map U_q→X times the SAME smooth proper parameter curve is proper; pushforward of the actual cycle family commutes with the refined restrictions at the two parameter points. The identity follows directly from the proper-pushforward/divisor formula, or from its Cartesian refined-pullback version. No henselized parameter product or pointwise algebraization is substituted. Thus

    direct_sum_q B¹(U_q)_Q -> B^{N-1}(X)_Q

is surjective in this coefficient-field setting. This gives a genuine reduction, but not a general vanishing theorem.

Over k=Fpbar, the surface terms vanish rationally: the strengthened C3be proof uses finite K0 detection, nilpotent invariance, determinant, and the negative exceptional intersection matrix to prove this for arbitrary excellent henselian normal surfaces, including mixed characteristic. ## 9. A finite support-lifting obstruction for restriction in characteristic p

This records the precise K-theoretic reduction proposed by the parent and checked here. It is not a solution of the high-codimension question and is not a new numbered result.

Let R be a noetherian local Fp-domain, let Z→Spec(R) be projective with Z regular and with an isomorphism off the closed point, and let E be the reduced exceptional fibre. Put X=Z−E. For 0≠f in the maximal ideal set D=Z×_R R/(f), and suppose Y=D−E is regular. No henselianity is needed for the following argument. Write j:D→Z and i:E→Z. All K groups in this paragraph are perfect-complex K groups; G0 denotes coherent K theory.

The enlarged centre V(f) still gives an abstract blowup square, since Z→Spec(R) is an isomorphism away from that centre. KST TheoremA and(1.6) give

    K0(R) → {K0(R/f^b)}_b ⊕ K0(Z) → {K0(D_b)}_b,

where D_b=Z×_R R/(f^b). Both local base-ring K0 groups are Z, and quotienting the diagonal graph yields a pro-monomorphism from the constant group K0(Z). Its decreasing kernel system has inclusion transition maps, so one finite b detects K0(Z). For that finite b, GH TheoremA and finite affine Zariski descent identify K0(D_b)_Q with K0(D)_Q: the immersion is nilpotent and p=0 on every affine chart. Consequently j*:K0(Z)_Q→K0(D)_Q is injective. The finite detecting level is important: no uniform p-exponent over an infinite tower is asserted or needed for this injection.

G-theory localization on regular Z gives

    G0(E)_Q --i_*--> K0(Z)_Q → K0(X)_Q → 0.

Perfect-complex localization on D gives

    K0(D on E)_Q → K0(D)_Q → K0(Y)_Q.

Therefore, identifying K0(Z)_Q with its image under j*, the restriction kernel is precisely

    ker(K0(X)_Q → K0(Y)_Q)
      ≅ ( j*K0(Z)_Q ∩ im[K0(D on E)_Q→K0(D)_Q] )
          / j*i_*G0(E)_Q.

The denominator is indeed contained in the numerator: exceptional classes vanish on Y. Both directions follow by choosing a lift in K0(Z), using exactness on D, and changing the lift by i_*G0(E). Thus the issue is a finite support-lifting problem on the whole singular fibre D, not failure to detect a class at any finite infinitesimal order.

The numerator cannot be silently replaced by coherent classes on E. A supported perfect class on the generally singular D has additional perfect-complex information; the map K0(D)→G0(D) need not be injective. Derived restriction of an exceptional coherent sheaf involves Tor terms, so replacing it by its ordinary sheaf restriction also changes the problem. No argument has shown that every class in this intersection is the restriction of an exceptional G0 class on Z, either in the high Adams weights or on the subgroup obtained from actual ordinary families. The usual rational Chern-character comparison with Chow must separately have its regular algebraizable/finite-model hypotheses verified before a weight-r reformulation is made. The formula by itself gives no dimension bound, no high-codimension injectivity, and no actual-family surjectivity.

Primary inputs are the already opened KST TheoremA/(1.6), Geisser--Hesselholt TheoremA, and Thomason--Trobaugh localization and Zariski descent. The exact localization applications here are to perfect complexes with support on D and to coherent sheaves on regular Z respectively; they are not interchanged.

## 10. Integral ordinary p-torsion: a distinct but unfinished lead

The high rational ranges in Section1 remain open in this work. An
integral-only counterexample would nevertheless have to be distinguished
from them. An abstract group calculation supplies a possible source of
ordinary p-torsion, but does not by itself give a geometric example.

Let E be an ordinary elliptic curve over an algebraically closed field of
characteristic p, and let G be a nonzero extension of E by Ga. Such
extensions are classified by H1(E,O_E). Write V:E^(p)→E for Verschiebung.
Since [p]^*=0 on H1(O), whereas relative Frobenius is bijective on that
space in the ordinary case, V^*=0. The pullback extension therefore
splits and gives a group morphism j:E^(p)→G over V. Its scheme kernel is a
subgroup of the étale group ker(V) of order p. If it were all of ker(V),
j would descend to a section of G→E, contradicting nontriviality.
Consequently j is a closed immersion, and its proper abelian image B has

    B intersect Ga = j(ker V) ≅ Z/p.

Frobenius independently checked this abstract calculation. No claim is
made that the extension is already the local Picard group of a pair in
the question. In particular, a split cone has a retraction and a split
Picard extension; there is no such nonzero proper-abelian intersection
with its vector factor. A genuinely nonsplit neighborhood is necessary.

The smallest suggested geometric test is r=2,N=5. One can try a
deformation of the cone with exceptional variety
V=P1×W×C, where W is a smooth quartic K3 carrying a line D, C is an
ordinary smooth plane quartic, and L=O_P1(1) external O_W(1) external K_C.
Replacing the split cone equation by F_C+t ell H_C, as in C3m, gives a
candidate nontrivial first neighborhood. The desired kernel direction
would lie in ell H1(V,O_V) inside H1(V,L). To obtain a counterexample one
must prove all of the following for this actual pair: the relevant
nontrivial vector extension is its actual local Picard extension; its
separable p-isogeny kernel is realized by actual ordinary line-bundle
families; the selected line bundle restricts to zero on the punctured
divisor; and its product with the nondivisible divisor class D remains
nonzero in CH2 of the source puncture. None of those four geometric
claims has been certified for this candidate.

The elementary obstruction in Section4.1 does not kill this proposed
product: its second factor is a Néron--Severi divisor, rather than an
ordinary divisible Picard class. However, the naive conormal dlog
detector has a new serious limitation. In a nonsplit square-zero
neighborhood the sequence with conormal term
L tensor Omega1_V and quotient Omega2_V need not split. Its connecting
map is contraction with the neighborhood's Kodaira--Spencer class.
For a direction a=c_kappa(omega) and a divisor pulled back from a factor
on which kappa is zero, the expression a cup c1(D) is the connecting
image of omega wedge c1(D). Thus that expression can vanish in the
absolute differential cohomology used by the split-neighborhood proof.
A relative K-theory or logarithmic de Rham--Witt argument would have to
control its additional boundary maps; the split conormal detector from
C3ao cannot simply be reused. This is a method limitation, not a proof
that the proposed cycle is zero.

torsion. Any candidate must either satisfy that hypothesis and therefore
fail as a Picard-kernel construction, or explicitly lie outside it. No

## 2. Why finite covers alone do not remove the remaining edge cycle

Let C and P be smooth projective curves, and let zeta belong to CH0(C times P)_Q. For a finite surjective morphism f:P'→P of degree d, smoothness of the curves makes f finite flat. Proper pushforward and flat pullback give

    (id_C times f)_* (id_C times f)^* zeta = d zeta.

Hence a nonzero rational zeta cannot become zero merely by this finite parameter change. This is a direct projection-formula calculation; it does not prove that a particular graph-family obstruction is nonzero. The marked edge construction of C.3bt does more than pull back a fixed cycle: it changes the rational unit, arranging that unit to equal one at each divisor-support point. That mechanism acts in K1 and does not itself provide a K0 correction of a component graph family.

For a curve A in a component S and a line-bundle family on A times P, the already recorded obstruction is a sum of products [q] exterior c1(N_q) on each double curve times P. Killing its two Albanese coordinates leaves an explicit Albanese-kernel product. No general injectivity or nonvanishing of that product map is claimed.

## 3. Why exceptional Picard images alone do not solve the problem

On a single smooth component S with Pic(S)_Q generated by an ample divisor H and normal class N a nonzero rational multiple of H, the map theta on Pic(S)_Q has nonzero degree on every nonzero divisor class. Consequently theta(Pic(S)_Q) intersect S00 is zero. Thus the proposed argument that exceptional divisor intersections alone must generate every component Albanese kernel has no general linear-algebra basis. No new example of a normal local threefold or new positive-characteristic K3 nonvanishing theorem is asserted here.

One tempting modification was checked explicitly. Blow up the regular ambient threefold along a smooth curve A in a component S. The new exceptional component R is a ruled surface over A. For L in Pic0(A), the theta image of its pullback to R has component restrictions of the form

    (i_{A,*} c1(L), -c1(L))

on S and R, up to the fixed normal/sign conventions and the other intersection coordinates. This is already an exceptional Poincare relation. It does not isolate the first coordinate: C.3bo's weighted Albanese map on the Poincare subgroup is an isogeny. Rationally that subgroup is a graph over the component Albanese coordinates, with zero intersection with T_E. The unique Albanese correction subtracts the same S contribution. A separate proper family on R with controlled restrictions to its boundary would still be necessary. This modification is therefore not a proved reduction.

## 4. Synchronized curve covers and framed-bundle routes

To glue actual graph correspondences across an edge, equality is required for the complete edge K0 classes on C times P. Prescribing equality at finitely many parameter endpoints is weaker. A proposed common finite cover of curves on adjacent components would have to synchronize the entire pullback divisors of the marked intersection points, including multiplicities. A map to P1 generally has additional points in every prescribed fibre; suppressing them would require rational functions with divisors constrained to the marked sets. No such general construction was proved.

A separate framed-bundle idea asks for complete families of bundles on a component with constant K-class along its boundary. The usual moduli spaces are quasi-projective, and a compactification by torsion-free sheaves does not automatically preserve the boundary restriction or yield a perfect family on the singular union. No general properness or rigidity theorem for these framed moduli was imported.

For an ample boundary D in a projective surface S, every closed curve in (S minus D) times a proper curve P which is proper over k has constant image in the affine variety S minus D. Thus literal zero-cycle families whose support avoids D on the whole proper parameter cannot move points in S minus D. This elementary observation does not classify relative perfect K0 families: a relative K-class on S times P need not be represented by codimension-two cycles disjoint from D times P. Equating these two notions would be an additional theorem, and is not assumed.

## 8. A limited relative-Picard proper-family construction

Let S be one smooth component and D its whole intersection with the union F of the other components. Suppose a line bundle M on S is equipped with an actual trivialization along D. The pair gives a relative K0 class m on (S,D) whose absolute image is [M] minus one. Let L belong to Pic0(S). Choose a smooth proper connected curve P through the origin and L in Pic0(S), and pull back a normalized Poincare line bundle L_P to S times P. The product

    m times ([L_P] minus one)

is an actual relative K0 class on (S times P,D times P). The closed-cover fibre sequence for E=S union F sends it to an actual K0 class on E times P, with zero restriction to F times P. Taking its finite weight-two projector gives a defining proper family. Its component endpoint on S is c1(M)c1(L), and every other component endpoint is zero. This proof uses the supplied boundary trivialization, not only equality of endpoint restrictions.

If M itself belongs to Pic0(S), the product has zero Albanese class by the already audited product-of-algebraically-trivial-classes statement. Thus products from ker(Pic0(S)→Pic(D)) times Pic0(S) are explicitly removed by proper families. This does not remove arbitrary component Albanese kernels; it may give nothing when the boundary restriction on Pic0 is injective up to isogeny. It is recorded as an auxiliary family mechanism, not a new main reduction.

## 9. Actual framed bundles: a precise rigidity statement and its limit

**Nevins, T. A. (2002). Representability for some moduli stacks of framed sheaves. Manuscripta Mathematica, 109(1), 85–91. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00229-002-0290-z**

The entire six-page primary v2 PDF at https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0008190, dated10May2002, was opened and read, including the complete proof of Proposition3 and the complete proof of Theorem1. The author's institutional publication record at https://experts.illinois.edu/en/publications/representability-for-some-moduli-stacks-of-framed-sheaves/ was separately opened to verify the journal metadata; the seven-page published layout was not read. The proof's external Cartan–Eilenberg spectral sequence and Sernesi representability references were not newly opened. An institutional route to a different framed-moduli paper returned403; no mathematical claim was taken from that unavailable file.

Nevins's Proposition3 constructs an affine-bundle tower A_n for vector bundles on the infinitesimal neighborhoods D(n), with a fixed framing F on a smooth curve D in a complex projective surface S, provided H0(D,End(F) tensor N_{D/S}^{-n})=0 for every positive n. For a fixed F the base of the tower is a point, so every A_n is affine.

This gives the following direct auxiliary consequence. Assume additionally that D is ample. A vector bundle V on S times a smooth connected proper curve P, with an actual isomorphism V restricted to D times P equal to the pullback of F, has pairwise isomorphic fibres on S. Indeed its maps P→A_n are constant because P is proper connected and A_n affine. The bundles V_t and V_o therefore have isomorphic restrictions to D(n) for every n. For fixed t, write H=Hom(V_t,V_o), a vector bundle on S. For sufficiently large n, Serre duality followed by Serre vanishing gives H1(S,H(-(n+1)D))=0. The exact divisor sequence then lifts an isomorphism on D(n) to a global homomorphism V_t→V_o. Its determinant is nonzero along D. Its zero divisor would be an effective divisor disjoint from ample D, which is impossible. The global homomorphism is therefore an isomorphism.

This consequence is used only in the complex, smooth-divisor scope just stated; no unproved extension of the source's moduli theorem to arbitrary characteristic is imported. It is a restriction on **actually framed vector bundles**. A class in relative K0 or an equality of virtual K0 classes on D times P does not provide such an actual fixed framing of any chosen vector-bundle representative. Equality in the Grothendieck group includes exact-sequence relations and does not mean the bundles are isomorphic. No compatible stabilization/presentation theorem bridging this distinction has been proved. Thus the rigidity statement supplies neither nonvanishing of the present quotient nor a counterexample to any C.3bt conclusion.

# Residual top ordinary quotient: research record

**Updated 2026-11-19, after the certification of C.3ab and C.3ad.**

The unrestricted groups still at issue are ordinary
\(B^{N-1}(\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus\{\mathfrak m\})\), for \(N\ge3\).
Here ordinary algebraic equivalence always means differences of fibres on
actual fixed products with smooth parameter curves. An equality in a
henselized product or a compatible system of classes on infinitesimal
neighbourhoods is not an actual-product family.

## 1. Certified positive subset and its precise limit

The final, independently checked `C3_surface_cone_top.tex` proves, integrally,
for the stated smooth surface cones with
\(H^2(V,\Omega^1_{V/\mathbb Q}\otimes L^j)=0\) for all \(j>0\),
\[
 CH^2(X)=CH_0(V)/(L\,CH^1(V)),\qquad B^2(X)=\mathbb Z/g\mathbb Z.
\]
This includes every such cone over \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\), and over arbitrary
algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields when \(H^2(V,L^j)=0\) for
all \(j>0\). It is a restricted-family result. It does not settle the
unrestricted top question or establish finiteness for all complex surface
cones. Root and Frobenius independently checked the complete eight-step
argument and the exact primary sources. It is integrated after C.3aa.

The final `C3_rational_top_cones.tex` (C.3ad), independently audited by
root and Frobenius, additionally proves for every such smooth projective
cone over Qbar in every dimension d+1>=3 that
`CH^d(X)_Q = CH0(V)_Q / L.CH^(d-1)(V)_Q` and `B^d(X)_Q=0`.
This is rational in dimensions d>2 and remains a restricted smooth-cone
statement; it is not counted as main-gate movement.

## 2. An explicit proper-curve family for every field \(K_2\) symbol

**Auxiliary lemma, proved; independently checked by Frobenius. No Chow
consequence is inferred.** Let \(k\) be algebraically closed and let
\(a,b\in k^*\). There exist a smooth projective connected curve \(C/k\),
points \(P,Q\in C(k)\), and \(\xi\in K_2(C)\) such that
\[
                    P^*\xi-Q^*\xi=\{a,b\}\in K_2(k).
\]

If either input is 1 the symbol is zero and the claim is immediate. Otherwise
put \(c=(a-1)^2(b-1)^2/(ab)\ne0\), and consider in
\(\mathbb P^1_f\times\mathbb P^1_g\) the closure of
\[
                 (f-1)^2(g-1)^2=c f g.                 \tag{T.1}
\]
Choose a component through \((a,b)\) and normalize its reduced structure.
There are no vertical or horizontal components: substituting any fixed
value in either coordinate never makes the homogeneous equation identically
zero. Thus both coordinate maps on the normalization are nonconstant and
surjective. The only point of (T.1) on \(f=0\) is \((0,1)\), and the
derivative with respect to \(f\) there is \(-c\). Hence this is a smooth
point of the original curve, with one point \(Q\) on the normalization.
The normalization of the chosen integral component is a smooth proper
connected curve over the algebraically closed field. A point \(P\) over
\((a,b)\) exists even if that point of (T.1) is singular.

The boundary points of the curve have the following forms:
\[
 (f=0,g=1),\quad(f=\infty,g=1),\quad
 (g=0,f=1),\quad(g=\infty,f=1).
\]
Consequently every tame residue of \(\{f,g\}\in K_2(k(C))\) is 1.
The localization sequence for a smooth curve therefore lifts this symbol
to \(\xi\in K_2(C)\). The exact primary input is Quillen (1973), Section 7,
Proposition 3.2, equation (3.3), printed p.127, together with the filtered
limit over nonempty affine opens; the geometric Gersten theorem, Section 7,
Theorem 5.11, printed pp.133–134, gives the injectivity
\(K_2(\mathcal O_{C,x})\to K_2(k(C))\) needed to identify evaluations
with the following local expressions. These statements were directly
opened in the primary PDF, not inferred from a later survey.

Near \(Q\), the curve equation gives
\[
 f=u(g-1)^2,\qquad u=(f-1)^2/(cg)\in\mathcal O_{C,Q}^*.
\]
The Steinberg relation shows
\(\{g-1,g\}=\{g,-1\}\), which is killed by 2. Thus
\(\{f,g\}=\{u,g\}\) in the function field, hence also for its unique
local lift. Its specialization at \(Q\) is \(\{u(Q),1\}=0\).
At \(P\), both functions are units and specialization is \(\{a,b\}\).
This proves the lemma. The proof also applies in characteristic 2: the
derivative \(-c\) at \(Q\) remains nonzero and the same Steinberg identity
holds. The integral statement for field \(K_2\) uses the usual Matsumoto
presentation of \(K_2(k)\) by Steinberg symbols.

This prevents treating a bare \(K_2(k)\) summand in a prospective
normal-crossing calculation as automatically rigid under proper parameter
curves. It does **not** show that a family on an exceptional divisor lifts
to its regular resolution. It also does not assert that all higher Quillen
\(K_n(k)\) are generated by Milnor symbols. There is, however, a precise
further consequence: for n>=2, multiplying the constructed class by
constant classes \(\{a_3,\ldots,a_n\}\) realizes the image of every
Milnor symbol \(\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}\) in Quillen K-theory as an actual
proper-curve evaluation difference. Additivity treats a finite sum.
Thus no Milnor-symbol term in a prospective top-weight exceptional-divisor
descent calculation is automatically rigid. The map from that exceptional
calculation to actual fixed-product families on the puncture is still
required; no such map is constructed by this observation alone.

## 3. The analogous absolute-differential spanning statement

**Auxiliary statement proved at the nilpotent-parameter level.** In
characteristic zero, every element of \(\Omega^1_{k/\mathbb Q}\) is a sum
of differences of evaluations of global absolute 1-forms on smooth proper
curves. It suffices to treat \(a\,db\), since these generate the module.
There is nothing to prove if \(b\) is algebraic over \(\mathbb Q\).
Take the fixed elliptic curve \(E:y^2=x^3-x\) over
\(\overline{\mathbb Q}\), with its regular form \(\omega=dx/y\), and
choose \(P=(b,y)\in E(k)\), where \(y^2=b^3-b\). Since \(b\) is
transcendental, \(y\ne0\). If \(Q\) is an algebraic point, then
\[
          P^*(a y\omega)-Q^*(a y\omega)=a\,db.
\]
The coefficient \(ay\) is a scalar multiplying the differential; no
differentiation of that scalar is implicit. The absolute form \(\omega\)
is the base extension of the algebraic invariant differential, and it
vanishes on pullback to an algebraic point because
\(\Omega^1_{\overline{\mathbb Q}/\mathbb Q}=0\).

For \(E_\epsilon=E\times\operatorname{Spec}k[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2\),
the calculation in C.3ab identifies
\(\mathcal K_2(E_\epsilon,E)=\Omega^1_{E/\mathbb Q}\).
The dimension-one descent spectral sequence has only columns 0 and 1,
so its edge map
\[
 K_2(E_\epsilon,E)\longrightarrow
 H^0(E,\mathcal K_2(E_\epsilon,E))
\]
is surjective. Consequently the preceding differences of forms really
are evaluations of actual relative \(K_2\) classes on the fixed proper
curve times the dual numbers. The same finite-order argument works for
each specified positive homogeneous degree of a split truncated polynomial
thickening. This is still a statement about finite thickenings.

## 4. The missing actual-family step

For a complex surface cone, the new part that C.3ab does not eliminate
comes from the absolute coefficient term in
\[
0\to\Omega^1_{k/\mathbb Q}\otimes\mathcal O_V
 \to\Omega^1_{V/\mathbb Q}\to\Omega^1_{V/k}\to0.
\]
The cohomological candidate is a quotient of
\(\Omega^1_{k/\mathbb Q}\otimes H^2(V,L^j)\); the relative term in
\(H^2(\Omega^1_{V/k}L^j)\) vanishes by Kodaira–Akizuki–Nakano.
The elliptic-curve construction explains why an assertion that all such
classes are constant on proper parameter curves would be false at the
differential level. It does not prove that the corresponding class on
\(V_a\times E\) is the restriction of a class on \(Z\times E\).

The two exact missing steps are: (i) construct the compatible classes or
objects on all exceptional thickenings, with the desired endpoint classes;
(ii) algebraize a family on the **actual** fixed product and, in the
henselian case, descend it from the completion. Finite-level injectivity of
\(K_0(Z)\to K_0(V_a)\), proved in C.3ab, alone implies neither step and
does not imply injectivity after quotienting by algebraic equivalence.

This is not an abstract precaution without a counterexample. Bloch,
Esnault, and Kerz (2014), *Deformation of algebraic cycle classes in
characteristic zero*, Appendix B, Proposition B.5, directly proves that
\(K_0(Y_{\mathbb C[[t]]})_\mathbb Q\to
(\varprojlim K_0(Y_{\mathbb C[t]/t^n}))\otimes\mathbb Q\)
is not surjective for a smooth projective even-dimensional \(Y/\mathbb Q\)
with positive geometric genus. Their Lemma B.7 nevertheless realizes the
specified finite-order differential contributions by actual moving point
sections. The counterexample assembles these with unbounded differential
complexity across orders. Both the complete statement and proof of
Proposition B.5 and Lemmas B.2, B.3, B.7 were read in the primary text.

The ample conormal bundle in the cone problem makes the relevant coherent
cohomology vanish in sufficiently high degree, unlike the trivial
\(\mathbb C[[t]]\) deformation in that counterexample. This is a possible
route to a stronger theorem, **not a proof** of a uniform algebraization
statement. Ordinary zero-cycle moving on a resolution and a proper-parameter
version of finite-order algebraization remain the next precise targets.

## 5. Literature examined and rejected in this scope

1. Kohrita (2024), *The algebraic part of motivic cohomology*, arXiv
   1512.02320v3, 10 April 2024, Theorem 1.1, Definition 2.3 and Proposition
   2.10: the general motivic equivalence uses smooth parameters and
   semiabelian varieties. It cannot silently replace actual proper-curve
   families on our non-finite-type puncture.
2. Kerz–Saito–Tamme (2019), *K-theory of non-Archimedean rings I*,
   Documenta Mathematica 24, 1365–1411, Section 1.1, p.1366: directly read
   the formulation of the \(K_0\)-algebraization problem and the warning
   referring to BEK Appendix B. Formal GAGA for coherent sheaves is not
   surjectivity on an inverse limit of Grothendieck groups.
3. Results of Lüders, Esnault–Wittenberg/Bloch, Saito–Sato and
   Binda–Krishna on relative zero-cycles over henselian **DVRs** do not
   directly apply to a resolution proper over the higher-dimensional
   local ring in this question. Lüders (2019), *Algebraization for
   zero-cycles and the p-adic cycle class map*, Mathematical Research
   Letters26(2),557-585, was subsequently opened in full at
   https://arxiv.org/pdf/1709.05622 (v3,28October2019). Theorem1.2,
   Proposition5.1 and its proof, and Corollary5.4, authorpp1-2,9-12,
   were read directly. The introduction and Section5 explicitly assume
   a smooth projective scheme over an excellent henselian DVR, despite
   the abstract's broader phrase “henselian local ring.” Its idelic
   proof may motivate a separately proved endpoint extension, but
   would still not give the one-dimension-higher proper-parameter
   family required here. The other listed works were search leads;
   no theorem from their unopened full text is claimed as an input.
4. A prospective normal-crossing exceptional divisor with spherical dual
   complex could produce a field \(K_n\) term in a descent computation.
   The resolution, exact differentials and actual-family survival must
